- The Heavenly Principles take the Sovereigns' Authorities and win the first war.
- The War of Funerary Flame ends about 6,000 years ago with the Celestial Nails.
- The Archon War: seats open about 6,000 years ago and the war closes about 2,000 years ago.
- The Cataclysm: about 500 years ago, Khaenri'ah's fall.
- Post-Cataclysm: the Abyss Order is founded and Albedo created.
- The Traveler wakes after 500 years of stasis.
- Gnoses reaching the Fatui in the story: Anemo (Prologue, taken by Signora), Geo (Chapter I, by contract), Electro (traded by Yae Miko to Scaramouche in Chapter II, taken by Nahida and then given to Dottore in Chapter III), Dendro (Chapter III, to Dottore), Hydro (Chapter IV, given to Arlecchino by Neuvillette). The Pyro Gnosis never reached the Fatui; it was used to burn Irminsul in the Nod-Krai arc and then vanished.
- Ronova's fall (7.1): Celestia confiscates her authority, Pierro mortally wounds her, and she uses Eitr to make the Celestial Nail over the Cryo Dragon's corpse crumble, after which the other fallen Nails emit pillars of light into the sky.

The count is consistent: the six Gnoses held for the Tsaritsa by 7.1 are Cryo, Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro, and she used them to manipulate time and space in Chapter VII Act IV. In Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (Song of the Welkin Moon Act X) the Traveler borrowed the Pyro Gnosis from Mavuika so Nahida could burn Irminsul, and it disappeared; the Traveler tells the Tsaritsa it burned with Irminsul, while she believes that, as a remnant of the Third Descender, it will eventually be ejected from the Ley Lines.

Accounts: Different sources frame the same history differently. The Heavenly Principles forbade knowledge of what came before the War of Funerary Flame, so most mortal myths are second hand. Celestia-aligned voices tell a story of purification and protection, Khaenri'ahn and Abyss-aligned voices tell of divine cruelty, and Dottore and Pierro claim secret knowledge. The wiki's editors add their own deductions and mark them as such.
For roleplay, a character should usually give only the era-slice they could plausibly know: Mondstadt folk know the Archon War through legend; Sumeru's scholars know more but from censored sources; Fatui and Khaenri'ahn survivors know most, with bias.

Open questions: Open as of 7.1: the exact date and cause of the Heavenly Principles' arrival, how much of the wiki's pre-war reconstruction is right, what the Heavenly Principles intend, what became of Nibelung, why the Three Moons died, and what exactly destroyed the Traveler's home world. Nothing past 7.1 is recorded here.
The sibling's exact goals, the Heavenly Principles' dormancy and the Third Descender's seal at the Zapolyarny Palace also remain unresolved.

Connections: Cross-reference the regional history entries (Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan, Snezhnaya, Khaenri'ah), the Archon War and Cataclysm lore entries, the Unified Civilization and War of Funerary Flame entries, and the Night Warden Wars. Cosmology entries for the Seven Sovereigns, Heavenly Principles, Four Shades, Celestia, Three Moons, False Sky and Celestial Nails give background; the Fatui and the Abyss Order drive the story-present.

Status as of 7.1: Current to Version 7.1 (2026-09-23): the Traveler is in Snezhnaya after Ronova's fall, and the fallen Celestial Nails have begun emitting pillars of light. Pre-Archon-War dating stays approximate.

36.comment: Timeline of Teyvat: Archon War dating
36.content: The Archon War ran from about 6,000 to 2,000 years ago, when seven divine seats opened and gods fought over them, ending when the last seat was claimed. See the dedicated Archon War entry for the war itself; here it is a marker between the War of Funerary Flame and the Post-Archon War.

37.content: The Cataclysm happened about 500 years ago: Khaenri'ah was destroyed by the Heavenly Principles and the Abyss invaded the surface world. Asmoday sealed both twins around this time, and the Traveler slept for 500 years. See the Cataclysm and fall of Khaenri'ah lore entries for the event.

38.comment: Timeline of Teyvat: War of Funerary Flame dating
38.content: Around 6,000 years ago the Heavenly Principles won the war against Nibelung's Abyssal rebellion and cast the Celestial Nails to purify Teyvat. Knowledge of the era before this war was forbidden. See the War of Funerary Flame entry for details.

39.comment: Timeline of Teyvat: The Wanderer's Trail
39.content: The Prologue's Wanderer's Trail shows the twins trying to leave Teyvat during the Cataclysm and being stopped by an unknown god (later shown to be Asmoday), who seals the Traveler and takes the sibling; the Traveler wakes 500 years later. Later quests show the twins had crash-landed on Teyvat earlier, before the Cataclysm. This anchors the story-present at roughly 500 years after the Cataclysm.

40.content:
Mondstadt/History (also: History of Mondstadt, Mondstadt Timeline, Mondstadt Chronology): Mondstadt's history runs from the lost northern kingdom of Arcadia and the snow-buried mountain city of Sal Vindagnyr, through the tyrant god Decarabian's walled city, which fell about 2,600 years ago when his people rebelled and the wind spirit Barbatos became the Anemo Archon. The noble clans who followed turned tyrannical until the gladiator Vennessa, about 1,000 years ago, overthrew them and founded the Knights of Favonius. About 500 years ago the Cataclysm brought the dragon Durin down on Mondstadt before Barbatos and Dvalin killed him. The recent past (to 7.1) covers the Ragnvindr family tragedy, the Stormterror crisis and Varka's expedition to Nod-Krai.

The sections below follow the order the wiki timeline uses: Unified Civilization, War of Funerary Flame, the Interim Period, the Archon War and Age of Kings, the aristocratic period, Mondstadt Reborn, the Cataclysm, the post-Cataclysm centuries, and the recent past. Many dates are only "unknown years ago", and the ordering is partly an editors' reconstruction.

Unified civilization: In Teyvat's unified civilization, the people of Arcadia lived in the vast oak forests of what became Mondstadt. Their city-state Elysium stood in Windrest Peak under the Gunnhildr Clan. They built the Temple of Space for Asmoday and the Thousand Winds Temple for Istaroth, and worshipped the Three Moons, especially the Frost Moon goddess under the name Prusmene. After a disaster the Temple of Space was lifted into the sky, where Asmoday made it "Segment-Domain Tau", while the ruins left on the ground became her sanatorium.

Separately, refugees from a land of snow and strife found a green mountain, raised a monument on its peak and called their civilisation Sal Vindagnyr and the mountain Vindagnyr. They built a large castle there. Starsilver ore is native to the mountain. A great white tree stood at the heart of the city; its princess, born under it, inherited her priestess mother's gift of foresight and once dreamed of Durin spreading poison across the land, which her people feared as a curse. Celestia was moored over the mountain for an unknown span.

War of funerary flame: About 6,000 years ago, according to the wiki timeline, an unknown calamity buried Arcadia under endless winter and the civilisation collapsed; the Thousand Winds Temple fell to ruin. Gunnhildr, the Knight of the Golden Bough, travelled the frozen north to find the legendary Golden Bough, a branch of Irminsul, hoping to restore the kingdom. He met the self-styled fae king Jack Frost King, fought him, and found the bough withered. Accepting that Arcadia could not return, he gathered its survivors and led them south to the tower where the wicked dragon had once been cast down, seeking shelter under Decarabian.

On Dragonspine, the Skyfrost Nail fell and shrouded Sal Vindagnyr in cloud and snow, then broke into three fragments, one of which turned the sacred tree into the Frostbearing Tree. The princess gave the outlander Imunlaukr a starsilver greatsword, and he left to seek a branch of Irminsul. While he was away the trees withered, the princess failed to finish her frescoes, tried to graft a branch onto another tree and died beside it when it withered. Imunlaukr returned to find everyone dead, left the sword between the frescoes and went to war, destroying three thriving kingdoms. The survivors hunted him, and he eventually gave up the life of a warrior. (The Imunlaukr Clan later bore his name.)

Interim period: Between the Great War and the Archon War the wiki places an unnamed stretch of peace. At an unknown point Boreas, the Wolf of the North, came to Mondstadt from Nod-Krai hoping to bring prosperity. Instead the region filled with blizzards and became inhospitable; canon is ambiguous about whether this was intentional. To shelter his city, Decarabian raised a storm wall around it.

Age of kings: More than 2,600 years ago Boreas declared war on Decarabian, but could not scratch the walled city, so the war between the two "Kings of Ice and Frost" became a stalemate. Decarabian's people began to see his rule as despotism. Gunnhildr's clan sought refuge in his city, but Gunnhildr's father led them out again; they built a shrine in the Thousand Winds Temple and prayed to Istaroth, and a tiny wind spirit, later Barbatos, answered and gained strength from their faith. A boy known only as the Nameless Bard befriended the spirit; he dreamed of birds, green grass and the world outside the walls. Inside the city a resistance used "Windblume" as its code word, the Red-Haired Warrior among the first to say it.

Further notes from this period: the first wine was supposedly brewed when the wind spirit in fox form fermented apples left with a careless guard; a wine for forgetting the past was also brewed so people could keep going. Leonard the adventurer invented the wind glider and failed to climb Pilos Peak (now Musk Reef), writing "Of Mountains and Seas" about the attempt. Boreas realised that blizzards could not nurture life and that he lacked the qualifications to be an Archon, so (in this placement) he let his body die and sent his power into the land; his spirit remains and can manifest a body of ice and wind. This placement is disputed, as noted in the uncertainties.

Decarabians fall: About 2,600 years ago the people rose, led by the Nameless Bard, the wind spirit Barbatos, Decarabian's former lover Amos, Gunnhildr and the Red-Haired Warrior, with Gunnhildr's clan fighting too. Decarabian and Amos died, and his death unleashed a violent tempest.

The Nameless Bard played his lyre with a melody that belonged to Istaroth, turning the storm into the song that became Mondstadt, but could not bear that power, died as the tower fell and was forgotten. Barbatos rose to godhood as the Anemo Archon and quietly kept the bard's lost name, Venti. The Red-Haired Warrior turned from Barbatos for reasons unclear; his line eventually produced Ragnvindr and the Ragnvindr family.

Barbatos then reshaped the land: his winds cleared snow and ice, Pilos Peak was levelled into Musk Reef, and the people moved from Decarabian's old city to Cider Lake to build the present Mondstadt. Prominent clans were the Gunnhildr Clan under Gunnhildr, the Imunlaukr Clan (leader at the time unknown) and the Lawrence Clan under Venerare. The Thousand Winds Temple was rebuilt for both Barbatos and Istaroth until Istaroth was forgotten, for unknown reasons. Seeing the people strong and wise enough to live without him, Barbatos left so he could never become a tyrant, and the Windblume Festival began in memory of those who fought for freedom; the code word later became tangled with real flowers and the festival became one of love.

Early aristocracy: From about 2,600 to 1,600 years ago aristocrats blessed with divine power led Mondstadt after Barbatos left, their clans descended from heroes of his early city (Lawrence, Gunnhildr, Imunlaukr and others), and at first they ruled for the people's good. Venerare of the Lawrence Clan built the statue of Barbatos before the Favonius Cathedral, with an inscription by the clan leaders pledging to defend Mondstadt. Many customs took shape: communal hunting, Ludi Harpastum (fifteen days celebrating wine, song and flight), Windblume and Weinlesefest.

Dvalin, the new Anemo sovereign, was born from converging elemental energy, was curious about the world and frightened humans by accident. Drawn by the Holy Lyre der Himmel, he landed beside Barbatos, who stayed calm and sang of the dragon's beauty; Dvalin stayed, learned human speech and Barbatos' singing. The Gunnhildr Clan returned to its ancient fortress in the north, the future Dornman Port, and founded Mondstadt's first sanctuary to Barbatos there; the port is said to be named for an ancestor called the Thorn King. At an unknown time the Hexenzirkel challenged Barbatos to a fight, he offered a song instead, and they became allies. Some time between 2,600 and 500 years ago the "Tyrant's Final Fury" occurred: for about a year a damaged Field Tiller fired from Decarabian's abandoned tower at anyone approaching, after Boreas, mistaking it for a challenger, had damaged it.

Late aristocracy: Around 1,600 years ago the Lawrence Clan became the foremost clan and degenerated into tyrants who enslaved and tormented commoners. Opponents were enslaved for labour or sport, historical knowledge was suppressed, the "starlit knights" served the nobles, royal mages kept people ignorant and the Church of Favonius split, its senior clergy backing the nobility. The Gunnhildrs were said to keep their honour but had little influence; at Dornman Port they threw a bishop sent from the capital out of the sanctuary tower and tore it down, and the port has had no church since. At some point Ursa the Drake began terrorising Mondstadt.

About 1,010 years ago Vennessa, born with a younger sister, Lind, into the Muratan tribe of the southern plains (exiled from Natlan by civil war), crossed Ursa and fled to Mondstadt, only to be enslaved. Her strength made her a gladiator; what bound her was her duty to her people. Around the same time the manipulative Eberhart, an illegitimate heir of Landrich's clan, plotted the aristocracy's downfall, secretly mastering the spear and sabotaging an aristocratic expedition to Sal Vindagnyr; the party never returned, and his fate is unknown. The Wanderer's Troupe, a musical and military company, tried and failed to overthrow the aristocrats in Mondstadt; Kreuzlied, a Lawrence who abandoned his clan, was the only known survivor and founded an underground organisation, and the Dawnlight Swordswoman's defiance inspired Ragnvindr, who later took the title Dawn Knight.

Mondstadt reborn: About 1,000 years ago, after Ludi Harpastum, the cries of the oppressed woke Barbatos, who came down as the bard Venti and befriended Vennessa after she angered Barca Lawrence, heir of the Lawrence Clan. She was sentenced to gladiator matches for her people's freedom, the last against Ursa the Drake itself, which Lord Lawrence had bartered with to buy peace.

Barbatos revealed himself on the field and gave Vennessa the power to win. Afterwards most aristocrats and their collaborators, including the royal mages, were exiled; the uncorrupted Gunnhildrs stayed. Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius as its first Dandelion Knight and Grand Master and restored the Church of Favonius so tyrants could not return.

The recorded history is only the start of a longer rebellion. Barbatos forged a contract claiming the aristocrats had sold Mondstadt, and their own troops, to Morax; discovered, this "treachery against the wind" turned the soldiers against them, and scholars learned only much later that it was fake. Ragnvindr, Kreuzlied and Church faithful mobilised by the Nameless Shepherd helped. Afterwards the Gunnhildr Clan pushed to abolish hereditary fiefs. Ragnvindr turned the aristocrats' bathhouse into the first Mondstadt Library, which became the largest in northern Teyvat until the Great Fire of Fall Equinox cut it to one-sixth; the Barbatos statue was restored, its original inscription lost. A Knight of Boreas came to the city and joined the Knights, though his wolf companion preferred the wild; when it died he buried it and became a wanderer. The Four Winds were established, with Boreas as Wolf of the North, Dvalin as Dragon of the East and Vennessa both Lion of the South and Falcon of the West; Vennessa later ascended to Celestia at Windrise, where a great oak grew. Boreas' pack moved to Wolvendom at an unknown time.

Cataclysm: About 500 years ago Arundolyn, Grand Master and the "Lion of Light", and his friend Rostam, the "Wolf Pup", led the Knights to fight monsters in Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm; Rostam died there, and Arundolyn gave up fighting.

Rostam had mentored a man called the White Knight, possibly Roland, who fought the monsters until people feared him as the Bloodstained Knight and who later joined the Abyss Order. Meanwhile the alchemist Rhinedottir sent her creation Durin to Teyvat, where he devastated Mondstadt; with no Lionfang Knight strong enough to stop him, Barbatos called on Dvalin and together they killed Durin. Dvalin swallowed Durin's poisoned, Abyss-tainted blood and slept in Decarabian's tower.

Durin's body fell on Dragonspine, his blood seeped into the mountain and revived the Frostbearing Tree, and his heart still beats in Wyrmrest Valley; his blood set as Scarlet Quartz. Rostam's lover Rosalyne-Kruzchka Lohefalter, who had left to study at the Akademiya just before the Cataclysm, returned, learned of his death and turned herself into living flame to avenge him, becoming the Crimson Witch of Flames. Dornman Port nearly fell and many knights died defending it; their graves lie beneath the city. Worship of the Four Winds faded afterwards.

Post cataclysm: Before the Crimson Witch burned away, Pierro of the Fatui found her and gave her a Cryo Delusion to quench the flames; she became Signora, eighth of the Fatui Harbingers. About 400 years ago a text on Mondstadt's customs, quoted in an in-game book, was written by an ancestor of Ella Musk and Dr. Edith. Around 300 years ago Olaf of Springvale was frozen by a Cryo Regisvine while hunting on Dragonspine; Springvale grew around a spring of melted Dragonspine snow. Less than 200 years ago a Lochfolk named Callirhoe, the Spring Fairy, left Fontaine and blessed Springvale's waters.

Recent past: Roughly 50 years ago the Spring Fairy befriended Old Finch as a child, the basis for a book. Amber's grandfather, a Liyue mercenary leader, moved to Mondstadt, joined the Knights and founded the Outriders. Seamus Pegg settled in Mondstadt, rose to Cardinal of Daybreak and married Frederica Gunnhildr; their daughters Jean and Barbara were later born, and the couple separated, with Jean staying with her mother. About a decade ago Kaeya was left near the Dawn Winery and raised by Crepus Ragnvindr alongside Diluc. Diluc became Cavalry Captain at 14, the youngest captain on record, and Jean became Dandelion Knight at 15.

Four years before the Traveler's arrival Crepus Ragnvindr died on Diluc's eighteenth birthday after using a Delusion against an attacker everyone took for Ursa the Drake (lured by a Fatui metal bug; later revealed as an imitation bred from Eroch and Dottore's experiments on the unsealed drake). Inspector Eroch ordered the cause covered up and Diluc resigned in fury; the same night Kaeya revealed his origins to him. Afterwards a Segment of Dottore slew the imitation, publicly credited as Ursa, leaving Mondstadt in the Fatui's debt. Eroch was later exposed as a traitor and purged, and Jean was promoted from Captain to Master of the Knights. Amber's grandfather resigned and vanished. Albedo arrived about three years ago with a note from Rhinedottir and became Chief Alchemist, and Klee was entrusted to the Knights. About six months before the Traveler arrived, Varka took the Knights' elite and the cavalry on an expedition, with Jean as Acting Grand Master; Diluc returned and began his night patrols as the "Darknight Hero". The official manga's Ludi Harpastum story, listed on the wiki timeline as the last Ludi Harpastum, involves Dottore's schemes, Collei and a Fatui death; it is a side medium.

Story present: In the Prologue the Traveler arrived after being attacked by the Unknown God and meeting Paimon, and with Venti and the Knights freed the dragon "Stormterror", Dvalin, from the Abyss Order's hold. Immediately afterwards the Fatui Harbinger Signora took Venti's Anemo Gnosis.

Dvalin had been poisoned by Durin's blood, and the Abyss Order had persuaded him that Mondstadt had abandoned him; he is honoured again since the Prologue. Venti healed by drawing on the Windrise oak's connection to Celestia.

Recent events 5 to 7: At a recent Windblume Festival (Paralogism, 5.6) Albedo's closed trial for murder was a long-planned trap that exposed beings born of Durin's lingering life force. A full assault on the city followed, repelled by the Knights, Diluc, the Church and the Traveler. Albedo convened a Tripartite Conference of the Knights and Church, the Anemo Archon and the Hexenzirkel, drained Durin's Core and, with Venti singing as Windblume Star, transmuted a kindly storybook dragon into a synthetic human body, so that Durin was reborn as a human in Mondstadt.

In 6.4 Varka's expedition, which had ended in Nod-Krai after the Knights fought the Wild Hunt from Favonius Keep, came home. Windrest Peak, with Dornman Port and Millhaven, opened in 6.5. In 6.6 Lohen's story quest found the real Ursa still held in Eroch's hidden experiment site, where Theodore had restarted serum experiments on its flesh; Varka, Diluc and the Traveler killed it, and Jean rescinded Lohen's commendation and planned promotion to Captain of the 5th Company. As of 7.1 Mondstadt is at peace and the Archon Quest is in Snezhnaya; Frederica Gunnhildr is on a secret mission known only to Varka and Jean.

41.comment: Mondstadt/History: Arcadia and Sal Vindagnyr Timeline
41.content: Arcadia was the oak-forest civilisation of old Mondstadt, with Elysium in Windrest Peak under the Gunnhildr Clan. About 6,000 years ago an unknown calamity buried it in winter; Gunnhildr, the Knight of the Golden Bough, failed to find a living branch of Irminsul and led survivors south to shelter under Decarabian. On Vindagnyr (Dragonspine) the city of Sal Vindagnyr died beneath snow after the Skyfrost Nail fell, while the outlander Imunlaukr was away seeking Irminsul.

42.content: About 2,600 years ago, with Boreas' blizzards beating on his walls, Decarabian's people rose in rebellion under the code word Windblume. Decarabian and Amos died; the Nameless Bard's last song turned the tempest into Mondstadt's wind but cost the bard his life. The wind spirit became the Anemo Archon and kept the bard's name, Venti, then built the new city on Cider Lake and later withdrew.

43.content: About 1,000 years ago the gladiator Vennessa, a Muratan enslaved by the aristocrats, fought Ursa the Drake with Barbatos' help; the nobles were exiled and she founded the Knights of Favonius and restored the Church. A longer rebellion also involved a forged treaty selling Mondstadt to Morax.

44.comment: Mondstadt/History: The Cataclysm in Mondstadt Timeline
44.content: About 500 years ago Rostam died in Khaenri'ah, Arundolyn stopped fighting, and the dragon Durin devastated Mondstadt until Barbatos and Dvalin killed him on Dragonspine. Rostam's lover became the Crimson Witch of Flames and later Signora.

45.content: Four years before the Traveler, Crepus Ragnvindr died fighting what was taken for Ursa (later revealed as an imitation), Diluc left the Knights and Kaeya revealed his past; Eroch was later purged and Jean became Master. About six months before the Traveler, Varka left on a long expedition with Jean as Acting Grand Master, and Diluc returned to patrol as the Darknight Hero.

46.content:
Natlan/History (also: History of Natlan, Natlan timeline, Natlan history): Natlan's history in order: a dragon civilisation (Natlantea) under the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl; its fall about 2,000 years ago to Xbalanque, the first mortal Pyro Archon; the Eternal Empire of the half-dragon tyrant Och-Kan and his overthrow; and the Cataclysm 500 years ago, when the Abyss invaded and the Night Warden Wars began. They ended in Version 5.3 when the Traveler and Mavuika purged the Night Kingdom and Capitano gave his life.

Natlan never joined the Archon War; dragon infighting filled that age. Its distinct feature is a throne won by mortals: Pyro Archons are humans who prove themselves in battle. Use this entry for sequence and cause; use the linked entries for people, tribes and places.

Old world: Xiuhcoatl was born from the primal flame as the Pyro Dragon Sovereign and, the same day, split off a portion of that flame to create his younger brother Kukulkan. He hollowed out a space inside the Great Volcano of Tollan, founding the Sacred City of Tollan, and made the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, artificial intelligences, to govern Natlantea. The Legendary Tonatiuh was built to anchor a "cable" at Chichen Uctokah that leads beyond Teyvat's sky.

The Heavenly Principles later took Xiuhcoatl's Pyro Authority and left him frozen in lava in a state of false death. During his absence Kukulkan acted as Regent of the dragon civilisation. In the war of funerary flame, which ravaged Natlan and damaged its ley lines, Xiuhcoatl woke when Nibelung returned to Teyvat. Kukulkan and the Lords tried to repeat the miracle of moon forging to reach worlds beyond Teyvat; Xiuhcoatl stopped them.

About 6,000 years ago Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night, rebuilt Natlan's ley lines as the Night Kingdom under the guidance of Ronova, and a Celestial Nail fell into the Night Kingdom. The wiki's note says all Celestial Nails are implied to have fallen at the same time, when the Heavenly Principles won the great war, so the 6,000-year figure is an inference. The dragon civilisation then reclaimed Natlan from a collapsed human one.

Ancient dragon era: From roughly 6,000 to 2,000 years ago the dragons of Natlantea ruled and humans were subordinate. Natlan took no part in the Archon War, because in-fighting among dragons absorbed everything; as a result its modern people know little about that war. Natlantea slowly declined and Kukulkan foresaw its end. He gave Phlogiston to the "primitive" humans and fathered Och-Kan, half dragon and half human, to unite the two peoples and rise to a new throne. Near the end of this age the tribes were founded, worshipping the Wayob (ancestors) and the Night Kingdom.

Kukulkan's scheme was discovered; the Thirteen Lords and the Three Princes tried to impeach him, but the trial halted when Xiuhcoatl appeared. Most of Natlan's angels were "devoured" by the dragons, according to item text. Xiuhcoatl also modified one of his pupils to serve as a control hub for Huitzilopochtli. The Sumeru fungus god Bifrons travelled to Natlan to recover and was buried with his attendant Chatraka by a volcanic eruption at the Great Volcano of Tollan.

About 2,000 years ago the human twins Ixquieh and Ahpub sealed Aj Imuch' Paxlaq Lahun, the Tenth Lord, in a wristband and buried it in a ruin. Other Natlan material makes Ixquieh the first bearer of the Ancient Name Baraka and founder of the Children of Echoes, and Ahpub founder of the Collective of Plenty; this entry only notes their link to the sealing.

Xbalanque and the first pyro archon: About 2,000 years ago Xbalanque and his army invaded the Sacred City of Tollan. He killed Xiuhcoatl and became the first Pyro Archon of Natlan, ending the civilisation of Natlantea. The Three Princes and ten of the Thirteen Lords died in the fighting.

Xbalanque and Kukulkan each took one of Xiuhcoatl's eyes, the Golden Entreaty, swearing to keep peace between humans and dragons. Xbalanque borrowed Ronova's power to set up rules by which mortal humans can ascend as the Pyro Archon, and the Ode of Resurrection. Chichen Uctokah, the territory of the Ninth Lord Ixlel, fell to ruins at about this time.

Ronova's price for this power is the thread that pays off at the war's end (see end_of_the_war): she kept a promise to Xbalanque of one last day among the living once Natlan had defeated the Abyss.

Ochkanatlan and och kan: About 2,000 years ago followers of Xbalanque founded Ochkanatlan, the Eternal Empire. After Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, Och-Kan became king. The seven tribes formed the Grand Alliance and put their authority in his hands. Och-Kan betrayed Xbalanque's commandments and became a tyrant: he sought to wipe out the dragons and their descendants, the Saurians, mistreated his people and banned ancestor worship and the Night Kingdom.

Och-Kan built Ochkanatlan on the remains of Chichen Uctokah. Ixlel first helped him, but when she resisted he trapped her in the Old Core of Chu'ulel and made a new Core of Chu'ulel from his own draconic half, one he could fully control. The Scarlet-Eyed Youth, who sympathised with the Saurians, was banished by his elder in an attempt to help him escape capture. In exile he ascended as the second Pyro Archon and gathered those who opposed Och-Kan.

Och-Kan was overthrown and Ochkanatlan became abandoned and "cursed". He survived by separating mind and body: his mind sat in the Core of Chu'ulel, and his body became the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash. Sovereignty returned to the six tribes, who reconnected with the Night Kingdom and made peace with the Saurians. The wiki here says seven tribes joined the Alliance but six regained sovereignty, and does not explain the difference (see uncertainties).

Post archon war: Later Pyro Archons held tournaments between tribes. More than 1,600 years ago (editors' estimate) an unnamed female Pyro Archon, whom Venti knew, held martial arts contests, as the manga prologue shows. More than 1,000 years ago a civil war in Natlan split the Muratans: some left Natlan and eventually settled in Mondstadt, and the rest were forced to live apart at Tenochtzitoc, where the Easybreeze Holiday Resort now stands. Also over 1,000 years ago the Pyro Archon Cochanina drove the Volcano Lord out of the People of the Springs. About 500 years ago Mavuika was born, before the Cataclysm.

The name 'Murata' for the unnamed Archon comes from the English manga and is probably a place or people name; the Chinese original does not name her. The date of the Muratan exile is inferred from a character's remark that they lived in neglect for millennia until darkness returned.

Cataclysm and night warden wars: Five hundred years ago the Abyss invaded, and Natlan, with weakened ley lines, suffered more than any other region. This began the Night Warden Wars. Great infighting among the tribes occurred as well. Bakunawa, a creature made by Rhinedottir, entered Tenochtzitoc and killed almost all the Muratans there except Tenoch, who had been exiled before the disaster. Several Pyro Archons (Cochanina, Shulevitz, Gloharry and Isaja) worked together to contain it; the first three died doing so and Isaja contained it.

Tenoch, known for his giant obsidian club, recruited allies from each of the six major tribes to defend Natlan against a "turbid black tide" (the Abyss) and they became the Heroes of Natlan. Mavuika ascended as Pyro Archon and joined the party. Their battle site became the Mare Jivari. Traore led the Children of Echoes against an Abyssal invasion in their territory, and with the Khaenri'ahn warriors Zephaniah and Irizar trapped the Abyss deep underground using the Shadow Pins.

Around 490 years ago the Ochkanatlan Adventure Team led by Taika went to the ruins in search of the Legendary Tonatiuh, rumoured to hold the key to beating the Abyss. It was a trap set by Kukulkan, who killed almost all of them and took their souls. Taika's daughter Bona followed, freed Och-Kan's mind from the Core of Chu'ulel and named it Cocouik; she met the same fate as her father at the Tonatiuh. By the war's end the tribes were decimated and their bonds with the Wayob nearly severed, and the Abyss rooted itself permanently in the Night Kingdom.

Mavuikas plan: Mavuika's plan was that the tribes would spend 500 years regaining their strength, after which the Wayob would choose six new heroes to drive the Abyss out for good. She sacrificed her life to the Sacred Flame so that she could reawaken 500 years later to oversee it. Because of long exposure to the Abyss, Natlanese people had to remain within their borders, where the Wayob could protect them.

Her sister Hine helped rebuild the Scions of the Canopy. Not long after the Cataclysm, Capitano (then called Thrain) and his platoon fled Khaenri'ah to Natlan and helped the tribes fight the Abyss for a time. Menilek tried to remove the Flamelord's Blessing from his Saurian companion Holawaqa Ngoubou, and failed.

Recent past: Under 100 years ago, Bennett's parents' adventuring team wandered into the Mare Jivari and died there; Bennett survived and an adventurer took him to Mondstadt. Some 20 to 30 years ago visitors reported a mountain-sized dark creature in the Mare Jivari, which was then said to have "disappeared", blown off Teyvat by Barbatos, with several departed souls unable to pass on. A Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame was held with Vichama, Mallko, Pisac and others; an Abyss attack on the eve of a Night Warden War wounded Vichama, and the rest lost their Ancient Names for good.

Mualani won three Night Warden Wars without needing the Ode of Resurrection. Chasca was abandoned as a child because of a rare disease, raised by a qucusaur named Chimpu, found by Allpa and adopted by Chuychu's family. Kinich found Ajaw in a ruin and made a contract with him, and was revived by a Dendro Vision after dying in a Night Warden War. By then three of six tribes (Kinich, Iansan, Xilonen) had heroes ready. The wiki dates Capitano's arrival in Natlan with his subordinates to Version 3.1 (around Mondstadt's Weinlesefest). His subordinates, including the Polychrome Tri-Stars, captured Saurians for Phlogiston experiments until the Traveler shut them down, as the permanent hidden exploration objective at the Phlogiston Extraction Research Center on Coatepec Mountain shows.

Present day 5 0 to 5 3: In Version 5.0 a Pilgrimage was held and Kachina beat Mualani in the finals; she, Chasca, Iansan and others fought in a Night Warden War, but the Ode of Resurrection did not revive Kachina when she fell. Mavuika suspended the Pilgrimage and the wars. With Vichama's help Kachina's Ancient Name was recovered, and the Traveler, Chasca, Iansan and Mualani entered the Night Kingdom and rescued her, then were trapped until Mavuika freed them by giving up keepsakes people had offered her in exchange for Contending Fire. Mualani was acknowledged by her Ancient Name, leaving only the Flower-Feather Clan and the Masters of the Night-Wind without heroes.

In 5.1 the party learned Capitano and Ororon intended to rewrite the ley lines, which would erase Natlan's history, and tried to stop them. The plan failed in its intended form but awoke Yohualtecuhtin, whose power destabilised Ororon's damaged soul and let the Khaenri'ahn Guthred possess him; Ororon regained control and was acknowledged as an Ancient Name bearer, and Capitano agreed to work with Mavuika. A nationwide Abyss invasion followed that cost thousands of lives and briefly put out the Sacred Flame. Chuychu died of Abyssal contamination, and Chasca, after her grief, was acknowledged by her Ancient Name as the sixth hero. The six channelled Ronova's power into Mavuika, who drove the Abyss back deep into the Night Kingdom.

In 5.2 the Traveler and Paimon went to Ochkanatlan, met Cocouik and Bona's spirit, and reached the Tonatiuh, where Kukulkan admitted luring souls with its legend for centuries. The Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash took the Golden Entreaty; in the Nursery of Nightmares Cocouik merged with the dragon, showing it to be Och-Kan, whom the Traveler defeated, taking the Golden Entreaty. The Traveler also freed Ixlel from the Old Core of Chu'ulel at her request.

End of the war: In 5.3 Xilonen forged the Traveler an Ancient Name, and the Traveler and Mavuika entered the corroded Night Kingdom to purge Gosoythoth's influence. With Yohualtecuhtin's blessing the Traveler gained Pyro power. Gosoythoth became the Lord of Eroded Primal Fire and seemed to win, but the support of the Natlanese restored the Traveler and Mavuika, and they defeated it, ending the Night Warden Wars.

It then emerged that Ronova had demanded Mavuika's death as payment for the power lent to her. Mavuika meant to use her life force to repair the Night Kingdom, but Capitano took her place: as a Khaenri'ahn cursed with immortality, he forced Ronova to choose between keeping his deathless "life" (denying her death) or lifting the curse on his people. She upheld the curse, and Capitano gave his life for the Night Kingdom.

With the war over, the Natlanese may leave the nation freely and the Pilgrimage became a sporting competition. Ronova kept her promise to Xbalanque and let him return to the living for one last day; Mavuika and the Traveler showed him the Natlan his sacrifice made possible, and he left smiling.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the Abyss war is over; Mavuika survived its end, while Capitano gave his life and merged with the Lord of the Night, his body left on the Throne of the Primal Fire. The wiki's Natlan history records no later events.

Open questions: How the seven ancient tribes became six, who all the Pyro Archons were and when they ruled, and the precise dating of events before the Cataclysm are not settled by canon (see uncertainties).

47.comment: Natlan/History: Ochkanatlan Adventure Team and Bona
47.content: The Ochkanatlan Adventure Team under Taika went to the ruins of Ochkanatlan about 490 years ago seeking the Legendary Tonatiuh, hoping it would help against the Abyss. Kukulkan had laid a trap and took nearly everyone's souls. Taika's daughter Bona later found Och-Kan's mind in the Core of Chu'ulel, named it Cocouik and travelled with it to the Tonatiuh, where she died too.

48.comment: Natlan/History: Tenoch and the Heroes of Natlan
48.content: Tenoch was an exile from Tenochtzitoc who survived Bakunawa. He gathered fighters from the six tribes to defend Natlan from the Abyss; they are the Heroes of Natlan, and Mavuika joined them as a new Pyro Archon. The Mare Jivari is the site of their battle.

49.comment: Natlan/History: Pyro Archons Who Contained Bakunawa
49.content: When Bakunawa destroyed Tenochtzitoc, four Pyro Archons (Cochanina, Shulevitz, Gloharry and Isaja) united to restrain it. Three died in the effort; Isaja held it. Pyro Archons are mortal, so their deaths pass the title on.

50.content: The Night Warden Wars were the long war against the Abyss in the Night Kingdom, beginning with the Cataclysm 500 years ago. The Pilgrimage selected warriors to fight them, and the Ode of Resurrection revived the fallen. They ended in Version 5.3.

51.content:
Snezhnaya/History (also: History of Snezhnaya, Snezhnayan history, Nod-Krai history, History of Nod-Krai): Snezhnaya's history runs from the golden city of Hyperborea (destroyed by a Celestial Nail about 6,000 years ago) through the Pale Star Court of the Belyi Tsar, first Cryo Archon, who ruled until he fell fighting the Abyss in the Cataclysm 500 years ago. Anastasya then became Tsaritsa, broke the fae aristocracy, founded the Fatui with Pierro, and let Nod-Krai become an autonomous land guarded by the Lightkeepers. As of 7.1 she holds six Gnoses and is waging a hidden war on Celestia.

Use this entry for "what came before what" in Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai. Order: Hyperborea and the first fae; the Pale Star Court (Kitezh, Belyi Tsar); the Abyssal gate and Anastasya's erasure and return; the Belyi Tsar as Cryo Archon and the pioneering age of Nod-Krai; the Cataclysm; the Tsaritsa's accession and reforms; the Fatui and Harbingers; Nod-Krai in the Song of the Welkin Moon; and 7.0-7.1. Absolute dates are mostly round figures from item texts and are partly wiki reconstruction.

Canon and the wiki disagree or stay silent on several early dates (see uncertainties); where a number is given it is attributed. Nod-Krai's history is told here because the wiki has no separate page for it.

Hyperborea: Over 6,000 years ago, in the Unified Civilization era, the Golden City of Hyperborea stood in ancient Snezhnaya, then a warm, green land. It drew on the power of the Three Moons. According to artifact texts, its people angered the angels by questioning the progress of knowledge; the voyager Anacharsis, living in the guise of a Hyperborean boy, was sent before the first angel Koitar, and the two became lovers who resolved to oppose the Heavenly Principles. Hyperborean artisans made the Snowland Fae using forbidden methods Koitar taught.

About thirty years after Koitar and Anacharsis met, a Celestial Nail destroyed Hyperborea, around the War of Funerary Flame. Only Canon, goddess of the Frost Moon, took pity on the survivors and led them to Nod-Krai, where they settled on Hiisi Island and called themselves the Frostmoon Scions. Over centuries the Scions kept to their faith and ran a bloodline project to produce a sacred heir for their goddess. A fallen remnant of a fourth moon that never fully formed became the land of Nod-Krai, steeped in kuuvahki.

Hyperborean experiments also tried to create a Primordial Human from the remains of the Cryo Dragon; the Dragon's released power afflicted the land with Holy Soil and froze Snezhnaya, and, per the wiki, turned its Ley Lines into Kresnik Kristall veins. Hyperborea's ruins lie within the Shadow Realm. Most of the Hyperborean content was revealed in the Nod-Krai arc (6.x) and item texts; the pieces are assembled by wiki editors.

Saarelainen and anastasya: Over 6,000 years ago the Third Descender Saarelainen came from the sea of stars to ancient Snezhnaya and entered a relationship with Anastasya; they had a son, and their descendants became the Khaenri'ahns. Thousands of years later, as a herald of the Belyi Tsar's Pale Star Court, Anastasya and Saarelainen were incited by the Tsar to open a gate to the Abyss (the Hymns of the Far North place it on Pohjola). The Abyss began seeping into the world and the Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya.

Saarelainen ascended to Celestia and offered his own remains, which were split into the seven Gnoses, in return for Anastasya's revival and a promise never to harm their descendants. Anastasya was revived, but all memory of him was removed through Irminsul. The Belyi Tsar, having fled into the Shadow Realm, kept the memory and later told her, though she never fully trusted him. She then began recording her days in a memory prism immune to Irminsul changes.

The wiki dates the gate episode loosely to between 3,200 and 2,000 years ago, an editors' inference from her service to the Tsar. These events were revealed in the Version 7.0 Archon Quest material and the Version 7.0 special program.

Pale star court: The Belyi Tsar (Monomakh Snezhnyi) is said to have emerged around 5,000 years ago from the Cryo Dragon's remains and to have believed himself a fae. He founded Kitezh, the first city of Snezhnaya and capital of the Pale Star Court, and about 3,000 years ago won the war against King Miscislav of the Volkodlak Alliance by killing him and two fae Grand Dukes with a thrown spear. All fae clans then swore fealty and he took the title Belyi Tsar. Snezhnaya was an imperial aristocracy led by the Snowland Fae, living in luxury.

Kitezh remained the capital for about 1,000 years. Around 2,000 years ago, after exploring Hyperborea's ruins through the Shadow Realm and learning he was an incomplete Primordial Human, he accepted Celestia's offer to become Cryo Archon, opened his realm to humans, moved the court to Snezhnograd and renamed the nation Snezhnaya. His court sat at Zapolyarny Palace. He attended the gatherings of the first Seven in Liyue when the Archon War ended.

He also pursued the Hyperboreans' aim of completing his ascension and overthrowing the Heavenly Principles, supported by the Hvergelmir institute, and raised the infant Aksinya, whom he found in a time capsule. Folk tales (a twin brother, a final immortal enemy) are legends the wiki doubts. Sources are chiefly the books A Brief History of the Pale Starborn and Notes by a Certain Noble Individual.

Pioneering age of nod krai: More than 500 years ago the Belyi Tsar ordered the borderland of Nod-Krai explored and developed in the "pioneering age": forests were cleared for cities, ports and factories. A Khaenri'ahn exile, Rauthvangi, arrived a few years in, took the name Professor Rotwang, and became a favourite at court for his alchemy and astrology. Per item texts, the Tsar began plotting a revolt the "sublunary order" could not tolerate; Rauthvangi pushed him to aim higher, toward what lay beyond the false sky, and acted as his envoy to Nod-Krai on a secret errand for a hidden treasure. Many fae nobles distrusted him as the "mad monk."

Meanwhile Lovia, last Archpriestess of the Frostmoon Scions, bred "pure" heirs; a maiden fled with a Snezhnayan officer and bore Avrelian, later called Reed Miller, who grew up as a friend of Solovei. After the maiden's death, Lovia raised twins Alia and Aila in seclusion and forced them to drink their kin's blood. This is told in weapon and artifact texts and the wiki's reading of them.

Cataclysm in the north: In the Cataclysm 500 years ago, Nod-Krai was the first land corrupted by the Abyss, which appeared as the Wild Hunt. Neither the royal court nor any god defended it, and Abyssal monsters razed it. The Belyi Tsar fell in a battle against the Abyss during his expedition. Solovei, called the first Torchforger, and Aila, the Scions' first Moonchanter, turned the tide with the moons' power, and Solovei and his allies founded the Lightkeepers, swearing to defend Nod-Krai.

Aila gave Solovei the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, a Frostmoon relic that dispels the Abyss. Aila then reformed the Scions, cutting references to Hyperborea and the heir project in favour of nature, kindness to outsiders and the coming New Moon, and a new Frost Moon goddess, Kuutar, was born on Hiisi Island afterward. The Lightkeepers later pledged fidelity to the Tsaritsa. Reed Miller became a famed thief and founded the Treasure Hoarders on the dream of an "Elysium" for the poor; whether his execution succeeded is disputed.

Tsaritsas accession: Anastasya succeeded the Belyi Tsar during the Cataclysm and was crowned Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. Some fae nobles, furious a non-fae ruled, refused to recognise her; the Dalegrad clan broke ties with Snezhnograd and Flins left in self-imposed exile. She was left bitter and cut ties with other Archons, including Barbatos (reason unclear). She approved Solovei's request to make Nod-Krai an autonomous region under the Lightkeepers by Edict.

In the second year of her reign the humans of Port Belovodye, exploiting the succession crisis, declared self-governance; Grand Duke Drevogorye failed to put it down. In the third year she founded the Fatui with Pierro as its first member and sent them to retake the port. The Fatui seized lands of several fae clans (Drevogorye, Volkhovan, Cirnareka) for negligence; Drevogorye accused her of treason and died fighting. The rebels were offered clemency for handing over instigators and accepted.

She then demanded absent fae princes give up their titles, had the Fatui build the fortress Glupov, and replaced fae aristocratic rule with the Snezhnograd Veche, first headed by the human I. Ivanovna N. In her seventh year the Imperial Order Reformation Edict led many princes to renounce titles and leave; many settled in Novokitezhgrad, rebuilt after Kitezhgrad was destroyed by the Abyss. The fae lost most of their political influence. The year numbers come from the wiki's Anastasya page.

Fatui and the harbingers: The wiki timeline places Pierro, a former Khaenri'ahn court mage, in a meeting with the Tsaritsa 500 years ago, after which they founded the Fatui and its Harbingers with Pierro as Director. Over five centuries the pair recruited the Eleven Harbingers; the Fatui came to run most of Snezhnaya's government and army. Snezhnaya became the most militarily and technologically advanced nation. Around 400 to 350 years ago the Frost Moon goddess Kuutar joined as Third Harbinger "Columbina," and later fulfilled a promise to the Tsaritsa that used up most of her power. More than a decade ago Anastasya pardoned House of the Hearth orphan Peruere, who became Arlecchino; Ajax became the youngest Harbinger, Tartaglia, afterward (see his own entry).

Shortly before the Traveler's journey the Tsaritsa launched her plan to collect the Gnoses, which Pierro explained to the Harbingers. After Signora's death in Inazuma, a funeral was held at the Sanctuary of Grief. Individual Harbinger histories belong to their own entries.

Nod krai in the welkin moon arc: A few months before the Traveler reached Nod-Krai, the Fatui pulled fragments of the Eternal Moon from the sky; the two largest fell on Paha Isle and Hiisi Island, and Sandrone and Dottore stayed at the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau built on Paha. Columbina, disillusioned, fled to Hiisi Island, and the Tsaritsa issued the Palestar Edict, her highest command, to bring her back. Lauma, the current Moonchanter, sheltered her at Silvermoon Hall. Dottore defied the Tsaritsa's will in a bid to seize the power of the Three Moons. After he was dealt with, the Palestar Edict was rescinded and the Tsaritsa questioned Pantalone and Pulcinella over the affair. The Frost Moon returned to Teyvat's sky; as of 7.1 it remains. This arc is Version 6.x content (Song of the Welkin Moon and its Archon Quest chapters).

Snezhnaya in 7 0 and 7 1: By 7.0 the Tsaritsa was overseeing Project Stuzha, an energy-saving policy tied to the secret Project Mistilteinn, an anti-Celestia weapon. Before the Traveler arrived she campaigned east against a monster causing endless snowstorms, saw Asmoday with a hooded figure, and killed the beast. In 7.1 she ended investigations of the Traveler, explained her aims and appointed them Consultant to the Tsaritsa. In 7.1 she used her six Gnoses to slow time around the Shade Rhinedottir, so the revival of the victims of Ronova's curse of death was delayed past Celestia's monitoring cycle; Celestia revoked Ronova's authority for abuse, and Pierro mortally wounded her with his new Delusion, the "Eye of the Fatui". Project Mistilteinn, stalled by the curse, resumed. The dying Ronova fused the Eitr with the Nail of Retribution hovering over the Cryo Dragon's corpse, which began to crumble as she disintegrated; the quest frames this as her attempt to let Holy Soil spread across Teyvat, and Celestial Nails everywhere glitched and sent pillars of light into the sky.

Pierro was left depleted after using the Eye of the Fatui; Arlecchino's Crimson Moon lineage served as the base for that Delusion, and in return Pierro agreed the House of the Hearth would no longer answer to the Fatui or train children as spies; corruption purges based on lists from Pulcinella and the House of the Hearth are under way. Whether these promises are carried out is not yet shown. Status is as of 7.1; nothing later is covered.

52.content: Hyperborea was the golden civilization of ancient Snezhnaya, over 6,000 years ago, that powered its magic with the Three Moons' tides. It created the Snowland Fae with Koitar's forbidden methods, and was destroyed by a Celestial Nail. Survivors fled to Hiisi Island and became the Frostmoon Scions.

53.comment: Snezhnaya/History: Pale Star Court and Kitezh
53.content: The Pale Star Court was the fae empire of the Belyi Tsar (Monomakh Snezhnyi), centred on Kitezh, the first city of Snezhnaya. Kitezhgrad was later destroyed by the Abyss and the survivors founded Novokitezhgrad. After the Tsar became Cryo Archon, the court moved to Snezhnograd and the nation was renamed Snezhnaya.

54.content: The Belyi Tsar's exploration and industrial development of Nod-Krai over 500 years ago. The Khaenri'ahn exile Rauthvangi came to court as "Rotwang" and encouraged the Tsar's rebellion against the Heavenly Principles.

55.content:
After the Cataclysm Solovei, the first Torchforger, and Aila used the moons' power against the Wild Hunt, and Solovei founded the Lightkeepers. The Tsaritsa's Edict approved their jurisdiction and Nod-Krai's autonomy. Aila gave Solovei the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. Their insignia is a nightingale holding a burning wick; headquarters are at Piramida.

Accounts differ on who raised the first beam of light, Aila at the Pillar of Embla or Solovei with Aila's borrowed power. Their oath is sworn by every member on joining.

56.comment: Snezhnaya/History: Reed Miller and the Treasure Hoarders
56.content: Reed Miller, born Avrelian to a Frostmoon maiden and a Snezhnayan officer, became an infamous thief across Teyvat who dreamed of an Elysium for the poor and founded the Treasure Hoarders. The royal court sentenced him to death; whether he died is disputed between item texts.

57.comment: Snezhnaya/History: Tsaritsa's Accession and the Fae Princes
57.content: Early in her reign Anastasya crushed fae opposition: the Port Belovodye rebellion, the seizure of Drevogorye's lands, the Veche replacing fae rule, and the Imperial Order Reformation Edict of her seventh year, after which many princes renounced their titles. Many settled in Novokitezhgrad.

58.content: The Fatui were founded about 500 years ago by the Tsaritsa with Pierro, who served as its first member and Director. Their first campaign retook Port Belovodye. Individual Harbingers are covered in their own entries.

59.content: The Tsaritsa's highest-priority Edict, issued when Columbina left the Fatui, ordering her recovery at all costs. It was rescinded after Dottore's rogue conduct was dealt with.

60.content: In 7.1 the Tsaritsa slowed time with six Gnoses so Rhinedottir could not finish reviving Ronova's victims before Celestia's monitoring cycle; Celestia stripped Ronova of her authority and Pierro mortally wounded her with the Eye of the Fatui.

61.content:
Sumeru/History (also: History of Sumeru, Sumeru timeline, Sumeru chronology): Sumeru's past runs from the dragon Apep's forest and the first Celestial Nail's burying of it, through the three God-Kings (Nabu Malikata, King Deshret and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata), Deshret's fall to forbidden knowledge and the desert's age of city-states, to the cataclysm 500 years ago, when Rukkhadevata was replaced by Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida) and the sages came to rule in her name. Chapter III (3.0-3.2) freed Nahida; in 6.6 she burned Irminsul to end Dottore's attack, and Aaru took over its work.

Use this entry for the order of events and rough "how long ago". Canon seldom gives years for pre-cataclysm Sumeru. The rainforest and the desert have separate histories (Rukkhadevata's and Deshret's) that were later tangled and distorted by the Akademiya's misinformation.

The periods used below follow the wiki: Old World, the Heavenly Principles, the Unified Civilization, the War of Funerary Flame, the Archon War (Ay-Khanoum, Dharma Forest, King Deshret's civilization, Gurabad), the Post-Archon War age of kingdoms, the Pre-Cataclysm, the Cataclysm, the Post-Cataclysm, the Recent Past and the Present Day.

Old world to war: In the Old World the Dendro Dragon Sovereign Apep ruled the land that became Sumeru and nursed ancient Dendro lifeforms. Irminsul first grew there as a fern in her court. The Heavenly Principles took Apep's Dendro Authority and remade Irminsul into the device that records Teyvat's information and keeps the cycle of erosion running. In the Unified Civilization the ancient city of Ys stood in what is now the Sumeru desert, and Rukkhadevata, Irminsul's avatar, already existed.

Apep joined Nibelung in the War of Funerary Flame against the Heavenly Principles. Nabu Malikata survived the downfall of the Angels. About 6,000 years ago the first Celestial Nail fell on Sumeru, buried the rainforest under the Great Red Sand and destroyed Ys. The wiki says the nail was used to combat the forbidden knowledge Apep had accumulated.

The wiki ties Mt. Damavand and the permanent storm around the Desert of Hadramaveth to the nail's impact, and legend says Deshret later found the nail. The timing of all the Celestial Nails right after the Funerary Flame is the wiki's inference from the Chasm's creation 6,000 years ago.

Three god kings: During the Archon War Nabu Malikata, a surviving Angel later called the Goddess of Flowers, befriended King Deshret and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. The three became known as the Three Eternal Companion-Gods of Sumeru and each held a share of the realm: the banquet, authority and life. Nabu Malikata and Deshret built Ay-Khanoum, the City of Amphitheaters, whose name means "City of the Moon Maiden" in the Jinn tongue. Deshret defeated many gods, among them Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth, who entered his service as the Seven Pillars; gods who refused, such as Remus, went wandering.

Nabu Malikata is said to have created the Jinn and Khvarena. Foreseeing the cataclysm she made a shard of Khvarena, called her daughter, and gave it to Rukkhadevata, who later turned it into the divine bird Simurgh and charged her with guarding the border between birth and death. Nabu Malikata warned Deshret of Celestia's wrath but agreed to help him seek forbidden knowledge. Rukkhadevata refused and left. Nabu Malikata used her lingering link to Celestia to grant Deshret divine knowledge and was "burned to ashes by the flames of wrath" for it. The wiki suggests she knew she would die and wanted the bitterness of her death to preserve her legacy, which Deshret never realised.

Her remains were scattered; Deshret buried what he found in the Eternal Oasis, and some fragments were lost. The Jinn were told she was only asleep and served him in exchange for help finding her. The Orchard of Pairidaeza was made as her cemetery and Gurabad was charged to protect it. Ay-Khanoum was then lost to sandstorms and abandoned. Dottore later gathered the missing fragments, and one ended up in Collei. Whether Deshret was "a son of the sky" is told by legend, but he seems to have been born after the Angels fell.

Dharma forest: After parting from Deshret, Rukkhadevata went east of the Great Red Sand and used the Varuna Contraption to turn part of the desert into rainforest. The Wall of Samiel was raised at the border. The forest's first lord, the tiger Viaghara, was born from moonlight on the water. With followers who founded the Amurta Darshan she grew the forest, and Sumeru City was built on the Divine Tree. She also created the Aranara.

Her devotees became the Sumeru Akademiya's scholars, who helped her govern. These events are assumed by the wiki to be roughly concurrent with Deshret's kingdom and Gurabad.

Deshret and gurabad: Deshret ruled the desert alone after Nabu Malikata's death, having made a deal with Apep that it would consume him after his death to take his knowledge. He chose vassal kings and priests, with the Jinn as messengers. The shepherd Ormazd founded Gurabad with help from the Jinni Liloupar, whom he married. Liloupar felt betrayed by his later tyranny and spent generations arranging the city's ruin. The folk book The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin blames Shirin and Shiruyeh; Liloupar's memories show otherwise. Deshret was furious on learning of it and split her soul into seven pieces, each guarded by a sage.

The book's version: Liloupar's son Kisra was raised by a great bird and adopted by Ormazd as Parvez. Shirin, under Liloupar's influence, poisoned Ormazd and his 300 heirs; Kisra took the crown as Parvezravan. Their son Shiruyeh was banished, returned with Liloupar's help, and Gurabad was destroyed by the power of the abyss with the king turned into a monster. Shirin and Shiruyeh fell into an abyss, where Liloupar says they remain.

The Eremites remember Shiruyeh as a coward and a traitor. Deshret's people built the Primal Constructs and the Khaj-Nisut mechanism, meant to carry people into a "golden slumber".

Fall of deshret: Deshret's research released forbidden knowledge. People heard whispers, dark scales (Eleazar) spread over them and the land withered. He asked Rukkhadevata for help. She came back to the desert, had priests build temples she filled with the power of life, and created the Akasha System to unite people's wisdom against the poison. The priest Kasala's record says the embers of Deshret's civilisation were preserved in Aaru Village, though other in-game accounts place the village's founding centuries later under the Old Blind Poet. This exhausted her and shrank her to a child's form. It was not enough, and Deshret sacrificed himself to end it. His civilisation broke into short-lived city-states.

Apep consumed his body, as agreed, and was corrupted by the knowledge. Rukkhadevata later promised one of Apep's creatures to erase the "apocalypse" and the two made the Fire Seed to cure Apep, though it was unstable. The Valuka Shuna, once Deshret's subjects, were given refuge in the rainforest. Rukkhadevata turned the Khvarena shard into Simurgh after the city-state age ended. The Traveler learns this in Chapter III (3.1).

Many people long thought Rukkhadevata and Deshret fought and that she betrayed him, a story kept alive by the Akademiya. The record of Deshret's priest Kasala, left in a device at his grave and projected by Alhaitham in Secret of the Scorching Desert, showed her as the desert's saviour.

Post deshret kingdoms: Between about 2,000 and 500 years ago desert history is told through weapon texts and wall inscriptions. Shah Ramshahr was credited with building seven towers (the "Towers of Betrayal") raised when forbidden knowledge was purged, and seven cities, among them a rebuilt Ay-Khanoum, a rebuilt Gurabad, Saleh and Tulaytullah, grew around them. Ramshahr's son Artaxir died young. The regent Turan Khagan was executed. Power passed among the free states.

Later, kings such as Humayun Gurkan of Tulaytullah, the Khagan Garshasp, and the rebuilt Gurabad's king Saleb Dowleh (born Goudarz, who answered a riddle of Thoth) ruled in turn. Saleb Dowleh was betrayed and killed by Muzaffar, a Dey from Port Ormos, who then built his city elsewhere. Muzaffar's son Zumurud had 99 children, and under them Sumeru had a golden age. The tale of Xiphos and the Jinni Makhaira, whom Thoth also questioned, covers the fall of Tulaytullah; Makhaira was killed by the prince Faramarz. The Old Blind Poet, Xiphos's master, took desert folk to Aaru Village to await Deshret's return. The realms were eventually buried by sand. Thoth's three questions (what causes rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, what determines truth and falsehood) were attempted in turn by Goudarz, Makhaira and, in 6.6, Nefer, whose answer was the intended one and freed Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf from Aaru. Xiphos's end is told in two incompatible versions, and the wiki doubts the mercenary-duel one.

Pre cataclysm: Slightly more than 500 years ago, Rosalyne-Kruzchka Lohefalter (later the Fatui Harbinger Signora) came from Mondstadt to study at the Sumeru Akademiya.

Cataclysm in sumeru: Five hundred years ago Rukkhadevata was not summoned to Khaenri'ah like the other Archons, because she was to protect Irminsul. Forbidden knowledge contaminated Irminsul and, since she was its avatar, her too. She used the Akasha System to borrow her people's wisdom and purge it, but could not erase herself, so she created Lesser Lord Kusanali from the purest branch of Irminsul to be her successor. She then left on a final journey and never returned. The forest's king Viaghara died defending the forest.

The Withering (the Black Tide) spread through both forest and desert. The Aranara saved the forest with help from the Traveler's sibling, whom they call Nara Varuna. The huntress Viridescent, after her duty, was eroded by the monsters' black blood and killed by the Bloodstained Knight.

The wiki suggests Rukkhadevata died before Simurgh finished her sacrifice. The phrase "Let the world completely forget me" is the start of the trail she left for Nahida.

Girdle of the sands: The Gate of Everlasting Mourning was the centre of the Abyssal invasion. Monsters tore a great rift at Tunigi Hollow, where the Hydro Archon Egeria fell and her body became the Amrita of the Vourukasha Oasis. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from it to anchor Egeria's remaining consciousness. Simurgh awoke and drank the Amrita, shattered into Khvarena, and her motes became the Pari. The Schwanenritter brought Khaenri'ahn refugees up into the Girdle and used their Ruin Golems against the Abyss, and are remembered as the heroes of Dahri.

The First Pari Zurvan found a weakened Dainsleif and brought him to the oasis. The Darshan of Nagarjuna arrived soon after. Together they performed the Rite of Chinvat, Zurvan purified the Harvisptokhm's seal and made the five Great Songs of Khvarena, four of which were scattered; some Darshan members stayed as the Order of Skeptics. Dainsleif later left with the Traveler's sibling. Later, the Skeptic Klingsor joined an Akademiya expedition into the Dahrian ruins, fell to the Abyss and became an Abyss Herald. Zurvan then sealed the oasis, and the Order lost its records and neglected its duty.

Post cataclysm: After the cataclysm Lesser Lord Kusanali was found and brought to Sumeru City. The people rejoiced and the Sabzeruz Festival moved to her birthday. The sages found her no wiser than an ordinary child and shut her in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, while espousing Rukkhadevata's legacy and building the Akasha into a public information network. Over 400 years ago the student Zandik, who became the Fatui Harbinger Dottore, studied at the Akademiya, and the Temple of Silence left the corrupt sages for a temple at Thamud Oasis.

Two hundred years ago the Akademiya graduated a scholar the wiki calls its most talented before Lisa. Faruzan was born over 120 years ago and was trapped in Deshret-era ruins for a century. Misinformation then pitted forest against desert.

After Chapter III Act V (3.2) Rukkhadevata's memory was erased from the world: Nahida is now believed, even by herself, to have always been the Dendro Archon who lost her memories in the cataclysm. Only the Traveler remembers.

Recent past: Roughly 20 years ago Kaveh's father, a scholar who had entered the Interdarshan Championship, left for Aaru Village to help its people and died saving a caravan from quicksand. About 10 years ago Cyrus took Cyno away from the Temple of Silence. Collei, born with Eleazar, was handed to a seer who was a Fatui agent and used her in Archon-residue experiments. Lisa graduated from Spantamad after two years and left for Mondstadt. Kaveh and Alhaitham became friends, started a joint study of Deshret's ruins and later fell out. In the last few years the sages grew more hostile to the arts, and Kaveh built the Palace of Alcazarzaray at the cost of his savings.

Faruzan escaped the ruins and was found with an Anemo Vision. In the manga, set shortly before the game, Collei leaves Mondstadt with Cyno for Sumeru. The precise order of these events is only estimated by the wiki from characters' ages.

Present day: In Chapter III (3.0 to 3.2) the sages' plan to build an artificial god with Dottore and the Fatui was defeated, Nahida was freed, the Akasha shut down, and Nahida purged Rukkhadevata from Irminsul, removing the forbidden knowledge and ending Eleazar. In Khvarena of Good and Evil the ex-Skeptic Klingsor tried with Nasejuna to break the Harvisptokhm's seal, and the Traveler and the Pari Sorush stopped them. In 6.6 Dottore attacked Irminsul from within and Sumeru City was evacuated; Nahida burned the tree with the Pyro Gnosis and Aaru, reprogrammed by Alhaitham and Kaveh, took over its role.

Limited-time events add small notes about this period; see the entry on Sumeru in limited events.

In 6.6 Nahida had collapsed, and Apep sheltered her. The Seven Pillars' freeing and the Irminsul burning for seven days are detailed in the lore files on the destruction of Irminsul. As of 7.1 Sumeru is at peace and rebuilding, the Archon Quest has moved on to Snezhnaya, and Sumeru's Celestial Nail began, like the other nails, to emit a strange light into the sky after the Hyperborea nail collapsed.

62.comment: Sumeru/History: The Three God-Kings and Ay-Khanoum
62.content:
Nabu Malikata, King Deshret and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata ruled Sumeru together for a time and built Ay-Khanoum as an earthly paradise. Each valued a different kind of wisdom and they debated often. The partnership broke over Deshret's quest for forbidden knowledge. Ay-Khanoum was later abandoned and then rebuilt among the seven cities of the post-Deshret era.

A chair crafted as a memorial to Rukkhadevata stands in the Orchard of Pairidaeza. Accounts differ on whether she left before or after Nabu Malikata died.

63.content:
Gurabad was a vassal state of Deshret founded by the shepherd Ormazd with the Jinni Liloupar. Liloupar, seeing her husband become a tyrant, planned its destruction and used her children and grandson. The in-world book blames Shirin; Liloupar's own memories show she was the planner. Deshret punished her by splitting her soul into seven parts.

Liloupar says Shirin and Shiruyeh fell into an abyss with the city. The Eremites still use Shiruyeh as a word for a traitor.

64.content: The rainforest was created by Rukkhadevata after she left the desert. The Varuna Contraption terraforms the land, the Wall of Samiel stops desertification, and the Aranara and the forest lords guard it. Viaghara, the first lord of the forest, died defending the forest in the cataclysm, and the Rishboland Tigers are his successors.

65.comment: Sumeru/History: Khvarena, Simurgh and the Pari
65.content: Nabu Malikata's shard of Khvarena became Simurgh, who sacrificed herself during the cataclysm to purify the Amrita at the Vourukasha Oasis. The Pari are her motes. In Khvarena of Good and Evil the Sign of Apaosha returned over the Harvisptokhm for the first time since the cataclysm and the Traveler helped the Pari Sorush complete the Rite of Chinvat again.

66.content:
In 6.6 Dottore corrupted Irminsul from within. Sumeru City was evacuated. Nahida, invoking her authority as keeper of Irminsul before the three Shades, burned it with the Pyro Gnosis that Mavuika had given the Traveler, and Dottore died in the fire, which burned for seven days and nights. Aaru, modified under Alhaitham and Kaveh's plan with help from the freed Pillars Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf, now holds the world's records. The Pyro Gnosis is gone.

The Belyi Tsar's notes suggest Aaru was the Goddess of Flowers' intended replacement for the Ley Lines. The wiki infers this, and the claim that Celestia no longer fully controls fate, from Nahida's remark that fate now has many more possibilities.

67.content: Kaveh's father died about 20 years ago helping caravans near Aaru Village. Kaveh built the Palace of Alcazarzaray for Dori and went bankrupt, then moved in with Alhaitham after meeting him again at Lambad's Tavern. These details come from Kaveh's character stories and the 3.6 limited event A Parade of Providence.

68.content: Event stories add small notes. In Marvelous Merchandise (2.6, limited event) the trader Liben left Sumeru after sensing an ominous air. In Summertime Odyssey (2.8, limited event) Chevka says a Harbinger found a way to link minds. In A Parade of Providence (3.6, limited event) Kaveh won the Akademiya Extravaganza championship. In the 5.1 limited event that included the Sabzeruz Festival, the festival was held for Kusanali.

69.content:
Archon War (also: Archon Wars, War of the Archons, era of warring gods): The Archon War (Chinese and Japanese: War of the Demon Gods) was the long age of fighting between gods that followed the war of funerary flame about 6,000 years ago and ended about 2,000 years ago. The Heavenly Principles set up seven divine thrones in Celestia, one per element, and let the gods fight over them and their Gnoses. The victors became The Seven, the Archons who founded and shaped the seven nations. Of the original victors, only Barbatos (Venti) and Morax (Zhongli) remain as of 7.1; the other five seats have changed hands.

The war was not one conflict but many regional struggles that ended at different times. Mondstadt's was settled 2,600 years ago when Decarabian fell; Morax was already fighting for Liyue before 3,700 years ago; the era as a whole closed about 2,000 years ago, when the last seat was claimed. Natlan was never part of it. Most defeated gods who survived fled beyond Teyvat into the Dark Sea.

Established: - After the war of funerary flame, the Heavenly Principles (the "usurper" of Neuvillette's Vision story) were too badly wounded to suppress the world's original order directly. They dismantled the unified civilization, banned its history and decided on a "new order".
- The angels who had guided humanity were cursed and cast out of Celestia, and a new class of gods emerged to take that role.
- Seven divine thrones were set up in Celestia, each holding part of an elemental Authority taken from the Seven Sovereigns. Gods fought for them and the matching Gnoses.
- Ningguang tells the Traveler that many gods walked the earth and fought long wars that did not abate until 2,000 years ago, with much blood shed.
- Zhongli's character story: Rex Lapis remembers the moment the final Archon took their seat, ending the Archon War and the era of warring gods.

- Neuvillette's Vision story describes the result bluntly: humans were left with only "seven remembrances," and all fragments of the primordial were driven to devour each other.
- Nicole's character story (from the original Chinese, "demon gods") says that once mankind lost the angels, the land fell to strange beings who gathered followers with a wave of the hand and a trace of a miracle.
- The war also unleashed monsters: Zhongli's own stories say every corner of Teyvat burned and "wicked things" sought to expand their domains alongside the gods.
- After the war, the victors founded the seven nations, setting their governance by their ideals and reshaping the land with their elemental power.

Theatres: - Mondstadt: Barbatos and the rebels overthrew Decarabian, God of Storms, 2,600 years ago; Boreas declined the throne.
- Liyue: Morax, after Guizhong's death, founded Liyue Harbor and sealed many gods (Osial, Chi, the mistress of Chenyu Vale); Havria and Marchosius fell or gave up their godhood.
- Inazuma: Makoto and Ei united the islands; Orobashi fled into Enkanomiya.
- Sumeru: King Deshret, Rukkhadevata and Nabu Malikata ruled together until Deshret's pursuit of forbidden knowledge; Rukkhadevata is presumed to have ascended afterwards.
- Fontaine: Remus' Remuria rose and sank; Celestia then made Egeria the Hydro Archon.
- Natlan: never part of the war; Xbalanque defeated the Pyro Sovereign and became the first Pyro Archon.
- Snezhnaya: Monomakh united the fae clans and became the Belyi Tsar.

Mondstadt: About 2,600 years ago, Old Mondstadt stood where Stormterror's Lair is now. Decarabian, God of Storms, walled it in a storm barrier against Boreas, the King of the North Wind, whose blizzards made the land almost uninhabitable. Neither could defeat the other. Barbatos was then only a wisp of the thousand winds. He befriended a young bard who longed to see birds, and with the bard, Decarabian's estranged lover Amos, a red-haired warrior and Gunnhildr, he led a rebellion that killed Decarabian. Amos and the bard died. Barbatos took a seat in Celestia as the Anemo Archon, took the bard's form, reshaped the land and left the people to rule themselves.

Boreas judged himself unfit to be the Anemo Archon, since he had little love for humanity, and withdrew to Nod-Krai. About a thousand years later he let his body die, turned his power into a blessing on Mondstadt's Ley Lines and remained as a spirit, the Wolf of the North among the Four Winds. Boreas' godhood came from an unwitting blessing by Koitar in Nod-Krai (revealed in 6.x content).

Liyue: Morax, Guizhong and Marchosius ruled the Guili Assembly together with the adepti. Guizhong, God of Dust, died in a battle that also flooded the Guili Plains, and Morax led the people south to found Liyue Harbor. He went on to defeat and seal many gods and sea monsters: Osial and others under the stone lances of Guyun Stone Forest, the beast-god Chi at Qingce, the mistress of Chenyu Vale, and the serpent Orobashi, who fled to Inazuma.

- Marchosius, God of the Stove, gave up his power and godhood to stop the war's calamities and plagues from destroying Liyue. Morax set the Yakshas to destroy the demons the war's dead gods left behind; the karmic debt killed or scattered nearly all of them, and Xiao is the last active Yaksha.
- Havria, the gentle Salt Goddess, kept giving ground until only Sal Terrae was left; her own king killed her, and the power released turned those nearby to salt. Survivors later founded Yinyuan Hall with a distorted account of events.
- In Chenyu Vale, the mistress' adepti Fujin and the Herblord turned against her, with the suanni Lingyuan, to save the vale's people when she tried to flood the Bishui River; she was sealed.

Inazuma: Makoto and Ei fought through the war together, conquering and uniting Inazuma's youkai; the youkai built Inazuma City on Narukami Island. Ei defeated the region's other gods and unified the archipelago under the Inazuma Shogunate. Ei was the stronger twin but judged Makoto fitter to rule, gave up her own body so Makoto could ascend, and was restored by Makoto to serve as her kagemusha. Orobashi, realising he could best neither Morax nor "Narukami", fled into Enkanomiya, where he became the people's god.

About 2,000 years ago Celestia sentenced Orobashi to death for reading Before Sun and Moon, a history of the age before the war of funerary flame. He prepared his people to return to the surface and raised Watatsumi Island from coral. After a period of peace, famine drove Watatsumi to invade Yashiori Island; Ei killed Orobashi and Akuou with one Musou no Hitotachi strike, splitting the island, after Akuou had killed her friend Sasayuri. Orobashi's resentment became the Tatarigami. This conflict came after Makoto's ascension and is told as an aftermath of the war.

Sumeru: Three God-Kings, King Deshret, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Nabu Malikata, shared rule of Ay-Khanoum peacefully. Deshret defeated other gods such as Heryshaf, Sobek and Thoth, who entered his service among the Seven Pillars; Remus refused and left. Deshret declined a "gift" from Celestia to pursue his ambition to rebel against it. Rukkhadevata left the desert and created the rainforest.

Nabu Malikata died guiding Deshret toward forbidden knowledge, and its corruption later brought Eleazar and the Withering. Rukkhadevata spent much of her power to contain it, shrinking to a child-like form, and Deshret sacrificed himself to end the disaster. Rukkhadevata is presumed to have then become the Dendro Archon. A minor god, the fungal Bifrons, fed starving people with clones of itself during the war and was later buried by an eruption in Natlan; when it woke in the present, it still thought the war was going on.

Fontaine: Fontaine had no native god at the start. Remus, after his defeat by Deshret, founded the empire of Remuria on the sea with the aid of the angel Sybilla and expanded it by diplomacy and conquest.
