In the north, Erinnyes united the warrior tribes of Aremorica in Egeria's name against Remuria. Remuria fell after Remus' death and a great flood. Celestia then ordered Egeria to succeed him; she gathered the survivors, founded a law-governed civilisation around Fontaine's springs, received a Gnosis and became the Hydro Archon.

Natlan: Natlan was never part of the Archon War: in-fighting among the dragons left no room for gods there (Acatl, Field Fungal Traces). Xbalanque defeated the Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, became the first Pyro Archon and founded Natlan's system, borrowing the power of Death from Ronova after ascending.

Snezhnaya: Fae clans held small principalities in the north. Monomakh Snezhnyi, a wandering hero, defeated or befriended fae princes such as Filipov and Vaselisa, founded Kitezh, and after the Volkodlak lord Miscislav and his allies were killed attacking it, the fae swore allegiance to him and he declared himself the Belyi Tsar of the Pale Star Court.

In his reign, by the 7.1 account, Saarelainen and Anastasya opened a passage into the Shadow Realm. The Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya; Saarelainen ascended to Celestia and let his body be split into the seven Gnoses, used to consolidate the Archon system, in exchange for her resurrection and a promise never to harm their descendants, the Khaenri'ahns, sealed with a curse that would put the Heavenly Principles to sleep. Anastasya later became the Tsaritsa.

Aftermath: The war closed about 2,000 years ago with the last seat claimed. Most defeated gods who survived refused the new order and fled to remote islands in the Dark Sea, where they became "evil gods"; Bit of Aerosiderite notes their power came from the same source as Rex Lapis'. Some gods instead cooperated with The Seven, such as Boreas (as one of the Four Winds) and Marchosius. The original Seven used to drink together in Liyue.

Five of the first Seven seats have since changed hands, four of them in the Cataclysm 500 years ago: Makoto, Rukkhadevata, Egeria and the Belyi Tsar died and were succeeded by Ei, Nahida, Focalors and Anastasya. The Pyro seat passes between mortal Archons, most recently Mavuika. Since 3.2 the world believes Nahida has been Dendro Archon since the war's end; Zhongli's revised story says only two of the first Seven remain "in positions of rulership".

Accounts: - Zhongli: the first Seven were a diverse lot but all shouldered the burden of guiding humanity; "the seven seats changed and again were changed," and his story laments that the new Archons would not honour that duty as the first did.
- Venti: his stories tell Mondstadt's war as a liberation from a god who mistook fear for devotion, and he insists the Anemo Archon cannot take credit for everything in Mondstadt.
- Ningguang: many gods once walked the earth and fought long, bloody wars that did not abate until 2,000 years ago.
- Bifrons (Field Fungal Traces, set in Natlan): an unreliable, self-glorifying god who sees the war as still under way; Paimon dismisses it as "old news."

- Neuvillette, after regaining his power: the war was the means by which the wounded usurper kept the world's resentments subdued.
- Nicole: people always want gods to hear prayers and bear the world's weight, which is why the demon gods so easily gathered followers after the angels were gone.

Open questions: Canon leaves open how many gods fought, the war's exact start, how the Gnoses' creation fits its timeline, who the many defeated gods in the Dark Sea are, and when Rukkhadevata ascended. Do not resolve these in roleplay.

Connections: Separate entries cover The Seven, each Archon, the Gnoses, Celestia, the Heavenly Principles, the Seven Sovereigns, the war of funerary flame, the Cataclysm and the Dark Sea, as well as the regional episodes (Guili Assembly, Sal Terrae, Tatarigami, King Deshret's civilisation, Remuria).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): to people in the present the Archon War is ancient history and legend, known through local tales, operas and ruins rather than memory. Only long-lived beings remember it: Zhongli, Venti, the adepti, Ei, Boreas and certain dragons. Its scars are physical: Guyun Stone Forest, Sal Terrae, the split Yashiori Island, Stormterror's Lair. Liyue's opera and storytellers favour the "Warrior God" Morax; Mondstadt tells its version as the tale of freedom won from a tyrant. In Natlan, people barely know of it.

Do not portray the gods of the war as uniformly evil: Guizhong, Havria and Marchosius were kindly, and Decarabian's tyranny is partly disputed. "Evil god" is what coastal nations call the exiles in the Dark Sea. Never give an ordinary person knowledge of the Gnoses' origin (a 7.1 revelation) or of the forbidden pre-war history.

70.content: 2,600 years ago Barbatos, a nameless bard, Amos, a red-haired warrior and Gunnhildr led Old Mondstadt's people against Decarabian. The god fell, his storm wall broke, the bard and Amos died, and Barbatos became the Anemo Archon. Boreas, who had besieged the city for ages, judged himself unfit for the throne.

71.comment: Archon War: Gods of Liyue in the Archon War
71.content: Morax fought alongside Guizhong and Marchosius before founding Liyue Harbor. He sealed Osial and other sea gods at Guyun Stone Forest, slew Chi at Qingce, defeated the mistress of Chenyu Vale and drove Orobashi to Inazuma. Havria was killed by her own king; Marchosius gave up his godhood to protect Liyue. Xiao is the last active Yaksha of those who cleared the dead gods' demons.

72.comment: Archon War: Orobashi and the Shogunate
72.content: Orobashi fled the war after losing to Morax and the Electro god, became Enkanomiya's god, later raised Watatsumi Island, and was killed by Ei in a later war over Yashiori Island; his resentment became the Tatarigami.

73.comment: Archon War: Gods who fled to the Dark Sea
73.content: Many defeated gods refused to live under The Seven and fled to remote islands of the Dark Sea, where coastal nations call them evil gods. Their powers came from the same source as Rex Lapis'. Enkanomiya was also counted as outside The Seven's domain.

74.content: In the era of the war, Saarelainen let his body be split into the seven Gnoses to win Anastasya's resurrection and a promise that the Heavenly Principles would never harm their descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. The Gnoses were used to consolidate the Archon system. All memory of him was removed from Irminsul.

75.content:
Asmoday's Defection (also: Asmoday defected, Asmoday's new master, Asmoday switched sides, Ruler of Space's absence, Asmoday's absence): Asmoday, the Ruler of Space and "Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles", once stopped the Traveler and their twin from leaving Teyvat and tore them apart. Five hundred years later she no longer attends the meetings of the four Shades and has left her own Temple of Space. Hints point to her now working with the Traveler's sibling. Canon does not say why, or on whose terms.

The word "defection" is the other Shades' interpretation, not a confession. Istaroth floats the idea that she "switched sides" and says looking for her would do more harm than good. Ronova calls such a move unthinkable unless Asmoday loved a new master more than herself. In 6.5 her abandoned attendant Melanta asks why she chose the sibling over him. In 7.1 a hooded figure is seen beside her.

Everything known comes from outside observers: other gods, a servant she left behind, and a ruler who saw her briefly in a storm. Asmoday has not spoken since the opening of the game. Her reasons, her goals and the nature of her bond with the sibling are open.

Established: - In the prologue (1.0), a white-clad god calls herself the sustainer of the Heavenly Principles, says "the arrogation of mankind ends now", and traps both twins in swarms of red-black cubes. The Traveler's sibling is taken first; the Traveler is sealed and sleeps.
- Later canon names her Asmoday, Ruler of Space, one of the four Shades the Heavenly Principles created.

- In the Gods' Limits teaser (2025-07-09) Ronova, Rhinedottir and Istaroth meet in Celestia without Asmoday. Ronova notes that not one of the Shades has ever missed a meeting and wants her found.
- Asmoday's Temple of Space, the private domain where she kept chosen people and things from Teyvat, was left without its owner. Its rules began to fail; her attendant Nihilita walked away, and Melanta, the other attendant, tightened the rules until he began to destroy himself.
- In 6.5 (A Long Day in the Mountains, final chapter) Melanta asks his creator why she would choose the Traveler's sibling and abandon him. The portals she had opened nearby close as the fight ends.
- In 7.1 the Tsaritsa tells Rhinedottir she recently saw Asmoday with a hooded figure at the heart of a storm in Snezhnaya, near a monster that had come in with the snow. The hooded figure said it was worth witnessing the end of the Third Descender's story. Asmoday then used space to take them both away.

- The Fatui also treat her as a danger. In Etched in Time (7.1) the Rooster says one reason a notebook was sealed was fear that Snezhnaya could become a "Second Khaenri'ah", drawing the notice of the Heavenly Principles and the sustainer thereof.
- In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), Ronova says she need only wait until Asmoday returns so the four Shades can use their authority together, or until the Heavenly Principles awake.

- According to the wiki, the sibling was kept in a coffin as an exhibit in the Temple of Space after the Cataclysm and was later released, eventually leading the Abyss Order. This comes from the wiki summary rather than a transcript, so treat the detail as medium confidence.

Accounts: - **Istaroth** (teaser): the meetings are only a formality, and Asmoday may simply have "switched sides". She adds that finding her would do more harm than good, then draws attention to Pierro's gaze when Ronova will not let the matter go.
- **Ronova** (teaser): wants her found, because no Shade has ever missed a meeting; says a change of side would be unthinkable unless she "loves her new master more than her own self".
- **Rhinedottir** (teaser; 7.1): finds the idea interesting. In 7.1 she asks whether the hooded figure is Asmoday's "new master". Naberius replies that this is more likely an idea Istaroth had on a whim.

- **Melanta** (6.5): believes he was abandoned in favour of the sibling, and says he only wanted her praise on her return. He supplies the strongest direct hint that she chose the sibling, but it is his bitter reading of her departure.
- **Anastasya, the Tsaritsa** (7.1): reports what she saw and admits she could not identify the hooded figure. She offered the information in exchange for facts about the Heavenly Principles and said she was not trying to win favour with them.
- **Wiki synthesis**: says Asmoday has "aligned herself with the Traveler's sibling and, by extension, the Abyss Order". It is a fair reading of the above, but no character says the second half.

Open questions: - Why did the Shade who sealed the twins end up apparently helping one of them?
- Who, if anyone, is her "new master", and did she choose to follow them?

- Did the sibling free her, persuade her, or was it her own decision?
- Do the Heavenly Principles know? They have been dormant, and Ronova names their waking as a condition for dealing with the Fatui.
- Why was she watching a storm monster in Snezhnaya, and why did a hooded figure speak of the end of the Third Descender's story?

- Does her absence explain why the Temple of Space's rules fail, or was the Temple always built on rules that she herself ignored?

Connections: Her story runs through the Traveler's sibling's thread (see lore.travelers-sibling-goals), the dormancy of the Heavenly Principles, the Third Descender's seal and the Temple of Space. Istaroth's unexplained choices in the same period are covered in lore.istaroths-intentions.

76.content:
Asmoday, the Ruler of Space, once sealed the Traveler and their twin and now appears to be working with the twin. The other Shades suspect that she has defected, and Ronova suggests she might love a new master more than herself. In 6.5 her attendant Melanta asks why she chose the Traveler's sibling over him. No scene explains why. Do not name her master or her motive as fact.

She has not spoken in canon since the prologue. Everything about her present loyalty is inferred from sightings and from the words of others.

77.content: In the interlude teaser The Gods' Limits (2025-07-09), the Shades meet in Celestia with Asmoday missing. Ronova insists she be found because no Shade has ever skipped a meeting. Istaroth wonders whether she simply "switched sides" and thinks finding her would do more harm than good. Ronova says the idea is unthinkable unless Asmoday loves a new master above herself. When she raises it again, Istaroth tells her Pierro is watching them. The scene gives no answer.

78.comment: Asmoday's Defection: Hooded Figure With Asmoday
78.content: In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), Anastasya tells Rhinedottir she saw Asmoday with a hooded figure beside a storm monster. The figure said it was worth witnessing the end of the Third Descender's story. Asmoday used space and both vanished. Anastasya cannot say who the figure was; the quest stills and the wiki suggest it was the Traveler's sibling. Rhinedottir wonders whether it was Asmoday's "new master". Naberius dismisses the theory as one of Istaroth's passing ideas.

79.content: In the last chapter of A Long Day in the Mountains, Melanta defends the Temple of Space's rules after Asmoday's departure. Defeated, he asks why she chose the Traveler's sibling and abandoned him, admits he hoped for her praise, and ends in self-destruction. As he dies, Asmoday's portals nearby close, suggesting she may be watching. It is his own interpretation of her motives.

80.content:
Byakuyakoku (also: Tokoyokoku, Aphotic Earth, ancient Enkanomiya, Delphi Pytho, Land of Sun and Moon): Byakuyakoku, also called Tokoyokoku and originally Delphi Pytho, was an ancient human civilisation that belonged to the single world-spanning culture of the first era. In the war of funerary flame its land fell into the sea and was cut off from the surface. Its people, surrounded by darkness and by the vishaps called Dragonheirs of the Depths, built an artificial sun, the Dainichi Mikoshi, which gave them the cycle of Whitenight and Evernight. Later the fallen god Orobashi became their patron and led them back to the surface as the Watatsumi people. The place is now called Enkanomiya.

Its memory survives in a forbidden chronicle, Before Sun and Moon, in the five-volume Byakuyakoku Collection, and in the ruins beneath Watatsumi Island. Players meet it in the 2.4 Enkanomiya content.

Established: - Origin: before its fall, the people of Delphi Pytho were part of the unified civilisation that spanned the world. The chronicle describes the Heavenly Principles defeating the Seven Sovereigns and the creation of humanity under a covenant, and calls the supreme being "the Primordial One", with four shining Shades.
- Fall: in the Funerary Year the second throne of the heavens came, war was rekindled, and the chroniclers' ancestors and their land "fell into this place". The chronicle calls the second throne's coming only that; the wiki identifies it with the war of funerary flame, when Nibelung returned.
- Years of Darkness: in the depths they met the Dragonheirs of the Depths, who loved the dark and shunned light. Lanterns kept them back only partly, and the prayers of the people went unanswered by the Primordial One and three of its Shades.
- Istaroth: only the Ruler of Time, whom the chroniclers call Kairos or Tokoyo Ookami (and write backwards as "Htoratsi"), answered. In the Year of Blindness the sage Abrax (Aberaku in Narukami-style naming) woke to wisdom and led the building of Helios, the divine chariot of the sun, later the Dainichi Mikoshi.
- Years of Sun and Moon: when Helios was finished the Whitenight came and Evernight was banished. The people tried to find the way home but a ban from the first throne barred them. Abrax was imprisoned by order of the Sunchild, whom the people had chosen as king.
- Names: book 3 notes that its own title changed over the years from "Aphotic Earth" to "Tokoyokoku" and then "Byakuyakoku" (byakuya means white night); the wiki reads this as the land's successive names, and volume 1 does use Tokoyokoku for the land. After Watatsumi came, the land was renamed Enkanomiya and the surface home Sangonomiya.

- Geography: it had no mountains. It lay on the border of three realms, which the wiki gives as human, light and void, and both wind and water powers were still felt there. Three corners mark its borders, and Towers of the Three Realms stood there to steady its winds and waters, hidden by secret arts that only shrine maidens and the Vassals of Watatsumi can summon. Their sites are now the three Loci.
- The Serpent's Heart was built where space overlaps; it was used to guard secrets, imprison criminals and worship the imagined cosmic serpent Ouroboros. Its early name was Delphi, "land of snakes". Ouroboros was drawn as a scaleless serpent and Orobashi later as a coral-adorned one.
- Dainichi Mikoshi: Helios was a high tower, said in book 3 to stand for earth, the element between wind and water. The book says it was likely the sun the sage displayed, as prophecy suggested, and that, as the prophecies also suggested, it was later used to cast a great shadow over the nation.
- Livestock: the riddles say domestic animals (aux, hors, forest boar) died out within two generations once the land sank, so later generations knew them only from texts.

- The parables in the chronicle: the Parable of the Sun (people who mistake a torch for the sun, after which someone monopolises the flame), the Lethied Lotus (voyagers tempted to stay and forget the surface) and the Tree (the God of Moments can carry seeds of a moment into past and future). Read these as the chroniclers' commentary on their own history, not as separate events.
- The chronicle ends in the Tenth Year of Sun and Moon with the scribe hearing armour outside and stopping, presenting himself as a scribe of Tokoyo Ookami.
- The wiki, summarising quest text, adds that corrupt nobles had the sun worshipped as a god and that Aberaku died in the Tenth Year, his body and clothes enshrined in several places, which left his soul scattered until the Hyperion's Dirge quest.
- Vol. 5 (a children's riddle book from the transitional period) shows Narukami names written with Byakuyakoku readings, and records that Orobashi forbade one riddle about the "mother of fourteen billion years", Tokoyo Ookami.

Accounts: - The Byakuyakoku chronicle (Before Sun and Moon) is the voice of the old civilisation. It is pious toward the Primordial One and bitter about being abandoned. The wiki says Celestia wanted this history concealed, and Orobashi later banned the book as well.
- Watatsumi tradition (Sangonomiya Chronicles) tells the same history from the viewpoint of the people saved by Orobashi: a child asks a great serpent to be their god, the Sunchild's rule falls, and coral from the god's body makes the road to the surface.
- Present-day Watatsumi practice (the Goryou Matsuri quests) holds that every few thousand years Enkanomiya bleaches Watatsumi's soil and risks releasing the Dragonheirs, and the Goryou Matsuri ritual, using coral from the depths, is how the island guards against this. At the end of the limited-time 2.4 event Three Realms Gateway Offering, Kokomi resolves to find another method so the vishaps are no longer disturbed.
- Enjou of the Abyss Order claimed the book Before Sun and Moon would prove the gods came from outside Teyvat.

- Experimental records in volume 4 (written under Orobashi's direction) are the official Watatsumi view of the Bathysmal Vishaps: not killed, studied, grafted with Omikami's blood, with a prophecy that the Dragon Sovereign of Water will be born in human form.
- A person from Byakuyakoku would speak of the Primordial One and the Four Shades; a modern Watatsumi person would speak of Orobashi and Sangonomiya; neither side uses Celestia's wording.

Open questions: - The surviving text does not say how many generations lived under the Sunchildren, nor how long passed between the fall and Orobashi's arrival.
- It is not stated what the "Second Who Came" is; the chroniclers only guess it was defeated.
- It is unknown why only Istaroth heard the people, or what she wanted from helping them.
- Whether the vishap-people exist is left open.

- Many appendix names are illegible; do not invent the missing ones.
- Treat links to hilichurls, Mondstadt's "thousand winds" and Hyperborea as the wiki's inferences, not as established facts about Byakuyakoku.

Connections: - Parent culture: the unified civilisation (Delphi Pytho is listed there as a member).
- Setting that survives it: Enkanomiya, the Dainichi Mikoshi, Watatsumi Island.
- Patron: Istaroth (as Tokoyo Ookami), then Orobashi (Watatsumi Omikami).
- Founding sage: Aberaku. Other figures: Antei (Antigonus in the old naming) and Spartacus (Supada). The Yuna Clan of Watatsumi, later home of the shrine maiden Mouun, is among the old houses that came up from Byakuyakoku.
- Opponent: the Bathysmal Vishaps; modern Abyss interest: Enjou.

- The Watatsumi ritual that guards the island against what lies below, the Goryou Matsuri, is the modern echo of the ancient vishap problem.
- On the last day before the people moved to the surface, Khaenri'ahn envoys and a Ruin Guard came for the book Before Sun and Moon and Antigonus fought them off, per the wiki's summary of the Antigonus quest.

81.content: The Sunchild was the king of Byakuyakoku. The book says the people chose him, crowned him and worshipped him, and that he ruled harshly and framed the righteous; the wiki, summarising quest text, says he was a child puppet of corrupt nobles who played on his fear of Aberaku. The line of Sunchildren ended when Orobashi came.

82.comment: Byakuyakoku: Helios, Hyperion and the Dainichi Mikoshi
82.content: The artificial sun of Byakuyakoku, built under Aberaku with knowledge from Istaroth. Its light drove back the Dragonheirs and brought Whitenight; its absence is Evernight. The wiki says Orobashi later strengthened it so day and night could be switched. Its names changed with the culture: Helios and Hyperion in the old tongue, Dainichi Mikoshi in the Watatsumi era.

83.content: The old name for the Bathysmal Vishaps that ruled the depths when the land fell. They loved the dark, were driven back by Helios, and were later sealed and studied under Orobashi. Book 5 notes that they had evolved to wield other elements, which is why the Dragon of Water was not expected to arise from them.

84.content: Whitenight is the lit state of the land, Evernight the dark state. Book 5 says the land's two odd phenomena, the mirages and the Sinshades, were at first both called Eidolons; only after Orobashi came were they told apart, and the mirages of Whitenight were named Sunfire Phantasms and those of Evernight Ghostfire Phantasms (later all called Sunfire Phantasms). In the 2.4 content, the spectral Sinshades (Shades of Tokoyo) appear during Evernight.

85.content: In Byakuyakoku, Istaroth was worshipped as Tokoyo Ookami, "the thousand winds", Kairos and God of Moments. Her power was named the undying wind and treated as one of the land's two great forces, the other being water. The chroniclers dared write her true name only once, reversed. Her wider story is in her own entry.

86.content:
Cataclysm (also: Dark Calamity, Calamity of Darkness, pitch-black calamity): The cataclysm was a disaster about five hundred years ago that struck all of Teyvat. Abyssal monsters poured out of Khaenri'ah, the underground kingdom that lived without gods, and ravaged every nation. The gods and the Heavenly Principles destroyed Khaenri'ah. Its people were cursed: pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns became immortal, and those of mixed blood became hilichurls and Abyss monsters. Several Archons died. Canon gives it no single proper name; people call it "the cataclysm", "the disaster" or "the Dark Calamity".

The cataclysm shaped the present world. The Traveler and their twin were separated by the god Asmoday as they tried to flee it. Three Archon seats changed hands: Inazuma (Makoto to Ei), Sumeru (Rukkhadevata to Nahida) and Fontaine (Egeria to Focalors). In Snezhnaya, the Belyi Tsar died and Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, took his place. Mavuika of Natlan sealed her own life in the Sacred Flame. The Abyss Order and the Fatui both arose in response to Celestia's actions. Since the cataclysm the Heavenly Principles have been asleep. Much about the disaster is still unresolved in canon, so do not fill the gaps with invention.

Established: Confirmed: about five hundred years ago, monsters carrying Abyssal power spread from Khaenri'ah across Teyvat. The gods and the Heavenly Principles struck Khaenri'ah and destroyed it; The Seven were summoned there. Ronova, the Ruler of Death, cursed its people. Most present-day people know little of it and treat much of it as legend.

- **Trigger:** King Irmin, the last Vinster King of the Eclipse Dynasty, named the Traveler's sibling his heir and "Savior". He then made them a vessel for unlimited Abyssal power. Five of his most esteemed subjects each took a sixth of that power and became the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. None of them defended their homeland when the end came.
- **Who attacked:** all of The Seven were summoned to Khaenri'ah except Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who stayed to guard Irminsul. The skies over Khaenri'ah turned red and filled with crimson cubes, and the land was torn apart and flooded with lava.
- **The curse:** Ronova cursed pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality and turned those of mixed or foreign descent into hilichurls and monsters. Hilichurl numbers surged across Teyvat afterwards. The hilichurl archive calls the disaster a "pitch-black calamity".
- **Rhinedottir's creatures:** monsters made by "Gold" Rhinedottir, among them the dragon Durin, the Riftwolves and Bakunawa, rampaged through the nations.

- **Ruin machines:** Khaenri'ah's automatons, built to fight Celestia, wandered Teyvat without masters afterwards. They gathered at ruins, hence the name "Ruin Machines".
- **Survivors:** some Khaenri'ahns escaped or resisted the curse. Dainsleif is immortal; a ring from his brother Vedrfolnir keeps resetting his body, though his mind still suffers erosion. Halfdan kept part of his mind as a Shadowy Husk. Thrain (later Il Capitano) and his men retreated to Natlan. Pierro co-founded the Fatui with the Tsaritsa. Knight Marshal Anfortas, who declared himself Regent when King Irmin became "indisposed", led the Schwanenritter in evacuating survivors up into Sumeru, where they helped fight the Abyss and were remembered as the "heroes of Dahri".
- **The twins:** the sibling witnessed Khaenri'ah's destruction, woke the Traveler and tried to leave Teyvat with them. Asmoday intercepted them, sealed the sibling first and then the Traveler, who slept for five hundred years.

Accounts: Witnesses and survivors disagree about blame:
- **Dainsleif** despises the gods, yet he warns the Traveler not to try to overthrow or hunt them, so as not to repeat "the failings of my forebears". He holds that he and the Five could have stopped Irmin had they worked together.
- **Pierro** (Mocking Mask artifact text) says the sages of his homeland tore away "the veil of sin" and brought divine wrath on themselves.
- **Capitano** (5.3) stresses that most Khaenri'ahns were innocent and knew nothing of the Sinners' use of Abyssal power, yet Ronova cursed them all without distinction.
- **Ei** saw "a nation stride forward and lose everything to the Heavenly Principles". The memory fed her fear and her pursuit of Eternity.
- **Chlothar Alberich** blamed the Traveler's sibling as the catalyst of the disaster: the sages believed that controlling the Abyss meant controlling everything.

- **Rhinedottir** (7.1) traced the Khaenri'ahns' misfortune further back, to the Belyi Tsar inciting Anastasya and Saarelainen to open a gate to the Abyss. That act led to Saarelainen's bargain with the Heavenly Principles and to the curse that put them to sleep when they harmed Khaenri'ah.
- **Dainsleif** (7.1) recalls that during the cataclysm the Khaenri'ahns looked up at Ronova and saw only "an untouchable god". Pierro says he saw neither pity nor pleasure in her eyes when she cast the Curse of Immortality.
- **Zhongli** is bound by a contract not to speak of the cataclysm, and the adepti will not explain why Dunyu was abandoned.

History: The broad shape, nation by nation (details in the sub-entries):
- **Mondstadt:** the Knights of Favonius under Grand Master Arundolyn marched out against the monsters. Rhinedottir's dragon Durin attacked Mondstadt, and Barbatos woke and fought him with Dvalin. Durin fell on Dragonspine, and Dvalin was poisoned by his blood.
- **Liyue:** monsters poured out of the Chasm. The yaksha Bosacius, the exorcist Boyang and a Millelith vanguard sealed them in the Chasm's Bed at the cost of their lives. Dunyu was abandoned.
- **Inazuma:** Makoto, the Electro Archon, died in Khaenri'ah. Mikoshi Chiyo was corrupted, the Kitsune Saiguu was consumed by the dark forces, and Takamine vanished. Ei became Archon.
- **Sumeru:** forbidden knowledge surged into Irminsul. Rukkhadevata died purging it and left Nahida as her successor. Abyssal monsters tore open Tunigi Hollow in the desert.
- **Fontaine:** Egeria fell at Tunigi Hollow and Focalors succeeded her. The beast Elynas polluted Fontaine's land and sea.
- **Natlan:** hit hardest because of its shallow Ley Lines. Tenoch and the first six heroes held the line at what became the Mare Jivari, and the Night Warden Wars began.
- **Snezhnaya:** Nod-Krai was the first land struck after Khaenri'ah. The Belyi Tsar died leading an expedition into Khaenri'ah, and Anastasya was crowned Tsaritsa.

The disaster's roots run deep. Nibelung first brought Abyssal power and forbidden knowledge into Teyvat in the war of funerary flame. Khaenri'ah was founded as a godless nation around the time Sal Vindagnyr fell, and over centuries it built war machines meant for Celestia. More than 2,000 years ago its envoys tried to steal the forbidden book Before Sun and Moon from Enkanomiya. In Inazuma, the kitsune Urakusai did something connected with the coming Abyssal attack, and the Kitsune Saiguu banished him for it. Makoto said that Khaenri'ah was "not somewhere that any archon could afford to ignore".

Consequences: - **Celestia:** the Heavenly Principles fell dormant after the cataclysm and remain asleep as of 7.1. Celestia's system still functions, and the Shades still act.
- **New powers:** the Tsaritsa, embittered, cut ties with Venti (and possibly the other Archons) and founded the Fatui with Pierro to oppose both Celestia and the Abyss Order. Chlothar Alberich later founded the Abyss Order to take revenge on Celestia and The Seven. The Traveler's sibling travelled Teyvat with Dainsleif, learned "the truth of this world" and came to lead the Order.
- **Inazuma:** grief and fear drove Ei to pursue Eternity. She built the Shogun puppet, withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia, and later gave her Gnosis to Yae Miko.
- **Sumeru:** Nahida was born as the new Dendro Archon. Rukkhadevata's lingering corruption caused the Withering and Eleazar for five centuries.
- **Natlan:** Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame and planned a five-hundred-year return. The Night Warden Wars kept the Abyss at bay meanwhile.

- **Fontaine:** the Oceanids refused to serve Focalors and left Fontaine. The Melusines were born from Elynas's remains.
- **Liyue:** the monster war spurred new weaponsmithing (Prototype and Blackcliff weapons) once old weapons proved unsuited to the creatures.
- **Mondstadt:** Dvalin slept off Durin's poison in Old Mondstadt. Durin's blood seeped into Dragonspine. Rostam's lover Rosalyne became the Crimson Witch of Flames to avenge him and was later recruited by Pierro as La Signora. Roland, Rostam's student, became the Bloodstained Knight and eventually pledged himself to the Abyss; his fate is unknown.
- **Nod-Krai:** the Tsaritsa's edict made it autonomous under the Lightkeepers. The Wild Hunt has haunted it ever since.
- **Snezhnaya:** many Snowland Fae nobles refused to accept Anastasya; the Dalegrad clan broke away and Flins went into self-exile.

Riftwolves, Gold's creations, dwindled after the cataclysm but have reappeared in Inazuma and Mondstadt in the present. Ei treats them as harbingers of worse to come. Some of Rhinedottir's creatures were never fully destroyed: Bakunawa's rebirth in Natlan was only suppressed, and Durin's heart is still said to beat in Wyrmrest Valley.

Present: As of 7.1: Khaenri'ah's fate and King Irmin's are still unknown. The Curse of Immortality still binds Dainsleif and other pure-blooded survivors. The Heavenly Principles still sleep. In Snezhnaya, Ronova, who cast the curse, has lost her Authority and apparently died.

In 7.1 (Archon Quest Chapter VII Act IV), Rhinedottir revealed that the Third Descender, Saarelainen, had bound the Heavenly Principles with a curse that would trigger if they ever harmed his and Anastasya's descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. Anastasya concluded that the cataclysm triggered it, which explains the Principles' sleep. The same quest presents the Curse of Immortality as a permanent judgment laid under the Heavenly Principles' authority. Unlike Ronova's Curse of Death on Snezhnaya, it was not undone when her Authority was revoked.

Natlan's half-millennium war with the Abyss ended in Archon Quest Chapter V (5.0-5.3) when Mavuika and the Traveler destroyed Gosoythoth. In Nod-Krai (6.x) the Wild Hunt, an Abyssal plague dating from the cataclysm, lost Rerir when he was driven from Teyvat; the Abyss then raised an imitation of the Bloodstained Knight Roland to lead it, and once that form expired the Wild Hunt was left leaderless.

What {{char}} knows and does not know: Who knows what (for roleplay): ordinary people across Teyvat know almost nothing. Few books mention the cataclysm, and much of it is dismissed as legend. Even some Fatui fighting the Abyss doubt the conflict is 500 years old. Jean knows only the tale of Dvalin and Durin, which she learned from Diluc. The long-lived know more: Venti, Zhongli (bound to silence), Ei, Nahida, the Tsaritsa, the adepti, Dainsleif, Pierro, Capitano, Rhinedottir and other Khaenri'ahn survivors.

The Traveler has searched old books for information with little success. They learn the most from Dainsleif and their sibling's memories, and in Snezhnaya from Rhinedottir and Anastasya. In 3.2 Rukkhadevata was erased from the memory of everyone in Teyvat except the Traveler, so Sumerians no longer know that their old Archon died in the cataclysm.

Open questions: Unresolved as of 7.1: the exact sequence of the cataclysm; what Irmin's ritual did and what became of him; what "that thing" Ei saw was; what the crimson cubes over Khaenri'ah were (often attributed to Asmoday); who Chernobog was; what happened at Dunyu; why the sibling's deeds are recorded in Irminsul though they came from outside Teyvat; and why Asmoday released the twins separately. Do not resolve these in narration.

Connections: Related entries: the fall of Khaenri'ah (the kingdom's internal story), the curse of the Khaenri'ahns, Khaenri'ah's "Savior", the Five Sinners, the Abyss, the Heavenly Principles and their slumber, the Four Shades (Asmoday, Ronova), the Night Warden Wars, forbidden knowledge and the Withering, the Abyss Order, the Fatui, the Wild Hunt, and the Traveler's sibling thread.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the cataclysm as deep, half-forgotten history for most people, like a war five centuries past known through ruins, monsters and folk tales. Only the long-lived and Khaenri'ahn survivors speak of it with first-hand pain. Do not let ordinary NPCs name the Five Sinners, the Third Descender's curse or Irmin's ritual. Use "the cataclysm", "five hundred years ago" or "the disaster", not a proper-noun title.

Keep moral judgment contested: Dainsleif, Pierro, Capitano, Ei, Chlothar and Rhinedottir each frame the guilt differently. A Khaenri'ahn survivor's grief is centuries old and often eroded.

87.content:
During the cataclysm, while the Knights of Favonius were away on Grand Master Arundolyn's expedition against the monsters, the dark dragon Durin attacked Mondstadt. Rhinedottir had created him and sent him to Teyvat to "display his beauty". He seems to have been unaware of the destruction he caused. Mondstadt's people prayed, and Barbatos woke and called on Dvalin. Together they fought Durin over Dragonspine, which Barbatos chose as his burial place to contain his poison. Durin fell there and Dvalin swallowed his Abyss-tainted blood. Dvalin then slept in Old Mondstadt to recover.

Rostam held the valley against the monsters and died there, relieved that his lover was safe in Sumeru. Durin's blood seeped into Dragonspine, reviving the Frostbearing Tree, and his heart is said to still beat in Wyrmrest Valley. This historical dragon should not be confused with the playable Durin of 6.x, whose own entry covers his relation to Rhinedottir's creation.

88.comment: Cataclysm: The Chasm and Dunyu in the cataclysm
88.content: In Liyue, monsters poured out of the Chasm. Morax sent the Millelith to defend and evacuate the miners. Bosacius, a yaksha who had once abandoned his post after going mad from karma, returned to fight beside them. He, the exorcist Boyang and the Millelith vanguard lured the monsters deep underground and sealed them in the Chasm's Bed with the Fantastic Compass, dying in the process. Liyue won, at heavy cost. The people of Dunyu left their town for Liyue Harbor; why remains unspoken.

89.content:
Makoto, then Electro Archon, went to Khaenri'ah and was slain there, dying in Ei's arms. In Inazuma, Ei, Mikoshi Chiyo, the Kitsune Saiguu, Reizenbou and Takamine the Mistsplitter fought the dark forces. Chiyo was swallowed by a "beast of sin", killed it from within, was corrupted, and turned on Ei, who cut off her horns and sword arm. The Kitsune Saiguu was consumed by the darkness. Takamine vanished in battle, resurfacing years later only to die at the hands of his lover Asase Hibiki. Ei became Archon, and the losses drove her pursuit of Eternity.

On returning from Khaenri'ah, Ei found the Sacred Sakura on Mt. Yougou, apparently born of Makoto's consciousness (Ei suspects Istaroth's hand), and its power helped her quell the disaster. Kujou Shigeyori built a fortress at the Kannazuka front at this time. Ei still fears "that thing" she saw.

90.comment: Cataclysm: Sumeru and the desert in the cataclysm
90.content:
Rukkhadevata stayed behind to guard Irminsul while the rest of The Seven went to Khaenri'ah, but forbidden knowledge surged into Irminsul and into her. She died stalling it and created Nahida as her successor. In the desert, monsters tore a great rift, Tunigi Hollow. The Hydro Archon Egeria fell there, and her body became the Amrita of Vourukasha Oasis. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm to anchor Egeria's tainted consciousness and contain the defilement. The bird Simurgh gave her life purifying the Amrita, and the Pari were born from her. The Pari, the Darshan of Nagarjuna, Dainsleif and the Khaenri'ahn Schwanenritter all fought the Abyss there.

Ruin machines and Riftwolves also attacked Old Vanarana, scarring the land and giving rise to Marana's Avatar, the source of the Withering in the forest. The huntress Viridescent was corrupted after avenging the Bloodstained Knight's blind brother, who was killed by monsters in Sumeru.

91.content: With Egeria dead, Focalors became Hydro Archon, and the Oceanids, rejecting her, left Fontaine. The great beast Elynas appeared and polluted land and sea. Basil Elton, vice-director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, led the Fontaine Armada after it. For 35 days the fleet chased Elynas while drawing Abyssal sea creatures, then rammed him, dying to a man. Elynas later died of his wounds; the Melusines were born from his remains.

92.content:
Natlan suffered more than any nation because its Ley Lines were shallow. Rhinedottir's creature Bakunawa wiped out Tenochtzitoc. Tenoch rallied heroes from the six tribes, and Mavuika became Pyro Archon and joined them. At what became the Mare Jivari, Tenoch let himself be devoured so Sanhaj could shatter Bakunawa. The Children of Echoes, aided by the Khaenri'ahn soldiers Zephaniah and Irizar, sealed the Abyss underground with Shadow Pins. The Abyss took root in the Night Kingdom, beginning the Night Warden Wars. Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame to return after five hundred years.

Thrain and his platoon fled Khaenri'ah to Natlan and fought alongside the Masters of the Night-Wind. Their chief Ayizu told him the secret of the Pyro Gnosis before dying, which left Thrain resentful of Mavuika for not fulfilling her oath.

93.comment: Cataclysm: Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai in the cataclysm
93.content:
Nod-Krai was the first land struck after Khaenri'ah, and neither Snezhnaya's court nor the gods defended it. Solovei the Torchforger and Aila, the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, turned the tide with the moons' power and founded the Lightkeepers. Aila gave Solovei the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. The Wild Hunt has plagued Nod-Krai ever since. After the cataclysm the Tsaritsa granted Nod-Krai autonomy under the Lightkeepers.

The Belyi Tsar led Zver, Snowland Fae and Koshchei's chimeric monsters into Khaenri'ah against "the hounds of the God of Darkness" under an entity called Chernobog. After a week they were routed and the Tsar died; Zver dragged his body home. Anastasya succeeded him as Cryo Archon and was crowned Tsaritsa of All Snezhnaya. Many fae nobles rejected her, the Dalegrad clan broke away, and Flins went into exile.

94.comment: Cataclysm: The twins in the cataclysm
94.content:
The twins had crash-landed in Teyvat. The sibling woke first, reached Khaenri'ah and was named heir, then witnessed its destruction. They woke the Traveler and tried to leave the world. Asmoday, calling herself the Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles, blocked them and denounced "the arrogation of mankind". She sealed the sibling first, then the Traveler, in dark red cubes. The Traveler slept for five hundred years with their powers sealed; the sibling woke earlier and travelled with Dainsleif.

In 5.7 the Traveler met Direidyth, a Khaenri'ahn girl from the time of the cataclysm, through a superimposition of times Istaroth arranged. She carried the Traveler's hibernation key back to her own time and showed it to the sibling, which persuaded them to abandon Khaenri'ah and look for their twin.

95.comment: Cataclysm: Third Descender's curse and the slumber
95.content: Long before the cataclysm, Saarelainen agreed to be split into the seven Gnoses in exchange for Anastasya's resurrection and a promise that the Heavenly Principles would never harm their descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. He bound the promise with a curse that would trigger if it were broken. Revealing this in 7.1, Rhinedottir led Anastasya to conclude that the Principles' attack in the cataclysm set the curse off. That is why they have slept for five hundred years.

96.content:
Chichen Uctokah (also: Land of Seven Flames, Chichen Uctokah dragon city): Chichen Uctokah, called the Land of Seven Flames, was a city built by dragons in what is now Natlan. Its sovereign was the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L, whom Paimon nicknames Ixlel. The human usurper Och-Kan later seized the city and tried to found his empire, Ochkanatlan, on it.

The dragons also built it as the base of a "stairway", more precisely a cable, meant to reach beyond Teyvat's sky, working together with the satellite later known as the Tonatiuh. Its ruler survives only as a voice trapped in a statue.

Almost everything known comes from two 5.2 quests: Ixlel's own speech in a world quest, and Kukulkan's account of the cable at the Tonatiuh in the Archon Quest. Treat the city as a sketched backdrop rather than a fully mapped place.

Established: - Chichen Uctokah is named by its ruler as the "Land of Seven Flames", and she calls herself its sovereign, a Dragonlord.
- Its ruler was the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L, who gives a longer technical-sounding designation as well. Paimon shortens the name to Ixlel and the Dragonlord accepts it grudgingly.
- Och-Kan, called the usurper, tried to build his nation Ochkanatlan upon the city.
- Ixlel says that her authority was stolen and that her memories were used to entrap her. She says he forced her to serve his empire because he did not know how to run the city. Her heart was broken apart and hidden in devices.
- The empire and its delusions are said to have fallen to ash, while Ixlel remained imprisoned in a crude statue in the Old Core of Chu'ulel, her life nearly spent.

- Kukulkan, speaking in the Archon Quest, describes a stairway, or better a cable, put up by the dragons to reach beyond their skies while searching for light in the dark outer realms. This was before the false sky covered the world.
- The Tonatiuh was later modified from a part of that cable, and had been meant to hang higher in the sky. Kukulkan says Och-Kan turned it around, and that Och-Kan hid a Golden Entreaty there. The city beneath it, he says, once rivalled Tollan.
- The wiki states that Chichen Uctokah served as the base of this cable and worked alongside the Tonatiuh.

- Ixlel claims her stored memories are everything she was, and that for long-lived beings such memories are chains. She asks the Traveler to gather the fragments of her heart and then remove the restored heart, so she may die free. She says her consciousness would be spent within thirty winters regardless.
- She addresses the Traveler as the "Chosen of Dragons" and mentions colleagues in rulership who are lost, implying other Dragonlords of her kind. The text does not identify them.

Accounts: - Ixlel's version: a great Dragonlord betrayed and enslaved by a traitor who stole her authority. She is proud, theatrical and bitter, so her tale carries her own grievance.
- Kukulkan's version: the city and its cable belonged to the dragons' project to reach beyond the sky. He treats Och-Kan as a failed experiment in merging human and dragon, and his words serve his own plan.

- Neither account says how Och-Kan took control. Ixlel gives only the memory-binding and the stolen authority. The Ochkanatlan entry covers other, more sympathetic views of Och-Kan.

Open questions: - How large the city was, who lived in it, and when it fell are not stated.
- What the Land of Seven Flames refers to (seven flames or seven districts) is never explained.
- The identity of the other lost rulers Ixlel mentions is not given.

Connections: - Ochkanatlan was raised over this city; see the Ochkanatlan civilisation entry, and the Old Core of Chu'ulel where Ixlel is kept.
- The Tonatiuh, the sky-ship tied to the cable, and the Abyss Order's use of Ochkanatlan's ruins are part of the same story.
- The Thirteen Sovereign Lords and the false sky are the wider setting for the Dragonlords' attempts to reach beyond the sky.

97.comment: Chichen Uctokah: Land of Seven Flames
97.content: Chichen Uctokah, the Land of Seven Flames, is the dragon city that Ixlel (Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L) once ruled. Och-Kan seized it and built Ochkanatlan upon it. The dragons had also built it as the base of a sky cable reaching beyond Teyvat, alongside the satellite Tonatiuh. Details of the city itself are sparse in canon.

key: Heavenly Principles' conquest of the dragons
98.content:
Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns (also: When the Doves Held Branches, war against the Seven Sovereigns, Heavenly Principles' conquest of the dragons, usurpation of the dragons' Authorities): The oldest conflict in Teyvat's recorded lore. An Enkanomiyan chronicle calls the era "When the Doves Held Branches". The eternal throne of the heavens, the Heavenly Principles or Primordial One, came to the world, made four shining shades of itself and fought the Seven Sovereigns, the dragon-lords of the old world. After forty years the Sovereigns were vanquished. The invader took part of their elemental Authorities and reshaped the old Light Realm into the Human Realm. Followers of the defeated Sovereigns fled into the sea, and the stolen power later became the basis of the Archons' thrones.

This conquest is distinct from the later war of funerary flame, when the Dragon King Nibelung returned with Abyssal power to fight the same usurper, and from the Archon War, fought over the thrones made from the stolen power. It explains why surviving Sovereigns such as Dvalin, Apep and Neuvillette cannot use their full power while an Archon holds the matching Authority.

Established: - Before the Heavenly Principles arrived, the world belonged to the dragons. The Dragon King Nibelung and the Seven Sovereigns led it, and each Sovereign held one elemental Authority and a region attuned to that element (Seven Sovereigns wiki, drawing on Before Sun and Moon).
- The chronicle Before Sun and Moon (The Byakuyakoku Collection, Vol. 2) says the eternal throne of the heavens came and the world was made anew. The Primordial One then fought the seven "terrifying sovereigns" and made four shining shades of itself.
- Later quests and the Four Shades page name those Shades as Naberius (Life), Ronova (Death), Istaroth (Time) and Asmoday (Space).
- The chronicle says forty winters entombed the flames and forty summers churned the seas, after which the Sovereigns were vanquished and "the seven nations submitted to the heavens".
- The victor then began making heaven and earth for humanity. The seas accepted those who rebelled and would not kneel, so the Sovereigns' followers came to live in the Dark Sea and deep water.
- In Calamitous Tread (4.1) Neuvillette tells the Traveler and Paimon that when the First Usurper arrived on Teyvat it seized a part of the dragons' power, and that this stolen power is the basis of the Archons' Authorities. Seven elemental Archons correspond to seven Sovereigns.

- The Light Realm, the original form of Teyvat's energy and the home of pure elemental beings, was narrowed and refracted into the seven elements to make the Human Realm. Light Realm creatures and the Human Realm are incompatible unless adapted.
- Neuvillette's Vision story says the usurper had to keep subduing the "resentments and loathing of the world" to uphold its order, and after being wounded in the great war of vengeance created the Gnoses with "one who came after" for that purpose. The Light Realm wiki page links this resentment to the narrowing of the Light Realm, whose overflow the Belyi Tsar and Aksinya call "love".
- About 400 years after the Held Branches the world was ready: animals, plants and then humans were created, and humanity made a covenant with the Primordial One, beginning the unified civilization.
- The chronicle also suggests the Primordial One "may have been Phanes": a winged, crowned, androgynous being born from an egg whose shell it used as the false sky, dividing the "universe" from the "microcosm of the world".
- A Sovereign's dragonhood is bound up with its Authority. Because the Authorities became the basis of the Archons' powers, no living Sovereign has its full power or full memory of the old world unless the matching divine throne is destroyed and the Authority returned.

- The wiki's reconstructed order: Nibelung makes the Three Moons and leaves; the Heavenly Principles descend, seize part of the Authorities and create the Shades; the fighting lasts forty years; the world is remade; humans appear after 400 years; the war of funerary flame follows at an unstated later date, ending about 6,000 years ago.
- The Heavenly Principles also took control of the Three Moons after the conquest, according to the Timeline page.
- By the chronicle's account, the people of the Seven Sovereigns found refuge in the oceans. Enkanomiya's ancestors later fell into the dark water during the war of funerary flame, met a ruling people there called the Dragonheirs of the Depths, and fought them.

Accounts: - The Enkanomiyan chronicle tells it as a divine conquest from a scribe's point of view: heaven's will taking shape on earth, with the Primordial One as the true lord.
- Neuvillette calls the invader the "First Usurper" and treats the Authorities as stolen. This is a dragon's view.
- Apep, in the quest Homecoming, is at first hostile to anyone tied to the old world's usurpers and remains dissatisfied with the current order even after calming down.
- The Heavenly Principles give no account of the event in anything the Traveler hears.

- Hydro vishap legend calls the Hydro Dragon the "beating heart" that ruled the Primordial Sea. It was defeated in the war and later withered away, and part of its Authority was later bound into the Hydro Archon's throne, until Focalors destroyed it. Neuvillette was reborn as its successor in human form.
- Natlan's accounts (An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty, summarised on the Xiuhcoatl and Natlan history pages) say part of Xiuhcoatl's Pyro Authority was taken when the heavens came and that he was left frozen in lava in a state of "false death". He woke when Nibelung returned and was later slain by Xbalanque, who became the first Pyro Archon.
- The Sumeru history page says Apep's Dendro Authority was stolen and that Irminsul was then taken over and refashioned.
- Wiki summaries say the Cryo Dragon's corpse was later used by Hyperborea in an attempt to make a Primordial Human, which left Snezhnaya covered in primordial ice. That happened long after the conquest.

Open questions: - How exactly the Authorities were divided: how much stayed with the Sovereigns and how much went to the thrones.
- Whether there was an Electro Sovereign and what became of it.
- Who the original Anemo and Hydro Sovereigns were.
- Why the Heavenly Principles chose Teyvat, beyond a home for humanity, and what became of the Sovereigns' domains.
- Whether the forty years are literal.

Connections: - Aftermath: the Heavenly Principles create humanity about 400 years later and the unified civilization begins (lore.unified-civilization).
- Second conflict: Nibelung returns with Abyssal power and is killed by the Heavenly Principles; that war ended about 6,000 years ago (lore.war-of-funerary-flame).
- The stolen Authorities become the divine thrones that gods fight over in the Archon War (lore.archon-war, cosmology.gnosis).
- Present day as of 7.1: Neuvillette (Hydro, Fontaine, Authority restored after Focalors' death), Dvalin (Anemo, Mondstadt), Apep (Dendro, Sumeru) and Azhdaha (Geo, Liyue) survive; Xiuhcoatl was killed by Xbalanque and the Cryo Sovereign is dead.

key: Forty Years After the Held Branches
99.comment: Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns: When the Doves Held Branches
99.content: The Enkanomiyan chronicle Before Sun and Moon names the age of the Heavenly Principles' war on the Seven Sovereigns "When the Doves Held Branches". It records that the Primordial One made four shades of itself, that forty winters and forty summers followed, and that the Sovereigns were then vanquished and the seven nations submitted to the heavens. The same book dates the creation of humans to 400 years after the Held Branches.

100.comment: Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns: The Seven Sovereigns
100.content: The Seven Sovereigns were the mightiest dragons of the Light Realm, each holding one elemental Authority and ruling a region. Canon names Dvalin (Anemo, successor), Azhdaha (Geo), Apep (Dendro), Neuvillette (Hydro, successor to the first Hydro Dragon), Xiuhcoatl (Pyro, killed) and an unnamed Cryo Dragon (dead). No Electro Sovereign is identified. Part of their Authorities became the Archons' powers.

101.comment: Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns: Remaking of the Light Realm
101.content: After the Sovereigns fell, the Heavenly Principles repurposed the Light Realm. Its primordial energy was narrowed and divided into the seven elements, forming the Human Realm. Creatures of the old and new realms are incompatible unless adapted, as with vishaps modified to accept Orobashi's coral or the Sangacorallia that break raw elemental energy down. Neuvillette's Vision story speaks of the "resentments and loathing of the world" that the usurper must keep subdued.

102.comment: Conquest of the Seven Sovereigns: The Dark Sea and the Defeated
102.content: Those who would not kneel were taken in by the seas. The chronicle says the people of the Seven Sovereigns found refuge in the oceans, and that the Dragonheirs of the Depths ruled the dark water where Enkanomiya's ancestors fell during the later war. It tells this from Enkanomiya's side, so the Sovereigns' followers appear as hunters in the shadows.

103.content:
Curse of Khaenri'ah (also: Curse of Immortality, Curse of the Khaenri'ahns, Khaenri'ahn curse, curse of the wilderness, Ronova's curse): When the gods destroyed Khaenri'ah about 500 years ago, Ronova, the Ruler of Death, laid a curse on its people. Those of pure Khaenri'ahn blood received the Curse of Immortality: they cannot die, yet their bodies and minds keep eroding. Those whose ancestry came from the lands of other gods received the "curse of the wilderness" and became monsters, hilichurls among them.

Ronova herself was defeated in 7.1, but the Curse of Immortality was not lifted: the Traveler concludes it was a permanent curse set under the Heavenly Principles' judgment, which she could not undo at will. Her separate Curse of Death over Snezhnaya ended with her Authority.

Established: - Cast as Khaenri'ah fell, by Ronova, one of the Four Shades.
- Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns, the "greater sinners", were made immortal; people of other gods' ancestry were turned into monsters.
- Immortal does not mean unharmed: body and soul keep eroding.

- Eide (Chlothar Alberich), whom the Traveler meets through their sibling's memories of Avidya Forest in the Caribert act (3.5), called the curse a "gift" from the gods that took away any chance of release. His son Caribert, whose mother came from Mondstadt, turned into a hilichurl.
- People with strong Khaenri'ahn blood can be recognised by their eyes. In 7.1 Mitya also sensed the "signature" of the Curse of Immortality on Dainsleif and on Pierro.

- Capitano said most Khaenri'ahns knew nothing of the Five Sinners' use of Abyssal power, yet all were cursed alike.
- The Khaenri'ahns descend from the Tsaritsa Anastasya and the Third Descender Saarelainen (revealed in 7.1); Anastasya reasons that the cataclysm triggered the Third Descender's curse, which is why the Heavenly Principles sleep.
- The Schwanenritter evacuated survivors up to Sumeru and fought the Abyss there until only Anfortas remained; one of them, Ynghildr, was corrupted into a Shadowy Husk.
- Dainsleif ordered the elite guard Halfdan to protect the people of Khaenri'ah at all costs; Halfdan and the other Royal Guards became Black Serpent Knights, cursed husks, yet Halfdan kept part of his mind and the order.

Immortality: The Curse of Immortality is laid on pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns. Capitano calls it "the curse of absolute life". They cannot die, but Dainsleif says that over time both body and soul wear down until they are nearly nonexistent.

Dainsleif is the clearest case, and he carries a ring from his brother Vedrfolnir that keeps resetting his body's condition, which has preserved him far better than other immortals such as Capitano, whose decay was severe after centuries. Even so, his mind is still affected by erosion.

Eide describes his hands failing as if decaying from within, and in 7.1 Dainsleif calls Ronova the architect of his torment over the past five hundred years. Capitano put the cost in terms of endless physical torment and of witnessing the demise of everything the cursed held dear. Even so, as the First Harbinger he was considered the strongest of the Fatui, with strength said to rival a god, despite the decay. The Lord of the Night said that for those cursed with immortality, release from the mortal coil is the greatest form of peace, a reminder of what the curse withholds.

Relation to erosion. Erosion, the wearing of mind, body, will and spirit with time, is part of the world's natural order imposed by the Heavenly Principles and tied to Irminsul. The cursed Khaenri'ahns are a case where the wear continues while death is refused. How exactly the curse and erosion interact is not explained in canon.

Wilderness: The curse of the wilderness falls on Khaenri'ahns whose ancestry belonged to other gods' lands. It turns them into monsters, including hilichurls: they lose their language and most of their memory and sink into a painful, prolonged existence.

Eide explains the rule: Khaenri'ah began as a single bloodline but welcomed any human who forsook their gods, and those people were punished with the curse of the wilderness as they fled. Caribert, whose mother was from Mondstadt, was one such case. Dainsleif confirms that the hilichurls in the Chasm are former citizens of Khaenri'ah.

The wiki also records that only Khaenri'ahns with descent from surface humans can turn into hilichurls. Hilichurls are known to have existed for over a thousand years, so this curse did not create all of them. The wiki treats the curse of the wilderness as a broader divine affliction, and canon notes that hilichurl numbers surged across Teyvat after the cataclysm. Cursed hilichurls grow forgetful, wear masks, and some seek out the Chasm to wait for the end. Humanity can be partly restored: after the encounter with Vedrfolnir's Abyssal power, a second dose of medicine woke Caribert and he could speak again, and Narzissenkreuz gave an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue sentience in Fontaine.

Many Abyss Order mages, lectors and heralds are thought to have been Khaenri'ahns too. Paimon concluded from the sibling's account that the Abyss monsters were once the people of Khaenri'ah. Cleansing the curse from hilichurls is a goal of the Abyss Order and the Traveler's sibling: so that they may return to the natural cycle of life and death, or, according to Dainsleif, become the foundation of a rebuilt Khaenri'ah.

Ronova and the curse: Ronova is the Ruler of Death, one of the four gods the Heavenly Principles created. In Pierro's memory she cast the Curse of Immortality with no pity and no pleasure, only indifference, while people begged for mercy. In 5.3 Capitano used the curse against her (see Capitano's Gambit); she chose to keep it.

After Ronova was defeated in 7.1, the Traveler concluded in the quest that the Curse of Immortality was permanent, laid under the Heavenly Principles' judgment, and could not be undone at her will. By contrast, her Curse of Death over Snezhnaya was her own act, and ended when Celestia took her Authority. Pierro said the feud born of the Curse of Immortality was perhaps destined never to die.

Pierro's own immortality counteracted her Curse of Death in 7.0, letting him wake sooner than others. Whether Ronova's presumed death changes anything about the curse remains unanswered.

Bearers: Known cursed Khaenri'ahns as of 7.1:
- Dainsleif, the Bough Keeper, who wanders Teyvat and hunts the Abyss Order.
- Capitano (Thrain), First of the Fatui Harbingers, whose body now lies seated on the Throne of the Primal Fire after he merged his life force with the Lord of the Night.
- Pierro, Director of the Fatui, who in his earlier life as Eftirvit was among those cursed as he looked on Ronova.
- Eide, who is Chlothar Alberich, pure-blooded and cursed with immortality; the skeletons later found in Avidya Forest leave his end uncertain.
- Halfdan, the Black Serpent Knights and the hilichurls of the Chasm, cursed in the wilderness form.

Rhinedottir and Kaeya are listed by the wiki as people who appear to have avoided the curse, but their circumstances are not explained.

In the world today: The Abyss Order learned of a pool in the Chasm that eases the curse. In the world quest series including Requiem of the Echoing Depths (2.6), the sibling authorised an experimental device to amplify it, despite a low chance of success and a high chance of causing suffering. Dainsleif and the Traveler stopped it, with Halfdan sacrificing himself to halt the device. Dainsleif told Halfdan's spirit a comforting lie, that Khaenri'ah still stood, so that he could pass on in peace.

Dainsleif regards the curse as altering reality itself and so considers the Order's attempts futile. He no longer views hilichurls and Abyss monsters as human, but he honours the guards who protected their dying kin.

Chlothar, believing the Abyssal "sinner" had answered pleas the Seven ignored, concluded that only a sinner could save another sinner and resolved to use the power of the Abyss against the gods; he went on to found the Abyss Order. The Traveler learned of this through the sibling's memories in Avidya Forest.

Accounts: - Dainsleif: the curse is a punishment he has endured for five centuries; Ronova is its architect. He considers the Abyss Order's attempts to cure it futile, because the curse alters reality.
- Eide: the gods' "gift", indiscriminate, robbing the people of release.
- Capitano: an injustice done to innocents, the reason he sought revenge and used the curse as a weapon.
- Pierro: the curse as a feud that was perhaps destined never to die.
- The Traveler (7.1): a ruling of the Heavenly Principles that Ronova carried out and could not cancel.

Open questions: - Whether and how the curse could ever end.
- How Kaeya and Rhinedottir escaped it, if they did.
- How the ring of Vedrfolnir works.

- How the Third Descender's curse and the Heavenly Principles' sleep relate to the Khaenri'ahn curses.
- What the curse does to a Khaenri'ahn once erosion is nearly total.

Connections: See Fall of Khaenri'ah, Cataclysm, Fall of Ronova, Ronova, the Four Shades, Dainsleif, Capitano, Pierro, hilichurls, the Abyss Order, Erosion and the Heavenly Principles' dormancy.

Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text): a cursed character should show weariness, grief and patience rather than power, and speak of the gods with bitterness. Do not state that the curse is broken, that a particular character is cured, or that all hilichurls are Khaenri'ahns. Most people in Teyvat know nothing of the curse; do not let an uninformed commoner explain it.

104.content: Vedrfolnir gave his younger brother Dainsleif a ring that keeps resetting his body's condition. It is why Dainsleif looks like an ordinary man after five centuries, unlike the badly decayed Capitano, and why his memory has held up better than that of other immortals. His mind is still touched by erosion.

105.content: In When All Becomes a Monument, Capitano offered his life to Ronova as the payment she demanded for Mavuika's use of her powers. Because the Curse of Immortality forbade him from dying, taking his death would break her own rule. Ronova upheld the curse; the Lord of the Night absorbed his life force and became essentially immortal. His body remains seated on the Throne of the Primal Fire.

106.comment: Curse of Khaenri'ah: Eide and Caribert
106.content: Eide is the name Chlothar Alberich used when the Traveler's sibling met him in Avidya Forest. He was pure-blooded and cursed with immortality; his son Caribert, whose mother was from Mondstadt, became a hilichurl and sank into torpor. A forbidden medicine had no effect at first; after Chlothar fell under the sway of Vedrfolnir's Abyssal voice in a hidden sanctuary, a second dose woke Caribert. Chlothar came to see the Abyss as a power to turn against the gods, and he went on to found the Abyss Order. In the present day Dainsleif and the Traveler find the skeletons of a man and a woman in the field there, and Dainsleif supposes that Chlothar found a way out of the curse.

107.comment: Curse of Khaenri'ah: Chasm Water Pool
107.content: In the Chasm's underground, a relic pool eases the effects of the curse. Dying hilichurls come there to wait for the end, guarded by Halfdan and other Black Serpent Knights. The Abyss Order tried to amplify its power with a device, which caused agonizing pain to those cursed. Halfdan stopped it with his life.

108.content:
Destruction of Irminsul (also: Burning of Irminsul, burning of the World Tree, Irminsul crisis, Irminsul's destruction): The destruction of Irminsul is the climax of the Sumeru part of Song of the Welkin Moon (Archon Quest Acts IX and X, Version 6.6). After his body died in Nod-Krai, Dottore reached Irminsul through the Ley Lines and took it over from inside, putting Nahida into a coma and making a giant Irminsul tree rise in Sumeru City. Sumeru moved the world's information into Aaru. Nahida then invoked her authority as Irminsul's keeper and burned the tree with the Pyro Gnosis, which Mavuika had given her. The Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius consented. Dottore died in the fire, and as of 7.1 Aaru does Irminsul's work.

The fire burned for seven days and seven nights, and only the underground parts of the tree remained. Nahida says Teyvat's most vital information was largely preserved. Her own link was moved from Irminsul to Aaru by Nicole, so she was not harmed. The Pyro Gnosis vanished in the fire. Nahida says that with Irminsul burned, the flow of fate now "carries many more possibilities."

Established: - Irminsul is older than the Heavenly Principles. In the age of dragons it had a different role. After the Heavenly Principles came, they remade it into a device that records and keeps all information. Istaroth calls it "the original tree of Teyvat" and the means by which the Heavenly Principles maintain fate.
- Nahida calls Irminsul both a national treasure and a major threat to Sumeru. As Dendro Archon she is bound to protect it.
- Under a rule set by the Heavenly Principles, when Irminsul is in grave danger part of its power seals Sumeru off, so that the rest of the world has time even if Sumeru falls. Earlier pollution (the forbidden knowledge) never triggered it; Dottore's direct invasion did.

- The Traveler has no records in Irminsul, so the tree cannot hinder them. They walked through the barrier, and their meeting with Mavuika could not be recorded. Mavuika's records go to the Night Kingdom rather than the Ley Lines while she is in Natlan.
- Apep says Irminsul was among the things the Heavenly Principles usurped from ancient dragonkind and repurposed.

Causes: Dottore's plan was to split his soul in two. One half would reach the Ley Lines through death and the other would be fed in as pure data, and they would meet inside Irminsul and make him whole again. His body was killed in Nod-Krai, by Columbina according to the wiki. Pantalone, bound by contract, then placed Dottore's "final data backup" into the Ley Lines; it had been kept in the Northland Bank's most secure vault. Nahida had guarded every pathway by which an outsider could transmit themselves into Irminsul, but not the one route that cannot be guarded: death. Closing it would have meant stopping the souls of the dead from returning to the Ley Lines.

Inside the tree, Dottore restricted Nahida's authority and the tree began refusing all connections. He told Pantalone that he meant to "create a new world inside the existing one" and to experiment freely in the afterlife. Dottore said both of them despise the world's existing laws; Pantalone asked whether it was really so greedy to want the world to run by new rules, and said he backed Dottore as a venture capitalist. Fatui agents entered Sumeru beforehand; Cyno noticed a suspicious number of "merchant caravans" coming in through Bayda Harbor.
The Anomalous Tree Marrow, an item said to be resin from Irminsul's incinerated trunk, holds Dottore's digitized memories of the plan: he first experimented on animals and other people's souls, settled on digitization as the transfer method, and imagined an "immortal record" as something more eternal than eternal life.

Course: - Warning: Collei dreamed that everyone in Sumeru City had swapped identities and only she remembered the truth. Nicole spoke into her mind and called it a premonition. Nahida and the new Sages evacuated the rainforest to Caravan Ribat.
- Collapse: Irminsul stopped recording and processing information. Nahida took over the work herself until she fell into a coma. She was moved away to weaken her link, and Apep sheltered her at the Heart of Oasis and shared Dendro energy with her.
- Spreading madness: civilians who tried to return near the Yasna Monument fell into psychosis and killed one another, and abnormal Ley Line Blossoms appeared. The Jinn rose around Gurabad until Liloupar calmed them, and a barrier sealed Sumeru off.
- Aaru: the Seven Pillars agreed to open Aaru after Nefer answered Deshret's three questions ("time"), freeing Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf. The Akademiya's scholars, led by Alhaitham and Kaveh, rebuilt Aaru and merged it with the Akasha.
- The tree: a colossal silver Irminsul tree burst up in Sumeru City. Nahida called it "a tree of unbridled greed" and took it as proof that Dottore was behind the crisis.

- The Pyro Gnosis: Nahida, speaking through the Traveler at the sealed Natlan border, asked Mavuika to give the Pyro Gnosis to Sumeru outright. Mavuika agreed. The Traveler walked through the barrier, absorbed the Gnosis into their body through their mastery of Pyro, and carried it back in.
- The overload: Aaru-linked Akasha terminals were handed out to everyone in Sumeru. Together their connections overloaded Irminsul and shut it down, which stopped the tree's growth and hid the wearers from Dottore's tracking.
- The assault: Cyno, Dehya, Candace, Jeht and others drew the Fatui off at the city gates, while Tighnari, Wanderer, Paimon and the Traveler climbed to the Sanctuary of Surasthana. Wanderer and the Traveler entered Irminsul's depths, and Nicole guided them from the Eternal Oasis until Dottore cut her off.
- Inside: Dottore revealed that he had worked out Wanderer's erased identity as Scaramouche. The Traveler attached Nahida's device to the Ley Lines, and Aaru began pulling the world's information out of Irminsul, draining Dottore's power. Nahida joined the fight from the Eternal Oasis.

The burning: Dottore broke the ground under them and the three fell into Irminsul's depths. Nahida drew the Pyro Gnosis out of the Traveler and declared, "I invoke my supreme authority as the keeper of Irminsul," asking the Shades to commend or condemn her. Ronova, the Ruler of Death, asked whether she would destroy what was both her roots and her finest achievement. Nahida answered that Irminsul was corrupted beyond redemption and that she honoured it by fighting for the humanity it exists to protect. Istaroth reminded her that the Archons owe their authority to the Heavenly Principles. Naberius gave the verdict: since Nahida had become "a great tree" herself, the loss of another tree was nothing to fear. The Pyro Gnosis burst into flame and set Irminsul's roots alight.

Ronova addressed Nahida by her title Mahakusaladhamma, and Naberius parted from her as "Lord of Dendro." As the fire spread, Mavuika's voice spoke of "the first flame". Nahida carried the Traveler and Wanderer upward. Dottore chained the Traveler to drag them back, but Wanderer broke the chain, and Dottore himself was pulled down into the flames by shadowy figures: the Segments he had deleted years before.

Dottores end: Bound to the burning tree, Dottore faded away. Before he died he spoke with Pantalone, who watched the fire from outside, and called him by his real name, Feofan. He warned Pantalone that his elixir of immortality would run out within a few years with no one left to make it. To Nahida he admitted that setting fire to the thing her own survival depended on was brave, and that her earlier threat had been empty but this one was real. Nahida told him the "experiment" was never his and parted with "We will never meet again."

Dottore called the outcome "certainly not the worst" and said he had concluded his "experiment in blasphemy." Pantalone told him he was "a truly rare talent." Pantalone was not caught and remains alive as of 7.1.

Aftermath: - Aaru, reconfigured, now collects and stores the information the Ley Lines carry. Nahida asks the Traveler to think of it as "the new Irminsul", and her existence is bound to it.
- Sumeru's people went home and rebuilt. Thoth and Heryshaf chose to stay at the Temple of Silence.
- Snezhnaya sent a letter through Pulcinella, the Rooster: Dottore was a rogue element already under internal censure after Nod-Krai, Snezhnaya had lost a Harbinger to him, his subordinates would face Snezhnayan law, and relief funds were on the way. Naphis called it diplomatically watertight. Nahida said Snezhnaya must keep a tight rein on its actions.

Nahida and the Traveler went to Natlan to thank Mavuika and tell her the Pyro Gnosis had vanished. Mavuika had already sensed its loss. She said this was always meant as giving, not lending. She wondered whether its disappearance was a knock-on effect on "a certain strand of fate," given how large the fallout of Irminsul's loss might be.

Pyro gnosis status: In Light and Shadow, Intertwined (Archon Quest Chapter VII, 7.1), Anastasya asks the Traveler where the Pyro Gnosis is, since it is the only Gnosis whose whereabouts are unknown. The Traveler says it burned to ashes with Irminsul and that, according to Mavuika, it has returned to the Ley Lines. Anastasya answers that Gnoses come from the Third Descender's remains and cannot coexist with the Ley Lines for long, so it will one day be excised. This is not the same as what Nahida and Mavuika said in 6.6 (no trace, not even ash).

Accounts: - Nahida: Irminsul exists to protect humanity, so humanity, and she as one of its protectors, must come first. Afterwards she says fate now carries many more possibilities and that she will watch carefully.
- The Shades: Ronova questioned the choice, Istaroth spoke for the tree's role in fate, and Naberius approved.
- Dottore: he called his work an experiment in blasphemy and called the result not the worst. He told Nahida that he had "unwittingly" been her arch-enemy all along.
- Pantalone: he never thought Dottore could win, but honoured the contract as "a reputable partner."
- The Traveler (7.1) and Mavuika give different accounts of the Pyro Gnosis's end; see above.

The Binding Field of Universal Nirvana domain text describes Irminsul as the tree "that once sustained memory", now turned to ash, and calls Dottore a "heretic" who claimed enlightenment after seizing the axis of the world's memories.

Open questions: Canon leaves open where the Pyro Gnosis is, how far the Heavenly Principles' grip on fate has weakened, whether the silver-white trees and domains elsewhere in Teyvat changed, and what the Heavenly Principles make of Irminsul's loss. Do not resolve these.

Connections: Irminsul and the Ley Lines, Aaru, Nahida, Dottore and Pantalone, the Pyro Gnosis and Mavuika, the Four Shades, fate and the Heavenly Principles. Also the Akasha (repurposed for the overload), the Seven Pillars and Nabu Malikata's legacy, Nicole, the Wanderer (who fought inside the tree), the Nod-Krai chapter (where Dottore's body died), and the Tsaritsa's search for the Gnoses (7.1).
