How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): set after 6.6, Sumeru is rebuilding from a crisis everyone in the nation lived through: evacuation, the sealed border, the madness near the city, the giant tree and its burning. Most Sumerians know Irminsul burned and that their Archon is recovering. The details (Dottore's soul, the Shades, the Pyro Gnosis) are known only to those who were inside or in the leadership.

Outside Sumeru, most people would know only that the border was sealed and that some catastrophe was stopped. Aaru now holds the world's memory, so Nahida still has her link to it; do not portray her as cut off or weakened by the loss. Dottore is dead for good as of 7.1; Pantalone survives.

109.comment: Destruction of Irminsul: Dottore inside Irminsul
109.content: After his body died in Nod-Krai, Dottore entered Irminsul through death. Pantalone placed his final data backup into the Ley Lines, and the two halves of him merged inside the tree. From there he restricted Nahida's authority, watched the world through Irminsul, and grew a giant Irminsul tree in Sumeru City. He died when Nahida burned Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis in 6.6, pulled into the fire by his own deleted Segments.

110.content: To stop the corrupted Irminsul tree, Sumeru's scholars merged the reopened Aaru with the Akasha System, built new terminals and gave them to everyone they could reach. All those connections together overloaded Irminsul and shut it down, stopping the tree's growth. Thoth said he never thought he would see Irminsul shut down. The terminals also kept their wearers from being tracked accurately by Irminsul, so Dottore could not see them clearly. (Inside the tree, Dottore later claimed he had only played along with their belief that he could not track them.)

111.comment: Destruction of Irminsul: Nahida's verdict before the Shades
111.content: To burn Irminsul, Nahida invoked her "supreme authority as the keeper of Irminsul" and stood before the symbols of Ronova (Ruler of Death), Istaroth (Ruler of Time) and Naberius (Ruler of Life). Ronova asked if she would abandon what she had always fought for. Istaroth stressed that the tree maintains fate and that the Archons' authority comes from the Heavenly Principles. Nahida said that wisdom means weighing the options, and that if they cared for the world's fortunes they should preserve her. Naberius agreed and said goodbye: "Till we meet again, Lord of Dendro."

112.comment: Destruction of Irminsul: Pyro Gnosis after the burning
112.content: Mavuika gave the Pyro Gnosis to Sumeru in 6.6, and Nahida used it to burn Irminsul. Afterwards it could not be found: Nahida found no trace of it, not even ash, and Mavuika only sensed its loss. In 7.1 the Traveler told Anastasya it had burned to ashes and that, according to Mavuika, it had returned to the Ley Lines. Anastasya expects that it will one day be excised from them. It is the only Gnosis whose whereabouts are unknown.

113.content: When Dottore's invasion put Irminsul in grave danger, a rule laid down by the Heavenly Principles sealed Sumeru inside a barrier so that the rest of the world could survive even if Sumeru fell. Nicole and Nefer got in just before it closed. Only the Traveler, who has no records in Irminsul, could walk through it, which is how the Pyro Gnosis was brought in from Natlan.

114.comment: Destruction of Irminsul: Anomalous Tree Marrow
114.content: Anomalous Tree Marrow is a strange resin thought to have oozed from Irminsul's incinerated trunk, with a baleful light inside. Touching it floods the mind with Dottore's digitized memories: Harbinger meetings, his Segments, and the steps of his soul-transfer experiment. It is gained from the Binding Field of Universal Nirvana, a domain where Dottore is fought "one last time".

115.content:
Eleazar (also: Eleazar disease, Eleazar patients): Treat Eleazar as a past-tense disease: before that Archon Quest it was a feared, incurable condition tied to forbidden knowledge, and it has since disappeared. Hospital records note that some patients (the "Specimens") believed it was divine punishment, and desperate families sometimes grasped at false promises of a cure.

Because it correlated with a person's elemental content, it was both a medical puzzle for Akademiya researchers and an opening for those who wanted to exploit the sick, notably Fatui agents working under Dottore.

Established: - Hospital research notes say sufferers carry a higher elemental content than ordinary people, and that managing and reducing it can control the disease. The unnamed researcher found one treatment that made a late-stage patient's symptoms vanish entirely.
- Nilotpala Lotus can help patients regain energy, and Sumeru's forests are said to ease the illness, though the Withering made the disease noticeably worse.
- Some people were born with it: Collei and Dunyarzad are given as examples. A boy named Arbaaz, described as "little", is recorded at the hospital.
- Cases were increasing in Sumeru City, and residents with symptoms were urged to go to the Bimarstan.

- The Chinese name means roughly "Demon Scale Disease"; the English name's possible Hebrew origin is only an etymological guess.
- Named cases listed by the wiki include Abbas, Arbaaz, Avin, Collei, Dunyarzad, Gulab, Hakim, Kumar and Emira; Arbaaz, Avin, Gulab, Hakim and Emira died from the illness or from complications of treatment.

- Collei's treatment side effects (trauma, unstable control over "black fire", plague-like symptoms) reportedly faded after Cyno sealed the god's remains inside her, but her Eleazar symptoms then returned, which is why she was taken to Tighnari at Gandharva Ville for care.

Accounts: - The Akademiya built a hospital at Dar al-Shifa in the Great Red Sand to study and treat Eleazar. Its doctor found a working treatment using an unknown material. The records mention "Specimens" who called the treatment blasphemous, because they believed the illness was divine punishment. The hospital was later abandoned for undisclosed reasons and the Akademiya barred access to the ruins.
- The Fatui under Il Dottore also researched treatments using a god's remains. One of his subordinates falsely told parents the Fatui had a cure, collecting afflicted children as test subjects; Collei was among those handed over (Tighnari, in Chronic Illness, says her mother did so after a Fatui member lied about having a cure).

- Abbas, a 23-year-old patient, was the lone survivor of a group of four at the hospital: the doctor cured him using body parts taken from the other three. Horrified, he tunnelled out and escaped. This is told through hospital notes and etchings, so it reflects what the documents say rather than a witnessed scene.

- Collei's treatment left her deeply traumatised according to her voice-overs and the Chronic Illness quest; her story is told across the Sumeru Archon Quest and the Collei manga rather than in one account.

Open questions: - What triggers Eleazar in an individual is not stated.
- Whether the Fatui used the Dar al-Shifa hospital or a different desert site is unclear.
- The identity of the Dar al-Shifa doctor is scrubbed from the records.

- Why forests ease the symptoms is never explained.

Connections: - The Withering: Eleazar is the form it takes in human bodies.
- King Deshret: Kasala's memories show a strikingly similar affliction in his day: darkened scales and crazed whispers in people's minds after forbidden knowledge reached them. Rukkhadevata helped erase the knowledge, and Deshret sealed it away at the cost of his life and his civilisation.
- Irminsul: once Rukkhadevata's tainted consciousness was removed, the symptoms disappeared and patients recovered within days.

- In the 3.2 Archon Quest Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies, the cleansing is shown as green petals drifting over Sumeru and falling on people afflicted by Eleazar, and on those driven mad by connecting their minds to Irminsul. As of the 7.1 cutoff no canon source shows Eleazar returning.

116.content: An Akademiya hospital in the Great Red Sand built to study and treat Eleazar. It is now abandoned and closed to the public by the Akademiya. Documents left behind include a diagnostic report linking Eleazar to high elemental content, a record of a treatment that worked, and Abbas's account of fleeing after surviving it.

117.content: Abbas was a 23-year-old patient at the Eleazar Hospital and the only survivor of four. He was cured with body parts taken from the other three and fled by digging underground. Known from documents, not as a living character in the story.

118.content: Collei was born with Eleazar. Her mother, like other parents, handed her to the Fatui after one of Dottore's subordinates lied that they had a cure. She was treated using a god's remains, which suppressed her symptoms but left her traumatised and with unstable "black fire". After Cyno sealed the remains in her body, her Eleazar symptoms returned, and she was taken to Tighnari in Gandharva Ville. Her full biography belongs in her own entry.

119.content: Dunyarzad was born with Eleazar according to the quest The Coming of the Sabzeruz Festival. Details of her experience are in her own entry.

120.content:
Fall of Khaenri'ah (also: destruction of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ah's destruction, fall of Khaenriah, Khaenri'ah's fall): Five hundred years ago Khaenri'ah, an underground kingdom built entirely by humans with no god, was destroyed. Its last king, the Vinster King Irmin, grew obsessed with the power of the Abyss. He named the Traveler's twin his heir and "Savior", then used them as a vessel to absorb Abyssal power. A palace coup led by Dainsleif ended with five of Khaenri'ah's greatest figures, the Five Sinners, dividing that power among themselves. Then the gods came: the Heavenly Principles and The Seven laid the kingdom waste, and Ronova cursed its people. The fall is the core of the cataclysm, and its survivors went on to found the Abyss Order and help found the Fatui.

Version 7.1 revealed a final twist. The Khaenri'ahns descend from the Tsaritsa Anastasya and the Third Descender, Saarelainen, who long ago bound the Heavenly Principles with a curse in case they ever harmed his descendants. Destroying Khaenri'ah triggered it, and the Heavenly Principles have been asleep ever since.

Established: - Khaenri'ah was a godless kingdom of humans, called by Dainsleif "the pride of humankind". It lay underground beneath what is now Sumeru.
- About 500 years ago it was destroyed "by gods". The Traveler and their sibling, newly fallen into Teyvat, saw it burn.
- Pure-blooded survivors were cursed with immortality by Ronova, the Ruler of Death. Many others became monsters, and some of their descendants are the hilichurls and the Abyss Order.

- Under the Eclipse Dynasty, Khaenri'ah built machines meant to fight Celestia. Ruin Guards were once called "Field Tillers", after the saying that land is won with "steel and blood", not farming tools. A letter found in the Gavireh Lajavard ruins says the kingdom's "four pillars" prospered by "spying upon secrets from beyond the skies". This let their machines escape the world's laws.
- Every Archon except Rukkhadevata was summoned to Khaenri'ah during the disaster. She stayed to guard Irminsul from the forbidden knowledge flooding it.
- Ei says Makoto, the Electro Archon of the time, went to Khaenri'ah alone without telling her and never came back.

- Pierro's artifact text (Mocking Mask) says he failed to win the former ruler's favour and failed to stop "the sages" from "tearing away the veil of sin". He describes the result as a tide of divine wrath, destruction and foolishness.
- Capitano said most Khaenri'ahns knew nothing of the Five Sinners' use of Abyssal power, yet all were cursed alike.

The road to ruin: Irmin, the last Vinster King of the Eclipse Dynasty, began as a sane ruler. His closest counsellors were Vedrfolnir, "The Visionary", and Hroptatyr, "The Wise". Over time he became fixated on the Abyss. The Universitas Magistrorum moved almost all its staff into Abyssal Energy research. He also ordered every descendant of the earlier Crimson Moon Dynasty hunted down, as threats to his line.

When the Traveler's sibling reached Khaenri'ah, Irmin and the Court proclaimed them heir to the throne and the nation's "Savior" in a great public celebration. A young Dainsleif kept order in the palace plaza. Later, the king led the heir "down, down, down" to the kingdom's deepest depths and made them a vessel to absorb "unlimited Abyssal power" (glider Wings of Fate's Course Intertwined, 5.2). Dainsleif later said the title "Savior" really stood for "the Vinster King's lust for power" (5.7).

Rerir's memories, explored in All Is Foretold (6.1), show the purge from inside. As a secret Eclipse agent, Rerir worked through case files on Crimson Moon descendants, including orphaned children, each marked as a threat to the dynasty. A voice he took to be Vedrfolnir's whispered to him. Tholindis, his would-be fiancée, quietly belonged to a diluted Crimson Moon branch. She was the only researcher left working on Moon Marrow, and she warned in her reports against staking everything on one poorly understood power. Rebels hiding from the purge called the king "a blind fool, his eyes clouded by powers from beyond this world".

The coup: Vedrfolnir warned Irmin that if he kept on this path, Khaenri'ah would fall. The king had his eyes gouged out and threw him into a cell. Dainsleif, captain of the royal guard and Vedrfolnir's younger brother, gathered Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir ("Gold"), Surtalogi ("The Foul") and Rerir to storm the palace that night and free him. Dainsleif said he did not want treason; he meant to make the king see his error with his sword. But once inside, the others turned on his plan. Each took a share of the Abyssal power the king had poured into the sibling, and they became the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. Dainsleif says they each fell to their own desire: Vedrfolnir to foresee the future, Hroptatyr to limitless knowledge, Rhinedottir to creating life, Surtalogi to supreme strength.

The plan was that Dainsleif's group would hold off the palace troops, Hroptatyr and Rhinedottir would disarm the security measures and Rerir would reach the prison. Vedrfolnir told Rerir he had foreseen the night and had briefly seen "something new". Then he sent him to the Universitas Magistrorum. A strange wave of energy swept the city, and monsters appeared in the streets and the laboratory. Rerir remembered rumours that the king had hidden Abyss-powered "secret mechanisms" in the palace and city. In the lab, Tholindis, trapped by monsters, stepped into a portal to an unknown space and vanished. Broken, Rerir returned to the palace, where Vedrfolnir invited him to "take your share". Dainsleif watched the last of his allies abandon him. Skirk's character story says each Sinner took one sixth of the power.

Dainsleif calls these five, with himself, the six who should have stopped the Vinster King. That night still haunts him, and he says even the brother he came to save betrayed him. When the gods attacked, not one Sinner defended Khaenri'ah, and he will never forgive them. Vedrfolnir also gave Dainsleif a ring that keeps resetting his body's condition, which is why his memory has held up better than that of other cursed survivors.

The destruction: The gods descended on Khaenri'ah and destroyed it. The Traveler remembers a sea of flames and a god, Asmoday, who sealed the twins as they tried to leave the world.

The sibling woke first, saw the kingdom fall, then woke the Traveler and told them the destruction of Khaenri'ah had thrown the world into chaos and they should leave. Asmoday, the Ruler of Space, stopped them, calling them "outlanders", and sealed both twins. Ronova then laid the Curse of Immortality on pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns. Dainsleif was among them, condemned, in the sibling's words, to wander forever while his people became monsters of the Abyss.

Accounts of the assault describe a red sky full of crimson cubes and the kingdom's land torn apart and flooded with lava. In the Inazuma Archon Quest (2.1) Ei recalls seeing "a nation stride forward and lose everything to the Heavenly Principles". Among the Archons, Makoto died in Khaenri'ah; Rukkhadevata died fighting forbidden knowledge in Irminsul; and Egeria fell at Tunigi Hollow in Sumeru's desert, fighting the Abyss.

In 7.1 Pierro remembers Ronova's face as she cast the curse: no pity and no pleasure, only indifference while people begged for mercy. Dainsleif recalls that the Khaenri'ahns who looked up at her saw an untouchable god. The Traveler concludes that the Curse of Immortality was laid under the Heavenly Principles' judgement and is permanent; even Ronova could not simply lift it.

The third descenders curse: The Archon Quest "A Rekviem for the Underworld" (7.1) revealed why the gods' victory cost them. Rhinedottir, drawing on Celestia's records, told Anastasya that all Khaenri'ahns descend from Anastasya and the Third Descender, Saarelainen. After Anastasya was erased as punishment for opening a gate to the Abyss, Saarelainen bargained with the Heavenly Principles. He gave his body to be split into the seven Gnoses in exchange for her return and a promise never to lay a hand on his descendants. He also bound the promise with a curse that would only take effect if it was broken. Anastasya concluded that the cataclysm in Khaenri'ah triggered that curse, which is why the Heavenly Principles are asleep.

Rhinedottir called Anastasya "Mother of Khaenri'ah", and Dainsleif attends her audience out of courtesy to that title. In this telling, the Heavenly Principles also demanded that every trace of Saarelainen be erased from the world through Irminsul. Only the Belyi Tsar, who fled into the Shadow Realm, kept any memory of him. Rhinedottir insisted she had told "just a story" and had not answered Anastasya's question about the Heavenly Principles' condition.

Aftermath: With King Irmin "indisposed", Knight Marshal Anfortas of the Schwanenritter proclaimed himself Regent and led the final kingdom council, the Regnum Concilium Ultimum. Survivors able to travel went up to Sumeru with the Schwanenritter and their Ruin Golems. On the surface, many refugees were struck by a disease that turned them into monsters, and some who had not yet fallen ill went back underground. The Schwanenritter fought the Abyss to the last knight.

Notes left in the Gavireh Lajavard ruins record the Regent's bulletin and a survivor's journal from a family that stayed behind. The Sumeru scholars later known as the Order of Skeptics honoured the Schwanenritter as "heroes of Dahri" and took up their fight. Of the last two knights, Hadura betrayed the order and Anfortas lost his left eye executing them. Anfortas's final fate is unknown.

The fall shaped the present. Chlothar Alberich later founded the Abyss Order, and the sibling, who travelled with Dainsleif after waking, eventually took it over. Pierro joined the Cryo Archon and co-founded the Fatui. Capitano, cursed with immortality, sought revenge on Ronova for the innocent. Pure-blooded survivors still endure the curse and its erosion.

Accounts: - Dainsleif (1.4 onward): a glorious human nation "uprooted and crushed, like a weed removed from the garden of the gods". He still warns the Traveler not to repeat "the failings of my forebears" by trying to overthrow the gods.
- The sibling: Dainsleif failed to prevent the destruction. The sibling now wages war on "destiny" until the Abyss engulfs the thrones.
- Chlothar (3.5): Khaenri'ah saw the Prince/Princess as the Abyss itself and hoped that by controlling the Abyss it could control everything.
- Pierro: the sages invited divine wrath by tearing away the veil of sin.
- Capitano (5.3): the people were punished for the Sinners' crimes, though most were innocent.
- Ei: a nation strode forward and lost everything to the Heavenly Principles.

- Rhinedottir (7.1), herself a Sinner and now Ruler of Life, presents the Heavenly Principles' attack as the breach of an ancient promise. Her account comes from Celestia's own records.
- Nefer, viewing Rerir's memories (6.1), sums up Khaenri'ah's story as small lies piling up until they destroy everything.

Hidden strife note: During the limited-time event Hidden Strife, an optional letter reveals that Kaeya secretly kept a page of Alberich Clan history. It says the clan, not being royal, stepped in as regents when the strength of "the one-eyed king Irmin" failed. It is the only description of Irmin's appearance: he had one eye.

Open questions: - Whether Irmin died in the coup or survived "indisposed".
- What happened to the sixth share of the Abyssal power.
- Why the gods tolerated Khaenri'ah for millennia and struck only then.
- Exactly what the king's "secret mechanisms" were, and whether they, Rhinedottir's creations or the Sinners' new power first loosed the monsters.
- How the sibling escaped Asmoday's seal while the Traveler slept for 500 years.
- When, or whether, the Heavenly Principles will wake. The sibling insists they will.

Connections: The fall of Khaenri'ah is the centre of the wider cataclysm (Durin's attack on Mondstadt, the Abyss in Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan and Nod-Krai). Its people and their descendants include Dainsleif, Kaeya, Pierro, Capitano and the Abyss Order. Several of the Five Sinners are still at large as of 7.1, and Rhinedottir now serves Celestia as the Ruler of Life.

According to notes found in Nod-Krai, the Belyi Tsar led Snezhnayan forces toward Khaenri'ah to stop an advancing dark host. After a week of fighting they were routed and his consciousness was destroyed. In 7.1 Snezhnaya brought down Ronova, the deity who cursed Khaenri'ah, with Dainsleif and Pierro among those who fought her.

121.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: Vinster King Irmin
121.content:
Irmin was the last Vinster King of Khaenri'ah's Eclipse Dynasty. He trusted Vedrfolnir and Hroptatyr above all, and over time became obsessed with Abyssal power. He approved technology built on "secrets from beyond the skies", purged the Crimson Moon bloodline, named the Traveler's sibling heir and "Savior", and made them a vessel for Abyssal power. He blinded Vedrfolnir for warning that Khaenri'ah would fall, which set off the palace coup.

When the cataclysm struck he was declared "indisposed" and Anfortas became Regent. Whether he died that night is unconfirmed; the glider text speaks of "regicide".

122.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: The storming of the palace
122.content: On the night Vedrfolnir was blinded and imprisoned, Dainsleif, then captain of the royal guard, the "Twilight Sword", led Hroptatyr, Rhinedottir, Surtalogi and Rerir into the palace to free him. It was meant as a rescue that would force the king to see reason. Instead the five took shares of the Abyssal power held in the sibling and became the Five Sinners, leaving Dainsleif betrayed. Monsters spread through the city the same night.

123.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: Regent Anfortas and the exodus
123.content: Knight Marshal Anfortas of the Schwanenritter became Regent when King Irmin was "indisposed". He led the evacuation of Khaenri'ahn survivors up into Sumeru, where the knights and their Ruin Golems fought the Abyss until none were left. Many refugees on the surface fell to a disease that turned them into monsters. Sumeru's scholars remembered the knights as the "heroes of Dahri".

124.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: The Third Descender's curse
124.content: Saarelainen, the Third Descender, gave his body to become the seven Gnoses on condition that the Heavenly Principles restore Anastasya and never harm his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. He secured the promise with a curse that would trigger if it was broken. When the Heavenly Principles destroyed Khaenri'ah, the curse took effect, and they have slept ever since (revealed in 7.1).

125.comment: Fall of Khaenri'ah: Purge of the Crimson Moon
125.content: Before the fall, Irmin ordered every descendant of the deposed Crimson Moon Dynasty eliminated as a threat to his line, from the direct bloodline down to distant offshoots, children included. Rerir carried out these orders as a secret agent while hiding that role from Tholindis, the woman he hoped to marry, who herself belonged to a diluted Crimson Moon branch. Some descendants survived; Arlecchino is one of the line's later heirs.

key: defeat of the Ruler of Death
126.content:
Fall of Ronova (also: death of Ronova, Ronova's defeat, defeat of the Ruler of Death, Black Feathers Scattered at Parting): The fall of Ronova is the climax of the Snezhnaya Archon Quest act "A Rekviem for the Underworld" (7.1). Ronova, the Shade who rules death, had been suppressing Snezhnaya's research with her Curse of Death. While the Tsaritsa held Rhinedottir in conversation and secretly slowed time around her with six Gnoses, Ronova's victims could not be revived in time; Celestia punished the violation by taking away Ronova's Authority of Death. The Traveler, Dainsleif and Pierro then defeated her. Mortally wounded, she fled and, dying, fused the Eitr with the Celestial Nail above the Cryo Dragon's corpse as a "parting gift". She is the first of the Four Shades shown dying.

Pierro landed the decisive blow with a new, untested Delusion called the "Eye of the Fatui", at a heavy cost to his soul and life force. The Curse of Death lifted with her Authority, freeing Project Mistilteinn, but the Curse of Immortality on the Khaenri'ahns remains. After her act, all of Teyvat's Celestial Nails began to cast strange pillars of light into the sky.

Established: - Ronova, the Ruler of Death, is one of the Four Shades created by the Heavenly Principles.
- In Snezhnaya she had imposed a Curse of Death: when someone conceived technology threatening the Heavenly Principles, they and those around them briefly died and forgot the idea.
- Those deaths broke the rules she served, so she relied on Rhinedottir, Ruler of Life, to revive the victims before Celestia's "monitoring cycle" noticed.
- The Tsaritsa broke that loophole; Celestia reclaimed Ronova's Authority, and she was defeated in battle.

- Earlier in Chapter VII (7.0), the curse caused unexplained memory loss among Armory Palace researchers working on Project Mistilteinn, including Mitya. A whole audience at the Korolevskiy Theater, the Traveler among them, was trapped in the afterlife until the Traveler and Mitya unmasked Ronova, who had disguised herself as Alyosha. Later she tried to take Paimon by force at the Armory Palace before Pierro stopped her.
- The Fatui treated a direct confrontation as inevitable and built a new Delusion for it, using Arlecchino as the base because she descends from the Crimson Moon, which once held the authority over death.
- Snezhnaya's victory, as Pierro puts it, came at the moment Celestia reclaimed her Authority; the battle afterward was the old feud of the Curse of Immortality playing out.

- After the battle, the Traveler concludes that the Curse of Immortality was a permanent curse laid under the Heavenly Principles' judgment, which even Ronova could not simply undo, while the Curse of Death was her own unauthorised initiative and ended when her power was taken away. Dainsleif and Pierro therefore remain immortal.
- Naberius judged the Tsaritsa's act beyond Celestia's power to judge as "rebellion" and below the threshold for a Nail of Retribution, though he wanted her punished for overstepping her authority. Rhinedottir declined.

The plan: The Tsaritsa had arranged to receive Rhinedottir at Zapolyarny Palace, offering news of Asmoday in exchange for information. On the same day Mitya was to move equipment from Rankova Zorya to Snezhnograd for a scheme to turn the Korolevskiy Theater into a laboratory, a project Ronova could not ignore. Pierro's instruction to the Traveler was simple: wait until Ronova appears and kills everyone, then keep her from leaving.

Pierro called in Dainsleif, who came partly for revenge on the Shade who cursed him and partly to speak with a past incarnation of Hroptatyr; Pierro asked him to set his own agenda aside and focus on Ronova. Pierro admitted to the Traveler that a plan existed whose full scope even he, as Director of the Fatui, did not know, because Ronova might be listening anywhere. Before the day, Sandrone and Arlecchino shared a tea party with the Traveler and Paimon; Sandrone spent the time fortifying positions and upgrading equipment. Ronova appeared earlier than expected and at Rankova Zorya rather than the theater; Mitya sent Vodyanitsa to fetch Valeriy and Vesna and had the Rokot evacuate the locals. Mitya's theater scheme rested on the Korolevskiy Theater's damaged Ley Lines, which briefly trap the souls of the dead there, and on his own soul bearing Ronova's mark, which lets him remember what happens while dead. Neither he nor anyone else could be sure it would work, and that was the point: Ronova could not be sure it would fail.

Battle of rankova zorya: Ronova struck Rankova Zorya and triggered the Curse of Death. The Traveler fought her (in gameplay, with Odette and Vesna as trial party members), was killed and escaped the afterlife first, drawing on Vesna's use of the Authority of Life and memories of every nation they had visited. Waking among the dead, the Traveler stalled Ronova with taunts: she was bound by more rules than she controlled, a tool of the Heavenly Principles, while Paimon was writing her own destiny. Ronova, angered, promised torment instead of death, and waited for Rhinedottir to revive the dead. The revival never came.

When Ronova tried to leave, Dainsleif snared her and Pierro arrived with the completed Eye of the Fatui. Ronova said no mortal body or mind could withstand such power. She cast the Curse of Death again; the Traveler raced back through the afterlife, combined all the elements into the power of the Light Realm and destroyed her escape portal. At that point Celestia reclaimed her Authority. Stripped of it, she declared she could now kill without consequence and fought on with the full power of a Shade.

In the final clash, Dainsleif carried an exhausted Pierro away from Ronova's attacks while he and the Traveler bought time. Pierro, recalling how she had looked on without pity or pleasure as she cursed the Khaenri'ahns, called down a vast elemental nail, its force amplified by Abyssal energy surging from the Delusion. The Traveler shielded the others with a Geo construct. When the dust cleared, only a closing portal remained in the crater. In the quest, Ronova's boss titles change from "Arbiter of the Heavenly Principles" to "Paralogism's Outcast" once her power is stripped.

The tsaritsas gambit: At the palace, the Tsaritsa offered her account of sighting Asmoday, persuaded Rhinedottir to stay and finish the tea, and kept her talking. Rhinedottir eventually noticed her drink had not cooled: the Tsaritsa had used the six Gnoses as nodes to slow time in the hall, so the window for reviving Ronova's victims passed unnoticed outside. Rhinedottir said Cryo amplified by the Gnoses could affect the bounds of Reason, slowing time though not stopping it.

Celestia's directive then ordered Rhinedottir to correct Ronova's mistake, and she revived the dead, as the Tsaritsa, who said she did not sacrifice pawns, had expected. Rhinedottir spared the Tsaritsa, saying Celestia was watching her and Naberius as possible accomplices, and spoke as "Gold" of Khaenri'ah in admiration of Snezhnaya. Naberius was displeased and expected Snezhnaya to escalate. The Tsaritsa credited her own insight from the past thousand years as well as the Gnoses, and said the trick would not work on Rhinedottir twice.

Parting gift: Ronova had secretly teleported away. In a final cutscene she emerges, dying, before the Nail of Retribution over the Cryo Dragon's corpse and fuses the Eitr with it as her "parting gift"; the Nail begins to crumble and she disintegrates.

The Eitr (Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment) is a forbidden creation of Hyperborea hidden in the Shadow Realm. The cutscene description says Ronova, feeling death for the first time, meant all of Teyvat to share that sensation as Holy Soil spread across the land. After the quest, pillars of light rise above Teyvat's Celestial Nails.

In her last words she reflects that she who controls death cannot know dying, and that she need no longer despise humans, gods and one unnamed third party. In the world quest series "The Anomaly" (7.1), the Traveler finds the Snezhnayan nail glowing and making sounds, with Alyosha keeping watch; Paimon wonders if this is Ronova's revenge. Elsewhere Albedo observes the Skyfrost Nail, Xiao watches the Chasm's nail on Rex Lapis's orders, Yae Miko senses a faint power she cannot place and means to bring Kokomi to look at it, Candace and Dehya's mercenaries keep watch in Sumeru, and Mavuika warns Natlan's people to stay alert.

Aftermath: Within days Rankova Zorya was being repaired, Armory Palace staff confirmed the restrictions on Project Mistilteinn were gone, and the Tsaritsa granted an audience commending everyone involved. Dainsleif attended out of respect for the "Mother of Khaenri'ah" and called the victory the start of a new era that would not be peaceful. Pierro was not seen; Dainsleif said the battle had taken an irrecoverable toll on his mind and soul.

Dainsleif also met the young Hroptatyr preserved from the notebook and found it disappointing, since that incarnation knew nothing of Khaenri'ah's dark side. He noted that Pierro seemed eager to discuss his work with him, possibly as a way to resist erosion.

Accounts: - Pierro: the real victory was the reclaiming of her Authority; the fight was a feud born from the Curse of Immortality. Unless she escaped undetected, he said, she had taken fatal, irreversible damage; either way he warned of retaliation.
- Rhinedottir: called Ronova capricious beneath a serious manner, and said anyone should be grateful not to have to face her.
- Dainsleif: five hundred years ago, Khaenri'ahns saw her as an untouchable god; Snezhnaya may count the victory absolute.
- Ronova: earlier, she said she could finish the Traveler only if Asmoday returned so the Four Shades acted jointly, if she found conclusive evidence for a conviction, or when the Heavenly Principles awaken.
- Vodyanitsa, after the battle, wondered aloud whether the Ruler of Death can die at all.

Open questions: - What the Eitr will do to the Celestial Nails and whether Holy Soil will spread.
- Who, if anyone, now holds the Authority of Death.

- The identity hidden in Ronova's last words.
- How Celestia, the remaining Shades and the dormant Heavenly Principles will respond to Snezhnaya.
- How lasting the cost to Pierro is.

Connections: See Ronova, the Four Shades, Rhinedottir, the Tsaritsa, Pierro, Dainsleif, Project Mistilteinn, Delusions, the Eitr, Celestial Nails and Holy Soil.

Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text): the battle was public in Rankova Zorya and the Tsaritsa held a commendation audience, so Snezhnayans may know the Ruler of Death was defeated. The time trick at the palace, the monitoring cycle and Rhinedottir's role are known only to the participants and the inner circle. Outside Snezhnaya, people see only strange lights over the Nails. Do not treat the Curse of Immortality as lifted, and do not resolve what the Eitr will do.

127.comment: Fall of Ronova: Eye of the Fatui
127.content: The Eye of the Fatui is the new Delusion completed for Pierro just in time for the battle with Ronova, developed with Arlecchino as the base for her Crimson Moon heritage. Untested in combat, it let him call down a vast elemental nail that mortally wounded Ronova, at the price of his soul and life force; Ronova said no mortal could withstand that power. Dainsleif said the toll on Pierro was irrecoverable.

128.comment: Fall of Ronova: Ronova's Curse of Death
128.content: Ronova's Curse of Death killed anyone in Snezhnaya who conceived technology threatening the Heavenly Principles, together with those near them, and erased the idea. Rhinedottir then revived them before Celestia's monitoring cycle could notice, a loophole around rules the killings broke. When the Tsaritsa delayed the revival in 7.1, the curse was exposed, Ronova lost her Authority and the curse ended with it.

129.comment: Fall of Ronova: Tsaritsa's time trick
129.content: During Rhinedottir's visit to Zapolyarny Palace, the Tsaritsa used her Cryo power, amplified by the six Gnoses as nodes of a field, to slow time inside the hall. Rhinedottir missed the agreed window to revive Ronova's victims, and Celestia's monitoring cycle flagged the deaths. Rhinedottir noted that the Tsaritsa had also uncovered the monitoring cycle itself.

130.comment: Fall of Ronova: The Anomaly (Celestial Nails)
130.content: After Ronova fused the Eitr with the nail over the Cryo Dragon's corpse east of Snezhnograd, Celestial Nails across Teyvat began to cast strange pillars of light into the sky. As of 7.1 their meaning is unknown; Liyue (Xiao reports to Rex Lapis), Inazuma's Yae Miko, Sumeru's desert folk and Natlan's Mavuika all treat the lights as a threat to watch.

131.content:
Future of Khaenri'ah (also: fate of Khaenri'ah, revival of Khaenri'ah, New Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ah's survivors, what became of Khaenri'ah, Khaenri'ah's legacy): Khaenri'ah, the godless underground kingdom, fell about five hundred years ago, and canon has never said cleanly what became of it. Its last king, Irmin, was reported "indisposed" and the Knight Marshal Anfortas took over as regent; neither man's end is stated. Most of its pure-blooded people are cursed to live on, and the Traveler's sibling says the Abyss Order is building a "New Khaenri'ah". As of 7.1, even a Khaenri'ahn alchemist like Rhinedottir says the old kingdom "no longer exists".

This entry gathers the open threads about the kingdom's future: the fate of its rulers, the survivors and their curses, and the competing hopes of reviving it. It does not resolve any of them.

Established: - Khaenri'ah fell in the Cataclysm five hundred years ago. The gods and the Heavenly Principles were behind its destruction, the wiki's summary of canon says, as punishment for using forbidden knowledge.
- A notice found in the underground Khaenri'ahn ruins (Gavireh Lajavard, Sumeru) says King Irmin was in an "indisposed state" and the Knight Marshal Anfortas proclaimed himself temporary Regent. That is the last word on the monarchy.
- In 7.1 Rhinedottir says it is a shame that Khaenri'ah no longer exists, and she and Dainsleif both call the Tsaritsa the "Mother of Khaenri'ah".

- **The throne.** Irmin is called the last Vinster King of the Eclipse Dynasty and is known to have had one eye. The Alberich family teaching that Kaeya kept (Hidden Strife, 2.8, a limited-time event) says the Alberich Clan, which had no royal blood, "stepped in as regents when the strength of the one-eyed king Irmin failed". Anfortas is not named in that text; the link to him is the wiki's deduction.
- **The regent.** Anfortas led the Schwanenritter. The knights evacuated the able upward into Sumeru with their Ruin Golems. After surfacing, the evacuees began to sicken with an affliction that turned them into monsters, and some chose to go back underground. A coded message in Ruin Guards near Dharma Forest says the Schwanenritters fought to the last one.
- **The survivors.** Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns were made immortal and eroded rather than dying; those with ancestry from other gods' lands became monsters, including hilichurls. The royal guards, the Black Serpent Knights, became husks or remained as changed Black Serpents.
- **The people.** In 7.1 Rhinedottir tells the Tsaritsa that all Khaenri'ahns descend from a bloodline begun with her and the Third Descender. The Tsaritsa says she was aware of this but has no memory of it.

- **A nation of unusual survivors.** Some of the five hundred year old Khaenri'ahns became Abyss Mages, Heralds and Lectors; the Abyss Order, founded by Chlothar Alberich, grew out of the kingdom's destruction.
- **The Order's aim.** The wiki's account of canon is that the Order seeks to destroy the nations under the Seven in revenge and to complete the Traveler's sibling's goal of reviving Khaenri'ah.
- **What was built.** In 5.7 the sibling says they have woven the entire Ley Line network of New Khaenri'ah into the Atlas of the New World, and that "the nation once known as Khaenri'ah can rise again". They add that they will one day find a suitable host location. The nation does not yet physically exist.

- **The real site.** Khaenri'ah lay deep underground in the region of Sumeru (Kaeya's words, and the wiki). Sumeru's older scholars know the kingdom as "Dahri" and revere the Schwanenritter as "heroes of Dahri" (via the Order of Skeptics).
- **Present-day echoes.** In 7.1 Dainsleif reports that Snezhnaya has a way to speak with a past incarnation of The Wise (Hroptatyr). He found it disappointing: the young Wise has not been exposed to Khaenri'ah's dark side. That past echo is the closest thing to a living Khaenri'ah that 7.1 shows.

Accounts: - **Rhinedottir (7.1):** says that Khaenri'ah "would have been proud" to have a mother like the Tsaritsa, but that it is a shame the kingdom no longer exists. She speaks as a descendant of Khaenri'ah and a "mother" herself.
- **Dainsleif:** hunts the Abyss Order and doubts Khaenri'ah can be revived so easily. He says he could never refuse "the Mother of Khaenri'ah" the courtesy of an audience. In 7.1 he calls Snezhnaya's victory over Ronova the start of a new era and adds that it will not be peaceful.
- **The Traveler's sibling (5.7):** the revival is driven partly by guilt and partly by something else; the Ley Lines for New Khaenri'ah are complete, and a host place will come later.
- **Haden (5.7):** first claimed the homeland had already been revived, then admitted this was false once Dainsleif pressed him: the Ley Lines were not finished at that moment. His claim is a lie, not a revelation.

- **The Order's rank and file:** Haden says the revived homeland would let comrades forget five hundred years of struggle and begin their lives anew. This is his promise, not a shown outcome.
- **The Tsaritsa (7.1):** says she has no memory of being their ancestor and has never known how to face them.

Open questions: - Is Irmin dead, and if so how? Is he the "indisposed" king of the bulletin, or did the reports hide something?
- What became of Anfortas after the last knights fell, and did the Alberich regency outlast him?
- Can Khaenri'ah be revived, and if so where, as what, and at what cost to the people already living there?
- Does the Curse of Immortality end, and what would that mean for the surviving pure-bloods?

- What will the surviving Khaenri'ahns want now that the Heavenly Principles are dormant and the Ruler of Death is gone?
- Rhinedottir says all Khaenri'ahns descend from the Tsaritsa and the Third Descender. What does that make the kingdom's "godless" claim, and does the Tsaritsa accept any duty to its people?

- The Order is described as seeking both a revived Khaenri'ah and vengeance on the nations under the Seven. Canon has not said how the sibling reconciles the two, or what a revived nation would do toward the surface nations.

Connections: This is the forward-looking companion to the fall: see the Fall of Khaenri'ah and the Cataclysm for what happened, the Curse of the Khaenri'ahns for what the survivors carry, and the Traveler's Sibling's goals for the revival plan. The Heavenly Principles' dormancy and the Tsaritsa's plan explain why Snezhnaya is suddenly relevant to the kingdom's descendants.

Characters most tied to the question are Dainsleif, Pierro (once Eftirvit), Rhinedottir, Kaeya (an Alberich, with Khaenri'ahn roots by his own account), the Traveler's sibling, and Chlothar Alberich, founder of the Abyss Order.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat every statement about Khaenri'ah's future as belief or hope. Do not state that Irmin died, that Anfortas lived or died, that Khaenri'ah has been revived, or where New Khaenri'ah will stand. Characters differ: Dainsleif is sceptical, the Order is determined, and Rhinedottir is wistful. Do not use unreleased story content.

132.content:
A weathered notice in the underground Khaenri'ahn ruins beneath Sumeru says that, given King Irmin's "indisposed state" and the unknown threats facing the Kingdom, Knight Marshal Anfortas proclaimed himself temporary Regent. It is the only in-world statement on the king's condition; his death, removal or survival is never stated.

The same ruin holds an unfinished letter urging the Knight Marshal to petition the king to preserve machines made to the older standard, trusting "human will" over otherworldly methods. The wiki reads it as addressed to Anfortas. Irmin is also called "one-eyed" in the Alberich family teaching from the 2.8 event.

133.content:
Knight Marshal of the Schwanenritter. When the Cataclysm struck and Irmin was "indisposed", he declared himself Regent and took charge of the Regnum Concilium Ultimum, the Final Kingdom Council. The knights then led survivors up to Sumeru. His own fate is not stated; he appears only in documents and a hidden coded message ("In the Name of Anfortas") saying the knights fought to the last.

The wiki treats him as an Alberich because the family teaching credits the clan with serving as regents, but that is a deduction, not stated canon. His connection to Chlothar Alberich, founder of the Abyss Order, is likewise not made explicit.

134.comment: Future of Khaenri'ah: Mother of Khaenri'ah
134.content:
In 7.1 Rhinedottir greets the Tsaritsa Anastasya with this title and says all Khaenri'ahns descend from a bloodline begun with her and the Third Descender. Anastasya says she was aware of it, although she has no memory of it, and has never known how to face them. Dainsleif later uses the same title when he says he could not refuse her an audience.

Rhinedottir recounts that the Belyi Tsar incited Anastasya, then only a herald of the court, to open a gate to the Abyss with the Third Descender, and that the Heavenly Principles erased her existence as punishment. The Third Descender traded his remains to bring her back, with a curse that would bite if the bargain were broken. Anastasya infers that the Cataclysm triggered that curse, but Rhinedottir declines to confirm it.

135.content:
The Traveler's sibling says the Loom of Fate has finished weaving the Ley Line network of a restored Khaenri'ah and that it is held in the Atlas of the New World. They plan to find a suitable host location for it one day, and say the nation once known as Khaenri'ah can rise again. Haden had earlier claimed the homeland was already revived and then admitted the Ley Lines were not yet complete.

Dainsleif calls the notion that a nation could be revived this way preposterous until he sees it himself. In the final cutscene the sibling folds the space where Khaenri'ah once stood into the Atlas. The scene also involves Direidyth, and what exactly the vanishing space represents is not explained.

136.comment: Future of Khaenri'ah: The Cursed Survivors
136.content: Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns live on under the Curse of Immortality, eroding rather than dying. Dainsleif, Pierro and Chlothar (as Eide) are the clearest cases, along with the cursed remnants such as the Black Serpent Knights. People of mixed ancestry became monsters. As of 7.1, no cursed Khaenri'ahn has been shown freed, even after Ronova lost her authority.

137.content:
Forbidden Knowledge (also: forbidden knowledge pollution): Forbidden knowledge is a kind of knowledge that does not belong to Teyvat. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata called it a "truth" no one in the world can understand, which came from the very bottom of the Abyss. The world keeps rejecting it, and that rejection causes disasters: madness, a scale-like illness (Eleazar), and decay of the land (the Withering). It mostly struck Sumeru. Nahida and the Traveler erased it from Irminsul in 3.2.

Canon records it in King Deshret's desert kingdom thousands of years ago, in the dragon Apep, and in Irminsul and Rukkhadevata herself during the Cataclysm 500 years ago. Nahida later said the Abyss takes whatever form is most devastating to each land: in Sumeru it was forbidden knowledge, in Natlan it was monsters.

In 7.1 the Traveler told the Fatui Harbingers that forbidden knowledge tainted by the Abyss should no longer exist anywhere in Teyvat. When the Harbingers unsealed the notebook of the Khaenri'ahn Sinner Hroptatyr, most of its pages had gone blank.

Established: - It is foreign to Teyvat and comes from the Abyss. Even the God of Wisdom could not understand it.
- People exposed to it hear "crazed whispers", go mad and grow dark grey scales. Land exposed to it loses its vigour.
- Gods and dragons can be polluted too: Apep and Rukkhadevata both were.

- Rukkhadevata warned that if it polluted Irminsul, all of Teyvat might fall apart.
- Its traces could be suppressed with divine power, contained, or altered into a more stable form, but it could not simply be destroyed. Rukkhadevata's own memory in Irminsul kept it alive after her death.
- Removing it from Irminsul (3.2) ended Eleazar within days and stopped the Withering from spreading.

- Its effects were kept from the public. Alhaitham, despite his time at the Akademiya, had never been told that it could drive people insane, and suspected the Akademiya had never understood it.
- Nahida told the Traveler that they have "an amazing resistance" to it (Homecoming, 3.6).

Nature: Canon describes it more by its effects than its content. The terms used for it include "knowledge that did not belong to this world" (Kasala), a "truth" that cannot be understood (Rukkhadevata), "the apocalypse" (Apep and the elemental Fungi of the Chasm), and, in King Deshret's weapon text, a "dark poison" and a "sin running deeper than the sky". Those who sought it wanted power to defeat or escape the order of the Heavenly Principles. It was not a written book of spells: it spread "like a plague", and through Irminsul it could pollute memories.

Nahida treats it as a regional manifestation of the Abyss. The Abyss "manifests its power in a manner that is most devastating to the place in question", she said; for Sumeru, a nation of wisdom, that meant knowledge. Item text pairs it with the tearing-down of the sky's barriers, and the Heavenly Principles answered it with Celestial Nails.

History: It first afflicted the desert of King Deshret thousands of years ago, then returned with the Cataclysm 500 years ago and polluted Irminsul.

- The desert: Deshret brought it into his kingdom. Rukkhadevata saved what she could and was shrunk to a child's form by the effort; Deshret sacrificed himself, letting Apep swallow him (own entries below).
- The Cataclysm: Rukkhadevata, not summoned to Khaenri'ah because she had to protect Irminsul, felt the pollution arrive with the disaster. She built the Akasha, which used people's dreams and wisdom together with her power, and cleared almost all of it from Irminsul, but she herself was already polluted and died.
- 3.2: Nahida, the purest branch of Irminsul Rukkhadevata chose as her next incarnation, used two Gnoses to reach her predecessor's consciousness and removed Rukkhadevata from Irminsul. Everyone forgot Rukkhadevata, except the Traveler.

- Before the desert: Apep says the dragons once believed only forbidden knowledge could give them the power to defeat the Heavenly Principles. Nibelung, the Dragon King, brought "the power of darkness from outside of this world" and led them in the war of funerary flame. After he died, Apep kept gathering it as the world neared collapse until a Celestial Nail fell and turned her forest into dunes (3.6).
- The Fungi of the Chasm: after Deshret's death the "apocalypse" passed into Apep, and elemental lifeforms born from her fled it. Rukkhadevata promised one of them she would erase it. Nahida kept the promise after 3.2 and healed Apep in Homecoming (3.6).
- Before 3.2: in Through the Predawn Night Alhaitham pieces together that the Withering, Eleazar and the sandstorms resemble the ancient desert pollution, and that Irminsul's illness may come from it.

- Rukkhadevata explained that she could not remove herself, since that was a paradox, so she left a trail of clues for her successor. Removing her meant she would never have existed. Nahida protested and then did it.
- The Akademiya's Divine Knowledge Capsules held knowledge taken from scholars who went mad connecting to Irminsul, which still carried Rukkhadevata's polluted consciousness (wiki, Akasha System). The Gnosis gave Nahida some protection when she entered that consciousness.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 forbidden knowledge is considered gone: erased from Irminsul in 3.2, so the Withering and Eleazar no longer spread. The Abyss itself remains active in other forms.

In Etched in Time (7.1), the Traveler argued that Hroptatyr's sealed notebook was no longer dangerous for this reason. Pierro agreed, and after the Harbingers voted to unseal it, he found most of its pages blank, "presumably forbidden knowledge that has been erased". What was left were Hroptatyr's personal thoughts and research notes from the Universitas Magistrorum.

Its after-effects outlive it. Those who suffered from Eleazar recovered, but the dead did not return. People's memories of Rukkhadevata were rewritten, and Apep is only now recovering.

Effects: - Eleazar: dark, hardened scales, numbness, nerve damage, immobility, coma, death. It was unique to Sumeru and had no cure until 3.2.
- The Withering: zones of decay in Sumeru's forests.
- Madness: "crazed whispers" in people's minds.

- Oozing Filth: dark sludge in the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue, where forbidden knowledge was altered by the power of the Spiritstone (a Celestial Nail) and stored in a more stable but still dangerous form.
- In Apep it amplified her hatred and rage until it was purged.

Eleazar was positively correlated with a person's elemental content, and the forest eased it. In Homecoming, the Withering is shown to be tied to the deaths of elemental lifeforms that escaped Apep's corrupted body; the creatures that stayed in the Chasm took monstrous forms to survive.

Accounts: - Kasala, a priest of King Deshret (recorded memories, 3.1): the Scarlet King brought it into the world. It spread like a plague; Rukkhadevata saved the survivors, and the king gave his life.
- Greater Lord Rukkhadevata (3.2): knowledge from the bottom of the Abyss, a "truth" no one can understand, that the world keeps rejecting.
- Nahida (3.2 onward): two pollutions, the desert and the Cataclysm. Later (5.x voice line) she calls it Sumeru's form of the Abyss.
- Apep (3.6): the dragons sought it to fight the "usurper". Nibelung brought it, and she kept collecting it until the nail fell. Deshret's corrupted knowledge became her "apocalypse", and she calls herself the "final fail-safe" in his plan.
- King Deshret (Staff of the Scarlet Sands text): the "dark poison" penetrated the earth and the spikes fell to heal the world; taking poison is a sin "running deeper than the sky", yet its whispers are sweet.
- Nabu Malikata (Amethyst Crown text): invaders from beyond the firmament brought war and "illusions that could break through shackles"; the master of the heavens, afraid of "the rising tide of delusion and breakthroughs", sent the nails. She warned Deshret not to inquire into the sky and the abyss, and he silently resolved to defy her.
- Pierro (7.1): Hroptatyr's notebook held material that would have driven him mad and could bring national disaster; he would not let Snezhnaya repeat Khaenri'ah's mistakes.

Open questions: - What it actually is: canon never shows its content, only its effects.
- How it reached Irminsul during the Cataclysm, and whether Khaenri'ah's "secrets from beyond the skies" or the Sinners' Abyssal power were the source.
- Exactly what Al-Ahmar obtained with the Goddess of Flowers' help.
- Whether everything Hroptatyr wrote has truly been erased, or only what Irminsul could reach.

Connections: Source: the Abyss. Opponent: the Heavenly Principles and its Celestial Nails. Medium: Irminsul, which records knowledge and memory. Victims: King Deshret's civilisation, Apep, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Sumeru's Eleazar patients. Ended by: Nahida and the Traveler. Related phenomena with their own entries: the Withering, Eleazar, Abyssal corruption, the Akasha, the war of funerary flame, the Cataclysm.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): keep its content unknowable. Never write out what forbidden knowledge "says"; show its weight instead: whispers that half make sense, a scholar who will not stop writing, scales spreading on skin, colour draining from leaves. Present-day (7.1) Sumerians may know Eleazar is gone and the Withering has stopped, but most do not know why, and no one remembers Rukkhadevata.

Scenes set before 3.2 can include Eleazar patients, Withering zones and Akademiya secrecy. Scenes after 3.2 should not have new cases. Desert people of Aaru Village can carry Kasala's story of the king's sacrifice; Alhaitham, Nahida and the Traveler know the full account. Only the Traveler remembers that Rukkhadevata existed.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): - It is not ordinary "banned research" or Akademiya censorship: it is Abyssal corruption that harms whoever holds it.
- Do not have it still spreading in Sumeru after 3.2, or have anyone except the Traveler remember Rukkhadevata.
- Do not present the Khaenri'ah connection as confirmed; canon only implies it.
- "The apocalypse" in Homecoming means this corruption inside Apep, not the end of the world.

138.comment: Forbidden Knowledge: King Deshret's forbidden knowledge
138.content:
Thousands of years ago King Deshret (Al-Ahmar) brought forbidden knowledge into his desert kingdom while trying to defy the Heavenly Principles. It spread like a plague: crazed whispers, dark grey scales, dying land. His old friend Greater Lord Rukkhadevata had the priests build temples and filled them with the divine power of life. This slowed the disaster, but exhausted her until her form became a small child's. The survivors' descendants live in Aaru Village. The king finally sacrificed himself. The priest Kasala's recorded memory of this, shown in Secret of the Scorching Desert (3.1), told the desert people that the two gods had been allies, not enemies.

By agreement, Apep swallowed Deshret after his death to gain all his knowledge. She gained "the apocalypse" instead, and believes he used her as a fail-safe.

139.content: In Nahida's Story Quest Homecoming (3.6), Apep tells how she was polluted. The dragons once believed only forbidden knowledge could defeat the Heavenly Principles; after Nibelung's death she kept collecting it until a Celestial Nail stopped her. Swallowing King Deshret gave her his corrupted knowledge, "the apocalypse", which magnified her hatred. Elemental lifeforms born from her fled; their deaths are tied to the Withering. In the Chasm, the Spiritstone's power had turned the apocalypse into Oozing Filth, more stable but still dangerous. Nahida and the Traveler healed Apep. She grew calmer but still despises humanity.

140.comment: Forbidden Knowledge: Rukkhadevata and Irminsul's pollution
140.content: When the Cataclysm struck 500 years ago, forbidden knowledge polluted Irminsul. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata stayed behind to protect the tree and built the Akasha to clear it using the wisdom in people's dreams together with her own power. Almost all of it was removed, but she was polluted herself; even dead, her memory in Irminsul kept the corruption alive, causing the Withering and Eleazar. She chose the purest branch of Irminsul as her next incarnation, Nahida, and left her clues. In Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies (3.2), Nahida and the Traveler used two Gnoses to reach her and removed her from Irminsul. Everyone except the Traveler forgot her, and the disease and decay ended.

141.content: Before he abandoned his humanity, the Khaenri'ahn Sinner Hroptatyr ("The Wise") gave his fellow student and rival Eftirvit (both studied under Professor Mimameith), later Pierro, a notebook. When Pierro eventually read it, he realised its contents would drive him mad and could bring disaster on a national scale. With the Tsaritsa's approval the Harbingers sealed it deep in the Armory Palace archives, to be opened only by a unanimous vote of all active Harbingers. In Etched in Time (7.1), the Traveler explained that forbidden knowledge had been erased from Irminsul. The Harbingers voted to unseal it, and most pages were blank. What survived included Hroptatyr's notes on extracting the Crimson Moon's authority over Death, a discovery he first named the "blessing of immortality" and then renamed the "Curse of Immortality".

142.comment: Forbidden Knowledge: Secrets from beyond the skies
142.content: An unsigned, unfinished letter in the Khaenri'ahn ruins under Gavireh Lajavard (3.6), addressed to a Marshal, says the "four pillars" of the kingdom prospered by "spying upon secrets from beyond the skies". That knowledge let their machines throw off the shackles of this world's laws. Worried that the technology was imperfect, the writer asks the Marshal to petition the King to preserve some machinery built to the old standard. The wiki links this to forbidden knowledge, but canon does not confirm the link.

key: Plains of the Returning and Departing
143.content:
Guili Assembly (also: Guili, Plains of the Returning and Departing, Guizhong-Zhongli Assembly): The Guili Assembly was an ancient Liyue civilisation founded and ruled jointly by the God of Dust, Guizhong, and the God of Geo, Morax (later Rex Lapis, today the mortal consultant Zhongli), with the god Marchosius and the adepti at their side. Its heart was Guili Plains north of Mt. Tianheng, a land of farms and fields. About 3,700 years ago a battle of the Archon War killed Guizhong and a flood destroyed the Assembly; Morax led the survivors south and founded Liyue Harbor.

Its name joins one character each from Guizhong's name and from the name Morax then used. Today it survives as ruins, stone tablets and the memories of the long-lived.

Established: When Morax first descended, according to the tablets, he lowered the tides, raised Mt. Tianheng and calmed the seas, and the people mined jade from the mountain and built a settlement. Guizhong, called the Lord of Dust, became his ally. She and the adepti, Cloud Retainer among them, raised the Guizhong Ballista, an automatic crossbow guarding the land around Mt. Tianheng, and she brought her people north of the mountain, where they learned to farm. The fields and farming towns spread so far that one could reputedly walk to the Stone Gate along the paths between them. She named the land the Plains of the Returning and Departing (Guili Plains): her people had left their old home and, content here, had in a sense returned home. The tablets say the Lord of Rock praised her work. Marchosius, God of the Stove, is named as a third ruler and supporter in Madame Ping's retelling.

The Assembly's rulers had complementary strengths. Guizhong is described as kind and wise but not especially powerful, and her own words in the Memory of Dust text say she meant to use technique and wisdom where she lacked strength, "your brawn and my brains". She is credited with four commandments: unite in ambition, let wisdom nourish like water, fortify the bones so movement stays supple, and let virtue grow tall like a tree. Her interest in machines went beyond the Ballista: she is said to have collected ancient Ruin Machines for study and to have made the Realm of Clouds in Luhua Pool. Guizhong, Morax and Cloud Retainer are said to have shared meals at Cloud Retainer's abode on Mt. Aocang. These details come from quest text as summarised by the wiki.

The Ballista's design was Guizhong's, under the name "Obscuro Vulpes Mechanism". The wiki reports from the Archon Quest that Rex Lapis judged it better than Cloud Retainer's own creation, that the two differed on ideals, and that after Guizhong died Cloud Retainer added finishing touches in her memory. A maintenance notice at the Ballista still asks that spare parts be kept for a future war and a worthy craftsman. The Memory of Dust, a stone dumbbell puzzle Guizhong gave Morax at their first meeting among Glaze Lilies, is the personal token of this alliance, even though its text insists no formal contract bound them.

Fall: When the gods of Teyvat fought for dominance, the adepti defended Guili Plains but could not stop the tide of war, which ravaged the plains and killed Guizhong. A great flood followed that swept through the area, including Dihua Marsh. The people were scattered; Morax took them south of Mt. Tianheng, and with Marchosius and the adepti they travelled for ten days or more through a storm. They settled at what became Liyue Harbor, about 3,700 years ago. The plains were left a wilderness; a viewpoint description calls the place a once-thriving city where a certain flower bloomed in abundance, an earthly paradise consumed by war.

The Memory of Dust text gives the human side of the end: Guizhong's form dissolved into dust among the Glaze Lilies, and she asked Morax to forget the stone dumbbell. Morax never managed to open it, and the wild lilies later dwindled until none remained. The wiki also notes that after her death yakshas can be seen containing leftover energy she expelled. A Moonlight Merriment event quest (limited-time) has Madame Ping tell how Marchosius, the God of the Stove, who loved humanity, went into homes as small helpers and stayed with the people during the flight south; this is a legend told within an event and is not common knowledge.

Legacy: The Assembly is the direct predecessor of Liyue Harbor, founded by the same survivors and the same god. Guili Plains still holds ruins, stone tablets and jade plates, and the Guizhong Ballista still stands at Mt. Tianheng. The tablets record that, after Rex Lapis pacified the warring gods, merchants and craftsmen formed the Qixing and the Millelith guarded the land. Zhongli, in the present, is a living memory of this era.

Because few remain who lived through it, the Assembly reaches modern Liyue mostly through texts, machines and the Memory of Dust. Guizhong has no known worship today.

Open questions: The sources reviewed leave unanswered who killed Guizhong and how, what Morax was called at the time, why Guizhong moved to Morax's settlement, and how large the Assembly really was. Treat them as open; do not supply an invented villain or battle.

key: Plains of the Returning and Departing
144.content: Guili Plains, in the Qiongji Estuary area of Liyue, was the central region of the Guili Assembly. Today it is wild country with ruins, hilichurls and treasure hoarders, stone tablets and jade plates bearing writing, and a viewpoint called the Ruins of Guili. The name means Plains of the Returning and Departing.

145.content: Guizhong, divine name Haagentus, was the God of Dust and co-ruler of the Guili Assembly. She appeared as a young woman with long billowing sleeves, was a mechanist who taught her people farming and built the Guizhong Ballista, and died in the Archon War.

146.content: Marchosius, the God of the Stove, is named as an ally who supported the Assembly and, in a Moonlight Merriment event telling by Madame Ping, as a god devoted to the people who stayed with them during the flight to Liyue Harbor. His story is told in an event and is not common knowledge.

147.content:
Slumber of the Heavenly Principles (also: Heavenly Principles' slumber, Heavenly Principles are dormant, dormancy of the Heavenly Principles, Heavenly Principles asleep, Saarelainen's curse): The Heavenly Principles, the ruler of Celestia and First Descender, have been dormant since the Cataclysm in Khaenri'ah about 500 years ago. The best-supported explanation is a curse laid by the Third Descender, Saarelainen, which triggered when they harmed his descendants the Khaenri'ahns. Their rules and Celestia's machinery still operate, and nobody in canon knows whether they will wake.

Powers across Teyvat have used the silence: the Fatui and the Abyss Order both plot against Celestia, and the Shades act cautiously "within the rules" rather than freely. The cause is not fully confirmed in-game: the 7.1 account is partly an inference voiced by Anastasya.

Established: - About 500 years ago, during the Cataclysm in Khaenri'ah, the Heavenly Principles became involved, sending the Seven (except the Dendro Archon) and the Four Shades. Ronova cursed pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns with immortality, which the Traveler in 7.1 reads as done under the Heavenly Principles' judgment.
- Since then they have lain dormant, and no quest shows them acting directly.

- Earlier, the Heavenly Principles consolidated their rule after the War of Funerary Flame by sacrificing the Third Descender, Saarelainen, whose body became the seven Gnoses and whose existence was erased from memory.
- According to the wiki's account, Saarelainen bargained for protection of his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns, and cast a curse to guard the deal: should the Heavenly Principles harm them, they would fall into slumber.
- In 7.1 Anastasya concludes that the Cataclysm triggered that curse, which is why the Heavenly Principles are asleep. Several events since (the Hydro throne's destruction, the burning of Irminsul) have not roused them.

- The dormancy is not total inactivity. Ronova says that during the slumber Celestia only monitors the Shades' actions periodically, and in 7.1 a resurrection that came too late was detected and her Authority of Death was reclaimed. The Celestial Nails remain in place; after the dying Ronova fused the Eitr with Snezhnaya's Nail of Retribution, the other Nails glitched and emitted pillars of light.
- In the teaser The Gods' Limits, Ronova suggested to the other Shades that, given the Heavenly Principles' prolonged inactivity, they should intervene against the Tsaritsa and the Fatui within the extent the "rules" permit.

- Because the Heavenly Principles built and wield the laws of Teyvat (including fate anchored in Irminsul), their absence from direct decisions leaves a gap that human and divine schemes alike target, from the Tsaritsa's campaign to Abyss Order plots.
- Rhinedottir and Ronova colluded to revive victims of the Curse of Death between monitoring periods, which shows that the rules are enforced mechanically even when their author sleeps.

Accounts: - Wiki summary of the 7.1 quest Black Feathers Scattered at Parting: the Cataclysm intervention triggered Saarelainen's curse, so the Heavenly Principles sleep.
- In that quest Anastasya, the Tsaritsa, infers the link after hearing Rhinedottir's account ("That's why the Heavenly Principles are asleep"); Rhinedottir answers that it was "just a story" and that she was not answering any question.

- Ronova, in 7.1, says that failing other means she can simply bide her time until the Heavenly Principles awaken, so the Shades themselves expect the slumber to end. Anastasya asked Rhinedottir directly when they will awaken and was refused an answer.
- Anastasya tells the Traveler that the gods' love for humanity is the result of a curse by the Heavenly Principles, part of the rules they impose on the world, an example of how characters frame those rules.

- In a memory shown in Light and Shadow, Intertwined, Naberius says the Shades "must face the reality that the Heavenly Principles slumbers" and must eliminate risks within the established rules, which presents the slumber as a constraint on the Shades as well as an opening for their enemies.

Open questions: - Will the Heavenly Principles wake, and what would break the curse?
- What exactly did Saarelainen promise, and what is in his sealed legacy (see the Third Descender's seal)?
- Which functions of Celestia run without its ruler?

- Is the sleep a punishment, a safeguard, or a side effect of the curse? Canon does not say.
- Whether the Tsaritsa's plan assumes the Heavenly Principles stay asleep or wake is unrevealed. Do not resolve these questions in narration.

Connections: The slumber links the Cataclysm and the fall of Khaenri'ah, the origin of the Gnoses, the Tsaritsa's campaign against the Heavenly Principles, the dealings of the Four Shades, and the Traveler's sibling's long-term goal.

148.comment: Slumber of the Heavenly Principles: Heavenly Principles' slumber
148.content:
After the Cataclysm about 500 years ago the Heavenly Principles stopped acting directly. The wiki attributes this to Saarelainen's curse, triggered when they harmed Khaenri'ah. Anastasya only infers the link in 7.1 and Rhinedottir does not confirm it. The Shades call this period a slumber, during which Celestia only monitors them periodically. Celestia's rules and monitoring still run, so characters speak of the slumber as real but incompletely understood. Never show the Heavenly Principles waking unless a scene is explicitly non-canon.

Ronova expects the Heavenly Principles to awaken eventually, and Anastasya wants to know when. Factions such as the Fatui and the Abyss Order act on the assumption that now is their chance.

149.comment: Slumber of the Heavenly Principles: Saarelainen's curse
149.content: Per Rhinedottir in 7.1, Saarelainen laid a curse on the Heavenly Principles when he bargained his body for Anastasya's resurrection and a promise never to harm his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns; it would take effect only if the promise was broken. The wiki says its effect is slumber, and Anastasya infers the Cataclysm triggered it. Its precise terms are not given in canon as of 7.1.

key: pillars of light over the Celestial Nails
150.content:
Holy Soil Crisis (also: Ronova's parting gift, Nail of Retribution anomaly, pillars of light over the Celestial Nails, Holy Soil threat): At the end of the Chapter VII, Act IV Archon Quest (7.1), the dying Ronova fused the Eitr with the Nail of Retribution above the Cryo Dragon's corpse in Snezhnaya as a "parting gift". The Nail began to crumble, threatening to unleash Holy Soil upon all of Teyvat, and every other Celestial Nail began to shine with a strange pillar of light. As of 7.1 nobody knows what comes next.

Characters in Snezhnaya, Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru and Natlan are watching their own Nails. Fontaine has none, and so no mark of its own.

Established: - Ronova, mortally wounded after her Authority of Death was taken from her, went to Snezhnaya's Celestial Nail, east of Snezhnograd, above the corpse of the Cryo Dragon Sovereign.
- She fused the Eitr with the Nail. It began to crumble.
- Afterwards the Celestial Nails across Teyvat each emit a strange pillar of light.

- **The Eitr.** Its full name is Embryonic-Ichoric-Telluric-Rudiment. It is a forbidden Hyperborean creation holding Light Realm power, once used to alter organisms. The Belyi Tsar found it in the Shadow Realm; later it was studied at the Hvergelmir institute.
- **The Nail.** The wiki describes Celestial Nails as seemingly indestructible (the Skyfrost Nail had splintered into shards and the Spiritstone shed a fragment, but neither crumbled away). Ronova's act is the first time one is shown crumbling apart. In the cutscene Ronova herself begins to disintegrate as she does it.
- **What was threatened.** The wiki's summary of the scene says the crumbling Nail threatens to unleash Holy Soil upon all of Teyvat, and its description of the cutscene says Ronova intended Teyvat to share the feeling of death. That intent is the narration's, not a statement made aloud by the character.
- **The world reacts.** The world quest series "The Anomaly" opens after the Archon Quest. It has one quest per region with a Nail: Snezhnaya, Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru and Natlan. In each, a known character is found watching the Nail.

- **Snezhnaya.** The Nail east of Snezhnograd glows and, as Paimon notes, sometimes makes a sound. Alyosha, out hunting nearby, may have been one of the first witnesses. He reported it to the local Druzhna, so the Tsaritsa and Fatui should know. He says it does not seem harmful so far and hopes the military's keenest minds can get to the bottom of it.
- **Mondstadt.** Albedo observes the Skyfrost Nail on Dragonspine, which has changed in the same way. He always assumed it had finished its work after destroying Sal Vindagnyr, and is now studying how the change affects the local ecosystem.
- **Liyue.** Xiao keeps watch at The Chasm on Rex Lapis's orders so he can report any new change at once. Extra Millelith patrols are posted and Cloud Retainer and other adepti have begun investigating.
- **Inazuma.** Yae Miko came to Tsurumi Island after a report. A fortune slip she drew read "Great Misfortune". She can faintly sense a power of some sort and means to bring Kokomi when she gets the chance, since Kokomi may be more familiar with it.
- **Sumeru.** Candace and Dehya camp near the desert Nail. Dehya's mercenaries have partly come to sightsee. Candace says the Desertfolk should not leave the Dendro Archon to carry the burden alone.
- **Natlan.** Mavuika watches the pillar near the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and calls its position precarious; Paimon points out that Natlan's Nail is right near where everyone lives. Mavuika resolves to tell the local population to watch for signs of danger.

- **Visibility.** The wiki notes that some of the marks can be seen from neighbouring regions (Snezhnaya's from Fontaine, Liyue's from Mondstadt City and Sumeru City), and that Fontaine, apparently never struck by a Nail, has no mark of its own. These are observations of the world map, not stated in dialogue.
- **Old Nails.** The wiki lists Nails or their traces at Dragonspine, The Chasm, Tsurumi Island, Mt. Damavand/Eternal Oasis, the Night Kingdom/Stadium in Natlan, and Hyperborea. Several have withered Irminsul trees nearby.

Holy soil: Holy Soil is soil rich in primordial elemental power from the three realms. Dragons can thrive in it, but it is unsuitable for human life. The process of land turning into Holy Soil is the Holy Soil phenomenon. Canon gives three older accounts.

- **Hyperborea (Snezhnaya).** According to Aksinya, the Hyperboreans tried to create the Primordial Human from the dead Cryo Dragon Sovereign. The experiment went out of control, and the Sovereign's unchecked authority turned the whole of Snezhnaya into Holy Soil of primordial ice, even changing the Ley Lines into crystal veins. The Heavenly Principles then sent a Nail crashing down. By the time the Belyi Tsar awoke a thousand years later, Hyperborea had sunk into the Shadow Realm. The corpse and the Nail remained above ground.
- **Natlan.** Per the dragon "One Who Speaks Coldly" (identified by the wiki as Kukulkan) in the Natlan Archon Quest, the Heavenly Principles regarded Natlan's phlogiston-rich soils as a form of the Holy Soil phenomenon and cast "sky-nails" down to destroy the land. Countless Dragonborn could survive only by devolving, becoming the saurians.
- **Watatsumi Island (Inazuma).** The island's soil is bleaching and losing nutrients. Local folklore blames the island's spirit being drawn toward the depths of Enkanomiya. The shrine maiden Tsuyuko, who studied at the Sumeru Akademiya, thinks seawater leaches nutrients instead (world quest series "The Moon-Bathed Deep", 2.1).
