In all three cases the pattern is the same: overflowing primordial power, a land unfit for people, and the Heavenly Principles answering with a Nail. That is why the Eitr's sabotage of a Nail alarms those who know this history; the old defence against Holy Soil is the thing now breaking. This reading is the entry's connection, not a statement made by a character.

Accounts: - **Paimon and the Traveler:** suspect the whole situation may be Ronova's revenge, and say they are not in a mood to celebrate.
- **Alyosha:** the Nail started behaving strangely only after the Ruler of Death fell; however it is read, it cannot be good.
- **Mavuika:** whatever happens, the Traveler's party will not be to blame. She says Ronova and the Heavenly Principles have long used Natlan as a tool against the Abyss and the world's destruction, and most of Natlan's past disasters came from them.

- **Albedo:** says the Skyfrost Nail was thought to have finished its task, and calls this change something he has never witnessed on Dragonspine.
- **Yae Miko:** unsure what trick the Heavenly Principles might be playing; senses a power.
- **Xiao:** says Rex Lapis himself is taking the phenomenon very seriously.
- **Ronova's own view:** the narration of the final scene gives only her last words about the unfamiliar sensation of death and the idea of a "parting gift".

Open questions: Whether Holy Soil is spreading, what the pillars of light mean, and whether the Heavenly Principles will answer are all unresolved as of 7.1.

Other open points: how the Eitr breaks a Nail, whether the Nails will fail one after another, and what the Tsaritsa and the Fatui will do. Canon shows only concern and watching.

Connections: Ronova's defeat is told in lore.fall-of-ronova, the Tsaritsa's wider confrontation with the Heavenly Principles in lore.tsaritsas-plan, and Project Mistilteinn, freed by Ronova's fall, in lore.project-mistilteinn. The Nails are described in the Celestial Nail entry, the Eitr in its own entry, and the old Holy Soil in the Holy Soil entry.

Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text): outside Snezhnaya most people know only that the Nails glow. Do not state that Holy Soil has begun to spread, that the Heavenly Principles have awakened, or that Mistilteinn has been used against them; none of that is shown by 7.1.

151.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: Eitr and the Broken Nail
151.content:
The Eitr is a Hyperborean product holding Light Realm power. The Belyi Tsar found it in the Shadow Realm on his 446th expedition. Ronova, dying, fused it with the Nail above the Cryo Dragon's corpse east of Snezhnograd, and the Nail began to crumble. Other Nails then began to shine.

Researchers Koshchei and Pavlina at the Hvergelmir institute experimented with it; it turned a snegovik named Donskoy into a snow giant, and fed into the decision to make the Wildwood Leshy. None of this explains its effect on a Nail.

152.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: The Anomaly (Nail Pillars of Light)
152.content:
After the Archon Quest, the Celestial Nails in Snezhnaya, Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru and Natlan each emit a strange pillar of light. Locals and notable figures watch them: Alyosha, Albedo, Xiao, Yae Miko, Candace and Dehya, and Mavuika. No harm is shown as of 7.1.

In the world quests, Albedo is struck that the Skyfrost Nail was not simply finished after Sal Vindagnyr's end, Yae Miko's fortune slip reads "Great Misfortune", and Xiao says Rex Lapis is taking it very seriously. Mavuika calls Natlan's Nail precariously placed, and Paimon notes it is near where people live.

153.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: Hyperborea's Holy Soil
153.content:
Aksinya says the out-of-control attempt to make a Primordial Human from the Cryo Dragon Sovereign's corpse turned all of Snezhnaya into Holy Soil of primordial ice, crystallising even the Ley Lines, until the Heavenly Principles sent their Nail crashing down; Hyperborea later sank into the Shadow Realm. A thousand years later the Belyi Tsar awoke from the dragon's remains.

The Nail and the corpse stayed above ground. They are the same Nail and the same corpse that Ronova chose for her last act.

154.comment: Holy Soil Crisis: Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri and the Holy Soil
154.content: During the limited-time event Three Realms Gateway Offering (2.5), Sangonomiya Shrine's answer to Watatsumi's Holy Soil phenomenon is shown: every few centuries someone retrieves a Bloodbranch Coral from Enkanomiya for the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. When Kokomi performed the rite in that event it only halted the bleaching instead of reversing it, which had never happened before; the cause was traced to the Void Realm's intrusion into Enkanomiya.

155.content:
Istaroth's Intentions (also: Istaroth's motives, Ruler of Time's interference, Istaroth meddling, Istaroth's plans): Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, is the Shade that few remember, and she has repeatedly nudged history: the Nameless Bard, Zibai's soul, Enkanomiya's sun, Makoto's tree, and the meeting that made the Traveler's sibling leave Khaenri'ah. Canon never tells us what she is trying to achieve. The only reason she gives on screen is that she needs to pass the time.

Her interventions help individuals and sometimes work around the Heavenly Principles' wishes, yet she also warns people not to defy them. She is not shown as an opponent of Celestia or as a loyal servant. Treat her goals as unknown.

The pattern is that she acts quietly and often after a disaster, in ways others only notice later, leaving the people she touched to carry the consequences.

Established: - In the teaser The Gods' Limits (2025-07-09), Ronova asks why Istaroth bestowed history upon "them". Istaroth answers that she had to find some way to pass the time.
- In A Space and Time Without You (5.7), the Traveler's sibling concludes that Istaroth made possible the meeting between the Traveler and the Khaenri'ahn girl Direidyth, which led the sibling to abandon Khaenri'ah to seek the Traveler. The sibling asks whether she is mocking them.

- Zibai: Istaroth gave her a Moon Wheel, making her a Moon Envoy, and warned her that blocking the Celestial Nail at Lang-Gan would cost her life. Zibai chose to protect her people anyway. Istaroth then held her at the moment of death and placed the fragments of her soul in her three selves, Ziju, Zizhi and Zijiao.
- Enkanomiya: after the island sank and its prayers went unanswered by the other Shades, Istaroth alone answered and gave Aberaku the knowledge for the artificial sun later called the Dainichi Mikoshi. She became Tokoyo Ookami there.
- Mondstadt: according to the wiki, the Nameless Bard played a melody that belonged to her at Decarabian's fall, and she preserved his lost name, Venti, when Barbatos ascended.
- Inazuma: Ei suspects that Makoto's plan to plant the Sacred Sakura through time involved a higher power; the wiki identifies it as Istaroth.
- Sumeru: in the scene where Nahida burns Irminsul (6.6), Istaroth appears with Ronova and Naberius and questions Nahida before they vanish.

- Hyperborea honoured her at winter solstice, and her worship survives in Mondstadt only in phrases about the "winds of time". The wiki says the Khaenri'ahn girl Direidyth was caught in a superimposition of Khaenri'ah over Natlan that Istaroth created.
- Wiki readings of artifact texts hold that she drew nostalgic delusions toward King Deshret after the death of Nabu Malikata; this is an interpretation, not a statement.
- In 7.1, Naberius says the idea that Asmoday has a new master was probably something Istaroth thought of on a whim, and that she barely considered it.

- The wiki says she once taught the Frost Moon goddess Canon the meaning of "hope", telling her that only humans can claim it and that where life exists, hope remains. This comes from a wiki summary I could not trace to a transcript, so treat it as medium confidence.
- Mondstadt's sundial inscriptions about stories carried by wind and grown by time are read by the wiki as her legacy. They are not an explicit statement of intent.

Accounts: - **Istaroth herself**: gives boredom as her reason (teaser). She advises Ronova that hunting for Asmoday would do more harm than good, and tells her Pierro is watching.
- **The Traveler's sibling** (5.7): treats her as the architect of the meeting with Direidyth and asks if she is mocking them.
- **Ei** (wiki summary): believes Makoto's plan relied on Istaroth.
- **Wiki** (Profile): says she considers every life equal in value and importance, and that it is unclear whether she acts out of favour for mortals or boredom.

- **Naberius** (7.1): dismisses her ideas as whims.
- **Enkanomiya's account** (wiki): she was the only Shade who answered when the Heavenly Principles did not.
- **Zibai's story** (wiki): Istaroth warned her, then froze the moment of her death; the sequence is the clearest case of advice followed by mercy.

Open questions: - What does Istaroth want, if anything beyond passing time?
- Why did she help bring about the sibling's decision to abandon Khaenri'ah?

- Does she act for mortals, for her own amusement, or for a plan across thousands of years?
- Do the Heavenly Principles know of her interventions, and would they punish them?
- Does her view of Asmoday's absence reflect knowledge she has not shared?

- Why has her worship been forgotten almost everywhere, and did she allow it?

Connections: Her interventions touch the Traveler's sibling's goals (lore.travelers-sibling-goals), Asmoday's possible change of side (lore.asmodays-defection), the Cataclysm, and the dormancy of the Heavenly Principles. Her own profile is npc.istaroth.

156.content: Istaroth has helped the Nameless Bard, Zibai, Aberaku, Makoto and the Traveler's sibling in ways that look unrelated. Her only on-screen explanation is that she must find a way to pass the time. Whether she cares for mortals, enjoys watching, or serves a plan is unknown. Do not give her a motive.

157.comment: Istaroth's Intentions: Direidyth and the Key
157.content: Direidyth was a Khaenri'ahn girl from the time of the Cataclysm who believed in the Savior. According to the wiki, she became caught in a superimposition of Khaenri'ah over Natlan created through Istaroth when the sibling activated the Loom of Fate. She met the Traveler there, and her account to the sibling in her own time led the sibling to leave Khaenri'ah to find the Traveler. In A Space and Time Without You, the sibling says Istaroth must have had a hand in it and asks whether she is mocking them. No reason is given.

158.content: Istaroth gave Zibai a Moon Wheel and later warned her that blocking the Celestial Nail over Lang-Gan would defy the Heavenly Principles and cost her life. Zibai blocked it so that her people could flee. Istaroth then froze her at the moment of death and sealed her soul in Ziju, Zizhi and Zijiao. The reason for the rescue is not given.

159.comment: Istaroth's Intentions: Sacred Sakura Higher Power
159.content: Ei believes Makoto's plan to plant the Sacred Sakura through time could not have worked without a higher power, which the wiki identifies as Istaroth. Whether Makoto knew, and what Istaroth gained, is unstated.

160.content:
King Deshret's Civilization (also: King Deshret's kingdom, Deshret's kingdom, Kingdom of King Deshret, Deshret's civilisation, Akhtamun): King Deshret's civilization was the desert kingdom of ancient Sumeru, ruled by the god-king Deshret, Lord of Deserts, alongside two companion gods: Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, the earlier Dendro Archon. After Nabu Malikata's death Deshret ruled the desert alone and pursued a utopia, Aaru, where no one would suffer age, hunger or loss. His research into forbidden knowledge destroyed his royal city and ravaged his people. He died sealing the disaster. Today's Eremites descend from his subjects, and Aaru Village and the ruins of the Great Red Sand preserve his legacy.

The kingdom's remains dominate southern Sumeru: the Mausoleum of King Deshret, Khaj-Nisut, Primal Constructs, Jinn lore and the unfinished afterlife Aaru. Because Aaru was reprogrammed after the burning of Irminsul (Archon Quest Song of the Welkin Moon, Act X "Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana", Version 6.6), his work now holds the world's stored memory in place of the old world tree.

Established: - Deshret was Lord of Deserts and one of the Three Eternal Companion-Gods, with Nabu Malikata and Rukkhadevata. He died thousands of years ago, in the Archon War era.
- He wanted an eternal paradise for his people and turned to forbidden knowledge, which polluted the desert.
- He gave his life to stop the disaster, while Rukkhadevata nearly exhausted her own power helping (Nahida, Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies).

- **The three gods.** The three ruled together as oathbound friends. Legend gives each a domain: the banquet to Nabu Malikata, authority to Deshret, life to Rukkhadevata. The wiki says this period was remembered as peaceful and prosperous, and that Deshret and Nabu Malikata built the city of Ay-Khanoum, "City of the Moon Maiden" in the Jinn tongue.
- **The split.** Deshret's ambition was great enough to defy the Heavenly Principles. Rukkhadevata would not join the plans and left to build her own civilization in the rainforest. Nabu Malikata died, and Deshret grieved; he used the power of a Celestial Nail of the sands and the Jinn to raise the Eternal Oasis as her resting place, guarded by Ferigees.
- **His rule.** Alone, Deshret sought vassal-kings and priests with incorrupt hearts and founded a royal city, Akhtamun. He was called the master of the thousand and one Jinn and "king of warriors, horticulturists and sages", and was also known as the Mourning King for his grief and nostalgia.
- **Apep.** Before building his kingdom he struck a bargain with the Dendro Dragon Apep, who claimed the desert: she would leave his people in peace if she could consume him after his death and take his knowledge.
- **Gurabad.** The city of brass rose in the desert after Nabu Malikata's death and is tied, in different accounts, to Deshret's guidance. Liloupar engineered its destruction; Deshret, enraged, had her spirit split into seven parts and hidden by his seven sages.
- **Aaru and the fall.** After Gurabad he doubled down on a plan for Aaru, an artificial afterlife for desert dwellers, made possible by the knowledge from Celestia that Nabu Malikata had given him. Accounts of her death differ: one says the Heavenly Principles executed her for this transgression, another that she gave her life in a ritual so he could receive that knowledge. His forbidden research released the knowledge that became the Withering; Rukkhadevata aided him, temples of life-power were raised, and Deshret finally sacrificed himself. Apep ate his body as agreed and was corrupted.

- **Culture.** Deshret Script is the kingdom's writing; obelisks at the Mausoleum, Opet Hall and Khaj-Nisut spell a word read as Akhtamon. His symbol is a sun and eye, seen on desert architecture. A mechanism at Khaj-Nisut let anyone who recited a prayer and sat on his throne enter a "golden slumber".
- **Primal Constructs.** The wiki says these were built to rebirth the paradise Deshret dreamed of; Faruzan spent a century in stasis in related ruins.
- **Seven Pillars.** The wiki lists Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf among Deshret's Seven Pillars; he imprisoned these three in Aaru, to be freed only by answering three questions about rise and fall, love and hate, and truth and falsehood. In the Version 6.6 Archon Quest (Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana) Nefer gave the intended answer, "time", and the three were freed.
- **Descendants.** Eremites descend from his subjects; some still worship him and want him back. The people and Guardians of Aaru Village, such as Candace, are called his metaphorical descendants.

- **Aaru's design.** The wiki describes it as a final land of dreams for desert dwellers, resembling the Akasha System in architecture and arguably its predecessor. Disembodied souls could enter it even while it was closed, as in the world quest series Golden Slumber.
- **Gurabad's line.** Parvezravan, his son Shiruyeh and the Brass Mask rebellion belong to Gurabad's story. According to the wiki, after Gurabad's fall and Deshret's death later 'kings of kings' rebuilt Gurabad to claim his legacy, and the Cities of the Seven Towers (among them Tulaytullah, Saleh and the old city of Ay-Khanoum) rose and fell in that era. See their entries.
- **Inspirations.** Wiki trivia notes that Deshret's lore echoes the Solomon and One Thousand and One Nights traditions (Jinn in bottles, riddles). Treat this as real-world inspiration, not in-world fact.

Accounts: - **Nahida** presents the disaster as forbidden knowledge polluting the desert, repelled thanks to Deshret's self-sacrifice and Rukkhadevata's near-exhaustion.
- **Apep** holds that Deshret meant her corruption as a fail-safe and says she thought little of him, though other texts call her his friend.
- **Ormazd** credited Deshret for Gurabad's prosperity and honoured him with temples, while **Liloupar** says Deshret charged Gurabad to guard the Eternal Oasis; other accounts credit Liloupar and say Ferigees defied Deshret.
- **Eremites** remember him as a god-king to restore.

Open questions: - Where Deshret came from, and when exactly his kingdom rose and fell.
- Whether Nabu Malikata returned his love.
- How much of Gurabad was his doing.
- Whether he foresaw Apep's corruption.

Connections: - Related entries: Nabu Malikata and Rukkhadevata (companion gods), Aaru and Irminsul (the afterlife and world-memory system), forbidden knowledge and the Withering, the Archon War, the Eremites and Aaru Village (present-day descendants).
- Do not merge with the Unified Civilization of the first era; the wiki's placement of Deshret after the funerary war is an inference.

161.content: Aaru is the unfinished artificial afterlife Deshret designed for desert dwellers so they could escape the dangers of Teyvat and its gods. Long closed off and unfinished, it held three imprisoned Pillars. After Nahida burned the corrupted Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis in the Archon Quest act Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (Version 6.6), Aaru was reprogrammed to store the ley lines' information. The wiki adds that the Heavenly Principles lost direct control over fate as a result.

162.comment: King Deshret's Civilization: Akhtamun and Ay-Khanoum
162.content: Akhtamun is the royal city Deshret founded in the desert and the place his forbidden research destroyed. Ay-Khanoum, "City of the Moon Maiden" in the Jinn language, is the older city he and Nabu Malikata built together; the wiki later records it as one of the Cities of the Seven Towers.

163.comment: King Deshret's Civilization: Deshret's Seven Pillars
163.content: Deshret's court of chief servants. Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf were locked in Aaru until the three questions were answered; Nefer's answer, "time", freed them in the Version 6.6 Archon Quest, and they agreed to unseal Aaru's Shut so Sumeru could modify it.

164.content: The wiki traces the Withering, and its human form Eleazar, to the forbidden knowledge Deshret unleashed. Rukkhadevata aided him with temples of life-power, but the threat persisted until his death temporarily ended it. See the forbidden knowledge entry for what that knowledge is.

165.content:
Archon Quest (Overall Premise) (also: Archon Quest, Archon Quests, Genshin main story, the Traveler's journey): The Archon Quest is Teyvat's main story. Twin travellers from another world try to leave Teyvat, and an unknown god (later named as Asmoday) blocks their way. She takes one twin and seals the other, the Traveler. On waking, the Traveler fishes the floating companion Paimon out of the sea, and the two cross the nations in turn: Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan, then Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya. In each, they meet that nation's Archon, one of The Seven, hoping the gods know where the lost twin is. In Liyue they learn the twin now leads the Abyss Order in a war against the gods. From then on the journey is also about understanding why.

Two threads run through every chapter. The Fatui, servants of the Tsaritsa, collect the Archons' Gnoses. The fallen kingdom of Khaenri'ah and its Cataclysm, about 500 years ago, link the sibling, Dainsleif, the hilichurls and the Harbingers. As of 7.1 the Traveler and Paimon are in Snezhnaya, the last nation of the twin's journey.

Established: Players choose which twin they play, so the Traveler is Aether and the sibling Lumine, or the reverse. Paimon is the guide and constant companion. The Traveler needs no Vision. They take up each nation's element, mostly by resonating with its Statue of The Seven. In Mondstadt, Venti remarks that he knew the Tsaritsa well five hundred years ago, but that after a catastrophe at that time she cut off all ties with him. That is the first hint of the Cataclysm.

The Traveler asked Mondstadt and Liyue to put up missing-person posters for the sibling. They stopped asking once they learned the sibling leads the Abyss Order. Later chapters stress that the Traveler is an outsider. Irminsul cannot record them, the Eye of Graeae in Snezhnaya recognises them as a Descender, and Ronova says a Descender's soul cannot enter the Ley Lines.

Structure: Story order (release versions): Prologue, Mondstadt (1.0); Chapter I, Liyue (1.0-1.4); Chapter II, Inazuma (1.6-2.6); Chapter III, Sumeru (3.0-3.5); Chapter IV, Fontaine (4.0-4.7); Chapter V, Natlan (5.0-5.7); Song of the Welkin Moon, Nod-Krai and later Sumeru (5.8-6.6); Chapter VII, "Everwinter Without Mercy", Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1).

From Chapter I on, each chapter ends with a "Traveler" act about the sibling and Khaenri'ah. These are "We Will Be Reunited", "Requiem of the Echoing Depths", "Caribert", "Bedtime Story" and "A Space and Time for You". A separate Interlude Chapter holds stand-alone follow-ups: "The Crane Returns on the Wind", "Perilous Trail", "Inversion of Genesis" and "Paralogism".

Act releases: Prologue 1.0. Chapter I Acts I-III 1.0-1.1, "Bough Keeper: Dainsleif" 1.3, "We Will Be Reunited" 1.4. Chapter II prologue "Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves" 1.6, Acts I-III 2.0-2.1, Act IV 2.6. Chapter III 3.0-3.2, Act VI 3.5. Chapter IV 4.0-4.2, Act VI 4.7. Chapter V 5.0-5.3, Act VI 5.7. Interlude acts 2.4, 2.7, 3.3 and 5.6. The 6.x versions carry "Luna" names (Luna I is 6.0, Luna VII is 6.6, Luna VIII is 6.7; the Song of the Welkin Moon Archon acts end in 6.6).

Journey: Chapter by chapter, in one line each:
- Mondstadt: the Traveler and Venti (Barbatos) free the dragon Dvalin from the Abyss Order, and Signora takes Venti's Gnosis.
- Liyue: Zhongli (Morax) stages his own death, and the Fatui release Osial. In Act IV the sibling appears as leader of the Abyss Order.
- Inazuma: the Vision Hunt Decree, Fatui Delusions, Signora's defeat and execution, and Ei's change of heart.
- Sumeru: Nahida is freed, the artificial god made from Scaramouche falls, and Rukkhadevata is forgotten.
- Fontaine: the prophecy, the truth about Furina, and Focalors' self-judgement.
- Natlan: Mavuika's war against the Abyss, Ancient Names, and Capitano's sacrifice.
- Nod-Krai: Columbina against Dottore. Dottore is finally destroyed when Irminsul is burned.
- Snezhnaya: Paimon's past, the Curse of Death, the Tsaritsa, and the fall of Ronova.
Each chapter's sub-entry has the details.

Sibling thread: The sibling is the story's hidden second protagonist. They lead the Abyss Order, still love the Traveler, and promise a reunion "at this journey's end". Khaenri'ah, a nation without gods, was destroyed about 500 years ago, and the gods cursed its people. The sibling was once its crowned heir, called "Savior". Dainsleif, once of its royal guard, travelled with them after the Cataclysm. He now opposes the Order's methods but grieves for the same people. As of 7.1 the sibling holds the Atlas of the New World, which carries the Ley Lines of a New Khaenri'ah, and is seen with the Shade Asmoday. Their goal is to stand before the Heavenly Principles as an equal, with a world behind them.

Recurring threads: - The Gnoses, links between each Archon and Celestia, which the Fatui gather.
- Celestia and the Heavenly Principles: the false sky, the Nails, Descenders, and the Shades (the Four Great Rulers).
- Khaenri'ah: the Cataclysm, the curse, the Abyss and the Five Sinners.
- Paimon: she seems a simple companion, but she came from Celestia, and Pierro pulled her down to Khaenri'ah.
- Each Archon's burden: freedom, contracts, eternity, wisdom, justice, war.
- The Fatui are not simply villains. The Tsaritsa aims to challenge the Heavenly Principles, and in 7.1 the Traveler fights alongside Harbingers.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, after "A Rekviem for the Underworld", the Traveler and Paimon are in Snezhnaya, on cooperative terms with the Tsaritsa and the Fatui. Ronova has lost her Authority and is dying. Before her end she made a Nail of Retribution crumble, which threatens to release Holy Soil. The sibling has not been found. The story has not yet reached Khaenri'ah.

The Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses. The Pyro Gnosis burned with Irminsul. Dottore and Signora are dead. Capitano is merged with the Lord of the Night.

Accounts: - The sibling: the gods are the enemy, and the Abyss can do what the Seven could not.
- Dainsleif, in the 2020 preview "Travail": the war against the gods "has already begun".
- The Tsaritsa and Pierro: Snezhnaya is preparing to rebel against the Heavenly Principles.
- Asmoday, at the start: she calls herself a sustainer of the Heavenly Principles. Her later alignment with the sibling is unexplained.

Open questions: Still open: what lies at the "journey's end"; what the sibling and Asmoday will do with the Atlas; whether and when the Heavenly Principles will wake; what follows the Nail's collapse; why the sibling was in Celestia. The Khaenri'ah chapter and "The Sea of Flowers at the End" are unreleased. Treat them as unknown.

Connections: See the entries on the individual chapters, the Traveler, Paimon, the Traveler's sibling, Dainsleif, the Abyss Order, the Fatui and the Harbingers, the Tsaritsa, the Gnoses, the Cataclysm and the fall of Khaenri'ah, Project Mistilteinn, the fall of Ronova and the Holy Soil crisis.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's advice): what characters know depends on where a scene falls in this order. Most residents never learn Archon Quest secrets. A default "present day" scene is set after 7.1.

Do not resolve the sibling's endgame, the Heavenly Principles or Khaenri'ah's fate, and do not invent a reunion. Do not make the sibling a simple villain, or simply in the right.

key: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
166.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Prologue and Chapter I
166.content:
Prologue (Mondstadt, 1.0). The dragon Dvalin, called Stormterror, attacks Mondstadt after the Abyss Order poisons him and turns him against it. The bard Venti is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon. With the Knights of Favonius, Venti and the Traveler free Dvalin. Afterwards the Harbinger Signora tears Venti's Gnosis out of him for the Tsaritsa, and Venti sends the Traveler on to Liyue.

Chapter I (Liyue). Rex Lapis is found dead at the Rite of Descension, and the Traveler is suspected. Tartaglia (Childe) leads them to Zhongli. The Fatui free the sealed god Osial, and Ningguang crushes him with her Jade Chamber. Zhongli then reveals he is Morax. He staged his death to test Liyue, and under a contract with the Tsaritsa he gives his Gnosis to Signora.

Act IV (1.3-1.4). With Dainsleif, the Traveler foils an Abyss plan to build a mechanical god. The sibling steps out of an Abyss portal as Prince or Princess of the Abyss Order. They say that Dainsleif and the Abyss monsters come from Khaenri'ah and that hilichurls are cursed Khaenri'ahns. They refuse to come home until their war with destiny is won, tell the Traveler to keep travelling and see the truth, and leave.

key: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
167.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Chapters II and III
167.content:
Chapter II (Inazuma). Under the Sakoku and Vision Hunt Decrees, the Traveler joins the Watatsumi resistance. The Fatui arm both sides and give the rebels Delusions that kill their users. Teppei dies of one. The Traveler defeats Signora in a duel, and the Shogun executes her. Then they persuade Ei, inside the Plane of Euthymia, to give up her rigid Eternity. Yae Miko had given the Electro Gnosis to the Harbinger Scaramouche to keep the Traveler safe.

Chapter III (Sumeru). The sages had imprisoned Nahida for 500 years, and with Dottore they try to make a god from Scaramouche and the Electro Gnosis. The Traveler and allies free Nahida and defeat the false god. Nahida cleanses Irminsul of forbidden knowledge. Only the Traveler remembers Rukkhadevata. Dottore leaves with the Electro and Dendro Gnoses.

Traveler acts. "Requiem of the Echoing Depths" (2.6): in Liyue's Chasm the sibling approves a risky device meant to lift the hilichurls' curse. Dainsleif, the knight Halfdan and the Traveler destroy it. "Caribert" (3.5): the Traveler relives the sibling's travels with Dainsleif after the Cataclysm. The sibling met Chlothar Alberich and his hilichurl son Caribert, was hailed as Khaenri'ah's heir, and came to join the Order.

key: A Space and Time for You
168.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Chapters IV and V
168.content:
Chapter IV (Fontaine). A prophecy says the seas will rise and every Fontainian will dissolve. Furina is revealed to be a human who played the Hydro Archon for 500 years so the god Focalors could have herself judged and executed. That returned the Hydro Authority to Neuvillette, who later gives the Hydro Gnosis to Arlecchino.

Chapter V (Natlan). Mavuika, the Pyro Archon, leads Natlan's war against the Abyss with heroes who hold Ancient Names. The Traveler receives the Ancient Name "Tumaini". The Pyro statue would not respond to the Traveler; the Lord of the Night grants them Pyro instead. The Harbinger Capitano first opposes Mavuika, then allies with her and gives his life in her place. He had asked the Tsaritsa to relieve him of the mission to take the Pyro Gnosis, and she agreed.

"Bedtime Story" (4.7): Caribert's lingering consciousness turns out to be the completed Loom of Fate, which can weave new Ley Lines. The sibling, intangible, admits loneliness. "A Space and Time for You" (5.7): the Traveler finds the key to their ship's hibernation chamber. Through Direidyth, a girl from 500 years in the past, a time loop closes: the key she carries back convinces the sibling to leave Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm to find their twin. The sibling then reveals the Atlas of the New World.

169.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Song of the Welkin Moon in the main story
169.content:
Song of the Welkin Moon (5.8-6.6). Varka invites the Traveler to Nod-Krai. There Columbina, the former Third Harbinger, opposes Dottore, who seizes the power of the moons. He is defeated. Columbina takes the Traveler to their crashed ship on the Frost Moon and loosens Teyvat's restrictions on their use of the elements. In the final Sumeru acts, Dottore attacks from inside Irminsul. Nahida burns Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis, and Dottore dies.

The ship's logs show it passed Teyvat thousands of years ago before returning to crash in Nod-Krai. Sandrone dies shielding the Traveler and is later revived. Aaru takes over Irminsul's role, and the Pyro Gnosis vanishes. Numbering: Snezhnaya was announced as Act VI in 2020 and became Chapter VII, but Song of the Welkin Moon is never officially called Chapter VI.

170.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Chapter VII in the main story
170.content:
Chapter VII (Snezhnaya, 7.0-7.1). Paimon falls ill on arrival. The Traveler gains Cryo and joins the secret society Rokot. Ronova, the Shade of Death, enforces a "Curse of Death" whenever Snezhnaya's research threatens Celestia, and she wants Paimon. Pierro reveals he pulled Paimon from Celestia to Khaenri'ah more than 500 years ago. The Traveler sides with Snezhnaya to protect her. The Tsaritsa (Anastasya) ends all investigations into the Traveler and explains that she gathers Gnoses to face the Heavenly Principles.

Act IV (7.1). Hroptatyr's notebook is opened, and Pierro reveals that Hroptatyr summoned the sibling from Celestia at the same time Pierro summoned Paimon. The Tsaritsa uses six Gnoses to slow time around Rhinedottir, so Ronova's victims miss their revival. Celestia strips Ronova of her Authority, and Pierro's new Delusion crushes her. Dying, she makes the Nail over the Cryo Dragon crumble.

171.content:
The Traveler takes up each nation's element: Anemo in Mondstadt, Geo in Liyue, Electro in Inazuma, Dendro in Sumeru, Hydro in Fontaine and Cryo in Snezhnaya, mostly by resonating with a Statue of The Seven. In Natlan the Pyro statue did not respond, and the Lord of the Night granted Pyro during the final battle against the Abyss.

In 6.3 Columbina removed some of Teyvat's restrictions on the Traveler, letting them use the elements more freely.

172.comment: Archon Quest (Overall Premise): Where the Gnoses went
172.content: Signora took the Anemo Gnosis from Venti (1.0) and received Geo from Zhongli (1.1). Electro went from Yae Miko to Scaramouche, then to Dottore. Dendro went from Nahida to Dottore (3.2). Hydro went from Neuvillette to Arlecchino (4.2). The Pyro mission was cancelled, and Mavuika's Pyro Gnosis burned with Irminsul and vanished (6.6). In 7.1 the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses, including her own Cryo Gnosis, and uses them to manipulate time and space.

key: fates that will not come to pass
173.content:
Nature of the Abyss (also: what the Abyss is, Void Realm, star-devouring darkness, fates that will not come to pass, hatred of unrealized fates): The Abyss is a dark, destructive power that comes from the sea of stars beyond Teyvat. It corrupts living things, spawns monsters and wants to force its way into the world. What it fundamentally is remains unresolved as of 7.1. The nearest thing to a definition is the Hexenzirkel's reading, relayed by Alice: its essence is the hatred carried by all the fates that will not come to pass.

Do not confuse the Abyss with the Abyss Order. The Order is a group of cursed Khaenri'ahns and monsters who use Abyssal power. Mavuika calls the Abyss itself a far greater threat.

Established: - The Abyss lies beyond the world the Heavenly Principles shaped. Canon calls it a power from the sea of stars and says it also exists on other worlds.
- It was brought into Teyvat during the war of funerary flame, according to the Abyss page's reading of quest and artifact text. Nibelung is blamed for bringing it in.
- It corrupts. Long exposure changes a person's nature or rots them, and large doses kill. The Traveler is immune and can cleanse Abyssal energy to a degree.

- Wiki summaries of quest text describe a Void Realm (the Abyss), a Human Realm (Teyvat, under the Heavenly Principles) and a Light Realm. The Abyss is said to be diametrically opposed to the Light Realm's power and to corrupt Human Realm beings, and its dark currents are likened to ley lines and elemental currents.
- Elemental beings, such as vishaps and dragons, are especially harmed by it. Humans who stay near it for long decay.
- Abyss monsters can use elemental power without Visions. Khaenri'ahn practitioners such as Skirk and Surtalogi use a technique called the Seven-Shifting Serpent (originally "Chaos Permeation") to make Abyssal power pass for elemental energy.
- Time passes differently inside it. Tartaglia spent about three months there and returned after only three days in Teyvat, and Skirk does not dispute Paimon's guess that a month there is a day outside.

- The Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah took the Abyss's power for themselves. The Abyss-linked monsters that devastated Teyvat in the Cataclysm were made by Rhinedottir, "Gold."
- In Natlan the Abyss adapted to each tribe and escalated as Mavuika's plan advanced, with Gosoythoth at the head of the 5.x invasion. It was beaten back by the Traveler, Mavuika and the souls of the fallen. Mavuika separates "the true Abyss" from the human organisation that bears its name (5.7).
- Nod-Krai has the Wild Hunt, led by Rerir, who is one of the Five Sinners. The Abyss imitated Roland to revive the Wild Hunt after Rerir's defeat. In the same region Kipumaki Cliff is described as the most heavily corrupted place.
- Nahida has said forbidden knowledge is a manifestation of the Abyss that hit Sumeru hardest. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata is said to have confirmed that it came from the very bottom of the Abyss, which does not belong to Teyvat.

- In the 7.0 notes of the Belyi Tsar, the Shadow Realm created by Anacharsis is described as a film of oil between Teyvat and the Abyss. When the Tsar opened the "passage" through it, a gash in time let the Abyss seep in without end. The Shadow Realm itself was untouched, since it "teems with possibilities yet unobserved". He suspected the Abyss and Shadow Realm repel one another.
- The Tsar also wrote that the Heavenly Principles confined the light's boundless possibilities to a narrow band in the name of certainty, and that "whenever we lay down an anchor into fate, the Abyss will naturally lay an anchor into us at the end of time". His fuller conclusion, that a few centuries remain, is covered under accounts.

Accounts: - **Alice and Barbeloth (6.4 event):** the Hexenzirkel has watched the Abyss's energies for a long time. In Alice's words, Barbeloth's reading is the most accurate. Every event that happens means a different possibility is gone, and those lost fates carry hatred. As an example Alice names Rhinedottir tapping the Abyss, which ended the tale of a future where she stayed pure. This hatred does not seek existence but the destruction of everything, and the Abyss is obsessed with entering the world at all costs. Alice also calls it cunning and obsessive, and jokes that it has "quite the victim complex".

- **Paimon, listening:** summarised it as hatred from not being chosen. This was a lighter and more personal gloss, not an additional fact.
- **Belyi Tsar (notes, 7.0):** treats the Abyss as something that anchors into a world that narrowed its own possibilities, not as an invader from nowhere. He holds that the Abyss will end everything under the false sky within a few centuries, and says Rotwang's calculations agree.
- **The Traveler:** after hearing Alice, reflects that fighting the Abyss many times has made them agree that existing at all is a spark of luck. During Project Moongazer (6.7) the Traveler also worries that a transmission might draw "the darkness that dwells amidst the stars" to the moon.

- **Item text (1.0, PlayStation-exclusive):** the Sword of Descension's description speaks of facing a "star-devouring darkness" that ends worlds. The Wings of Descension text names a "boundless darkness" and "all-consuming radiance" as forces that can destroy "one, or even two worlds".
- **Wiki readers:** note that Neuvillette's Vision text, Aksinya's talk of a world of love run dry, and Barbeloth's line all describe the world's original order turning into resentment. They infer the Human Realm's creation produced the Abyss in Teyvat. No quest confirms this.

Open questions: - What is the Abyss at its root? Is it a force, an enemy, a will, or the leftover of possibilities removed from a world?
- Why does it seek only destruction? Alice describes this as hatred, but not where the hatred is aimed.
- What is the "true Abyss" that Mavuika contrasts with the Abyss Order, and is the Order's power the same as its power?

- Did the Abyss end the Traveler and their sibling's world? Item text says a "star-devouring darkness" did, but no scene names it.
- Does the Abyss answer to anything? It adapts, speaks in Natlan, and imitates figures such as Roland, which suggests a mind, but canon has not said whose.
- If the Tsar is right, how long does Teyvat have?

- How can Hexenzirkel astrology see the Abyss's source in "unchosen fates" while the Belyi Tsar sees an anchor laid by the Principles? Are these the same claim?
- The Abyss destroyed Throgg, a world known only from a message the Moongazer Nin-Kiggia received. It is unclear whether the whole planet or only its civilisation ended.

Connections: The Abyss runs through the Abyss Order and its Loom of Fate, the Cataclysm and the Curse of the Khaenri'ahns, the Five Sinners, Natlan's wars and the Night Kingdom, the Wild Hunt of Nod-Krai, and forbidden knowledge in Sumeru. Cosmologically it is tied to the Light Realm, the Shadow Realm, the false sky and the Celestial Nails, which the Heavenly Principles used to burn away Abyssal corruption. For the Traveler it bears on the destruction of the twins' homeworld and on what the sibling has been doing with Abyssal power. See the twins' origin and the sibling's goal entries.

Individuals tied to the Abyss include Skirk, who lived within it and trained Tartaglia there, and Tartaglia, whose time in the Abyss changed how conflict follows him. Other characters met its power through Dvalin's corrupted blood, Chiyo's "beast of sin", and the sealed Enkanomiya.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation): treat the Abyss as dangerous and unexplained. A character may say what they actually know or believe, and should say who told them. Most people in Teyvat have only met Abyss monsters and the Abyss Order. Only Hexenzirkel members and a few others have words for the Abyss's essence. Do not turn the Hexenzirkel reading into a settled fact in the mouth of someone who has no way of knowing it.

Who could plausibly speak to the Abyss's nature: Alice and Barbeloth (hexenzirkel), the Belyi Tsar (dead; only his notes survive), Skirk, the Natlan leaders for their own war, and the Traveler for what they have seen. Dainsleif and Abyss Order members know it as a power they use, not a theory. Never have a character state who or what the Abyss "really" is.

Keep a clear line between three different things: Abyssal power, which can be used by individuals and corrupts them; the Abyss Order, a human faction; and the Abyss itself, the cosmic source nobody has explained. Characters often blur these in speech. That is fine, but do not make narration blur them.

key: fates that will not come to pass
174.comment: Nature of the Abyss: The Abyss's essence
174.content:
In the Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind event (6.4), Alice tells the Traveler that the Hexenzirkel has long studied the Abyss and that she finds Barbeloth's interpretation most accurate: its essence is the hatred carried by all the fates that will not come to pass. She says every event removes alternatives, from a lunch choice to Rhinedottir's decision to take Abyssal power, and that the Abyss resents being unchosen. She adds that it seeks the end of everything, not existence, and urges not to lose sleep over "what ifs".

The context was an accident in Alice and Nicole's magic bubble, a recreation of the past in which a nascent form of Abyssal power developed with no outside source. Alice said that some added variables had let a certain number of "unchosen fates" come close to reality. The Abyss "showed its teeth", and the bubble's Dvalin was corrupted.

175.comment: Nature of the Abyss: Abyss versus Abyss Order
175.content: Mavuika tells the Traveler in 5.7 that the Abyss Order is a smaller threat than "the true Abyss" Natlan's warriors have just beaten, because the Order cannot replenish its forces endlessly. The Order is made of former Khaenri'ahns and monsters who wield Abyssal power. Its members are not the Abyss itself.

key: Notes by a Certain Noble Individual
176.comment: Nature of the Abyss: The Belyi Tsar's notes on the Abyss
176.content: The notes at the Pale Crown Palace record the Belyi Tsar's conclusions after many expeditions into the ruins of Hyperborea. The Shadow Realm acts as a film between the world and the Abyss. His opening of the passage tore a hole in time, and the Abyss has been seeping in since. He also suggests that whenever people anchor themselves in fate, the Abyss will anchor in them at the end of time. He writes that the Abyss's seepage will end everything under the false sky within a few centuries, and that Rotwang has reached a similar figure independently.

177.comment: Nature of the Abyss: Time in the Abyss
177.content: Tartaglia fell into a hole at fourteen and lived about three months in the Abyss, learning from Skirk, only for three days to have passed in Teyvat. In the Skirk story quest (Sinister Undercurrent) Paimon asks whether a month there is a day outside and Skirk does not contradict her. Takamine the Mistsplitter, in weapon lore, returned from it to find Asase Hibiki no longer young. The wiki notes it is unclear whether the ratio is fixed.

178.content:
Night Warden Wars (also: Night Warden War, the Night War, Night Wars, Natlan's war against the Abyss): The Night Warden Wars were the continuous war Natlan fought against the Abyss, which began with the Cataclysm five hundred years ago. Natlan's warriors, led by bearers of Ancient Names, fought the Abyss in the Night Kingdom, the realm of the dead and of the Wayob, while the Pyro Archon could raise fallen Ancient Name bearers through the Ode of Resurrection. The war ended in the Natlan Archon Quest, when Mavuika and the Traveler defeated Gosoythoth, the heart of the Abyss.

The war shaped almost everything in modern Natlan: the Pilgrimage tournament, the Sacred Flame fed by Contending Fire, the system of inherited Ancient Names and the tribes' bond with their Wayob ancestors all exist to wage or sustain it.

Established: - The Abyss invaded Teyvat in the Cataclysm 500 years ago. In Natlan it first appeared on Tenochtzitoc, an island on the far western edge. Natlan, without stable, deep-rooted ley lines, suffered more than any other nation.
- The tribeless warrior Tenoch gathered six warriors, one from each tribe; they became the original Heroes of Natlan. The Abyss was driven out of the overworld but kept attacking the Night Kingdom, weakening the tribes' ties to their Wayob.
- Natlan's warriors fought the war as teams sent from the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Fallen Ancient Name bearers could be revived by the Pyro Archon's Ode of Resurrection if at least one teammate won.
- The war ended in the Natlan Archon Quest with the defeat of Gosoythoth.

- After the Cataclysm the tribes were shattered and hopeless. The Pyro Archon Mavuika gathered the Heroes and reasoned that the Abyss had been repelled only because the tribes had united. Her plan was to restore each tribe's strength; when a tribe's bond with its Wayob was whole again, the Wayob would acknowledge a new hero who inherited the Ancient Name of one of the original six. When six were gathered, Natlan would be strong enough to expel the Abyss from the Night Kingdom for good.
- Because an Archon's life is of ordinary human length and the plan would take generations, Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame so she could return near the time the tribes were ready.
- The Pilgrimage selected the strongest warriors. Ancient Name bearers among the winners were sent to the Night Warden Wars; the Pilgrimage also generated Contending Fire, which fuels the Sacred Flame. Only Ancient Name bearers were sent, since only they could be revived.
- The Ode of Resurrection needed two conditions: the dead warrior bore an Ancient Name, and at least one member of the team returned victorious. If the whole team fell, no revival was possible. Souls not brought back stayed in the Night Kingdom and their Ancient Names were forgotten. Warriors who survived retired when too old or badly hurt, and the name passed to a successor.

- By the time the Traveler arrived, Mavuika had been back for some time, but only three of the modern heroes (Iansan, Kinich and Xilonen) had been acknowledged, because the Abyss had infected the Wayob and weakened their link to the tribes.
- Kachina's Ode failed after her team won: Mavuika could not find Kachina or her Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom, because Abyssal unrest there blocked the rite. She suspended the Pilgrimage and stopped sending anyone to the war, falling back to defend the overworld. The Sacred Flame, short of Contending Fire, risked going out; as a stopgap Mavuika fed her Archon power into it.
- With the Traveler's help Kachina was found in the Night Kingdom and Mualani was acknowledged, then Ororon. In response the Abyss launched a nation-wide invasion, and Gosoythoth, described as the heart of the Abyss, appeared in the sky and rained Abyssal tumors across Natlan. Many died, including Chasca's sister Chuychu; her death led to Chasca's acknowledgement as the sixth hero.
- The six heroes gathered at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and, through Ronova, the Ruler of Death, empowered Mavuika and temporarily extended the Ode's blessing to every Natlanese warrior, with or without an Ancient Name. Casualties effectively dropped to zero, the overworld was cleared, and Gosoythoth was banished back to the Night Kingdom.
- Mavuika forbade other warriors from following, since the Abyssal energy near Gosoythoth would kill them instantly. She and the Traveler went alone into the Night Kingdom, helped by souls there (including the original six Heroes and the Lord of the Night). Gosoythoth took the form of the dragon Xiuhcoatl; the Lord of the Night awakened the Traveler's Pyro power, and when the Sacred Flame faltered Kachina led the gathered Natlanese in an Ode that returned its strength and unlocked the Nightsoul's Blessing of the Traveler's Ancient Name. They drew the weapon A Thousand Blazing Suns from the Sacred Flame and defeated Gosoythoth, ending the Night Warden Wars.

- Afterward the Ode was discontinued, since no warriors were sent to the Night Kingdom any longer. The Pilgrimage was retooled into a purely athletic tournament with outsiders able to take part; the Traveler served as its supervisor, and Kinich won the first of the new kind.
- Five years before the Traveler's arrival, Vichama and Mallko of the Scions of the Canopy won the Pilgrimage. An Abyssal attack on their tribe the day before the war injured Vichama, who stayed behind with Mavuika's permission; the rest of the team, Mallko included, was overwhelmed and killed, and their Ancient Names were lost. Mualani had prevailed in three Night Warden Wars without ever needing the Ode.

Accounts: - Natlan's official explanation (through the Pilgrimage and the Archon's words) presents the war as a duty of Ancient Name bearers, honoured and ritualised; most players meet it through the Archon Quest rather than as a single recorded history.
- The Cataclysm-era Heroes are known through the Talking Stick weapon text, Tenoch's page, the Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc Local Legend and Archon Quest flashbacks. Details of each death differ in tone from source to source.

- Gosoythoth is shown speaking as an individual, with confidence, arrogance and fear, and it worked out Mavuika's plan to stop the last hero being found. That reading comes from the Archon Quest scenes and the wiki's reading of them.

Open questions: - Whether the Abyss is wholly gone from Natlan: canon describes the war as ended and the Pilgrimage as repurposed, but the Abyss as a whole persists elsewhere.
- What Ronova's death in 7.1 means for the Ode of Resurrection and for the Night Kingdom, which she helped to shape.
- How the Tenochtzitoc island, the Mare Jivari battle and Bakunawa fit together exactly.

Connections: Part of the wider Cataclysm. The Night Kingdom was built as Natlan's replacement for its war-damaged ley lines, see the War of Funerary Flame. The Ode's power is attributed to Ronova (see the Fall of Ronova). The tribes' Wayob and Ancient Names, the Pilgrimage, and Mavuika's Sacred Flame each have their own entries.

179.comment: Night Warden Wars: Heroes of the Cataclysm
179.content:
Tenoch, a tribeless, battle-hardened Muratan warrior exiled before the Cataclysm, wielded a great obsidian club called the Talking Stick and recruited one warrior from each of six tribes against the Abyss. The Cataclysm-era six, with the Ancient Names they carried, were Sundjatta (Baraka, Children of Echoes), Sanhaj (Bidii, Masters of the Night-Wind), Burkina (Malipo, Scions of the Canopy), Tupac (Umoja, People of the Springs), Wanjiru (Uwezo, Collective of Plenty) and Menilek (Vuka, Flower-Feather Clan). Mavuika, Capitano, Tenoch, the Traveler and Paimon are also counted as Heroes of Natlan for their part in the war.

The names themselves go back to Xbalanque's day; each Cataclysm Hero inherited one. Deaths: Burkina died when his saurian companion Kongamato, corrupted by the Abyss, turned on him; Sanhaj and Tenoch died in the Mare Jivari when Sanhaj summoned a miniature Night Kingdom inside the monster Bakunawa and destroyed it; Menilek and Sundjatta fell in a final battle beside Mavuika; Wanjiru is assumed to have died afterward; Tupac carried the unconscious Mavuika to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame for her sacrifice and died standing. Tenoch could not be revived because he had already lost his Ancient Name.

180.comment: Night Warden Wars: Ode of Resurrection in the war
180.content: Performed at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. After an officiant's eulogy, the Pyro Archon steps into the Sacred Flame to find the dead warrior and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom; those gathered bow and sing, and the Archon emerges with the revived warrior. It restores only fatal injuries, not old wounds, and works only if the team achieved victory. Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, borrowed Ronova's power to set down the rules of Natlan that the Pilgrimage and the Ode belong to.

key: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame
181.comment: Night Warden Wars: Pilgrimage and the Night Warden Wars
181.content: The Pilgrimage was held as needed and more often as the war worsened. Teams, usually led by an Ancient Name bearer, battle for Contending Sparks; winners proceed to one-on-one matches. Top Ancient Name bearers were sent into the war. It also feeds the Sacred Flame with Contending Fire, produced only by fights between Natlanese, so outsiders could not take part until it was reformed as a sport.

182.comment: Night Warden Wars: The Abyssal invasion and Gosoythoth
182.content: After the Sacred Flame was snuffed out, the heart of the Abyss manifested above the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and Mavuika reignited the Flame with a Gnosis. Gosoythoth then spread Abyssal tumors and monsters across Natlan. In the Night Kingdom it assumed the form of the dragon Xiuhcoatl and was defeated by Mavuika and the Traveler, with the whole nation's support through the Ode.

183.comment: Night Warden Wars: Tenochtzitoc and the first invasion
183.content: The Abyss first appeared in Natlan on the island of Tenochtzitoc at its far western edge. An Abyssal creature named Bakunawa devoured the island's tribespeople. Tenoch and Sanhaj later destroyed it from within, and successive Pyro Archons built a temple to contain what remained (the wiki suggests four Archons were involved). The Local Legend The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc and the Mare Jivari battle preserve this history. The Easybreeze Holiday Resort now stands where this occurred.

184.content:
Ochkanatlan (Civilization) (also: Cinder City, Eternal Empire, City of Flowing Ash, Cinder Keep): Ochkanatlan, called the Cinder City and, in a vision, the "Eternal Empire", was an ancient human-ruled city-state of Natlan. Followers of Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, founded it on the ruins of a dragon city, and Och-Kan, a half-dragon "Python King", became its sovereign. He turned into a tyrant, and was overthrown by a scarlet-eyed youth and his companions, who then became the second Pyro Archon. The city was abandoned, and today its ruins on an island north of Quahuacan Cliff are considered cursed, fouled by the Abyss and guarded by a dragon that was once Och-Kan's own body.

It features in the 5.2 world quest series Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm, in the Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City artifact set, and in the Archon Quest as a base of the Abyss Order. Its ruins and the sky-ship Tonatiuh draw adventurers with a legend of treasure and a "Jade of Return" said to repel the Abyss. That legend is a lure.

Established: - Founding: Ochkanatlan was built thousands of years ago by followers of Xbalanque, with Och-Kan as its king. It stood on the ruins of Chichen Uctokah, a city of dragons once ruled by the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L (Paimon shortens her name to Ixlel).
- Seizure of the dragon city: Och-Kan took Ixlel's authority and imprisoned her in a statue inside the Old Core of Chu'ulel. The city's Source Mechanisms answered only to draconic power, but Ixlel refused to operate them for him.
- A new core: being half-dragon, Och-Kan chose to bind his own draconic half and placed his mind inside a new Core of Chu'ulel, a power source meant to serve humans alone. His body and mind were thereafter separate.
- Fall: the Scarlet-Eyed Youth and his party overthrew Och-Kan, after which the city was abandoned. The first-glimpsed city is remembered as having palatial courtyards and noble feasts.
- Aftermath: Kukulkan turned Och-Kan's body into an Abyssal conduit, the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, and spread the legend of the Tonatiuh's treasure to lure adventurers in.
- Present: the tribes forbid entry. The Flower-Feather Clan flies patrols over it, and the Saurian Relics Association avoids it after an investigating group vanished.

- The Eternal Empire: in Revelations from the Past (5.2) the Traveler touches a stone slate and hears a voice proclaim "Glory, glory, the Eternal Empire, Ochkanatlan" while one of two Golden Entreaties lies in shadow under a dragon's raised wings. This is how the Traveler learns to look for the second Entreaty in the ruins.
- Layout and remains: Khaenri'ahn Ruin Machines, including disabled Aeonblight Drakes, litter the island, and different animals and Saurians occupy different parts of it. Beneath it lie the Core of Chu'ulel, once the power source of the whole city, and the deeper Old Core of Chu'ulel. After the Traveler cleanses the Abyssal energy in the Palace of the Vision Serpent, the core loses the last of its vitality and only a piece of Pyrophosphorite remains.
- The Tonatiuh: originally a dragon-built satellite anchoring a stairway or cable that rose from Chichen Uctokah beyond Teyvat, it was turned on its side after Och-Kan seized the city. The Jade of Return aboard it is really a Golden Entreaty.
- Abyss Order base: in the Archon Quest act A Space and Time for You (5.7), the Scions of the Canopy locate the Order's headquarters at Ochkanatlan. The Traveler and Dainsleif fight through it and meet an Iniquitous Baptist inside.

- Quest placement: the Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm chapter has Act I City Buried By Ash, Act II A Dream of Gazing Upon the Distant Sky, Act III The Tonatiuh Quivers (with Moment of Awakening) and the epilogue The Chosen One's Promise. Open Your Heart to Me, a separate world quest, frees Ixlel in the Old Core.
- The Old Core quest lets the Traveler return Ixlel's heart fragments and free her from her bindings after millennia of captivity. She still speaks in the old sovereign's grand manner and names herself sovereign of the Land of Seven Flames (Chichen Uctokah).
- Evidence of Abyssal decay: notes in the area show that by the time of the adventurers the city was already corroded and some people had been replaced by Tenebrous Mimiflora in disguise.

Accounts: - Tribal memory: Ochkanatlan is remembered as a tyrant's city where Saurian sympathisers were persecuted and the tribes had to hand their authority to the Grand Alliance. The Scarlet-Eyed Youth, from the Flower-Feather Clan, was banished by his elder for sympathising with Saurians and later led the revolt.
- Och-Kan's own memories (shown in Moment of Awakening): he saw himself as protecting humans and Xbalanque's legacy. He banned live sacrifice and worship of the Night Kingdom, used the Turnfire against opponents and broke Xbalanque's commandments on peaceful coexistence with dragons.
- Kukulkan's version: he reproached his son for breaking Xbalanque's oath and opening the door to malevolent forces, and demanded the Golden Entreaty, which Och-Kan said he had hidden. Kukulkan warned he would come back to collect Och-Kan's soul.

- Yupanqui, Och-Kan's friend, disagreed with his rule but accepted a post as ordnance officer in the Grand Alliance, before the Scarlet-Eyed Youth persuaded him to join the rebels.
- The Ochkanatlan Adventure Team (unofficial name) went up about ten years after the Cataclysm, to find a weapon said to defeat the Abyss. Its members came from several tribes; only the young mystic Liriwu returned. Bona, daughter of the leader Taika, followed a couple of decades later and died too, fighting Kukulkan.
- Och-Kan's last words as the dragon: after the fight he said the Entreaty is "as important as it is dangerous", gave it to Little One, whom he compared to himself as a bearer of the Flamelord's Blessing, and shared memories with the Traveler before dying. His spirit returned to the Night Kingdom and later guided the Traveler through its corroded depths.

Open questions: - Exactly when Ochkanatlan fell and how long it stood is not stated.
- What Och-Kan unearthed that made him burn the excavation is never named.
- Why Kukulkan wanted adventurers' souls and what his "experiment" finally achieved is given only in part, through the wiki's reading of the quests.

- The wiki notes the Scarlet-Eyed Youth asked Chief Sakkuk to remove his name from history, so his real name is not recorded.
- Whether the Abyss Order's headquarters here was destroyed or abandoned after the Traveler's visit is not made clear in the summary used for this entry.

Connections: - Founder-god: Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, who left commandments on coexistence that Och-Kan broke.
- Ruler: Och-Kan, son of Kukulkan; also known as the Sacred Lord and Python King.
- Conqueror: the Scarlet-Eyed Youth, who became the second Pyro Archon.
- Parent site: Chichen Uctokah, the dragon city beneath it, and the Tonatiuh above it.
- Later users: the Abyss Order, who made a base here.

- Tribes: the Flower-Feather Clan and Scions of the Canopy watch the ruins; the Grand Alliance of tribes arose in its era.
- Artifact sets: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City (the Ochkanatlan Adventure Team) and Unfinished Reverie (the youth's rebellion).

185.content: Son of the dragon Kukulkan with a human soul, raised among tribes and then made a test subject by dragons in his childhood. He served Xbalanque and, after Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, ruled Ochkanatlan as the Sacred Lord. His rule became tyrannical. His mind lived on in the Core of Chu'ulel and woke in the form of Cocouik, the companion of the adventurer Bona; his body became the fell dragon of the city. He regained himself and died in Moment of Awakening.

key: Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
186.comment: Ochkanatlan (Civilization): Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
186.content: The Abyss-tainted body of Och-Kan, the guardian that attacks everyone entering the ruins. Kukulkan made it an Abyssal conduit, and its victims' souls were used for masks. It stole the Jade of Return from the Traveler in Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm and was ended in the Moment of Awakening fight.

187.content: An unofficial name for the adventurers, drawn from several tribes, who went to Ochkanatlan after the Cataclysm hoping to find a weapon against the Abyss. The Tonatiuh was not what they thought and most perished. Only Liriwu came home. Their stories appear in the Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City artifact set.

188.content: A sky-faring ship built by dragons as a satellite for a stairway beyond Teyvat, later modified by Och-Kan. Rumoured to be full of treasure, a legend fabricated by Kukulkan. In truth it holds Pyrophosphorite and the hidden Golden Entreaty.

189.comment: Ochkanatlan (Civilization): Ixlel in the Old Core
189.content: The Dragonlord who ruled Chichen Uctokah before Och-Kan took her authority. She was trapped in a draconic statue and her heart was split so her strength could power the city. The Traveler frees her in the quest Open Your Heart to Me.

190.content:
Paimon's Identity (also: Paimon's origin, Paimon's nature, what Paimon is, Paimon mystery, creation of Celestia): Paimon is the small, floating, talkative companion who has stayed at the Traveler's side since the start of the game, and for years nobody knew what she was. She says she was fished out of the sea by the Traveler and remembers almost nothing before that. In Version 7.0 (Snezhnaya, Chapter VII) the Fatui Director Pierro revealed that he drew her down from Celestia in Khaenri'ah more than 500 years ago, and Ronova, the Ruler of Death, called her a creation of Celestia with none of its power. Paimon has no memory of any of this, and what she is and why she was sent remain open.

The answer is partial. Canon now fixes where she came from and roughly when, but not what she is, who intended her or what she is for. The Traveler's reply, that she is still Paimon to them, is the story's current resting point.

Established: These points are stated in canon by the 7.0-7.1 Archon Quest and earlier scenes.

- Paimon has been the Traveler's guide and companion since the opening of the story. She says she was exhausted, caught in a strange whirlpool and swept out to sea, and would have drowned had the Traveler not fished her out. She says nothing worse ever happened to her.
- In Chapter VII Paimon fell ill in Snezhnograd. The cause was the energy being developed for Project Mistilteinn, the Fatui's "anti-Celestia energy": her reaction to it points to her Celestial origin. Pierro personally carried her to the Armory Palace and had the researcher Mitya adjust the project so its energies would no longer affect her. Afterwards she was well again.
- Pierro, whose Khaenri'ahn name is Eftirvit, told the Traveler that in his Khaenri'ah days he used technology upon the heavens and the response was Paimon descending from Celestia. She then lived in his palace until the Cataclysm. Paimon, who was told this with the Traveler, pointed out that this was about five hundred years ago and that she remembers none of it, and that she has memories only from the past few years.
- Ronova, the Shade who rules over death, called Paimon a creation of Celestia that possesses none of Celestia's power, let alone its authority. She tried to take Paimon by force and was stopped by Pierro, then fought by the Traveler, and said she would "reclaim" Paimon next time.
- Paimon still feels oddly close to Pierro, though she remembers nothing about him.

- She has no Vision and no element of her own and does not fight, yet she is unharmed by things that normally need an elemental affinity: dense Ley Line energy, Abyssal corruption, and diving in Fontaine, where she can even talk underwater. Mavuika kept her away from the final battle in the Night Kingdom because the Abyss would likely target a non-combatant, not because the corruption would injure her.
- When Dr. Luneva in Snezhnaya asked whether she was a fae, Paimon said she was not sure, only that she was not the same kind as the fae at the train station, and insisted she is basically the same as a human. Luneva found her vital signs normal and took the illness for a cold.
- Further Khaenri'ah details, all from Pierro: he presented Paimon to the Vinster King Irmin as a gift, but Irmin took no interest in her, so she lived in Eftirvit's palace; he completely ignored her, being wholly focused on his struggle against Hroptatyr "the Wise", president of the Universitas Magistrorum. When she arrived her consciousness was like a newborn's, and none could say what kind of being she had been in Celestia; her personality then was no different from now. In 7.1 (Etched in Time) Pierro added that when he summoned Paimon from Celestia, Hroptatyr summoned someone else at the same time: the Traveler's sibling.
- Pierro's stated reason for protecting her now is that she seems to be the only sane thing that survived what he called that era of insanity. Ronova found his obsession baffling.
- Paimon is one of the beings who is affected when Irminsul is rewritten, as only those native to Teyvat are (the wiki cites Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies and The Kabukimono's Finale for this, and a Scaramouche-related memory loss in which she forgot while the Traveler did not; the exact scenes were not re-read). This fits her being bound to Teyvat in practice, whatever her origin.

Accounts: - **Paimon's own account.** She remembers falling asleep or being exhausted, being swept out to sea and rescued. She is shown to have no memory of Khaenri'ah, of Pierro or of the five centuries between. She decided that being a creation of Celestia changes nothing and joked she may be "the fairy of food and fun". She also asked the Traveler whether they would abandon her; they said no.
- **Pierro's account.** He says his device on the heavens produced Paimon, and that she lived in his palace until the Cataclysm. He says she arrived with a newborn's consciousness and that none could say what she had been in Celestia, and he guesses her memory loss may be some curse from living through the Cataclysm. He told the Traveler that this was their first official meeting; he had already met Paimon when they first arrived in Snezhnaya and told her they had once spent time together in the distant past.
- **Ronova's account.** A being that may be a creation of Celestia but possesses none of its power, let alone authority; she called it worthless, yet said she would reclaim it next time. She says this while Pierro is the one standing against her, and she treats his attachment as a puzzle.

- **Kukulkan's remark (Natlan).** He speaks of the Traveler and the "little emissary" by their side, without saying whose emissary.
- **Barbeloth's reading.** The Seer-Witch wondered whether Paimon wanted to know her own fate, then fell silent. Most seers cannot read Paimon's fate at all, according to the wiki.
- **Melusine sight.** The Melusine Canotila (in the quest Book of Esoteric Revelations, per the Paimon page) described Paimon as a little rainbow balloon with a string leading upward to somewhere beyond the sky, and insisted that Melusines can see what humans cannot. Paimon found this baffling. It is a poetic image, not an explanation.
- **Teyvatian impressions.** Most characters take Paimon for a flying pet, a fairy or a sprite. Verr Goldet calls her a floating elf; Starsnatcher a talking fairy; Vseslav mistook her for a young Vila. These are guesses by people with no inside knowledge.

Open questions: - What kind of being is Paimon, and was she made, born or sent?
- Why did Celestia's response to Pierro's device take the form of Paimon?
- Where was she, and in what state, from the Cataclysm to the time the Traveler met her, and why does she remember only the last few years?

- Does she hold any hidden power? Ronova says she holds none of Celestia's, yet she shrugs off Abyssal corruption and Ley Line energy.
- What did Barbeloth see, and what did Kukulkan mean by "emissary"?
- How does she connect to the Traveler's sibling, whom Pierro says Hroptatyr summoned from Celestia at the same time he summoned Paimon? Beyond that simultaneity, canon has not tied the two together.
Canon so far gives no hint that Paimon is dangerous, hostile or a plant; she behaves exactly as she did before the reveal. Keep her this way in portrayal. Do not state a purpose, a hidden power or a destiny for her.

Connections: Pierro and Ronova (and, through Ronova, the Heavenly Principles) are the two parties in canon who have spoken about Paimon's origin. The reveal is tied to Project Mistilteinn and the Fatui's plan against the Heavenly Principles, to the Cataclysm in Khaenri'ah, and to the Traveler's own origin and the sibling thread. In 7.1 (A Rekviem for the Underworld) Paimon is still with the Traveler through the Fatui's preparations; Ronova had her authority confiscated by Celestia for her transgression in Snezhnaya and was mortally wounded by Pierro's new Delusion; she spent her last act shattering a Celestial Nail with Eitr and is presumed dead (the wiki lists her as having died), so her threat to reclaim Paimon is no longer active and her reason for wanting Paimon was never explained.

See the entries for Pierro, Ronova, Hroptatyr, Irmin, the Traveler's origin and the Traveler's sibling for those figures' own accounts; do not copy their biographies here.

Usable framing: Paimon is the one fixed companion who has been present at every major reveal without being part of any, and the story treats her loss of memory as unexplained rather than as a hidden clue. Anyone portraying her should keep her cheerful, loyal and unaware, and let other characters supply any speculation.

191.content:
In the Archon Quest Mistilteinn, after Pierro (the Jester) rescues the unwell Paimon and Ronova is driven off, he explains why the Fatui's anti-Celestia energy affected her: in Khaenri'ah, centuries ago, he used technology upon the heavens and Paimon descended from Celestia in answer. She stayed in his palace until the Cataclysm. Paimon, who remembers none of it, realises this happened five hundred years ago (the Traveler can remark that she must be at least that old), asks whether she was super smart back then, and says she still feels weirdly close to him, though he is basically a stranger to her. Pierro answers that she had a newborn's consciousness and that he ignored her entirely, but that she now seems the only sane thing to survive that era. Asked whether they will abandon her, the Traveler can answer that she is still Paimon to them.

This is the first time canon names Paimon's origin and gives her a place in Khaenri'ah's last days. In 7.1 Pierro adds that Hroptatyr summoned the Traveler's sibling from Celestia at the same time. It does not say why Pierro called, what he hoped for, or what she was before she arrived.

192.comment: Paimon's Identity: Ronova's Interest in Paimon
192.content:
Seeing Paimon, Ronova said "That thing... is coming with me" and fired at her; Pierro blocked the attack. She then said that thing may be a creation of Celestia but possesses none of its power, let alone authority, that Pierro's obsession with it baffled her, and that it was worthless, yet she would reclaim it next time. The Traveler, hearing this and that she wanted to retrieve Paimon, treated Ronova as an enemy. In Snezhnaya her Curse of Death was a barrier to Project Mistilteinn; in 7.1 she lost her authority, was mortally wounded by Pierro and is presumed dead, so she is no longer pursuing Paimon.

Ronova did not explain why a creation of Celestia without its authority should be taken back, nor what she would do with Paimon.

193.comment: Paimon's Identity: Paimon's Illness in Snezhnaya
193.content:
In Snezhnograd Paimon grew dizzy and feverish. The doctor Luneva, after Paimon insisted she was basically the same as a human, found her vital signs normal and took it for a cold; the real cause was Project Mistilteinn's anti-Celestia energy, which affected her even from far away. When the Traveler was away at the theatre, Pierro carried her off, still asleep, to the Armory Palace; the Traveler took it for an abduction. Paimon woke there and told the Traveler that the Jester and Mitya had used some kind of energy on her that she could feel cancelling out what was making her unwell; Mitya said they had reversed the experimental energy's effects on Pierro's instructions. Afterwards her head stopped spinning and the fever was gone.

Pierro explicitly links the illness to her being a creation of Celestia. Mitya and Pierro treated it as a side effect to be avoided, not a threat.

194.comment: Paimon's Identity: Paimon and Irminsul Changes
194.content: According to the wiki, Paimon is affected by Irminsul modifications that only affect those native to Teyvat: when Scaramouche's record was altered in Irminsul, she forgot him while the Traveler remembered. This is as summarised by the wiki; the primary scenes were not re-read here. It shows she is bound to Teyvat's Irminsul record despite her Celestial origin.

195.content: When Paimon asked the Seer-Witch Barbeloth to read her fortune, Barbeloth hesitated, asked in a serious tone whether she truly wished to know, and then fell silent. The scene is a hint, not an answer. Treat it as such and do not invent what she saw.

196.content:
Project Lunar Veil (also: Lunar Veil, Lunar Veil Project, Lusalim's Lunar Veil, Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment): Project Lunar Veil was a research project of the dragon scholars living on the Frost Moon. Professor Maagees-Geti and her student Lusalim set out to build a veil that could hide the entire moon from outside eyes. It was meant as a safeguard for Project Moongazer, the plan to send the Stellar Blackbody's message back into space. It was never finished: the Heavenly Principles arrived, Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory was destroyed, and he handed his research over to them.

The project is learned about in the Version 6.7 Moon Gazing world quests, from terminal records left across the Frost Moon. Columbina points out that a veil that hides the moon resembles the false sky. Whether one became the other is not settled by canon.

Established: - Purpose: Project Moongazer aimed to transmit the message of the Stellar Blackbody into the universe. Lusalim saw no evidence that whatever received such signals would be friendly, and feared the transmission could invite disaster. The Lunar Veil was meant to hide the moon so that this risk could be reduced.
- People: it was run by Professor Maagees-Geti with her student Lusalim, with a research team that included Nu-ur-Gestug. Lusalim is named as its chief architect.
- Basis: Maagees-Geti's studies of Blackbody Matter, the black filamentous substance taken from the Stellar Blackbody creature. Matter found on the hull of the spaceship Moongazer reflected in an unusual way, which probably explains why the ship was cloaked when it hit the Space Lifeform Capture Station. Experiments also showed that Blackbody Matter could stimulate and be stimulated by Archaeolune Energy and could fuse with plants and animals.
- First stage: researchers chose Moonshade Trees compatible with Blackbody Matter. Once stimulated with Archaeolune Energy, these gave off reflective waves, and stronger stimulation formed a stable "curtain-form" containment that spread beyond the whole Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab.
- Phase I: a miniature Lunar Veil was laid over Ungien's Circle, which looked empty from outside but was quite different inside. Lusalim wrote that the project name actually came from his "daughter" Nin-Kiggia, who could hardly speak at the time.
- Phase II: Maagees-Geti's health kept failing. The team at the Eye of Ibni-Belum carried out the signal transmission as her last wish. Lusalim, still uneasy about it, wanted the full-scale Veil immediately despite the much larger energy cost, and asked the Moon Goddesses for help.
- End: Kalag, the moon's Security Chief, took control of Ungien's Circle, so Lusalim continued at his Lunar Veil Laboratory in what became the Moontide Sea, where he built a huge Veil generator able to conceal the whole moon. Before it took shape the Heavenly Principles arrived; the laboratory and generator were destroyed in an explosion that created the Moontide Sea.
