Lusalim moved to his laboratory on the Dark Side of the Moon and eventually surrendered his research to the Heavenly Principles, probably to protect the moon's facilities from further destruction.

- Reaction of colleagues: Nu-ur-Gestug suggested larger-scale trials and Maagees-Geti agreed, which led to Phase I. He later called the project an uninspired, short-term fix that would only buy time before the Dark Destroyer inevitably arrived.
- Eggie, narrating records to the Traveler and Paimon, says the success of the miniature Veil pushed the project to its next phase and that Lusalim designed the Veil as a crucial part of Project Moongazer, which had to be suspended after the explosion.
- Eggie's account of the end is that an entity from beyond the stars pierced the Veil before it could take shape, the device went haywire and the laboratory exploded. The Traveler and Columbina conclude the culprit was likely the ruler of the firmament.

- In the Moon Gazing quests Columbina compares the Veil to the false sky, and Paimon jokingly calls it a baby version. This is a character observation, not a statement of how the false sky was made.
- The sequence of locations matters in a scene: Maagees's Greenhouse and the Containment Lab (Blackbody Matter and the curtain-form stage), Ungien's Circle (the miniature Veil), the Archaeolune Storm Research Center and Kalag's grounds (the moon's security took over), Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory (the full-scale generator, now the Moontide Sea) and finally Lusalim's Laboratory on the Dark Side of the Moon.
- Later, in the final act of Moon Gazing, Columbina offers to use her power as a Moon Goddess to shield Eggie's transmission as it passes through the false sky. This is a separate, later act and not part of the old project.

Accounts: - Lusalim's records: cautious and fearful of the unknown listener; he treats the Veil as protection for the Moongazers' work.
- Maagees-Geti's side: she wanted the message sent out to inspire other civilisations. Her final wish was the transmission, which was carried out while the Veil was still unfinished.
- Nu-ur-Gestug: critical of the Veil as a stopgap that does not answer the coming Dark Destroyer.
- Columbina and the Traveler: see the explosion as the work of the ruler of the firmament and compare the Veil to the false sky.

- Eggie reports what she reads from the records and states some parts hesitantly (she says the exact principles are unclear). Keep that hedging when she speaks of it.

Open questions: - Whether the Heavenly Principles used Lusalim's research to make the false sky is not stated. Treat Columbina's comparison as a suspicion.
- Why Lusalim gave his research to the Heavenly Principles is given only as a probable motive: to spare the moon's facilities.
- What became of Lusalim after surrendering the research is not stated in the sources read.

- The exact principle by which the Veil conceals the moon is described only in terms of reflective Blackbody Matter and Archaeolune Energy.

Connections: - Parent project: Project Moongazer.
- Sites: Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab, Ungien's Circle, Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory (now the Moontide Sea), Lusalim's Laboratory.
- People: Maagees-Geti, Lusalim, Ungien, Nu-ur-Gestug, Nin-Kiggia, Kalag, Eggie, Columbina.
- Related cosmology: the Heavenly Principles and the false sky over Teyvat.

- The Stellar Blackbody message that motivates both projects is said to warn of pitch-black annihilation, likely the Abyss.

197.content: Student of Ungien and Maagees-Geti and chief architect of Project Lunar Veil and executor of Project Moongazer. He feared that sending the signal could draw disaster, built the Veil to hide the moon, raised Nin-Kiggia as his "daughter", and eventually gave his research to the Heavenly Principles.

198.content: Dragon professor and Mistress of the Greenhouse. Her research on Blackbody Matter was the basis of the Lunar Veil. Her health declined and her last wish was to send the Stellar Blackbody's message out through the Eye of Ibni-Belum.

199.content: Black, filamentous, information-bearing substance extracted from the Stellar Blackbody creature by Maagees-Geti. It has a reflective property, interacts with Archaeolune Energy, and can fuse with plants and animals; this is what makes the curtain-form containment and the Veil possible.

200.content: A lunar sea on the Frost Moon that formed where Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory and its generator exploded when the Heavenly Principles arrived.

201.content:
Project Mistilteinn (also: Mistilteinn): Project Mistilteinn is the Fatui's secret weapon project in Snezhnaya, overseen by Pierro and carried out at the Armory Palace. Its aim is a weapon that would let the Tsaritsa fight the Heavenly Principles, powered by the energy of Stellar Linchpins. It needs enormous energy, which is why Project Stuzha rations Snezhnaya's supply. Ronova's Curse of Death stalled it until her authority was revoked in 7.1; it has since resumed.

It is the hidden purpose behind much that the Traveler meets in Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai, from public energy rationing to the Kuuvahki research bureau. The Fatui describe the Linchpin-derived power it uses as "anti-Celestia energy".

Established: - It is a Fatui project run by Pierro together with the Armory Palace, a sister project to Project Stuzha.
- Purpose: a weapon for the Tsaritsa's final battle against the Heavenly Principles.
- Power source: energy extracted from Stellar Linchpins, which the Fatui link to the Third Descender.
- Obstacle: Ronova's Curse of Death, which killed everyone near a technological breakthrough. It lifted in 7.1 when her authority was revoked.

- Why ordinary elements will not do: Pierro explains that elemental energy is the power of the Human Realm in a form the Heavenly Principles themselves converted it into, so turning it on them would be futile. Kuuvahki alone cannot breach Celestia's defences either, and the Heavenly Principles is used to fighting Light Realm power. The Fatui therefore turned to the energy associated with the Third Descender and the Stellar Linchpins.
- The method: Mitya, a Royal Energy Commission researcher and himself a Linchpin user, is in charge of the energy research that reverse-engineers the Linchpins' energy into a source the Fatui call "anti-Celestia energy".
- Energy cost: the project needs vast power. Pierro states that Project Stuzha, the energy reforms and rationing that Snezhnaya endured, exists to serve Mistilteinn.
- Hidden aims behind public projects: Pierro says the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau in Nod-Krai was a facade for studying kuuvahki; its core objective was to use local resources and findings to build Mistilteinn itself.
- Protection: Pierro says the technology, though not fully developed, has reached a stage where Celestia's creations cannot damage it.

- Where: the research is done deep beneath the Armory Palace in Glupov. Odette remarks that the facility seems to use structures requisitioned from a past civilisation, which also serves as a disguise; this is her guess.
- The curse's rule, as Mitya works it out in 7.0: when a moment of technological progress occurs, all life nearby is taken. Researchers, technicians and witnesses "die", then come back later without any memory of the time they were dead. Materials and energy gathered through Stuzha were lost each time.
- The 7.0 pause: Mitya's final-phase energy experiment, begun ahead of schedule, triggered the curse. He recommends suspending the experiments and Mistilteinn, and Pierro agrees to put the project on hold until the Ruler of Death has been eliminated.
- The 7.1 resumption: after Ronova's authority is taken back, the curse is undone with it, because Ronova imposed it on her own initiative and the Heavenly Principles never authorised it. Mitya says the blockade on Snezhnayan technology is lifted and the project can finally move forward; research staff of the Armory Palace confirm the restrictions are gone.

- Mitya also stresses that Ronova cannot simply do as she pleases, since he is standing there alive after being killed by her curse.
- In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting the last batch of newly purchased equipment for Mitya's new lab is being delivered, with military support arranged through Valeriy and Vesna. Afterwards Pierro tells Dainsleif that in the struggle against the gods no one can see the full picture of fate.
- Paimon's reaction to the project's emissions is what first exposes the link to Celestia (see accounts).

Accounts: - Pierro (7.0): many of the things the Traveler has encountered so far exist to advance the project, including Stuzha and the Nod-Krai bureau. He tells the Traveler openly, speaking of allies.
- Mitya (7.0): he stresses that he speaks purely as a scientist: with the curse active no breakthrough is possible, so the project must stop.
- Columbina (6.3): she says the word "Mistilteinn" often seemed to come up in connection with Project Stuzha when she lived in Snezhnaya, but she kept her distance and did not know more.
- The Traveler (7.0): when Pierro's description comes up, the Traveler says they were given some intel and made their own deductions, and does not name a source in the text read.

- Odette (7.0), as Lelek, enemy of Project Stuzha, enters the Armory Palace to rescue Paimon and sees the large machinery; the Traveler wonders aloud whether the whole reason for Stuzha was to support the research there.
- The quests read show the Tsaritsa's goal of overthrowing the Heavenly Principles, but she is not shown describing Mistilteinn herself in these texts; the link to her plan comes from Pierro and the wiki.

Open questions: - What exactly the weapon is, how it will be used and when. Canon shows only a sword-like form in the machinery.
- Whether the project can be completed, and what the Heavenly Principles, currently dormant, would do about it.
- Whether Project Stuzha's rationing returns now that Mistilteinn is unrestricted.

Connections: - Project Stuzha: the energy pipeline; its renewal vote and hardships belong to its own entry.
- The Tsaritsa's plan to overthrow the Heavenly Principles, which the weapon serves.
- Ronova and the Curse of Death; her fall in 7.1 frees the project.
- Stellar Linchpins and the Third Descender: the source of its energy. Known Linchpin users include Sandrone, Odette, Vesna, Danica and Mitya.
- Paimon: a being of Celestia whose illness exposed the project's effect on Celestia's creations.

- The Armory Palace under Glupov, managed by Sandrone, is the site.
- Pierro's history with Paimon and Ronova is told in their own entries, not here.

202.content:
Anti-Celestia energy is the Fatui's name for the power obtained by reverse-engineering Stellar Linchpins, which Pierro describes as associated with the Third Descender. It is meant to give Mistilteinn a chance against the Heavenly Principles, since ordinary elemental energy and kuuvahki are judged useless against Celestia. Mitya leads the research. Its emissions made Paimon ill, even from far away, until Mitya and Pierro used another energy on her that cancelled its effect.

Mitya says the effect on Paimon was reversed and that Pierro specifically instructed him to do so. Paimon later tells the Traveler she could feel one energy cancelling out the other. Pierro explains the cause: Paimon is a creation of Celestia.

203.comment: Project Mistilteinn: Mistilteinn Pause and Resumption
203.content:
In 7.0 the project is put on hold because Ronova's Curse of Death makes breakthroughs impossible. In 7.1, after her authority is revoked, the curse is undone and Mitya declares that Project Mistilteinn can finally move forward.

The 7.0 suspension follows Mitya's early final-phase experiment, which killed all who were present; the 7.1 resumption follows the fight at Rankova Zorya and Celestia's revocation of Ronova's authority. Pierro still warns that retaliation is possible, since Ronova may have escaped unseen.

204.content: During Welkin Moon's Homecoming Columbina, asked about the Fatui, says the Rooster and Regrator seemed friendly but worked against each other in secret, and adds that the term "Mistilteinn" often seemed to come up in connection with Project Stuzha. It is the earliest mention of the name in the quests read.

205.comment: Project Mistilteinn: Pierro's Briefing in the Armory Palace
205.content:
After saving Paimon, Pierro offers the Traveler "hospitality", answers questions about Mistilteinn and the Tsaritsa, and explains that Stuzha serves the project. He proposes openly joining forces against Ronova. At Paimon's request he activates the machinery, and a large sword-like form appears in it.

He says the Fatui need not hide anything from allies given the circumstances; the project, in his words, cannot move on until the Ruler of Death has been dealt with.

206.content:
Project Moongazer (also: Moongazers, the Moongazers, Moongazer project, Stellar Blackbody message): Project Moongazer was the work of the Moongazers, a group of dragon researchers on the Frost Moon, who set out to keep sending into the universe the message once carried by a creature called the Stellar Blackbody. That message came from a distant world and warned against pitch-black annihilation. The project was completed by passing the Moongazers' data into the moon's core, from which new information-based beings are reborn and repeat the transmission through the Eye of Ibni-Belum. The latest of them is Eggie, in the Version 6.7 Moon Gazing quests.

Its safeguard, Project Lunar Veil, was meant to hide the moon so that the transmission would not draw a hostile listener. A reply to an earlier signal once reached the Traveler and their sibling, who were inspired by it.

Established: - The Stellar Blackbody: many years after Ibni-Belum's death a second signal and coordinates were captured. Ungien flew the spaceship Moongazer to them, although the destination was too far for a safe return. On the way he met an unknown creature, the Stellar Blackbody, and chose to fuse with it so it could deliver a message to the dragons. Years later the cloaked ship crashed into the capture station. His wife Maagees-Geti was first to enter and found a round, black, spiky creature whose data signature matched Ungien's. After delivering its message it began to die.
- The message, recorded in Moongazer's Engraving, came from a distant world and warned others against pitch-black annihilation, which the wiki reads as probably the Abyss.
- The project: inspired by the message, Maagees-Geti began Project Moongazer to send it back into space and inspire other civilisations as it had inspired her. With her former student Lusalim she widened the research. Because some researchers feared the signal would invite disaster from malicious aliens, she and Lusalim also began Project Lunar Veil.
- The arrival of the Heavenly Principles: Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory and generator were destroyed, and he surrendered his research to them to protect the moon's facilities. He entrusted Project Moongazer, one step from completion, to Nin-Kiggia, whose last step was to merge the data into the moon's core. She did so.
- Legacy: the beings born from the project consume each other to acquire more data until their mission is clear, then return to the moon's core, open the Moongazer module in the Eye of Ibni-Belum and send the message again. Columbina says this cycle may have occurred more than once. One signal reached the Traveler and their sibling, who did not know its origin but were inspired by it.
- The present: Eggie, a black kuuhenki born from the moon's will, is found unconscious by Columbina in Maagees's Greenhouse and slowly awakens by merging with others of her kind. With the Traveler and Paimon she collects data from terminals across the Frost Moon, receives the key from the moon's core, opens the Moongazer module and sends the message once more. Her energy runs out and she returns to the cycle of life.

- Origins: Ibni-Belum, the first Moongazer, received a signal from deep space. The researchers could not decipher it, but Ibni-Belum believed Nibelung, who had once journeyed into the sea of stars, might have sent it, and built the Eye of Ibni-Belum to catch it again. The researcher Ungien thought it came from a creature beyond the stars and built Ungien's Circle and the Space Lifeform Capture Station to catch alien lifeforms. Ibni-Belum later expelled Ungien as an oath breaker.
- Blackbody Matter: Maagees-Geti studied the creature in her greenhouse as "Containment Object-1" and extracted a black, filamentous, information-bearing substance she named Blackbody Matter. Hoping to preserve what remained of Ungien, she turned it into a living being of Archaeolune Energy and Blackbody Matter, Ungie, an enormous artificial kuuhenki. Ungien's consciousness was not preserved.
- Information-based life: Lusalim came to want to engrave the full measure of a researcher's affections, desires and ideals into data and create a life-form that could be reborn from it repeatedly, so the message would be broadcast across the ages. Nu-ur-Gestug told Xiuhcoatl, the Dragon King, about the plan, and the king offered practical suggestions that were passed back to Lusalim. Lusalim succeeded in the dragon-like Nin-Kiggia and raised her as his "daughter".
- Maagees-Geti's end: she used her own body to feed Ungie, declined and fell into a coma. Her final wish was to send the Stellar Blackbody's message out through the Eye of Ibni-Belum, and the transmission was made. She also asked Lusalim to perform on her the same technique she used on Ungien, and she became the Mega Kuuhenki Maggie.
- Lusalim's plan: he planned to collect the Moongazers' ancient moon energy data and merge it in the moon's core. He asked the Moon Goddesses to lend him the primordial power of creation, and they agreed, so the Moongazers' data could be reborn as information-based life.
- Ibni-Belum, according to the wiki's note, did not approve of the Moongazers' aim and expelled them as traitors; the title "First Moongazer" was given to him afterward for paving the way.
- Moon Gazing, third act: the Traveler, Paimon, Eggie and Columbina enter a dragon-built base on the Dark Side of the Moon, where Eggie reads that the base was built by a "Lord of Darkness" as a space-borne weapon powered by the moon's core. The group suspects this is the returning Nibelung. Columbina is drawn into the core and later reappears, explaining that the last step must be done at the Eye of Ibni-Belum since Ninnin cannot survive inside the core. She retrieves the key with the Traveler.
- At the core, the Traveler and Columbina defeat a guardian called the Warden of the Flame and find the seat of the moon's will. A recording of Nin-Kiggia, called Ninnin, tells them she left an imprint to guide future inheritors, and that the Traveler has met earlier incarnations of the moon's researchers, among them Ibni-Belum, Ungien and Maagees.
- At the Eye of Ibni-Belum, Eggie accepts that sending the message may expose Teyvat to the darkness of space, and is willing to give herself up for it, echoing the earlier Moongazers who held that courage and light must persist in a dark forest universe. Columbina proposes to shield the signal as it passes the false sky with her power as a Moon Goddess and erase its traces if danger approaches. Eggie then broadcasts the names of all the Moongazers before her, and her body dissolves, leaving her hat.
- The transmission unseals a stored reply: the Traveler's sibling, thousands of years earlier, thanked the moon's people for their bravery, compared their signal to a bonfire in a dark forest and promised to find them when their own troubles were over. In the aftermath, at the Traveler's Crater ship, the Traveler tells Columbina they once received a message too corrupted by distance to make out.

- Known Moongazers (wiki table): Ibni-Belum (first Moongazer, built the Eye); Ungien (life sciences researcher, built the Circle and capture station, flew the Moongazer); Maagees-Geti (researcher, professor, mistress of the greenhouse; created Ungie); Lusalim (executor of Project Moongazer and chief architect of Project Lunar Veil); Nin-Kiggia (final inheritor, left a recording at the core); Eggie (successor who opens the Moongazer module and sends the message).
- Related terminal sites: Nuur Stone Circle (Nu-ur-Gestug's Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array, which holds the account of the Dragon King's advice), Lusalim's Laboratory, Maagees's Greenhouse, the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab and the Archaeolune Storm Research Center.
- The Lunar Veil's role in the larger plan: see Project Lunar Veil. Lusalim designed the Veil as a crucial part of Project Moongazer, and it had to be suspended after the explosion.

Accounts: - Ibni-Belum: believed the signal might be Nibelung's; later refused the Moongazers' aim.
- Ungien: believed the signal came from a creature beyond the stars and went to meet it.
- Maagees-Geti: saw the message as inspiration and wished to pass it on.
- Lusalim: feared disaster from an unknown listener, but carried the work forward and eventually entrusted it to Nin-Kiggia.
- Nu-ur-Gestug: sceptical of the Lunar Veil as a stopgap.
- Eggie: willing to be consumed to complete the mission, and chooses to send it.
- Columbina: accepts the transmission with a plan to shield it.

- The Stellar Blackbody message uses a dark-forest framing: a civilisation that shows its light may be hunted, yet those who send it do so out of courage and hope. Different characters stress different halves of this.

Open questions: - What created the first signal Ibni-Belum received is not stated.
- Whether the reply the Traveler and sibling got came from the earliest transmission, or another in the cycle, is not stated beyond the stored reply.
- Who or what may be listening beyond the stars is left open.

- How the Moon Goddesses lent "the primordial power of creation" is described only in those words.
- The relationship of Eggie to Nin-Kiggia is read differently in different sources (see uncertainties).

Connections: - Safeguard: Project Lunar Veil.
- Place: the Frost Moon, its moon's core (Moonheart Gap), the Eye of Ibni-Belum, the Dark Side of the Moon.
- Dragons: Xiuhcoatl advised, Nibelung is suspected as the signal sender and the "Lord of Darkness".
- Cosmology: the Heavenly Principles and the false sky; the Abyss (likely the "pitch-black annihilation").
- Nod-Krai arc: see the Return of the Frost Moon for the larger moon story (Version 6.3), of which these quests are a side chain.

- The Traveler's own origin: the stored reply links the project to the Traveler and their sibling's journey, and to the Traveler's wish to return home one day.

207.content: The unknown creature Ungien met in deep space and fused with. It carried a message from a distant world, delivered it to the dragons and began to die. Its tissue gave rise to Blackbody Matter.

208.content: A book in the Frost Moon content that records the Stellar Blackbody's message in its first volume and an earlier deep-space signal in its second. The project page cites it for the warning against pitch-black annihilation.

209.content: A black kuuhenki-like lifeform born from the moon's will under Project Moongazer. Found unconscious in Maagees's Greenhouse, she awakens by merging with others of her kind and has no early memory of her mission. The group reads terminal logs as saying she is Ninnin, Lusalim's "daughter". She completes the transmission and dissolves.

210.comment: Project Moongazer: Ibni-Belum and the Eye
210.content: The first Moongazer, who received the first deep-space signal and built the Eye of Ibni-Belum to catch it again. He later expelled Ungien as an oath breaker. The Eye holds the Moongazer module used for the final transmission.

211.content: Husband and wife among the Moongazers. Ungien flew the Moongazer and fused with the Stellar Blackbody; Maagees-Geti studied the creature, created Ungie from it and later became the Mega Kuuhenki Maggie at her own wish.

212.content: The information-based dragon-like being Lusalim made and raised as his "daughter". She was the final inheritor of Project Moongazer and merged the data into the moon's core, leaving a recording to guide later inheritors.

213.content:
Project Stuzha (also: Stuzha, Project Icy Cold, Severe Winter Project, Snezhnaya's energy rationing): Project Stuzha ("severe cold" in Russian) is the package of energy-saving measures passed by the Snezhnograd Veche that forced Snezhnaya's factories and households to use less Kresnik Kristall, so the saved energy could go to research at the Armory Palace. Announced as temporary, it was extended again and again, leaving much of the country cold, short of goods and angry. Its hidden purpose is to feed Project Mistilteinn. It was put on hold in 7.0, when Ronova's curse stalled the research.

It was first mentioned in 4.6 and became the backdrop to Snezhnaya in 7.0. It is the clearest example of the Tsaritsa's grand plan reaching ordinary lives: the people pay in warmth and wages for a goal they were never told.

Established: - The Veche passed a resolution requiring all factories and households to cut energy use. Kresnik Kristall, the crystal fuel Snezhnayans burn to survive the cold, is the energy in question.
- The saved energy was diverted to the Armory Palace in Glupov.
- Alyosha says the project was announced for six months but has been extended repeatedly, and that no one outside knows where the energy goes.
- The extensions need a majority vote in the Veche. Pulcinella, the Veche's chair, steers those votes; Alyosha says detractors cave to his political pressure.

- **Effects.** Businesses closed, trains stopped serving some towns, and Kristall deliveries became fixed rations. In Sretomorozsk the Fatui delivered Kristall twice a month. In the village of Alatyr, deliveries stopped entirely, according to Shishkin (the act summary elsewhere calls Alatyr an abandoned town). Shishkin and the town's mayor were caught skimming Kristall for resale; Shishkin said he did it for his home village.
- **Who is involved.** Lyney says Pulcinella and Pantalone work on the project together (4.6), and that the House of the Hearth was given a key and dangerous role after winning the Hydro Gnosis. Tartaglia was summoned back from Fontaine for it. Pierro, in 7.0, explains its real purpose.
- **Real purpose.** Pierro says Stuzha is a set of measures to consolidate the nation's resources whose greater aim is to serve Project Mistilteinn, a weapon for the Tsaritsa's fight against the Heavenly Principles.
- **Suspension.** The curse of Ronova prevented any breakthroughs at the Armory Palace, so in 7.0 the project is suspended. Citizens and factory owners are told so.

- **Politics.** Opposition grows through 7.0. Tartaglia says a mock vote went badly and Pulcinella was furious. In the real vote the project passes with 61 percent, a smaller majority than before, after the factory owner Chugunov unexpectedly votes against.
- **Resistance.** The Rokot, a covert organisation of anonymous members, works against it, mostly through evidence and official channels. Its most radical member, Lelek, flips Veche votes by coercion; in Mistilteinn Odette reveals she is Lelek. Alyosha says the Veche would crack down on the Rokot if it crossed a line.
- **The Traveler's question.** In Great Deeds on the Tundra the Traveler, with Odette present, bluntly asks Tartaglia and Sandrone why they will not stand up for ordinary people. Tartaglia says he would vote against it if the Tsaritsa allowed him, but calls the hardship a sacrifice worth making for her long-term vision; he and Sandrone keep raising concerns in the Veche while speaking for those they represent.
- **After the pause.** In 7.1 Tartaglia says the atmosphere in the Veche had become lighter because more energy could go to the people.

Hardship and rationing: Daily life under Stuzha is shown most in Sretomorozsk (7.0). Shops are shut, the inn is unavailable, and a Fatui officer, Polonsky, arrives to hand out the town's Kristall under watch. A near-fight breaks out over the amount. Shishkin mediates and later confesses that he and the mayor were diverting shipments. A villager, Zolotova, speaks of falling sales and tightened belts; in Snezhnograd a guild trader, Savva, says his guild's trade was halved even as strong liquor sold better.

- Alyosha does not blame ordinary Fatui: he says they always act in the Tsaritsa's interest, and notes that Sretomorozsk still gets Kristall because of a relief proposal from Pulcinella himself, while the Northland Bank gave some Mora for disaster relief.
- Vodyanitsa describes Kristall rations as barely enough to survive on. She says Chugunov of the Iskra Manufacturing Plant drew energy illegally and underpaid workers, which Mitya confirms is rumoured; Mitya adds that Pulcinella is now demanding strict tracking of every Kristall batch.
- Tartaglia reports that Fatui families in remote areas have around 15 percent less Kristall than a typical Snezhnograd family and calls for clear allocation rules. Pantalone replies that fairness is relative.

Purpose: Mitya, the Royal Energy Commission researcher, tells Vodyanitsa that the Armory Palace needs a brand-new energy source that is neither the Light Realm's power nor elemental energy. Only the power in Stellar Linchpins qualifies, but harnessing it burns enormous amounts of Kristall with little progress. In the Armory Palace itself the Traveler wonders aloud whether the whole point of Stuzha was to support this research, and Pierro confirms it.

Pierro says the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau in Nod-Krai was part of the same effort. Columbina recalls that, in the past, she noticed the word Mistilteinn coming up together with Stuzha but kept her distance. Mitya says that when Ronova's curse struck, the materials and energy gathered through Stuzha were wasted.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Stuzha is described as suspended since the 7.0 events. Mistilteinn's restrictions have been lifted, but canon does not yet show whether the rationing returns.

When Chugunov's factory is told in 7.0 that Stuzha is suspended, his staff propose expanding production; Chugunov instead orders production halted and the workers compensated, leaving the energy for those who need it. The Rokot celebrates an interim victory but warns against complacency.

Open questions: - Whether and how the rationing returns now that Mistilteinn can move forward.
- What the Tsaritsa's people will do about the damage caused over the project's long run.

- The wiki says the project resumes after Ronova's authority is revoked; the quests read for this entry do not show it.

- Zolotova, a villager, says things only got worse once Stuzha began and, after Mistilteinn, that it is over and life may improve; Savva, a guild trader, says it is merely on the back burner. Their differing words show that ordinary people did not know its true status.

Connections: - Project Mistilteinn: the reason for Stuzha. Its own entry covers the weapon.
- The Tsaritsa's plan against the Heavenly Principles.
- Ronova's fall in 7.1, which frees the research.
- The Rokot, the Veche and the Royal Energy Commission.

214.comment: Project Stuzha: Veche Vote on Stuzha
214.content:
In Silence Alone is Disfavored the Traveler watches a Veche session. Pulcinella presents energy statistics and declares that Stuzha will continue. Tartaglia protests the Kristall gap for Fatui families in remote areas; Pantalone says fairness is relative; Sandrone steers debate back to data. The motion passes with sixty-one percent, narrower than before, after Chugunov votes against. Vodyanitsa suspects Lelek pressured him.

A reporter, Mironova, turns the debate into a sensational article. Vodyanitsa explains that elites usually back the project because ending it would force their factories to absorb the Tsaritsa's unchanged energy demand.

215.content: The Rokot is a covert organisation of anonymous, codenamed members who choose their own methods within its principles. Members such as Vodyanitsa oppose Stuzha's abuses by gathering evidence of corruption and leaking it so officials investigate; Lelek used coercion instead. The Traveler joins it in Silence Alone is Disfavored; one application option reads that they oppose Stuzha. A Fatui officer, Polonsky, says Rokot members hide under false identities working against Stuzha.

216.content: Sretomorozsk depends on twice-monthly Kristall deliveries from the Fatui under Polonsky. Alyosha and the Traveler discover that Shishkin and the mayor are siphoning part of each shipment. They are arrested and sent to Snezhnograd; Shishkin says he wanted to help his home village of Alatyr, which no longer got deliveries. Afterward the Traveler and Alyosha persuade Polonsky to help get their train onto the tracks.

217.content: After Mitya's experiment triggers Ronova's curse and everyone present 'dies', he recommends halting the work, and Pierro agrees to hold Mistilteinn until the Ruler of Death is dealt with. Stuzha is reported suspended to factory owners and villagers. In 7.1 Tartaglia says the Veche has become lighter. Mistilteinn can move on after Ronova's authority is revoked; Stuzha's own fate is not shown.

218.content:
Prophecy of Fontaine (also: Fontaine prophecy, Fontaine's prophecy, the prophecy of Fontaine, prophecy slates, prophecy slate, prophesied flood, original sin of Fontaine): The prophecy is a doom foretold for Fontaine. Every Fontainian is born with a sin that no trial can absolve. One day the waters will rise, the people will dissolve into them, and only the Hydro Archon will be left, weeping on her throne. Only then will their sins be washed away. Rumour links it to Egeria, the first Hydro Archon. For years it was a gloomy rumour, until the sea really began to rise and people really began to dissolve. Its truth and resolution are the climax of the Fontaine Archon Quest (Version 4.2).

The fans' name for it is "the prophecy of Fontaine"; in game people just call it "the prophecy". Lyney, who first explains it to the Traveler, says "prophecy" is almost the wrong word: what it describes is already happening.

Established: The truth, revealed in Masquerade of the Guilty (4.2): Fontainians descend from Oceanids, Egeria's water familiars. Because they longed to live as humans, she gave them human bodies by pouring Primordial Seawater into their "blood vessels". She had no permission from the Heavenly Principles to create a new human race. Celestia judged this a sin, and Egeria and all her creations were branded with an "original sin". Primordial Seawater dissolves a Fontainian back into an Oceanid; non-Fontainians are not dissolved.

Focalors, an Oceanid made human by Egeria, inherited the problem when she succeeded Egeria as Hydro Archon. She decided to deceive the Heavenly Principles: let the prophecy seem fulfilled while saving everyone. She split her divinity from her human self, Furina, and had Furina play the Hydro Archon for about 500 years. In 4.2, Fontaine put Furina on trial, and the Oratrice sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death. Focalors executed herself with the Oratrice, destroying the Hydro Archon's divine throne and returning its Authority to Neuvillette, the Hydro Dragon Sovereign. Neuvillette then declared the people's sins forgiven. The flood still came, but nobody dissolved, and the waters receded.

Behind the scheme:
- Focalors hid her divinity, with the Hydro Gnosis, inside the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale.
- The trials at the Opera Epiclese turned the people's belief into Indemnitium. Focalors used only a small part of it to power Fontaine and stored the rest for 500 years, building enough power to destroy a divine throne.
- She cursed Furina so that she could not die, or freely live for her own happiness, while Focalors existed.
- She had arranged for Neuvillette to serve as Iudex so that centuries among humans would make him unwilling to declare them guilty.
- Once his Authority was restored, Neuvillette's verdict made the Fontainians true humans, and he could separate the Primordial Sea's power from the All-Devouring Narwhal.

The prophecy text: The prophecy as Fontaine tells it (Lyney, Soloist's Prologue, 4.0):
1. Everyone in Fontaine is born with sin, and no trial can absolve it.
2. One day the water will rise and slowly drown the sinners.
3. The people will all dissolve into the waters, leaving only the Hydro Archon weeping on her throne.
4. Only then will Fontaine's sins be washed away.

The prophecy names no date and no cause. Nobody knew what the sin was, so at first most people ignored it. Then, in the years before 4.0, sea levels rose and places were submerged. In 4.0, Neuvillette notes that two parts had already come true: the rising sea, and the fact that Fontainians can be dissolved (the serial disappearances case showed that).

Accounts: Who claims what:
- Lyney (4.0): some say Fontaine's ancestors stole the power of the seas and roused its wrath; others say the people ignored the first Hydro Archon's warnings and offended Celestia. Lacking evidence, Fontaine treats both as conjecture.
- Neuvillette (4.0): rumour roots it in the last words of the previous Hydro Archon, Egeria. He suspects it is the "conundrum" she left to Furina.
- Augereau, a Fontainian in the 4.0 opening: an old story says people once lived in the ocean and grew blood vessels to carry the sea inside them. To him, dissolving would be like going home.

- Wriothesley (4.1) does not much believe in prophecies, but he found that this one kept proving accurate. He describes the waves of panic a prophecy causes: first when people hear it, again when they see signs, and again when it happens.
- Mona (4.2) came to Fontaine to speak on the prophecy as an astrologist. She says it concerns the fate of Fontaine and perhaps of all Teyvat, and must come from a powerful visionary.
- N of the Hexenzirkel (4.2) tells the Traveler that prophecies are "the history of the future" and will be fulfilled. She also hints that prophecies show the future as the gods see it, and that things happen in corners where the gods do not look.
- Focalors (4.2): Egeria knew the prophecy would come to pass, and knew that defying the Heavenly Principles is dangerous. Focalors calls the theft of the Primordial Sea's power Fontaine's "original sin", and the people's right to exist its "original justice".

- Nahida (voice-over, "About Furina", after 4.2): the prophecy was carved into Irminsul long ago, yet it seems everything has changed; she says "we both know her" to be smart enough to turn the fate of the world around.
- The Fontaine glider Wings of Merciful, Wrathful Waters tells another version. Celestia's envoy made a new "heart" for the Primordial Sea, Egeria, after the first heart, the first Hydro Dragon, was removed. Egeria's compassion led her into "all the sins" that beings of pure water must beware. The item presents these as tales told by vishaps, Oceanids and scholars, and warns that they may not be true.

Slates: The prophecy slates are four stone slates, set out as if as an offering in ancient ruins near Poisson. Navia, Neuvillette and the Traveler found them in Meeting Is Also Parting (4.2). Only three were there; the first was missing. An inscription below reads, roughly: reason dictates that this nation be destroyed, so its future history is recorded here in its past. The slates call themselves a "history of the future". Navia wondered whether this place was where the prophecy began.

What each slate shows:
1. Egeria using divine power to turn Oceanids into people. Freminet, sent by the Knave, recovered it from the sea floor and brought it to the trial in Apocalypse.
2. Egeria kneeling with her people before a floating island in the sky, as if confessing, as judgement falls on them.
3. The Hydro Archon (it looks like Furina) sinking into water, surrounded by people.
4. The scene the prophecy describes: the people dissolved and the Hydro Archon alone, weeping on her throne.

The order of slates three and four troubled everyone. Neuvillette later read the third slate symbolically: the people in it are humans, not dissolved Oceanids, so the water stands for judgement. In other words, the people of Fontaine would put the Hydro Archon on trial. Their trial meant to escape the prophecy was itself part of it.

Neuvillette sensed a second layer of information etched into the slates with "a different power source". He could not read it with only three slates. Once the set was complete, he decoded the true history of the Fontainians' creation and announced it in court. Who carved the slates is unconfirmed; the Traveler later thinks Vedrfolnir likely did (see uncertainties).

Fulfilment: Before the end, the prophecy's signs kept arriving:
- In 4.1, Wriothesley showed the Traveler a great sluice gate under the Fortress of Meropide, holding back the Primordial Sea. Its water had risen dangerously high, and Wriothesley built the airship Wingalet in case the gate failed.
- In 4.2, Primordial Seawater leaked around Poisson and some residents dissolved.

At the trial in the Opera Epiclese, the All-Devouring Narwhal, which had fed on the Primordial Sea, broke in, drawn by the Fontainians. Childe, in his Foul Legacy form, and Neuvillette drove it back.

After Focalors's execution, Neuvillette and the Traveler fought the Narwhal in the Primordial Sea. The battle's Hydro energy then flooded Fontaine, so that only part of the Opera Epiclese stood above the water. Furina wept alone on the defendant's stand, her "throne", as the water reached her feet. Navia in a boat, Wriothesley's Wingalet, and Lyney, Lynette and Freminet pulled people from the water. Then the flood receded. Survivors shouted that the prophecy had been wrong, and Furina, freed from her curse, walked out into the sunlight as a human.

Those who had already dissolved earlier were not restored. Skirk shrank the subdued Narwhal into her hand and called it her master Surtalogi's "pet". Afterwards, Neuvillette gave the Hydro Gnosis to the Knave as a diplomatic gift. She had earlier received the Tsaritsa's permission to use the Gnosis against the prophecy first, and she passed it on to the Tsaritsa. After the prophecy came to a head, the amount of Primordial Water on Teyvat's surface greatly diminished.

Open questions: - Who carved the slates, and why? The Traveler suspects Vedrfolnir (4.7), but nobody confirms it.
- Did the prophecy come true or fail? It was fulfilled in form but defeated in effect, and canon keeps both readings.
- How a prophecy "carved into" Irminsul could be outwitted, and what deceiving the Heavenly Principles means for the world's fate in general, are not explained.
- Whether Egeria herself spoke the prophecy, or only knew it, is unresolved.
- What the second, hidden layer in the slates was made with is not explained beyond "a different power source".

Connections: Remuria, Fontaine's earlier civilisation, lived under its own prophecy of doom. Lore texts say Sybilla foretold that Remuria's desire for justice would bring it down. Remus sought out the imprisoned Egeria, guarded by the dragon Scylla, for a way out, and she gave him a goblet of Primordial Seawater. Remuria sank anyway. Wriothesley knew a theory that the sea which swallowed Remuria would rise again, and that the prophesied flood was part of the same idea.

- The prophecy explains why Fontaine is obsessed with trials, why its god was an actress, why the Oratrice existed and why Neuvillette was Iudex.
- The Narzissenkreuz Ordo was founded to help Fontaine survive a coming apocalypse that its founders, Rene and Jakob, had predicted.
- The Fatui's interest in Fontaine was partly about this prophecy.
- Focalors destroyed the Hydro Archon's divine throne and Celestia took no action; in 4.7 the Traveler's sibling cites this as proof of the Heavenly Principles' dormancy.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text). Before 4.2, Fontainians knew the prophecy as a common, uneasy rumour. Most of them did not know they were made from Oceanids, why they could dissolve, or that Furina was not a god. Those truths came out publicly at the trial in 4.2.

After 4.2 the danger is over. Fontainians are true humans and no longer dissolve, the Hydro Archon's throne is gone, and Furina lives as an ordinary person. People remember the flood and the "miracle" of the receding water. Characters who were not present (for example, most people outside Fontaine) would know only rumours. Do not have the prophecy threaten Fontaine again, and do not treat Vedrfolnir's authorship as fact.

219.content:
Four stone slates in ancient ruins near Poisson depict Fontaine's prophecy as a "history of the future". They show:
1. Egeria turning Oceanids into people.
2. Egeria and her people kneeling before Celestia as judgement falls.
3. The Hydro Archon in water, surrounded by people, which Neuvillette read as the people putting her on trial.
4. The people dissolved and the Archon weeping on her throne.

Three were found in 4.2; Freminet recovered the missing first slate from the sea floor. Neuvillette decoded a hidden layer that revealed the true origin of the Fontainians. The Traveler suspects Vedrfolnir made them (unconfirmed).

220.comment: Prophecy of Fontaine: Original sin of Fontaine
220.content: Fontaine's "original sin" was Egeria's theft of the Primordial Sea's power to make her Oceanids human without the Heavenly Principles' permission. Celestia branded her and all her creations with it. The sin meant that Primordial Seawater would dissolve them back into Oceanids. In 4.2 Neuvillette, with his restored Hydro Authority, declared the people of Fontaine forgiven and made them truly human. Focalors called their right to exist Fontaine's "original justice".

221.content:
Focalors's 500-year plan to make the prophecy look fulfilled while saving Fontaine had five parts:
1. She split her divinity from her human self, Furina, and had Furina play the Hydro Archon.
2. She hid herself and the Hydro Gnosis in the Oratrice, storing the Indemnitium raised by trials.
3. She brought Neuvillette in as Iudex so he would come to understand humans.
4. When the people tried "the Hydro Archon", she executed herself and destroyed the divine throne.
5. Neuvillette, restored to his Authority, absolved the people.

Furina knew only that she had to keep up the act; if her identity were exposed, everything would be lost. The epilogue sums it up: Focalors deceived the Heavenly Principles and used Furina's endless performance to save Fontaine.

key: fall of the false sky over Nod-Krai
222.content:
Return of the Frost Moon (also: the Frost Moon's return, fall of the false sky over Nod-Krai): The return of the Frost Moon is the climax of Song of the Welkin Moon, the Nod-Krai Archon Quest chapter (Act VIII, "True Moon", Version 6.3). Dottore seized the Moon Marrows, drove Columbina into hiding, built an artificial Marrow and became the "Heretic of the False Moon". Columbina had fled into the moon's reflection, where she met the imprisoned Moon Sisters and took their authorities. To bring her back, Sandrone built a world-formula, Pulonia and the Wanderer's Irminsul core carried the computation, and Arlecchino, Varka and Nicole hauled the Frost Moon through the false sky. Columbina returned as the Trilune Goddess and vaporised Dottore (he was later revealed to have survived). Sandrone died protecting the Traveler. Afterwards the Frost Moon stayed within Teyvat, the Eternal Moon Marrow went to Lauma and the Iridescent to Arlecchino, and the Palestar Edict against Columbina was revoked.

Established: **Place in the story.** Song of the Welkin Moon Act VIII, "True Moon" (The First Sliver of Moonlight, Descending Moon, Welkin Moon's Homecoming), released with Version 6.3 on 2026-01-14, after Act VII.

**Setup.** On Moon-Prayer Night, as Columbina tried to return to the Frost Moon with the help of the Moon Marrows, Dottore diverted her with a decoy bearing the Frost Moon's signature, held the Marrows and began drawing on the Three Moons' power. Columbina removed herself by falling into the moon's reflection; he built an artificial Marrow and captured the Traveler.

**What happened.**
- In the reflection, where time flows backwards, Columbina met the imprisoned Moon Sisters (Canon, Aria, Sonnet), who passed her their authorities. She "died" there so her moonlit body could be reconstituted in the present.
- Sandrone built a world-formula, run on the Wanderer's Irminsul core hidden in Pulonia, covering about ninety percent of reviving her. The rest required bringing the Frost Moon down.
- Dottore, now the "Heretic of the False Moon", tore the false sky open and isolated the Traveler's companions. Sandrone took a blow meant for the Traveler and died.
- Arlecchino, Varka and Nicole pulled the Frost Moon through the false sky, shattering it. Columbina became the Trilune Goddess, opened her eyes, and with the Traveler destroyed Dottore and his artificial Marrow.

**Aftermath.** The Frost Moon stayed in Teyvat. The Tsaritsa revoked the Palestar Edict. Columbina gave the Eternal Moon Marrow to Lauma and the Iridescent to Arlecchino, and moved to Hiisi Island among the Frostmoon Scions.

**The reflection.** Columbina meets Rerir and Tholindis before the sisters. The sisters are made mortal by the transfer, so at their request she returns them to the real world first. In the present, Nefer, aided by Lauma, reads Luonnotar's memory of Columbina's past, and the Wanderer offers his core at the risk of being reset or lost. Sandrone drew on research by the Remurians and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and used Luonnotar as an anchor.

**The reasoning behind the plan.** Dottore's trilune authority came from the Marrows, which Columbina and the Traveler describe as inferior to what she gained directly from the sisters. His artificial Marrow was cracked and shattered by her final beam.

**Details of the siege.** Before the fight the Traveler checks the group's Dodocommunication Devices with Sandrone, who has added a channel to track the formula's progress. The Traveler's companions split to defend Nasha Town. Sandrone and Pulonia attack Dottore in the arena and are beaten. Sandrone's last words to him are defiance ("go to hell"); Dottore then destroys her heart. The formula, which Dottore believes is stalled at ninety percent, keeps advancing in Pulonia, and the Frost Moon appears in the gash he opened.

**Departures after the battle.** Arlecchino takes Sandrone's and Pulonia's cores to the Fontaine Research Institute, following Sandrone's verbal will, and keeps her notes at the House of the Hearth, with one book sent to the Traveler's room on the Flagship. Sandrone had asked that Columbina not be told, which Arlecchino carries out without comment. The Wanderer returns to Sumeru to help Nahida with Dottore's damage. Nicole warns that the disaster has made Teyvat easier for the Abyss to detect. Varka writes to Jean that the Knights' expedition will return to Mondstadt in waves.

**The Frost Moon visit.** Columbina opens a portal from Hiisi Island to the Frost Moon, where the Traveler's ship waits. The flight logs show it passed Teyvat once thousands of years before and returned later, after which the Traveler was forced to crash-land at Nod-Krai. The Traveler tells her Teyvat feels like home, though different from what they knew. Columbina, who says she will return part of the Frost Moon to Nod-Krai as kuuvahki, lifts some of Teyvat's restrictions on the Traveler's use of the elements and gives them a Moon-Prayer Blossom.

**Order of participants' roles.** Arlecchino, Varka and Nicole pull down the moon, working with a plan in which Nicole and Alice, her Hexenzirkel colleague, had agreed to help Varka. Flins, Lauma and Nefer are held in extradimensional spaces by Dottore and are freed only when Columbina uses the Iridescent Marrow taken from him. Jahoda minds the Curatorium for Nefer under an earlier agreement. Arlecchino organised the evacuation of civilians from the area so the fight could happen without bystanders.

**The Moon Sisters in the reflection.** The sisters tell Columbina they were imprisoned by their creator Nibelung and explain the Heavenly Principles to her. They say they knew what was coming. They had never heard of kuuvahki, which suggests it did not exist in their time. They warn her that taking their authorities could tear her apart and that the prison would not let her leave alive; she asks whether she could leave while dead. Canon asks why her eyes are always closed. Columbina says she wanted to avoid lies, from the false moon to what others wanted from her, and Canon asks her to open them in the future and see the true smiles of her friends.

**Rerir and Tholindis.** Rerir tells Columbina that Dottore revived him and planned it to coincide with her weakness, and asks her to pass a message to Tholindis. Tholindis, once a Moon Marrow researcher, says she entered the reflection hoping to change her past and was torn apart, leaving only her soul. She forgives Rerir.

**The Frost Moon as a place.** After its return the Frost Moon is a playable region of Nod-Krai, reached through the Moon Gazing quest chain, where Archaeolune energy affects gravity. Its first exploration is in Version 6.7 content.

Accounts: - **Who pulled the Frost Moon down.** The quest shows Arlecchino, Varka and Nicole doing the physical pulling. The computation that made it possible is credited to Sandrone's formula, run on the Wanderer's Irminsul core hidden inside Pulonia. Treat it as a joint effort.
- **Why Sandrone died.** Characters present attribute it to her choosing to take a blow meant for the Traveler. Arlecchino later explains that this was also a deliberate deception: the formula was in Pulonia and a false version in Sandrone's own body. The Traveler's statement to Dottore that Sandrone was part of the team is the party's view; Dottore's view was that her inability to trust caused her fall.
- **Why the Heavenly Principles put the ship on the Frost Moon.** Columbina offers two possible reasons and does not claim to know. See uncertainties.

- **Dottore's account.** He frames his plan as becoming Teyvat's new "creator-god", and calls Columbina's rescue futile. He is an antagonist and an unreliable narrator on motives.
- **Rerir's account of the Abyss in the reflection.** He says some Abyssal energy was already there before he arrived and that rejecting it silenced the voices in his head. Columbina notes he only partly denies responsibility.

Open questions: - Where exactly the Frost Moon sits and how it relates to the broken false sky.
- Whether Canon left a Moon Marrow.
- Why the Heavenly Principles hid the spaceship there.

- What happened to the Moon Sisters after Columbina returned them to the real world. Canon says they wished to face the end at their own point in time; canon does not show it.
- How much of Columbina's nature changed beyond what she says: she returned some of her power to protect the world and keeps only enough to live with her friends.

Connections: This event ends Dottore's hold over Nod-Krai and leads to the revocation of the Palestar Edict, restores the Frost Moon that the Heavenly Principles flung beyond the false sky during the war of funerary flame, and ends the shadowmoon's purpose. It leads into Act IX, As All Falls to Emptiness, where Dottore's story continues. See Columbina, Sandrone, Dottore, the Three Moons, Moon Marrow, the false sky and Nod-Krai.

Later, in Version 6.6, Act X reveals that Dottore survived: before dying he had one half of his soul recorded by the Irminsul and uploaded another half as data, and he returned as the Exalted Master of the Heretical Path. @version tags apply to the sub-entries below.

223.comment: Return of the Frost Moon: Moon Marrows after the battle
223.content:
After the fight Columbina gave the Eternal Moon Marrow (from Aria) to Lauma of the Frostmoon Scions, and the Iridescent Moon Marrow (from Sonnet, once corrupted by Abyssal energy and purified earlier by the Traveler) to Arlecchino. Dottore's artificial Marrow was destroyed. A Marrow forms only after a Moon Goddess has died; Columbina is the living Frost Moon goddess and has none of her own. Each Marrow is tied to its goddess: one goddess cannot use another's power through a Marrow or hold two Marrows at once, though a Moon Goddess can draw on one to restore some of her own power.

Before the battle, the Traveler and Arlecchino had used the Marrows to guide Columbina's return to the Frost Moon, which Dottore subverted; during the battle Columbina and the Traveler wrested both Marrows from him. Columbina has implied a Marrow is a symbol of godhood comparable to a Gnosis. Lauma restored the Eternal Moon Marrow to its place in the Frostmoon Scions' secret chamber.

224.comment: Return of the Frost Moon: The Frost Moon after its return
224.content:
After Dottore's defeat the Frost Moon remained within Teyvat's sky rather than returning beyond the false sky. Columbina can move between Teyvat and the Frost Moon by portal and has said she will give part of it back to Nod-Krai as kuuvahki. The Traveler's spaceship is there. Columbina says the Heavenly Principles put it there.

The Frost Moon later became an explorable region, entered by the Moon Gazing quest chain (Version 6.7). There, Archaeolune energy, a form of energy very like kuuvahki, lowers effective gravity.

225.comment: Return of the Frost Moon: Sandrone's sacrifice and return
225.content:
Sandrone built the world-formula with the Wanderer's Irminsul core and was killed by Dottore while shielding the Traveler. Her last words to him were defiance. The true formula was in Pulonia and the version in her body was a decoy. Columbina mourned her alone, and Sandrone had asked that Columbina not be told of her arrangements. Her cores and Pulonia's went to the Fontaine Research Institute.

In later content Sandrone appears alive again and reunites with Columbina. This is covered in the Sunny Summer Fontinalia story quest, introduced with the limited-time event of the same name (Version 6.7), and in Sandrone's own entry.

226.comment: Return of the Frost Moon: Sandrone's reunion with Columbina
226.content: In the Sunny Summer Fontinalia story quest (introduced with the Version 6.7 limited-time event of the same name; the quest stays available afterwards), Columbina goes to Fontaine looking for Sandrone during the Fontinalia Film Festival, where she is cast as lead in the film "A Homecoming". Sandrone, alive again after her death, had been avoiding her; once Columbina finds her, Sandrone hugs her. The two visit Alain's grave with the Traveler and attend the party on the Wingalet.

key: Exalted Master of the Heretical Path
227.comment: Return of the Frost Moon: Dottore's survival after the battle
227.content: Dottore was widely believed dead after the Nod-Krai battle. Act X of Song of the Welkin Moon reveals he had planned his death: one half of his soul was recorded by the Irminsul and the other half uploaded as data, and he returned as the Exalted Master of the Heretical Path. He is finally killed when Nahida burns the Irminsul. Characters in Nod-Krai before this revelation believe he is dead.

228.comment: Return of the Frost Moon: Aftermath in Nod-Krai
228.content: The Tsaritsa revoked the Palestar Edict, Columbina's arrest warrant, once Dottore's intentions were known to her. A new League was formed jointly by Nod-Krai's factions. Flins urged Illuga to represent the Lightkeepers in it, and Tarno addressed the public in Nasha Town. Aino and Ineffa helped distribute food on behalf of the Frostmoon Scions. Columbina took Lauma's suggestion to live on Hiisi Island, and hopes to attend the next Moon-Prayer Night openly as herself.

229.content:
Sacred Heir Prophecy (also: Sacred Heir Project, Sacred Heir, Prophecy of the Sacred Heir, heir of Elysium, Ruler of Elysium, King of Elysium, Seed of Life Project): The Sacred Heir Prophecy is the Frostmoon Scions' old belief that a chosen child of their purified Hyperborean bloodline would one day be born to rule Elysium, an age of abundance and peace. The Sacred Heir Project is the long programme of controlled breeding and rules on marriage that was meant to produce that child. Its decrees survived in a sealed chamber on Hiisi Island, the Court of the First Edict, until the Traveler and Verna opened it in 6.0. The project ended about 500 years ago, when the maiden chosen to bear the heir eloped, and the Archpriestess Lovia's desperate replacements ended in murder, rebellion and her own death at the hands of her granddaughter Aila.

Established: - **The prophecy.** The decrees in the Court of the First Edict quote it. In the fullness of time Elysium will come, and with it a sovereign ordained to rule it. The "false sevenfold radiance" of the high heavens will fall at that ruler's feet, the bones of the earth will rise to follow, and from the ruler will spring union with the world and the rebuilding of the first great cause.
- **The Sacred Heir Project.** A protocol written after Hyperborea's fall, by Spargapiris of Haxathrausa as Acting Archpriestess of Hyperborea, says the project is the old Seed of Life Project of the Hyperborea era, renamed. The original relied on Tekhneikos processes (gene editing and the work of the fae), which were lost in the fall, so the Scions fell back on slow artificial selection: recorded generations, chosen pairings, persuasion rather than force, and a ban on pairs sharing ancestry within five generations. The expected result was a Sacred Heir who would command pure, unaltered elemental forces at will, without ritual tools or loss of soul, and who would at last be fused with the world.
- **The collapse, about 500 years ago.** The Archpriestess Lovia was driven by fading kuuvahki and failing rites. A maiden of exceptionally pure blood, chosen to bear the heir, fell in love with a Snezhnayan officer and left. Lovia had Rauthvangi retrieve her; the officer died and the maiden killed herself, leaving a son, Avrelian. Lovia then raised the twins Alia and Aila in isolation as replacements and had them kill other Scions and drink their blood to raise their purity.

- **Marriage law.** Decree III forbids marriage to blood relatives, to clans guilty of blasphemy, murder of the innocent, oath-breaking or parricide, to clans without antlered crowns, to the mentally disturbed, to descendants of the fae, to people outside the faith and to outlanders. Marriage needs the Archpriestess's permission. Breakers are cursed for seven generations, then seven more, and are to have their horns cut off with a silver blade.
- **The Sampo Mill.** Decree VI says only the prophesied heir can rouse the SAMPO (Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb), the sacred relic forged by the apostle of the Golden City. Followers below priestess rank were forbidden to enter the sanctum where it was sealed. A separate protocol records that its control module was lost with Hyperborea, so it could not be properly activated even by force.
- **Phasing out.** The same protocol planned to end widespread artificial breeding after about seven generations, after which limited intermarriage with outlanders could be allowed. The wiki notes that later priestesses instead leaned harder on the heir, which raised the importance of bloodline purity.
- **Items as sources.** Most of the story of the collapse is told by artifact and weapon texts rather than dialogue. Frost Devotee's Delirium tells of the bloodline "purified for over a thousand years" and of the chosen girl who cut off her bloodstained antler crown for a young officer. Pristine Plume of the Blessed tells of the twins, the faded storybook of white birds and their promise to leave together. Moonweaver's Dawn quotes Lovia ordering Aila not to marry the son of an outlander because she is "destined to bear the heir to Elysium."
- **The Court's documents.** Decree CMLXIII, "Alternative Plan for the Sacred Heir's Selection," is approved by Lovia, but its content has been erased, so the details of her replacement scheme are not recorded there. The older decrees are issued by Saredne, called the 13th Archpriestess since Hyperborea fell. The protocols name Vinda of Hithamthrausa as the priest who led the original project.
- **How it ended.** Alia fled Hiisi Island. Aila, now the sole focus, obeyed until Solovei told her Lovia was lying, then killed Lovia with the ritual sword Moonweaver's Dawn. As first Moonchanter she abolished the Archpriestess office and the Hyperborean rites, revised the hymns, and sealed the Court of the First Edict with the project's records and evidence of Lovia's deeds so there would be no second Lovia.
- **Aila's verdict.** In her recorded notes Aila writes that even if the maiden had borne the heir as foretold, the ruler would only have brought greater chaos to Snezhnaya, and that the new moon (Kuutar, later Columbina) had nothing to do with Lovia's schemes.

- **Version tracking.** The Court of the First Edict, the Silken Moon's Serenade and Night of the Sky's Unveiling artifact texts and Moonweaver's Dawn arrived in 6.0. Sacrificer's Staff and Dawning Frost (6.1) add Lovia's own backstory and the maiden's last dreams. Alia's confrontation with Rauthvangi in Nightingale's Song and the Treasure Hoarders legend in The Raven's Legacy are 6.3.
- **Dawning Frost.** In its text the maiden, now a mother, warns her unborn child never to set foot in Nod-Krai and never to be taken in by "that fool's dream of Elysium," saying no earthly paradise under the moon has been built for mortals. She is troubled by dream visions of Hyperborea's rise and fall and a voice vowing to raise a boundless Elysium "not to be king, but so that no other can ever claim that role."
- **Sacrificer's Staff.** This text presents Lovia as an orphan from another land, unaware of it, who was adopted by the previous Archpriestess after faith had waned and the moon no longer answered. After her adoptive sister, the purest maiden of the far north, died protecting her, she hardened her resolve; the text ties her path to the day her late sister's orphan would be born the sacred heir.

Accounts: - **The Scions' official doctrine** (decrees, protocols): a prophesied child of pure blood will rule Elysium and wake the SAMPO. The project aims at a being of pure elemental power fused with the world.
- **Lovia** (through Moonweaver's Dawn and Sacrificer's Staff): the project and the Heir are the Scions' hope and duty, justifying even killing. Her certainty is undercut by the reveal that she is not herself of Scion blood and bleeds red.
- **Rauthvangi** (Crown of the Befallen, The Last Night, the First Light): he calls Avrelian the prophesied Ruler of Elysium and says the two of them are "chosen by fate", and he treats the Sampo Mill as a treasure to seize. The Elysium he speaks of himself lies beyond the sky's veil, reached by getting out of the false sky. Alia says he used Avrelian from the start.

- **Aila** (recorded notes): Lovia's quest was futile and the Heir's rule would have been harmful; the faith should be rebuilt without the Hyperborean rites.
- **Avrelian's legend** (Treasure Hoarders): he wanted an Elysium "for the hungry and the poor" funded by the wealth of the haughty. How far this relates to the title Rauthvangi gave him is not stated.
- Item texts differ on the chosen one: the Silken Moon's Serenade texts say the girl was meant to "bear the sacred heir," and the decree speaks of a ruler to whom the heavens bow "at her feet," while Aureate Radiance of the Far-North Scions calls the maiden's son the "prophesied son." Preserve that mismatch rather than resolving it.

Open questions: - What the Heir would have been in practice, and whether it was ever a real possibility rather than a belief the Scions inherited.
- Whether the Heir, the Ruler of Elysium and the Primordial Human are the same thing. The wiki links them; the in-game texts read do not say so.
- Who the "other three" failures are that Rauthvangi mentions.

- Lovia's exact relation to the twins and to the maiden is given differently in different texts.
- Whether Lauma's rare sensitivity to kuuvahki is meaningful to the old prophecy. No source says it is; the wiki only notes her unusual purity.

Connections: Lovia, Aila, Alia and Avrelian are the people it touches most directly. It is the backstory for the Moonchanter title, the Court of the First Edict, the Sampo Mill, the Treasure Hoarders and Reed Miller's legend, and for Rauthvangi's schemes at the Pillar of Embla during the Cataclysm. The Hyperborean Primordial Human experiment on the Cryo Dragon's remains (see the Primordial Human entry) is a related but separate Hyperborean project that produced the Belyi Tsar.

Do not merge the Scions' project with the Tsar's: the Scions' version is a human bloodline project, while the Tsar's origin was an experiment on a dragon's corpse.

230.comment: Sacred Heir Prophecy: The Maiden Who Fled
230.content:
The unnamed maiden of exceptionally pure blood was chosen to bear the Sacred Heir about 500 years ago. She met a young Snezhnayan officer, cut off her antler crown and left with him, bearing a son, Avrelian. A spy sent by Rauthvangi, at Lovia's request according to the wiki, caught her; the officer died, and she took her own life with a dagger. Her name is not given in the texts read.

Item texts treat her as the orphaned daughter of Lovia's late sister. Dawning Frost shows her as a mother haunted by visions, hoping her child would live in peace and keep away from Nod-Krai. Frost Devotee's Delirium says her death forestalled the prophecy.

231.content:
After the maiden's death, Lovia took the twins Alia and Aila from a lesser branch of the bloodline and raised them on Hiisi Island. To make up for their thinner blood she had them kill other Scions and drink their blood. The sisters promised each other, from a faded storybook of white birds, to leave together. Alia broke the promise by escaping, leaving Aila to take the full weight of Lovia's attention. Treat this as a harrowing, abusive upbringing.

Aila's notes say she lied to Solovei when he asked whether she felt hate, as Alia and Lovia had also lied. The wiki describes her as destined to bear the heir only as a replacement, and as forbidden to marry the son of an outlander. Alia later became the second Reed Miller and died at the Pillar of Embla.

232.comment: Sacred Heir Prophecy: Court of the First Edict
232.content:
The sealed chamber on Hiisi Island where the Scions' decrees, protocols and evidence of Lovia's crimes were kept. Aila sealed it about 500 years ago to bury the evil, and the Traveler and Verna broke the seal in the world quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past. Its documents are the main in-game source for the prophecy's exact wording and the project's rules.

Aila's recording for the Traveler is also kept there. She did not want the Scions' obsession with Hyperborea to survive her and believed a Traveler would one day come to Nod-Krai and finish Rauthvangi for good.

233.comment: Sacred Heir Prophecy: Rauthvangi and the Ruler of Elysium
233.content:
Rauthvangi (Rotwang), the Belyi Tsar's envoy, told the outlaw Avrelian that he was the prophesied Ruler of Elysium and that they were both chosen by fate, and used him to steal the Sampo Mill from the Scions. Rauthvangi himself was after the Elysium beyond the sky, not the Scions' one. Avrelian believed him; Alia later saw through the lie.

In The Last Night, the First Light, a fading Rauthvangi mistakes Alia for Avrelian and urges her to wield the Sampo Mill "with the sacred heir's blood burning inside you", calling "those other three" failures. Alia refuses him and takes up the Reed Miller name against him. This is Rauthvangi's claim, not an independent confirmation that Avrelian or Alia carried an Heir's blood.

234.comment: Sacred Heir Prophecy: The Sampo Mill and the Heir
234.content:
The Hyperborean relic was held to belong to the prophesied Heir, who alone could rouse it, and was sealed from lower-ranking Scions. Records say its control module was lost with Hyperborea, so it is nonfunctional. Rauthvangi sought to use it at the Pillar of Embla; Alia ended that by throwing herself into it and igniting it with her Scion blood.

The Mill's decree promised unending gold, grain and salt and required offerings of wheat, goat's milk and salt each spring. A protocol decided to seal it indefinitely and not to reassess its activation for many generations.

235.comment: Sacred Heir Prophecy: Lauma and the Bloodline Today
235.content: Silver blood, sensitivity to kuuvahki and an antler crown are the marks of the Hyperborean bloodline. The wiki records only two Scions of unusual purity: Avrelian's mother and, today, Lauma, whose sensitivity is said to appear once a century. Lauma is the Scions' Moonchanter, and no text read calls her the Sacred Heir.

236.content:
Sakoku Decree (also: Sakoku-rei, Country-Locking Decree, the closure of Inazuma, Inazuma's closed-border policy): The Sakoku Decree ("country-locking order") closed Inazuma's borders. It was issued in the name of the Raiden Shogun and enforced by the Kanjou and Tenryou Commissions, with a ring of constant thunderstorms around the archipelago. Outsiders could not leave Ritou without a travel permit, and trade collapsed. It was issued about a year before the Traveler arrived (2.0), together with the Vision Hunt Decree. Ei abolished it in the Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, after her duel with the Shogun puppet.

Where the Vision Hunt Decree was how the Shogunate treated its own people, the Sakoku Decree was how it treated everyone else. The two are linked in the story: the Watatsumi Army drew people who opposed either one.

Established: - The Shogun, Ei's puppet, ordered Inazuma's borders shut. Anyone entering or leaving legally had to pass strict checks by the Kanjou Commission, which handles Inazuma's finances, customs and borders.
- Outsiders who were not Inazuman could not go beyond the port town of Ritou without a Travel Permit.
- The Tenryou Commission also helped enforce the decree.
- Storms were set around Inazuma to keep ships away. Few ships were able or willing to brave them.

- The decree was in force when the Traveler arrived by ship in Setting Sail (Chapter II, Act I, 2.0). Thoma, the Traveler's contact, takes them to the border checkpoint first and warns that evading inspection is not possible.
- The Kanjou Commission's Outlander Affairs Agency took advantage of the stranded outsiders. Yurika first asked the Traveler for two million Mora; Thoma negotiated it down to 600, and says such fleecing is common. Foreign merchants at the International Trade Association are shown struggling.
- Inazuma's economy suffered. Exports, imports and domestic trade dropped; ships that crossed the storms often lost goods, and fishing declined because the Kanjou Commission treated all vessels as suspect.
- Restrictions did not at first apply to the Fatui and Snezhnayan merchants, because of their diplomatic ties.
- In-game, the storm appears as the climate A Nation Closed by Thunder; its description says Ei has closed Inazuma and no one may enter or leave without good reason. It is cleared when Transient Dreams is completed.

- The decree was issued about a year before the Traveler's arrival. Chapter II explains it as part of the Fatui plot (see `accounts`), which used the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions to destabilise Inazuma.
- When the Vision Hunt Decree was abolished (Chapter II, Act III, 2.1), the Sakoku Decree did not immediately follow. Restrictions on foreigners were relaxed and the Kanjou Commission was purged of corrupt officials; the Outlander Affairs Agency later became more helpful, but the decree was still formally in place.
- After her duel with the Shogun puppet in Transient Dreams, Ei abolished the decree, thanking the people for their support. Visitors poured in and foreign trade returned to normal. Several NPCs in Ritou and Inazuma City gain new dialogue about it afterwards.

- The Inazuma culture article records that life was healthy before the decrees; Paimon says Inazuma had no problems in the year before she began travelling with the Traveler. Once the decree ended, Inazumans could trade with other nations, host visitors and travel abroad; those who leave to train sometimes call themselves "shugenja".
- The name echoes the historical Japanese Sakoku policy, and Ritou resembles Dejima, per the wiki's trivia. This is a real-world reference, not an in-universe fact.

Accounts: - **The Fatui plot.** In Chapter II the Fatui conspire with the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions, using the closure and the Vision Hunt Decree to cause instability and create a market for Delusions. Hiiragi Shinsuke supplied the Fatui with Crystal Marrow and Kujou Takayuki fed the Shogun false reports of the war (per the Inazuma culture and history pages).
- **Ei's endorsement.** Ei knew the Fatui were involved but did not see them as a threat, and the policy suited her ideal of eternity at the time (see Vision Hunt Decree). She lifted it only after the Traveler and Yae Miko led her to reconsider.

- **The people's view.** The Watatsumi Army fought the Shogunate partly over this decree and the Vision Hunt Decree. Merchants at the International Trade Association describe being treated harshly under the Kanjou Commission.

Open questions: Canon gives no start date for the decree and does not detail the arrangements for Fatui and Snezhnayan traders. Do not invent specific incidents, laws or numbers beyond what quests state. See `uncertainties`.

Connections: - **Vision Hunt Decree**: issued at the same time; ended earlier.
- **Kanjou Commission and Ritou**: the border authority and the one open port.
- **Fatui and Snezhnaya**: the plot behind the decrees, and the people exempt from the closure.
- **Watatsumi Army**: the resistance that formed partly in opposition.

- **Tatarigami**: the war the decrees inflamed led Watatsumi Army fanatics to break the wards on Yashiori Island, which unleashed the Tatarigami.
- **Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter**: Ei's Story Quest, in which the decree ends.

Timeline: - About a year before the Traveler's arrival: the Sakoku Decree and the Vision Hunt Decree take effect.
- Chapter II, Act I (2.0): the Traveler crosses the storm, registers at Ritou and meets the Outlander Affairs Agency.
- Chapter II, Act III (2.1): the Vision Hunt Decree is abolished and the Kanjou Commission is purged.
- Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, Act II (Transient Dreams): Ei abolishes the Sakoku Decree.
- No canon through 7.1 reinstates it.

237.content: A branch of the Kanjou Commission in Ritou that processes foreign visitors. Under the decree it overcharged stranded outsiders; after the commission was purged, it became more helpful.

238.comment: Sakoku Decree: A Nation Closed by Thunder
238.content: The storm belt around Inazuma. Entering it by sea sends travellers back to their starting port, so in play Inazuma is reached only through the story or by teleportation. It clears after Transient Dreams.

key: Civilization of the God of Salt
239.content:
Sal Terrae (Civilization) (also: Sal Terrae civilisation, Sal Terrae civilization, Civilization of the God of Salt, Havria's people): Sal Terrae ("Salt of the Earth") was the small civilisation of the gentle God of Salt, Havria, in what is now Liyue's Bishui Plain. During the Archon War she refused to fight and gave up land to other gods again and again, until only one hidden haven remained.
