The Traveler's alternate outfit "As Heaven and Earth Are Made Anew" came from a cabinet aboard, and the Traveler notes it is a matching pair with the sibling's, which the sibling liked more.

274.comment: The Twins' Origin: The ship's first pass over Teyvat
274.content: The flight logs the Traveler reads on the Moon show that the ship visited Teyvat a very long time before the Cataclysm (the wiki says thousands of years). It came close and moved on without landing, then travelled for a long time before a forced landing in Nod-Krai. The Traveler suspects the sibling left during that first pass. Canon does not confirm this.

275.comment: The Twins' Origin: The star-devouring darkness
275.content: The Sword of Descension text, a PlayStation-exclusive item, says the twins' world was one humankind tried to preserve against destruction and that facing a "star-devouring darkness" required a sword. The wiki presumes this means the Abyss, which is described elsewhere as ending worlds. The text never names it. Treat the identification as an inference.

276.comment: The Twins' Origin: The twins and the Moongazers
276.content: The Moongazers were dragon researchers on the Frost Moon who passed on a message from the Stellar Blackbody into space. According to the Project Moongazer page, one of the signals reached the twins, who were inspired by it. In 6.7 a hidden data segment in the Moongazers' terminal plays their reply: they promise to look for the sender one day. The Traveler worries that the signal might draw the darkness among the stars to Teyvat.

277.comment: The Twins' Origin: The Universitas Magistrorum's prediction
277.content: A namecard description (Achievement: Orbits) quotes the Universitas Magistrorum's report to the "Almighty Sovereign", Irmin, that the "two stars" had been captured by the world's gravity and, after a lengthy orbit, would meet again that day. The wiki reads this as the twins' ship returning to Teyvat. The text names no ship or twins.

278.content:
The Sibling's Goal (also: Abyss Prince's goal, Abyss Princess's goal, war with destiny, Atlas of the New World, New Khaenri'ah): The Traveler's twin (Lumine or Aether, whichever twin the player did not choose) leads the Abyss Order as its Prince or Princess. They have said they will not go home with the Traveler until their "war with destiny" against the Heavenly Principles is over. Their two confirmed aims are reviving the fallen nation of Khaenri'ah and gaining enough power to face the Heavenly Principles as an equal. Their final purpose, and the "truth of this world" that set them on this path, are still unrevealed as of 7.1.

Their methods have changed from quest to quest: a corrupted Dvalin, a mechanical god, a curse-cleansing device, the Loom of Fate. By 5.7 the sibling had woven a complete Ley Line network for a "New Khaenri'ah" and sealed it in the Atlas of the New World. Asmoday, the Shade of Space, has apparently left Celestia to follow them.

Established: - In 1.4 (A Soul Set Apart) the sibling asks the Traveler not to stop them or the Abyss. They say they cannot leave for a new world until the Abyss has "engulfed the thrones", and that they have already travelled this world once and seen its true nature.
- In 5.7 (A Space and Time Without You) they explain that guilt over abandoning Khaenri'ah drives the revival, but is only part of their motive. To speak with the Heavenly Principles as an equal, they say, they need the might of an entire world behind them.

- They regard Khaenri'ah as a second home. They arrived there with no memory, were made royal heir and "Savior", and only recovered their memories of the Traveler after years as Prince or Princess.
- When the Cataclysm began, the sibling was preparing to fight for Khaenri'ah. Then Direidyth brought news that the Traveler was looking for them, and they chose their twin over the nation, knowing they would regret it whichever way they chose.
- In 4.7 they said they still had time to unlock the Loom of Fate's full potential before the Heavenly Principles "awaken". The Principles had shown no sign of activity since the Cataclysm, and Celestia did nothing when Focalors destroyed her own divine throne.

- In 2.6 (seen as a memory in Memories of Inteyvat), they told an Abyss Herald that the Order had focused so single-mindedly on confronting the Heavenly Principles that it had neglected "our original mission", the revival of the homeland. They approved a risky device anyway, saying even a one-percent chance was enough: the cursed would rather return to the natural cycle of life and death than go on paying for "so-called sins."
- The Atlas of the New World holds New Khaenri'ah's entire Ley Line network. The sibling says they will one day find a "suitable host location" for it.

- The sibling still loves the Traveler. In 4.7 they say they miss their twin too, but that while the war continues they do not even know how to face themselves, let alone their twin. In 5.7, asked what the plan has to do with the two of them, they answer that it has "only ever been about us" and do not explain.

Accounts: - **The sibling**: frames it as a war with "destiny" and the Heavenly Principles. In 4.7 they point to Caribert, a cursed Khaenri'ahn denied any place in the world, and ask the Traveler who took that right from him. They add that their feelings about the Principles are too complicated to explain briefly.
- **Abyss Order members**: Haden, leading the Natlan operation, called reviving the homeland the Order's "greatest wish". He trusted that the sibling's regret was sincere, and asked whom else proud Khaenri'ahns could place their faith in, since they could hardly turn to the gods.
- **Dainsleif**: hunts the Order and doubts Khaenri'ah can be revived so easily. He believes the curse cannot be undone and read the Chasm device as an attempt to make cleansed hilichurls the foundation of a rebuilt Khaenri'ah.
- **Chlothar Alberich** (3.5, in a memory from centuries ago): told the sibling that Khaenri'ahns once believed they would bring "new strength and hope" and saw them as the Abyss itself. Dainsleif suspects this encounter was where the sibling's path began, but notes they never told him about it.
- **The Traveler** wonders privately whether the sibling is so set on reviving Khaenri'ah because they feel they failed as its Savior.

- **Celestia's side** (all speculative, and none of these speakers knows who the sibling is): in the "Gods' Limits" teaser, Istaroth suggests that the absent Asmoday may simply have "switched sides", and Ronova says that would be unthinkable unless Asmoday loved a new master more than herself. In 7.1 Rhinedottir still wonders whether the hooded figure beside Asmoday is that "new master". Naberius calls the idea Istaroth's passing whim.

History: How the stated goals developed, in release order:
- 1.0, Prologue: Asmoday seals both twins in cubes as they try to flee Teyvat during the Cataclysm. The Abyss Order is exploiting Dvalin. In the "We Will Be Reunited" story teaser the sibling is shown overseeing that operation.
- 1.4, We Will Be Reunited: the Order plans to build a mechanized god from a Defiled Statue, Osial's limbs and the eye of the first Field Tiller. The sibling appears, reveals who Dainsleif is and declares their war with destiny.
- 2.6, Requiem of the Echoing Depths: the Chasm device meant to cleanse the hilichurls' curse backfires and is destroyed.
- 3.5, Caribert: through disturbed Ley Lines, the Traveler relives the sibling's past with Chlothar and the cursed Caribert in Sumeru.
- 4.7, Bedtime Story: the sibling recovers the Field Tiller's eye and pushes on with the Loom of Fate.
- 5.7, A Space and Time for You: the sibling weaves New Khaenri'ah into the Atlas of the New World.
- 6.5, A Long Day in the Mountains: Melanta reveals Asmoday chose the sibling.
- 7.1, A Rekviem for the Underworld: the sibling's Khaenri'ahn origin story gains a Celestia link, and they are seen in Snezhnaya with Asmoday.

Background to the goals: the Vinster King Irmin named the golden-haired newcomer heir to the throne and later used them as a vessel for unlimited Abyssal power. According to the glider text Wings of Fate's Course Intertwined, the Five Sinners' storming of the palace was tied to this, and it made the heir "the key to the world's near-annihilation". The same text says that, having lost their own world, they came to long for "a single realm".

Present: As of 7.1 the sibling holds the Atlas of the New World, with no host location chosen. Asmoday appears to be with them, and the Heavenly Principles are still dormant.

In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), the Tsaritsa tells Rhinedottir about a monster that brought blizzards into Snezhnaya. Deep in the storm she saw Asmoday with a hooded figure, and the quest's stills show this figure is the sibling. The figure said it was worth witnessing "the end of the Third Descender's story". Asmoday then opened portals and both vanished, and the Tsaritsa killed the half-conscious monster.

In the same quest Ronova tells the Traveler she is waiting for Asmoday to return so the Four Shades can jointly activate their authority, or for conclusive evidence for a conviction, or failing that for the Heavenly Principles to awaken. In Etched in Time, Pierro reveals that his colleague Hroptatyr summoned the sibling from Celestia at the same moment Pierro summoned Paimon. Vedrfolnir had foretold that a blond "crowned heir" would answer Hroptatyr's call.

Open questions: - What is the "true nature of this world" the sibling learned at the end of their first journey?
- What would speaking with the Heavenly Principles as an equal achieve: negotiation, defiance, or something else?
- Where will the Atlas of the New World be set down, and what would that mean for the people already living there?

- What does "it's only ever been about us" mean for the twins' own fate?
- What condition did the Lord of the Night impose?
- Why did Asmoday turn to the sibling?
- Why did the sibling come to witness "the end of the Third Descender's story"?
- What were they doing in Celestia before Hroptatyr's summoning?

- In 4.7 the sibling hinted that it was no coincidence they found the Sea of Flowers at the End, a place where the Inteyvat flower (the one the twins once searched the stars for) was in full bloom. They did not explain what they meant.
- In 5.7, Direidyth's time-crossing errand, made possible by Istaroth, caused the very choice the sibling has regretted for five centuries, and they asked aloud whether Istaroth was mocking them. How Istaroth's intentions bear on the sibling's goals is unknown.

Connections: The goals tie into the Abyss Order and its Loom of Fate, the curse of the Khaenri'ahns, the Savior of Khaenri'ah, the dormancy of the Heavenly Principles, Asmoday's defection, and the Descender idea, since a Descender's power is described elsewhere in canon in terms of the backing of a world. The Traveler's own goal of reuniting with their twin is the other half of this thread.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation): present the sibling's goals only as far as canon states them. Never give a definitive answer to what the "truth of this world" is, what they want from the Heavenly Principles, or where New Khaenri'ah will be placed. Ordinary Teyvat residents know nothing of this. Most do not even know that the Abyss Order has a Prince or Princess, let alone that it is the Traveler's twin.

Characters who could plausibly know parts of this: Dainsleif, Paimon, the Traveler, and senior Abyss Order members such as Heralds and Haden. Citlali knows of the Atlas through the Lord of the Night, and Pierro knows of the Celestia summoning. The Tsaritsa and Rhinedottir saw or heard about a hooded figure, but do not know who it is.

Keep the sibling's tone as canon shows it: affectionate and regretful toward the Traveler, resolute about the war, and unwilling to explain everything. Do not portray them as wanting to destroy Teyvat's nations or as a simple villain; canon has not shown that. Equally, do not soften what they have done: they authorised the Chasm device knowing it would likely cause great suffering if it failed.

279.comment: The Sibling's Goal: Atlas of the New World
279.content:
The Atlas of the New World is what the Loom of Fate produced. It holds the full Ley Line network of a "New Khaenri'ah". The sibling believed Teyvat's Ley Lines were locked by the Heavenly Principles, so that none could be added or replaced, but learned that Natlan's Night Kingdom seemed to be an exception. They had the Abyss Order fake an invasion of Natlan to buy time to negotiate with the Lord of the Night, who gave room for the weaving but no new Ley Lines.

With an Inteyvat flower as the base, the sibling grew a realm modelled on the Khaenri'ah of five hundred years ago and superimposed it on present-day Natlan's spacetime. This is how the Traveler met Direidyth. Order members meditating to recall the old nation supplied memories as raw material. The operation also drew in Dainsleif, whose memories of Khaenri'ah Haden called the most complete of any survivor. According to Citlali, the Lord of the Night allowed this because preserving a whole nation as an "Atlas" seemed a possible third option between Mavuika's view, that culture and memory should be protected, and the Captain's, that Ley Lines should be preserved above all. She did so once satisfied it would not affect Natlan, and probably on an undisclosed condition.

280.comment: The Sibling's Goal: The war with destiny
280.content: At the 1.4 reunion the sibling says home is wherever the twins are together, but that they cannot go to the next world yet. Until the Abyss has engulfed the thrones, their war with destiny (meaning the Heavenly Principles) will not end. They tell the Traveler that, by the end of their own journey, they too will see the world's true nature, and add that they have more than enough time to wait.

281.comment: The Sibling's Goal: The Chasm cleansing device
281.content: In the Chasm the sibling found a pool whose water eased the curse, where dying hilichurls had gathered. They approved a device to amplify its effect a hundredfold, saying even a one-percent chance of success was enough. Dainsleif warned that failure would mean pointless agony for the hilichurls. Halfdan, Dainsleif and the Traveler destroyed it when it went wrong.

282.comment: The Sibling's Goal: Asmoday and the sibling
282.content: Asmoday sealed the twins during the Cataclysm and kept the sibling in a coffin in the Temple of Space. She later stopped attending the Shades' meetings. In 6.5 her abandoned Domain Keeper Melanta demanded to know why Asmoday had chosen the Traveler's sibling and abandoned him. Her portals are seen closing after the sibling's 5.7 conversation with the Traveler, and again after Melanta's defeat. In 7.1 she escorts the hooded sibling away from the Tsaritsa. Her reasons remain unknown.

key: end of the Third Descender's story
283.comment: The Sibling's Goal: The hooded figure in Snezhnaya
283.content: In 7.1 the Tsaritsa went alone into the heart of a snowstorm brought by an unknown monster and found Asmoday and a hooded figure beside it. Quest stills show the figure is the sibling. The figure remarked that it was worth witnessing "the end of the Third Descender's story" before Asmoday's portals took them both away. Rhinedottir wondered whether they came to witness the monster's existence or its death. Neither she nor the Tsaritsa identified the figure.

284.content:
Tribes of Fontaine (also: Northern Barbarians, northern chiefdoms, Fontaine tribes, Mistress of Many Waters faith): The Tribes of Fontaine were the many chiefdoms that lived in Fontaine after Meropis was drowned and before Egeria founded the modern nation. Remuria's records call them the Northern Barbarians. Most were clan societies ruled by councils of chiefs, though some had kings, castles and wealthy cities. Under Erinnyes, a singer who ruled Aremorica, they united in the name of the Mistress of Many Waters and rebelled against the Remurian empire.

Their story is known almost entirely through Remurian documents and through the knightly songs of La Chanson d'Erinnyes, so who counts as a tribe, and how barbaric they were, depends on who is speaking. After Remuria fell, Egeria gathered the survivors of both sides and had them build new cities around springs.

Established: - After Meropis was destroyed by huge waves and a hundred days of rain, survivors lost their inherited knowledge and lived among forests and rivers. Over time many tribes arose across Fontaine.
- Remuria, founded by the God King Remus, set out to conquer and pacify the northern chiefdoms and called them barbarians.
- Erinnyes united the northern tribes under the Mistress of Many Waters and led the resistance that ended Remuria's rule.
- Afterward Celestia ordered Egeria to return from the Primordial Sea and rule Fontaine as the Hydro Archon.

- **Social structure.** A Remurian field report by a legion officer, found in the Faded Castle, says most chiefdoms were rudimentary clan societies whose highest authority was a council of clan chiefs. It also admits that for some of them "tribe" was no longer an accurate word, since they had left primal barbarism behind.
- **Remurian conquest.** Early on the empire relied on diplomacy. The Harmost Aurelius finished a northern campaign without violence: legionnaires announced the conquest and many insular chiefdoms submitted and were absorbed. After Aremorica was taken, such easily pacified tribes became rare, and the Iron Legions met organised resistance and needed different methods.
- **Named tribes.** Aremorica; Lugdunensis; a tribe ruled by a council of astrologists; and the tribe of Erinnyes and Cassiodor (see the entries below). La Chanson d'Erinnyes also names Atrebatis, Bellouacoi, Gellone, Lyonnais, Rhenanie and Uiromanduoi; NPC dialogue names Dunnaer and Uxellobrogi; Peiregord and Aisias are named too but may have been Remurian.
- **Erinnyes's rise.** Her own tribe was massacred by a Remurian army, leaving her and Cassiodor as the only survivors. Cassiodor joined Remuria under the Harmost Boethius, while Erinnyes was taken in by the chieftain of Aremorica, a northern border tribe, to guard waters not yet seized by the God King. She later became its ruler, raised an army that united the warring tribes, and led it, the later Lochknights, in open rebellion.
- **Aftermath.** Egeria mediated the feuds of the survivors and told them to found cities around flowing springs, beginning an era of law that has lasted to the present.

- **Dates.** No year counts are given in the sources read. Remuria's history was written down a century after its destruction, and the Remurian report says Aremorica had been under Remuria for two decades before the uprising.
- **Faith and oaths.** The Mistress of Many Waters became the common object of loyalty. In the knightly songs Erinnyes tells Remus's emissary that she kneels to no one but the Mistress, and the princes who accepted her did so with sworn allegiance.
- **Sack of Petrocorii.** According to a text in the Pillar Hall, Erinnyes's forces went as far as sacking Cassiodor's palace in Petrocorii, the site of present-day Petrichor.

- **Remuria's final war.** Remuria's own history says that when Boethius ordered all barbarian tribes destroyed, he plunged the empire into ceaseless war and rebellion, which ended its golden age. The same account has Remus waking to the tribes' suffering, realising his error and giving a last order, but too late. A tsunami then swept Remuria away. See the Remuria and Remus entries for that side of the story; this file concerns the tribes.
- **Two pictures of the north.** Remurian history describes the post-flood peoples as living no differently from wildlife, while the Remurian report and the knightly songs show chiefdoms with kings, castles and cities. Both pictures appear in the sources, and the sources do not reconcile them.

Accounts: - **Remurian view.** The northern peoples were savages to be civilised, and their devotion to the "Mistress of All Waters" a false, even evil, faith. The Faded Castle report itself calls that picture a distortion born of the conquest of Aremorica, because its ruler forced other chiefdoms to say that all their gods were aspects of the Mistress.
- **Tribal and knightly view.** In La Chanson d'Erinnyes the lords of the north are knights who swear to Erinnyes and the Mistress of Many Waters, and who see Remus's demand for water and earth as a threat dressed as mercy.
- **Cassiodor's view.** The emissary of Remus (Cassiodor) argues that unity under one ruler is wisdom and that Remus's orders come from pity. He is a survivor of the same massacred tribe as Erinnyes, which sets their two paths against each other.

The Remurian report is written by a vicarius under the authority of Harmost Euergetia, and a note in it records that the astrologists' city was razed by Boethius and its name erased. So the empire both studied the tribes and deliberately wiped some of them out of memory.

Open questions: - The astrologists' tribe has no recorded name. Whether any of its elementally gifted warriors survived is not stated.
- The full list of tribes, and where each lay, is not given.
- It is not stated how long the tribes existed before Remuria, or how their gods were worshipped before Erinnyes's unification.

- How much of La Chanson d'Erinnyes is history and how much poetic embellishment is not established; it is a knightly song cycle and its place names do not all map onto known locations.
- The relationship between the pre-Remurian tribes and the unified civilisation recorded elsewhere in Teyvat lore is not explained in canon.

Connections: - Erinnyes, Cassiodor, Boethius, Aurelius, Euergetia and Remus are the main named individuals touching the tribes; each has their own entry.
- The Lochknights descend from Erinnyes's army; the Mistress of Many Waters is Egeria, the earlier Hydro Archon.
- Remuria and the Sea of Bygone Eras are the setting of the empire the tribes opposed; Petrichor stands on the old Petrocorii.
- Scylla and the vishaps appear in Remurian history among the "barbarian" forces Remus feared.

- Present-day Fontaine's law-centred society is presented in the Remurian history as beginning when Egeria settled the survivors' feuds and ordered cities built around springs.
- Fontaine's prophecy-centred history is a later matter; see the prophecy entry.

285.content: Aremorica, also written Aremori, was a northern border tribe, at first obscure. Its ruler Cunoricus voluntarily submitted it to Remuria, and it stayed under Remurian rule for about two decades. Later, after Erinnyes was taken in by its chieftain and became its ruler, Aremorica became the political centre of the resistance and the place from which the northern tribes were united in the faith of the Mistress of Many Waters. Remus's emissary is shown visiting Aremori Castle in La Chanson d'Erinnyes.

286.content: Lugdunensis was a city-state and the main trade hub of the northern tribes, wealthy enough to compare with Remurian cities. Its ruler took the title Holy King rather than chieftain and held that his authority came from a sword given by the Mother of Many Springs, a claim the Remurian report mocks. The city was eventually razed by Legio V.

287.comment: Tribes of Fontaine: The astrologists' tribe
287.content: A tribe governed by a council of astrologists, who picked out children with an elemental affinity and trained them into warriors nearly able to rival the Remurian legions. The Harmost Boethius conquered and razed it and had its name erased from memory, so canon does not give the name.

288.comment: Tribes of Fontaine: Erinnyes's tribe and the rebellion
288.content:
Erinnyes and Cassiodor came from a tribe that was among the first destroyed by Remuria, leaving only the two of them alive. Cassiodor went over to Remuria, and Erinnyes, taken in by Aremorica's chieftain, eventually led the northern tribes under the Mistress of Many Waters, who is Egeria. Her army was the forerunner of the Lochknights.

The book cycle La Chanson d'Erinnyes shows her receiving the princes of Bellouacoi, Atrebatis and Uiromanduoi and then answering Remus's emissary, who asked for water and earth and submission to the Sumphonia Capitolii. She refused, ordering that the emissary not be harmed. Knights named in the song include Guillaume of Gellone, Otkerus of Rhenanie and Drest, prince of Lyonnais.

289.comment: Tribes of Fontaine: Other named tribes and peoples
289.content: Besides the four described above, Fontaine texts name Atrebatis, Bellouacoi, Gellone, Lyonnais, Rhenanie and Uiromanduoi (La Chanson d'Erinnyes), Dunnaer (an NPC's text) and Uxellobrogi (another NPC's text). Little is said about each beyond their name. Peiregord and Aisias are named in the same song but may have been Remurian rather than tribal.

key: Snezhnaya's rebellion against the Heavenly Principles
290.content:
The Tsaritsa's Plan (also: Tsaritsa's plan, Tsaritsa's grand design, Her Majesty's plan, Snezhnaya's rebellion against the Heavenly Principles, Gnosis collection campaign): The Tsaritsa (Anastasya, the Cryo Archon) intends to confront and overthrow the Heavenly Principles. To that end she founded the Fatui and sent her Harbingers to collect the other Archons' Gnoses. As of 7.1 she holds six of the seven; only the Pyro Gnosis is missing. She also backs Project Mistilteinn, a weapon for that fight. Her goal was long kept secret even from her own people, and her endgame is still unresolved.

Venti put the question in the Prologue: he had not seen her in five hundred years and wondered what she was planning. Snezhnaya answered it openly in 7.0 and 7.1.

Established: - The aim was stated openly by Pierro (7.0) and by Anastasya herself (7.1).
- Besides her own Cryo Gnosis she holds the Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses.
- She keeps a seal left by the Third Descender in Zapolyarny Palace. Only a Gnosis seems to respond to it.

- **Why the Gnoses.** They are made from the Third Descender's remains and amplify their bearer. Anastasya says that, fully exploited, they could let a bearer transcend the limits of their authority, a necessary step towards facing the Heavenly Principles. Pierro calls them a key bargaining chip.
- **Why the fight.** Snezhnaya long ago reached the technological boundary the Heavenly Principles permit and lives under threat of a Nail of Retribution. To her, civilization as it stands can be negated at any moment.
- **Mistilteinn.** Project Stuzha, the Veche's energy rationing, exists to feed Project Mistilteinn.

- **More on the Gnoses.** They do not come from Teyvat's own system. The Seven can raise a storm, Anastasya says, but cannot shake the world's foundations; that would need a supreme authority that has always been out of reach.
- **The seal.** It came to her from her predecessor, the Belyi Tsar, who said it was the Third Descender's last legacy before the Heavenly Principles killed him. Every attempt to open it has failed. She hopes it may open once the Third Descender's remains are no longer scattered.
- **Pierro's framing.** Unless civilization stops being something the Heavenly Principles can "negate" on a whim, the fates of Khaenri'ah and Hyperborea will repeat. The Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau in Nod-Krai was a front for building Mistilteinn itself.
- **The love she rejects.** Anastasya names her authority as "love" but refuses to identify with it or use it. She says the gods' love for humanity is a curse the Heavenly Principles carved into them, and that this cheapened love. She chooses instead to be her true self and do her duty as Tsaritsa. Pierro calls the same curse one of many "rules" of the world that are really curses, and says she has ample reason to hate the Heavenly Principles.
- **Energy.** Pierro says elemental energy is Human Realm power converted by the Heavenly Principles, so turning it against them would be futile. Mistilteinn therefore relies on energy reverse-engineered from Stellar Linchpins, which carry the Third Descender's power. He calls it "anti-Celestia energy".
- **The Harbingers' latitude.** The Harbingers were given wide autonomy in retrieving the Gnoses, and Pierro says their actions do not fully represent Snezhnaya's official stance.

Gnosis campaign: The Gnoses were gathered one by one across the Traveler's journey.
- **Anemo (1.0):** Signora ambushed Venti in Mondstadt and tore the Gnosis from his chest.
- **Geo (1.1):** Zhongli handed it over as his "contract to end all contracts" with the Cryo Archon. He never said what she offered in return.
- **Electro and Dendro (3.2):** Dottore's segment received the Electro Gnosis from Nahida, who had taken it from Scaramouche. In return he agreed to erase his other segments. He received the Dendro Gnosis in exchange for information about the false sky.
- **Hydro (4.2):** Arlecchino got the Tsaritsa's permission to use the Hydro Gnosis first to try to avert Fontaine's prophecy. The prophecy was resolved by other means, and Neuvillette's diplomatic gift put the Gnosis in her hands.
- **Pyro (5.3-6.6):** Capitano dueled Mavuika but would not exploit her weakness. He asked to be relieved of the mission, and the Tsaritsa agreed; after his sacrifice she kept his rank intact. In 6.6 Nahida used the Pyro Gnosis, which the Traveler had borrowed from Mavuika, to burn the corrupted Irminsul. The Gnosis vanished afterwards.

In 7.1 Anastasya's only question to the Traveler was where the Pyro Gnosis is. Told it had been lost to the Ley Lines, she was surprised but calm. Because Gnoses are made from the Third Descender's remains, she reasoned, it cannot stay in the Ley Lines for long and will one day be expelled, so Snezhnaya will find it eventually.

The ruler of death: Ronova's Curse of Death halted Mistilteinn in 7.0. In 7.1 Anastasya used the six Gnoses to outmaneuver the Shades, and Celestia stripped Ronova of her authority. The project then resumed.

The curse kills everyone nearby at moments of technological progress. Anastasya said the Heavenly Principles could not be faced until Ronova was dealt with, and she made life-force research, starting from the sliver of the authority of life inherited by Vesna, Snezhnaya's single most important task. She then baited Rhinedottir, the Ruler of Life. Snezhnaya collected Seals of Life knowing the scale of it would draw her out, and Anastasya used what she had seen of Asmoday as her bargaining chip to invite Rhinedottir to tea at Zapolyarny Palace. Over the tea she used the six Gnoses, amplifying her Cryo power with her own insight of the past thousand years, to slow time in the hall. Rhinedottir missed the window she and Ronova had arranged to revive Ronova's victims without the Heavenly Principles' monitoring cycle noticing. Celestia then reclaimed Ronova's Authority of Death for abuse and ordered Rhinedottir to revive the dead. Pierro, Dainsleif and the Traveler defeated the weakened Ronova, and the restrictions on Mistilteinn were lifted.

Naberius conceded that the act could not be judged by Celestia and fell far short of the threshold for a Nail of Retribution, but wanted Anastasya punished for overstepping her authority. Rhinedottir declined, since Celestia was watching her closely, and called the Tsaritsa a worthy rival. Speaking as a descendant of Khaenri'ah, she added that Snezhnaya might achieve monumental things. Asked whether she had counted on all this, Anastasya replied that she does not sacrifice pawns to reach an end. When the Traveler called it the beginning of a new era, Dainsleif agreed, adding that it would not be a peaceful one. In the act's final cutscene the dying Ronova fused the Eitr with Snezhnaya's Nail of Retribution, which began to crumble and threatened to spread Holy Soil across Teyvat.

History: After the Cataclysm 500 years ago Anastasya succeeded the Belyi Tsar as Cryo Archon; Venti says that after that catastrophe she cut off all ties with him. In the third year of her reign she founded the Fatui with Pierro as its first member and leader. Over the following centuries the two of them recruited the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, and she gave them Delusions, a power separate from Visions. Snezhnaya became the most militarily and technologically developed nation in Teyvat.

In the animated short "The Final Gift" (released in the 6.6 period, set before the Traveler's journey), Pierro briefs the Harbingers that the Gnoses are an indispensable part of Her Majesty's grand design. He assigns Pantalone to finances and Sandrone to technical needs. Afterwards Signora, about to leave for Mondstadt and Inazuma, says she shares aspects of the Tsaritsa's vision, and that is enough for her. After Signora's death in Inazuma, the teaser "A Winter Night's Lazzo" shows Pierro playing chess with the unseen Tsaritsa. The Anemo and Geo Gnoses serve as pieces on the board, and her ice later seals Signora's mausoleum.

In the teaser "The Gods' Limits" (2025), Ronova scoffs that the Cryo Archon dares set her gaze on the Heavenly Principles with "paltry powers". Rhinedottir observes that the Heavenly Principles have yet to awaken and that in the Tsaritsa's place she would not pass up the opportunity either. Pierro answers, on the Tsaritsa's behalf, that even the gods have their limits.

Accounts: - **Pierro (7.0):** the Gnoses are a key bargaining chip; Mistilteinn is the weapon; the reason is that civilization is an illusion that can be negated at any time.
- **Anastasya (7.1):** the Gnoses are a step to transcending authority; civilization is "a lie told to us by fate"; Snezhnaya lives under threat of a Nail of Retribution.
- **Dainsleif (Teyvat Chapter Storyline Preview):** she is a god with no love left for her people, and her followers hope only to be on her side when her rebellion against the divine comes.

- **Rhinedottir (7.1):** after the tea she concludes that Anastasya's hostility comes less from past grievance than from Snezhnaya's ideals and future. In the teaser "Sudden Snow" she says over a chessboard that she hopes the Tsaritsa understands the nature of the game she is playing.
- **The Snezhnayan public (7.0):** people endure Project Stuzha because it is Her Majesty's will. No one knows where the gathered energy goes, since it has never been made public.
- **Several of her own subordinates,** among them Vesna and Danica, believe she is kinder than she admits.

Open questions: What lies inside the Third Descender's seal; whether the Pyro Gnosis will resurface; what Mistilteinn is and whether it can harm the Heavenly Principles; and how and when Snezhnaya will finally confront them. None of these is answered as of 7.1.

Also open: what the Tsaritsa gave Zhongli for the Geo Gnosis; when the dormant Heavenly Principles will awaken (Rhinedottir refused to say); and what Ronova's final act at Snezhnaya's Nail of Retribution will bring.

Other loose threads: what the hooded figure seen with Asmoday beside the blizzard-beast that Anastasya killed in 7.0 wanted there (the wiki identifies the figure as the Traveler's sibling; Rhinedottir does not know who it was); how the Third Descender's curse binds the Heavenly Principles; and what the Tsaritsa's own memory records (her transcription prism) show of a past she cannot trust.

Connections: The plan ties together the Gnoses and the Third Descender (Saarelainen), whose remains became them; the Fatui and the Harbingers; Projects Stuzha and Mistilteinn; Stellar Linchpins; the Four Shades of the Heavenly Principles; and the Traveler, whom Anastasya treats as a potential ally from 7.1.

It also connects to Khaenri'ah. The Khaenri'ahns descend from Anastasya and the Third Descender, and Rhinedottir and Dainsleif address her as "Mother of Khaenri'ah". Pierro, once of Khaenri'ah, carries a grudge against Ronova from the Cataclysm.

How {{char}} behaves: For roleplay: before 7.0, outsiders and ordinary Snezhnayans should not know the Tsaritsa's aim; the Harbingers' Gnosis thefts looked like naked aggression. From 7.1 the aim is open among her inner circle and known to the Traveler. Do not invent the plan's final step, the contents of the seal, the shape of Mistilteinn, or a resolution with the Heavenly Principles. Canon leaves all of these unrevealed. Do not present the Tsaritsa as acting out of "love" for humanity; she explicitly rejects that.

key: seal left behind by the Third Descender
291.comment: The Tsaritsa's Plan: The Third Descender's Seal
291.content: An object kept in Zapolyarny Palace, inherited from the Belyi Tsar, who called it the Third Descender's last legacy. It went unnoticed by the Heavenly Principles and has resisted every attempt to open it. Only a Gnosis seems to respond to it. Anastasya hopes that once all of the Third Descender's remains (the Gnoses) are gathered, its secret can be seen. Its contents are unknown as of 7.1.

292.content: Pierro explains that Her Majesty believes memory cannot be completely trusted, so long ago she began storing each day's memories in a transcription prism. (Act IV of 7.1 later reveals that the Heavenly Principles did alter her memories of the Third Descender.) Like a Stellar Linchpin, he says, it holds the Third Descender's power and so is free from certain laws of Teyvat, which makes it an indispensable tool against the Heavenly Principles.

293.comment: The Tsaritsa's Plan: Gnoses in Snezhnaya's hands
293.content: As of 7.1 the Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses: Cryo (her own), Anemo (Signora, from Venti), Geo (Signora, by Zhongli's contract), Electro and Dendro (Dottore, from Nahida) and Hydro (Arlecchino, from Neuvillette). The Pyro Gnosis vanished after it was used to burn Irminsul. In 7.1 she used the six together to slow time inside a palace hall, a feat Rhinedottir called power beyond what a god should have.

294.content:
Unified Civilization (also: unified civilisation, single unified culture, Ancient Unified Civilization): The unified civilization was a single human culture that once covered all of Teyvat, in what Fontaine's histories call "the first era". It arose after the Heavenly Principles came from beyond the world, defeated the Seven Sovereigns (the dragon rulers of the old world) and, according to an Enkanomiya chronicle, created humanity, who made a covenant with them. Angels, divine envoys sent from Celestia, lived among mortals, guided its kingdoms and taught them. It ended about 6,000 years ago in the war of funerary flame, when the dragon king Nibelung returned and the Heavenly Principles cast down Celestial Nails that destroyed many of its cities. Its ruins lie under every modern nation.

Known parts of it include Arcadia and Sal Vindagnyr (Mondstadt), Lang-Gan (Liyue), Delphi Pytho, whose sunken remnant is Enkanomiya (Inazuma), Ys and Khab (Sumeru), Meropis (Fontaine), a civilization under the Lord of the Night (Natlan) and Hyperborea, the Golden City (Snezhnaya). Few people today know the era existed: the heavens seem to have suppressed its memory, and much of what survives comes from forbidden chronicles, artifact legends and the angels themselves.

Established: - **Origin.** Before Sun and Moon, the chronicle in The Byakuyakoku Collection, tells it this way. When the "eternal throne of the heavens" came, the Primordial One fought and defeated the seven dragon-lords of the old world and made four shining shades of itself. The seven nations "submitted to the heavens". Then the Primordial One and one of its shades made animals, plants and finally humans. Humanity made a covenant with the Primordial One and "entered into a new age".
- **A guided paradise.** The same chronicle describes years of plenty. If people were hungry, the heavens sent food and rain; if they were sad, the heavens answered. The one taboo was to give in to temptation. Istoria, a philosopher of that age, remembers it as a "mortal paradise" in which the angels answered humanity's practical problems.
- **Angels.** Mortals could not bear to look directly at them and called them angels. They had pale silver wings and crowns of "sevenfold radiance". The crowns carried a command to love all beings of the earth equally, or perhaps a mandate to rule over "the nations of the earth" (Deep Gallery's Lost Crown). Divine envoys "spoke openly with the people then, bringing them the word from the heavens" (Amethyst Crown). Each region had its own envoy; Zibai, for example, watched over Lang-Gan.
- **Its end.** Eboshi says a great war broke out "in which the heavens capsized and the earth was ripped asunder". Byakuyakoku's chronicle calls it the coming of the "second throne of the heavens" in the Funerary Year.

- **What the angels taught.** Nicole's elders recall that the angels kindled fire in their palms and taught mortals to use it against the night, for cooking and against beasts. They twisted hemp into rope for climbing, clothing, shoes and river craft. They also taught "thoughts profound and ideals pure": steadiness of heart, endurance in hardship, and "dreams that belonged to mankind alone". Zibai taught Lang-Gan to till and weave, and its people worshipped her as the God of Soil and Grain.
- **Worship.** Besides the "heavenly god" (the Heavenly Principles) and the Four Shades, peoples of this age worshipped the Three Moons. Artifact text says believers loved the moons' gentle light more than the "wrathful and merciless Formidable Father". Pilgrims climbed Vindagnyr with laurel-crowned verses, carried carved jade to Lang-Gan's altars and took golden boughs from Arcadia's sacred oak groves. Some envoys, such as Zibai, also served as envoys of the moons; the wiki calls them Moon Envoys.
- **Rules.** The heavens set limits on knowledge. "To probe the heavens was forbidden, for every quest beyond the appointed rules led only to destruction" (Moonlit Offering's Libation). The eldest angel, Koitar, gave the law as: the laws shall not be tested, the strictures not questioned, the scriptures not infringed, and every transgression will be punished.
- **Writing.** The old script found on ruins, ley-line seals and divine sites across Teyvat (fans call it "Abyss language"; the wiki calls it the Ancient Teyvat Script) is mostly found in inscriptions of this civilization.
- **Ruins.** Ruins in a shared architectural style survive in every nation. This shared style is so noticeable that even a Snezhnayan newspaper contributor builds a theory on it.

Regions: Known parts of the civilization, by present-day territory. Canon does not say whether they formed one realm or many kingdoms under one faith; the sources speak of "nations of the earth" and city-states with their own envoys.
- **Mondstadt:** Arcadia, which worshipped Istaroth and Asmoday and also made offerings to the Three Moons, and Sal Vindagnyr on the mountain now called Dragonspine.
- **Liyue:** Lang-Gan, a realm of Sand Crystals and gemstones under the angel Zibai, where the Chasm is now.
- **Inazuma:** Delphi Pytho, part of which sank and became Enkanomiya (Byakuyakoku). There were also ruins of a moon-worshipping civilization on Tsurumi Island.
- **Sumeru:** Ys, a rainforest harbour now under the Great Red Sand, and Khab, a tower civilization beneath Chatrakam Cave.
- **Fontaine:** Meropis, at what is now the Sea of Bygone Eras, guarded by the angel Sybilla.
- **Natlan:** an unnamed civilization guided by Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night.
- **Snezhnaya:** Hyperborea, the Golden City, under Koitar, the first angel.

More detail:
- **Sal Vindagnyr's** founders fled a land of snow and strife and settled on a green mountain. A Celestial Nail, the Skyfrost Nail, later fell there, and the mountain became today's frozen Dragonspine.
- **Arcadia** included the city-state of Elysium at what is now Windrest Peak.
- **Lang-Gan** was tainted by Abyssal malice from the war, and Celestia sent a Nail to purge it. Zibai defied heaven to hold the Nail back long enough for survivors to flee. Its ruins are the Inverted City under the Chasm, and the survivors settled mostly in Chenyu Vale.
- **Delphi Pytho:** in the funerary war its people and land fell into the depths, where they warred with the Dragonheirs of the Depths and lived in darkness until the sage Abrax built the artificial sun.
- **Tsurumi Island:** underground ruins there have murals of Celestia and the Three Moons. A Nail is said to have struck the island, after which the fog began.
- **Khab's** tower and others like it were "man-made towers that could touch the skies", built all across the land; they collapsed under their own weight into the depths (Steeple of Ignorance).
- **Natlan:** the civilization there kept ritual sites where sages studied flame and the transformation of Phlogiston.

Fall: The ending, as canon pieces it together:
1. **Transgression.** Over time, some peoples took their knowledge past the limits the heavens set. Meropis's descendants stopped heeding the oracles. In Hyperborea, a youth possessed by the star-voyager Anacharsis questioned why seeking knowledge was a sin. Koitar fell in love with him, broke her crown, and the two led Hyperborea in rebellion against the Heavenly Principles.
2. **War.** Nibelung, the dragon king of the old world, returned in the Funerary Year and fought the Heavenly Principles, bringing the corruption of the Abyss. The Goddess of Flowers remembered "invaders" from beyond the firmament who overturned rivers and spread plagues, and who also brought "illusions that could break through shackles".
3. **Nails.** Afraid of the "rising tide of delusion and breakthroughs", the master of the heavens sent down divine nails to "mend the land", laying waste to the mortal realm. Hyperborea, Lang-Gan, Sal Vindagnyr and Ys are among the places struck.
4. **Exile of the angels.** Divine envoys lost their connection to heaven. The angels were cursed; many lost their minds and forms and became Seelie.
5. **Aftermath.** The heavens appear to have tried to erase the era from memory. Eboshi says the heavenly order "did not wish for those who remembered all this to remain on the earth", so Byakuyakoku was denied any road home until "heaven's powers of prohibition" weakened much later. A new order followed under gods rather than angels, leading to the Archon War.

Survivors scattered. Frost Moon worshippers from Hyperborea fled to what is now Nod-Krai and became the Frostmoon Scions. Lang-Gan's people went east toward Chenyu Vale. Ys's survivors probably became the desert's nomadic tribes. Fontaine's survivors lived "shorn of all knowledge and wisdom" among forests and rivers until Remus founded Remuria on Meropis's ruins. Natlan's angels were almost all devoured by dragons after the war, and its last envoy, the Lord of the Night, rebuilt a ley-line network as the Night Kingdom. Asmoday's watchers carried some people of the age, among them the philosopher Istoria, to the Temple of Space as living memory.

Angels parables: Nicole's character stories (6.6) record three cautionary tales the elder angels told her about cities that overstepped:
- A city that bound fire to its rule so that its light never dimmed, then turned that sun-bright fire on its own people and reduced countless lives to bone and ash. The heavens put out the flame and later raised new life on the dead ground.
- A city that wove everything from rope and tried to climb to "the most sacred heavens" by golden cords, binding them into an upside-down tower to reach a fruit it imagined there. The heavens cut the cords and sealed the trespassers inside their own canvases, bound by the cords forever.
- A city that pushed knowledge to its limit, cast off its bodies as burdens and sank into the lightless sea to explore further. Before it could look on the dark gulf beyond the world, the heavens boiled the sea away, purged the intellect that drove it and returned its people to their first shape.
These three match the gifts the angels taught (fire, rope, profound thought), turned into overreach. Canon does not name these cities or date their punishments.

Accounts: - **Enkanomiya's chronicle** (Before Sun and Moon) is written by descendants of the civilization who fell into the depths. It is reverent toward the Primordial One but records being abandoned and kept from home. The book is "forbidden" to ordinary readers.
- **Fontaine's history** (Pulteney, The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria) describes a heaven-blessed "first era" ending in floods sent against people who rejected their fate.
- **Angels** (Zibai, Nicole, the Goddess of Flowers via Amethyst Crown) remember it from the inside, with grief and warnings.
- **The Byakuyakoku chronicle's own guesses:** after the war, its writers assumed the Primordial One "must have defeated the Second Who Came", because the ban on returning home stayed in place.
- **The Goddess of Flowers** (Nabu Malikata) warned King Deshret never to seek the Master of the Four Shades or ask about the mysteries of sky and abyss; he chose to ignore her.
- **Istoria,** an Uplifted philosopher at the Temple of Space (6.5), says the priests and angels gave his people the answers to practical problems, and that the songs of the angels could cure melancholy.

- **Snezhnaya Vestnik:** a contributor's "Theory of Historical Echoes" (7.x) argues that the shared ruin style everywhere proves the "unified civilization" was Emperor Monomakh's tsardom, and that other histories are rewrites of his conquest. This is in-universe pseudo-history and should be treated as such.

Open questions: - How long the civilization lasted, and whether it was one state or many kingdoms under one faith.
- Exactly what the heavens forbade, and why some cities were destroyed before or apart from the war.
- Patraipolis is named by an Uplifted from King Deshret's era; where it stood, and whether it belonged to this civilization, is unknown.
- Whether all angels and envoys were the same kind of being, and how many regions had one.
- How far the heavens' erasure of the era reached, and what was lost.

Connections: Successor to the old world of the Seven Sovereigns; ended by the war of funerary flame; followed by the age of gods and the Archon War. Closely tied to the angels, the Four Shades, the Three Moons, Irminsul trees (angels were linked to them; Sybilla and Koitar each lived by one) and the Celestial Nails.

Modern echoes: the Seelie are cursed angels; Enkanomiya and Watatsumi descend from Delphi Pytho; Chenyu Vale's people descend from Lang-Gan; the Frostmoon Scions descend from Hyperborea; the Snowland Fae were first made in Hyperborea; the Spiral Abyss is said to have been an underground Hyperborean city-state.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): ordinary people in present-day Teyvat do not know the unified civilization existed. They see old ruins, strange script and monsters, not a lost world culture. Scholars, Uplifted, angels such as Nicole and Zibai, and people of Enkanomiya know more. Treat the era as hidden, fragmentary and dangerous to dig into.

Do not give the era a single capital, ruler, name or calendar; canon gives none. Do not present it as a technological empire everywhere; Hyperborea's advanced devices came after Koitar and Anacharsis rebelled. Keep the tone of a lost, guided paradise with strict, deadly limits.

295.content: Meropis was the unified-civilization city at what is now Fontaine's Sea of Bygone Eras. From its harbour, a great silver ship carried souls to the moons' golden halls, and its people offered songs and dances to the Three Moons. The angel Sybilla guarded its Irminsul tree. When its descendants rejected the oracles and tried to escape their fate, heaven sent giant waves and a hundred days of rain. No city was left above the waters, and the survivors lost their knowledge. Ages later, Remus found the ruins, met Sybilla (by then reduced to a golden bee) and built Remuria there.

296.content:
Ys was a harbour city in the rainforest that once covered what is now Sumeru's Great Red Sand. After the war of funerary flame, a Celestial Nail fell, the forest became desert, and the city sank beneath the sands. Its survivors probably became the desert's nomad tribes.

Weapon text from a limited-time reward (Silver Radiance of Gradlon, 7.0) says a divine envoy of the high heavens gave the city's high priest that claymore, granting the right to lead the harbour.

297.content: Patraipolis is an ancient city named only once, by the Uplifted architect Vitruvius at the Temple of Space in Unofficial Chronicle of the Desert Pavilion: his chosen epitaph begins "Please, tell my love in Patraipolis that..." before he turns to sand mid-sentence. Vitruvius himself lived in King Deshret's era, after the war of funerary flame, so canon does not show that Patraipolis belonged to the unified civilization; the wiki merely lists it alongside Arcadia, Lang-Gan and Delphi Pytho. Nothing else is known about it.

298.comment: Unified Civilization: Natlan before the Funerary War
298.content: A civilization in Natlan was guided by an angel now known as Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night. Its sages studied the mysteries of flame and Phlogiston at ritual sites. When Nibelung returned, the Pyro dragon Xiuhcoatl awoke and destroyed it, and dragons devoured most of its angels. Because the land was corrupted by the Abyss, a Celestial Nail fell there; the Basin of Unnumbered Flames is believed to be its crater. The surviving envoy rebuilt a ley-line network from fragments, creating the Night Kingdom.

299.comment: Unified Civilization: Forbidden chronicle of Byakuyakoku
299.content: Before Sun and Moon, Vol. 2 of The Byakuyakoku Collection, is a chronicle that ordinary folk were forbidden to read. It is the fullest native account of the unified civilization. It covers the Primordial One's victory over the dragons, the creation of humans and their covenant, the "Year of Jubilee" when the heavens met every need, the "Funerary Year" when the second throne came, the fall into darkness and the building of the artificial sun. It also records Istaroth's secret name, written backwards, because it was taboo to speak it.

300.content:
Vision Hunt Decree (also: Vision Hunt, Megari-rei, the Vision Hunt): The Vision Hunt Decree was an order in Inazuma to confiscate Visions from their bearers and inlay them on the Statue of the Omnipresent God, in front of Tenshukaku. It was issued in the name of the Electro Archon, the Raiden Shogun (Ei), and enforced by the Tenryou Commission. By the time the Traveler arrived about a year later, 99 Visions had been taken. In Archon Quest Chapter II the Traveler and Yae Miko led Ei to abolish it, and the Visions were returned.

The decree is a cause of the resistance movement of the Watatsumi Army and a central subject of Chapter II. It was also a Fatui scheme (see `accounts`), though Ei knew of that and approved it anyway.

Established: - The decree ordered Vision bearers in Inazuma to hand over their Visions. They were inlaid on the Statue of the Omnipresent God, built in front of Tenshukaku as the "Symbol of Eternity."
- The Tenryou Commission, one of the three Commissions, carried it out. The Raiden Shogun's government issued it.
- It began about a year before the Traveler's arrival, around the same time as the Sakoku Decree. Refusal and concealment were punished severely.
- The Traveler met the decree in Chapter II, Act II (2.0): during the Vision Hunt Ceremony, the Traveler intercepted Thoma's Vision. After the Traveler and Ei fought in the Plane of Euthymia in Act III (2.1), Ei abolished it.

- By Chapter II, Act II, 99 Visions had been seized; the 100th was meant to be Thoma's, at a public Vision Hunt Ceremony marking the milestone.
- Seized Visions could not be used by their owners, and many bearers lost their ambition along with their Visions, a side effect described in canon. Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu, whose Visions were seized, seem to have been unaffected.
- People who opposed the decree but not the government made decoy fake Visions. The Watatsumi Army on Watatsumi Island, which fought the Shogunate, drew members who had lost or feared losing their Visions, and also those who opposed the Sakoku Decree. It also sheltered people unwilling to fight.
- Kamisato Ayaka, Kamisato Ayato, Yae Miko, Sayu and Kujou Sara kept their Visions in public without incident. Sara served the Shogun directly; Thoma kept his until the ceremony. The Tenryou Commission dismissed Kurosawa Kyounosuke for poor performance and then took his Vision, so service was no permanent protection.

- Kaedehara Kazuha took his friend's Vision after the friend was killed, before it could be seized. Seizures were attempted against Kazuha, Hanshirou, Thoma, Yoimiya and Kazuha's friend. Kazuha's arrest warrant was cancelled after the decree ended.
- Seized Visions named in canon include those of Arataki Itto, Kuki Shinobu, Domon, Tejima, Iwakura Mitsunari and Kurosawa Kyounosuke, plus many Watatsumi Army fighters. After the decree ended, all seized Visions were returned to owners who were alive and reachable.
- The decree is what first set the Raiden Shogun against the Traveler: at the ceremony the Traveler used elemental power without a Vision, and the Shogun called them an exception: "Exceptions... the enemy of Eternity."
- The Balladeer says generating conflict creates a big market for Delusions.

- Because of the danger in Inazuma, even people without Visions avoided travelling there (per Alrani, Atsuko and Bibo).
- The reaction abroad: at Liyue Harbor, the scholar Alrani (World Quest Endless Research, 1.1) mentions the decree as rumour, linking it to the year with no new Electro Visions, and decides not to go to Inazuma at the time.

Accounts: Three accounts of why the decree existed:
- **The Fatui plot.** In "Delusion" (Chapter II, Act III) the Harbinger known as the Balladeer states the Fatui worked hard to make the decree happen. The Fatui hoped to produce unrest and build a market for Delusions in Inazuma, and they say it was in their interest.
- **Takayuki's deal.** In "Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage" the Tenryou Commissioner Kujou Takayuki admits to a bargain with Snezhnayan diplomats: generous rewards if he kept the decree enforced. He wanted to protect the Kujou Clan's position and believed the Fatui could not threaten Inazuma. He reported to the Shogun that the decree was proceeding without obstacle (see the Official Tenryou Commission Document).
- **Ei's reasoning.** Ei, in the Plane of Euthymia, says she gave tacit approval. She says Fatui actions so far were no threat to eternity, that individual ambition cannot coexist with eternity, and that nobody lost their life for having a Vision taken; those who died, she argues, died pursuing aspirations. Her pursuit of eternity follows her past losses, including the end of the previous Shogun, Makoto.

Yae Miko, who knows Ei well, disagrees. She tells Ei that a nation without ambition or the potential for change is a hollow shell, and that what her people want from her is attention, not promises. Sara, once she learns of Takayuki's deal, says she had already doubted the decree.
Characters weigh responsibility differently: Sara blames Takayuki, the Traveler points to the Fatui, and Yae Miko challenges Ei's own rigidity. Ei says she was well-informed about the decree.

Open questions: Canon does not give the exact date the decree began, or say why no new Electro Visions appeared during it. Ei denies controlling Visions, and Alrani and the Akademiya scholars suspected otherwise; the matter is left unresolved. See `uncertainties` in the header. Do not invent a link between the decree and the origin of Visions.

Connections: - **Sakoku Decree**: issued about the same time and enforced by the same government. Abolishing the Vision Hunt Decree did not end the Sakoku Decree at once; restrictions on foreigners were relaxed, and Ei lifted the Sakoku Decree later, after her duel with the Shogun puppet in Transient Dreams (Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, Act II).
- **Statue of the Omnipresent God**: after Chapter II, Act III the Visions were removed from the statue and returned.
- **Watatsumi Army and Sangonomiya Kokomi**: the resistance fought the decree and the Shogunate.

- **Thoma, Ayaka and the Kamisato Clan**: Thoma was scheduled to lose his Vision at the 2.0 ceremony; Ayaka wanted to rescue him herself, but intervening would have compromised the Yashiro Commission's neutrality, so the Traveler went instead and retrieved the Vision.
- **Kujou Clan**: Sara and Takayuki's conflict over the decree is a major storyline in Chapter II.
- **Snezhnaya**: the Fatui say the decree served their interests, and Takayuki dealt with Snezhnayan diplomats.

Timeline: - About a year before Chapter II: the decree and the Sakoku Decree take effect in Inazuma.
- Chapter II, Act II (2.0): the Vision Hunt Ceremony, Thoma's Vision, the Traveler's fight with the Raiden Shogun, and the order for the Traveler's arrest.
- Chapter II, Act III (2.1): Delusion and Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage; in The Omnipresent God Ei admits her tacit approval and, defeated, abolishes the decree. The Visions return to their owners.
- Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter, Act II (after Chapter II): Ei abolishes the Sakoku Decree.
- No later canon through 7.1 reinstates the decree.

301.comment: Vision Hunt Decree: Vision Hunt Ceremony
301.content: A public event at the Statue of the Omnipresent God to mark the 100th Vision seized under the decree, held in Chapter II, Act II (Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow). The target was Thoma, who was bound on an execution block. The Traveler intercepted his Vision as it flew toward the Raiden Shogun, who pulled the Traveler into another dimension and quickly knocked them out. As she raised her sword over the unconscious Traveler, Thoma freed himself, threw a polearm at her and fled with the Traveler. The Shogun ordered the Traveler seized "under the decree" and vowed to "strike twice" next time, and the Tenryou Commission added the Traveler to its wanted list. Thoma then went into hiding at the Komore Teahouse and the Traveler joined the Watatsumi Army.

302.comment: Vision Hunt Decree: Statue of the Omnipresent God
302.content: The statue in front of Tenshukaku was built after the decree to hold confiscated Visions. Its Chinese and Japanese names mean "Statue of the Thousand-Armed, Hundred-Eyed God." After Chapter II, Act III, the Visions were removed and returned to their owners.

303.comment: Vision Hunt Decree: Vision seizures in canon
303.content: Seized: Arataki Itto, Kuki Shinobu, Kurosawa Kyounosuke, Domon, Tejima, Iwakura Mitsunari and Watatsumi Army members. Attempted: Kazuha, Kazuha's friend, Hanshirou, Thoma, Yoimiya. Retained in public: Ayaka, Ayato, Sara, Sayu, Yae Miko. Unknown from canon: Gorou, Kokomi and others. Fanon should not extend these lists.

304.comment: Vision Hunt Decree: Takayuki and the Fatui bargain
304.content: Kujou Takayuki, Tenryou Commissioner and head of the Kujou Clan, told Kujou Sara and the Traveler that Snezhnayan diplomats offered rewards in return for upholding the decree. He judged the Fatui could not harm Inazuma while the Shogun's Musou no Hitotachi existed. Sara disagreed, and the Traveler and Yae Miko used the exposed evidence to press for the decree's end.

305.content:
War of Funerary Flame (also: war of the funerary flame, Funerary Year, great war of vengeance): The war of funerary flame was a world-shaking war fought about 6,000 years ago, in the "Funerary Year", between the Dragon King Nibelung and the Heavenly Principles for dominion over Teyvat. Nibelung returned from the sea of stars carrying the power of the Abyss and led the surviving dragons against the heavens. The Heavenly Principles won and killed him, but were badly wounded. In the fighting the Eternal and Iridescent Moons were shattered and the Frost Moon was flung beyond the false sky. Celestial Nails then fell across the land, and the old unified civilization was destroyed.

Most of what the people of Teyvat know about it survives only as fragments: Celestia banned knowledge of the history before this war, so it appears in ruins, item texts and the memories of ancient beings such as Apep, Nicole and the moon goddesses. Its scars are everywhere in the modern world: Dragonspine, the Chasm, the deserts of Sumeru, Enkanomiya and the shattered remnants of the moons all date from it.

Established: - Sides: Nibelung and the dragons (including the surviving Dragon Sovereigns) against the Heavenly Principles, the First Descender who had conquered the Seven Sovereigns long before.
- Nibelung brought the Abyss and forbidden knowledge into Teyvat; the corruption it spread nearly brought the world to collapse.
- Outcome: Nibelung was killed; the Heavenly Principles won but were left crippled.
- The Three Moons were destroyed or banished and their goddesses later died.

- Before the war, Nibelung had left Teyvat to travel the sea of stars and created the Three Moons and their goddesses (Aria, Canon and Sonnet) to watch the world in his place. The Heavenly Principles arrived while he was gone, defeated the Seven Sovereigns in a 40-year war, created the Four Shades and raised the false sky. The moon goddesses, too weak to resist, kept an uneasy peace with them.
- When Nibelung returned, the moon sisters disagreed over whether to side with him. He judged them disloyal, sealed them in a prison called the "moon's reflection", and turned their moons into weapons against the heavens. The Heavenly Principles answered by shattering the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and throwing the Frost Moon beyond the false sky. The surviving dragons later cheered the moons' fall, seeing the goddesses as traitors to their kind.
- After the war the Heavenly Principles cast down Celestial Nails to purge the Abyssal corruption. The Nails cleansed it, but they ruined landscapes, damaged ley lines and wiped out most of the unified civilization.

- The Heavenly Principles' wounds were lasting. In Neuvillette's Vision story, the "usurper", hurt in the "great war of vengeance", had its functions ruined and could no longer use absolute authority to suppress the world's original order. To keep control, it made the seven Gnoses with "one who came after" and built the new order of the Seven Archons.
- The Angels, Celestia's envoys to humanity, were punished afterwards for the archangel Koitar's part in the Hyperborean rebellion: Koitar lost her memories, and the others lost either their power (becoming Seelie) or their wisdom (becoming mindless beasts).
- Knowledge of the era before the war was forbidden. Before Sun and Moon, the Enkanomiya text that records it, is the book for which Celestia found Orobashi and Watatsumi guilty; Orobashi took the guilt on itself and died about 2,000 years ago.
- With the moons gone, the Moon Envoys who ferried souls to the moon were no longer needed, and souls of the dead were sent into the ley lines instead.

Course of the war: Canon gives no full battle history; it is pieced together from several accounts:
- Hyperborea, a golden city in what is now Snezhnaya, had rebelled against Celestia under the angel Koitar and the star-voyager Anacharsis. A Celestial Nail destroyed it. Dragons had joined that rebellion and kept fighting.
- Nibelung then returned, tore open the false sky and led the dragons against the Heavenly Principles. Apep says he "acquired the power of darkness from outside of this world".
- The moons were turned into weapons and then destroyed, as described above.
- The heavens and the earth were "rent asunder". Delphi Pytho sank into the depths and became Enkanomiya.
- Nibelung was finally destroyed. Kukulkan says the "reaver" annihilated him "at great cost".
- Apep, the Dendro Sovereign, aided Nibelung with her hoard of forbidden knowledge. She says she was stopped by a "giant spike" from the sky while gathering more from a collapsing world; that Nail turned her lands into desert and her emerald body to a sand-coloured grey.
- In Natlan, the Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, whom the Heavenly Principles had frozen in lava in a false death, woke when Nibelung returned. The dragons destroyed the local ley lines and devoured the region's angels, and the human tribes fell back into barbarism. When Nibelung died, Xiuhcoatl, already steeped in the Abyss, had a brief, grim moment of clarity.
- The moon goddesses had already decided to take countermeasures against the Heavenly Principles' harsh rule when Nibelung returned and interrupted them. Aria says Nibelung built the moon's reflection specifically to stop them from interfering in his war.

- Before Sun and Moon calls Nibelung "the second throne of the heavens", and says war was "rekindled, as it was in the world's creation". This Enkanomiyan view casts the war as a second contest for the heavens after the Heavenly Principles' original conquest.
- Lauma calls the war a conflict brought about by Descenders. The Heavenly Principles are counted as the First Descender. Treat any label for Nibelung as a Descender as the wiki's synthesis of these remarks.
- Before Nibelung left Teyvat, the star-voyager Anacharsis met him and warned that his world was doomed. The Deep Gallery artifact texts tell this, and say that when Anacharsis returned to Teyvat she found him gone and the heavens in control.

Aftermath: After the war:
- Celestial Nails fell across Teyvat. Known or implied impacts include Sal Vindagnyr (the Skyfrost Nail on Dragonspine), Lang-Gan (the Spiritstone, which carved out the Chasm in Liyue), Ys and Mt. Damavand in Sumeru (desertification), and probably Tsurumi Island in Inazuma and the Basin of Unnumbered Flames in Natlan.
- The unified civilization was dismantled and its history forbidden.
- The Heavenly Principles hid the shattered moons and the Frost Moon beyond the false sky and hung an illusory moon in the night sky.
- The Angels were cursed and cast out; Hyperborean survivors, guided by Canon, became the Frostmoon Scions.
- The Archon War, which began within a century or two of the war's end and lasted until about 2,000 years ago, placed the Gnoses in the hands of the Seven.

- Sal Vindagnyr's Nail destroyed its Irminsul tree and froze the verdant mountain into today's Dragonspine; its people did not survive.
- In Lang-Gan, Zibai, the city's divine envoy, slowed the Nail long enough for survivors to escape to Chenyu Vale.
- In Sumeru, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata later raised the Wall of Samiel to stop the desert spreading into the rainforest, and King Deshret drew on the Nail's power to build his Eternal Oasis.
- In Natlan, Kukulkan says the sky-nails destroyed the phlogiston-rich soil, so the dragons regressed to survive and most eventually became saurians. Ronova had the Lord of the Night build the Night Kingdom to repair Natlan's ley lines, an act the Heavenly Principles saw as overreach.
- Enkanomiya was barred from returning to the surface. Only Istaroth did not forsake its people, who were eventually led up to Watatsumi Island by Orobashi.
- Asmoday's watchers carried some people of that era, such as Istoria, to the Temple of Space as living memory.

- The moon goddesses survived in their prison but lost their place in the world. When they returned to Teyvat, Aria soon died, Sonnet fused with the Abyss and became the Crimson Moon, and Canon guided the Hyperborean survivors to Hiisi Island before fading. In the True Moon act (6.3), Columbina visits them in the moon's reflection from the future before this happens, and they pass the Trilune authority to her.
- Dragons that survived the war cheered the moons' destruction, as Fractured Halo records.
- Arcadia, an ancient nation in Mondstadt's lands, was buried under endless winter when "Eternity" ended with the war's outbreak.

Present day: The war still shapes the world as of 7.1. The Abyss that Nibelung brought remains Teyvat's great threat. The Celestial Nails still stand, and ley line disorders persist around them, though at the end of the 7.1 Archon Quest the dying Ronova fused the Eitr with Snezhnaya's nail of retribution, which began to crumble. The Heavenly Principles have been dormant since the Cataclysm 500 years ago. The Frost Moon returned to Teyvat's sky in 6.3 with Columbina as its goddess.

7.x revelations about the Third Descender Saarelainen tie into the war's aftermath. The Heavenly Principles made the Gnoses from his body in exchange for restoring his lover Anastasya, whom they had erased, and never harming their Khaenri'ahn descendants. A curse he laid on that bargain is what put the Heavenly Principles into their slumber when they broke it during the Cataclysm. In the 7.1 Archon Quest, beams of light rise into the sky over the six Celestial Nails.

Accounts: - Nicole, an ancient angel, tells the Traveler and Lauma the war's history in Where Does Her Name Rest? (6.2). She notes that the Heavenly Principles may not have known the goddesses were imprisoned.
- The moon sisters' own version, given to Columbina in True Moon (6.3), stresses the Heavenly Principles' harshness and the goddesses' failure to act. When Columbina calls it the "war of funerary flame", Canon remarks that this must be the name later ages gave it, and Sonnet asks who won.
- Apep and Kukulkan speak as dragons who lived through it, and both describe Nibelung as the dragons' rightful king.
- Neuvillette, Dragon Sovereign of Hydro, learned of the war only after regaining his full power; his Vision story calls it a great war of vengeance and the Heavenly Principles "the usurper".
- The Liyue moon legends (Moonlit Bamboo Forest) speak vaguely of disasters overturning the moon goddesses' carriage and ruining "the halls of the stars".
- Before Sun and Moon is written from Enkanomiya's point of view: ancestors who fell into the dark during "the Funerary Year", forsaken by three of the four Shades.
- Nabu Malikata's artifact text (Amethyst Crown) says the invaders brought war to her angelic kin, and the master of the heavens, fearing "delusion and breakthroughs", sent down nails "to mend the land".

Open questions: - How long the war lasted, and the precise order of the Hyperborean rebellion, Nibelung's return and the first Celestial Nails.
- Whether the Heavenly Principles knew Nibelung had imprisoned the moon goddesses.

- What Nibelung found in the sea of stars, and how he was corrupted by the Abyss.
- The full extent of the damage to the Heavenly Principles, and how it relates to their later dormancy.
- When exactly Saarelainen's bargain and the making of the Gnoses happened relative to the war.

Connections: See the entries on Nibelung, the Heavenly Principles, the Three Moons, Celestial Nails, the Abyss, the unified civilization, the Archon War, Hyperborea and Enkanomiya.

Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text): ordinary people in modern Teyvat know nothing of this war by name. Scholars may know of ancient ruins and fallen "nails", and a few ancient beings (Nicole, Apep, Kukulkan, Neuvillette, the moon goddesses, Columbina) know the history. Characters who heard Nicole's account in Nod-Krai, such as the Traveler, Lauma, Arlecchino and Columbina's companions, know the outline. Do not have characters speak openly of Nibelung or the Funerary Year unless they have a canon reason to know.

306.comment: War of Funerary Flame: Funerary Year (Enkanomiya)
306.content: In Enkanomiya's book Before Sun and Moon, "the Funerary Year" is the day the "second throne of the heavens" (Nibelung) came and war was rekindled as at the world's creation. Heaven collapsed and the earth split, and the ancestors of Enkanomiya fell with their land, Delphi Pytho, into the depths. Of the four Shades, only Istaroth did not forsake them. Celestia later forbade the history this book records. The sage Aberaku, a pupil of Istoria, became trapped there when the kingdom sank.

307.comment: War of Funerary Flame: The moons in the war
307.content: Created by Nibelung, the three moon goddesses split over whether to follow him when he returned: one argued they should follow the one who had hung the moons in the sky, another that taking sides would only bring the world closer to ruin, since he had returned bearing the Abyss. Nibelung judged them disloyal and sealed them in the moon's reflection, a prison of warped space and time, then used their moons as weapons. The Heavenly Principles shattered the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and flung the Frost Moon beyond the false sky. Rejected by a world they no longer belonged to, the goddesses later died. The Frost Moon's survival is why a new moon goddess, Columbina, could later be born in Nod-Krai.

308.comment: War of Funerary Flame: Hyperborean rebellion
308.content: The archangel Koitar and the star-voyager Anacharsis ruled Hyperborea for thirty years in open defiance of the Heavenly Principles. When their experiments with the Cryo Dragon's corpse froze the region, the heavens sent a Celestial Nail; Hyperborea rose against Celestia, joined by some Angels and dragons, but the city was destroyed and sank into the Shadow Realm. The fighting dragons were then joined by the returning Nibelung. Afterwards Koitar was stripped of her memories and all Angels were cursed.

309.comment: War of Funerary Flame: Natlan in the war of funerary flame
309.content: In Natlan, the Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl woke from a false death in Tollan's frozen lava when Nibelung returned, restored the Sacred City under the Thirteen Dragonlords, and joined the war. The dragons destroyed Natlantea's ley lines and devoured its angels, and the local human civilisation fell. After Nibelung's death Xiuhcoatl, corrupted by the Abyss, briefly regained clarity and used the last of his time and wisdom to transform the dragon city and create the Tzitzimimeh and Huitzilopochtli. The sky-nails ruined Natlan's phlogiston-rich soil and most dragons regressed into saurians. Ronova later had the Lord of the Night create the Night Kingdom to mend the ley lines.

310.comment: War of Funerary Flame: Apep in the war of funerary flame
310.content: Apep, the Dendro Dragon Sovereign, fought for Nibelung and gathered forbidden knowledge for him. She tells the Traveler and Nahida that the war's destruction nearly made the world collapse. A Celestial Nail stopped her, turned her domain around Mt. Damavand into desert, and turned her body from emerald to sand-grey.
